# Lectures from a Disciple. Vol. 3

## Lectures from a Disciple. Vol. 3

**Volume 3**

**Nirañjana Swami**

## Introduction

Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the most munificent incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, came to this world in order to teach us what it takes to love Kṛṣṇa. In the introductory song to his book Śaraṇagati, Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains that the very heart and soul of this love is complete surrender to the Lord. Then he adds that one should learn that science of surrender from genuine devotees—followers of the six Gosvāmīs of Vṛndāvana, who were the most confidential disciples of Lord Caitanya. Received from the bona fide spiritual masters in the line of disciplic succession, this confidential mood is transmitted from heart to heart. As Śrīla Prabhupāda describes in his purport to Bhāgavatam 4.28.51, such empowered gurus truly know that Kṛṣṇa is the well-wishing friend of everyone and the Supersoul in the heart of every living entity. Thus one attains complete fearlessness and becomes a learned person.

Our Śrīla Prabhupāda was no doubt such a guru. His faith and surrender turned so many sinful people into sincere devotees of the Lord. He filled his books with pure devotion and eagerness to share with everyone the bliss of loving service. Prabhupāda never compromised on the principles of unconditional surrender, inspiring his followers to continue making voluntary sacrifices in order to please guru and Kṛṣṇa. He knew that, as Nārada Muni says to Śrīla Vyāsadeva in Śrīmad Bhāgavatam (1.5.19), having even once experienced this sweet taste of surrender, one will never forget it. Then one in turn becomes the carrier of this mood, instilling the same faith in bhakti in the hearts of his disciples and followers.

I was fortunate to meet one of these wonderful gems of Śrīla Prabhupāda. Śrīla Nirañjana Mahārāja’s example and instructions completely changed my life. With all his great knowledge and realizations, he remains a chaste and humble servant of Śrīla Prabhupāda. In his Lectures from a Disciple, he quotes many renowned ācāryas in our Gaudīya line, expanding on what was given by Śrīla Prabhupāda, and never eclipsing Prabhupāda’s teachings and mood. As such, this book will be an invaluable asset in strengthening our faith and nourishing the creeper of bhakti. Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī in his maṅgalācaraṇa to Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu prays that his book would be viśrāma-mandira, a pleasant resting place for his elder brother Sanātana Gosvāmī and all the readers. Vaiṣṇavas are true connoisseurs of pure bhakti; for them anything opposed to genuine love or mixed with ulterior motives is like singing out of tune for an expert musician. This book of Nirañjana Mahārāja will definitely please anyone for whom Lord Caitanya and Śrīla Prabhupāda are dearer than life. Composed in the topical format like Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī’s Sandarbhas, it provides quick and efficient answers to the questions and problems one may meet on their way to Kṛṣṇa. Furthermore, it shows us Kṛṣṇa as He is—sometimes afraid of Mother Yaśodā’s punishment, sometimes gentle and grave, sometimes strict and demanding, but always merciful and well-wishing to His beloved devotees—the same Kṛṣṇa that Śrīla Prabhupāda so much wanted to give us, at the cost of any struggles and sacrifices.

Sarvajña dāsa

## Chapter 1 – The Supreme Personality of Godhead

## Understanding Kṛṣṇa

*nūnaṁ janair īhitam īśvarāṇām*  
*asmad-vidhais tad-guṇa-sarga-māyayā*  
*na jñāyate mohita-citta-vartmabhis*  
*tebhyo namo vīra-yaśas-karebhyaḥ*

**“My dear Lord, I am also the creation of one of Your energies, composed of the three modes of material nature. Consequently I am bewildered by Your activities. Even the activities of Your devotees cannot be understood, and what to speak of Your pastimes. Thus everything appears to us to be contradictory and wonderful. (Bhāg. 4.17.36)**

PURPORT

The activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead in His various forms and incarnations are always uncommon and wonderful. It is not possible for a tiny human being to estimate the purpose and plans of such activities; therefore Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī has said that unless the Lord’s activities are accepted as inconceivable, they cannot be explained. The Lord is eternally existing as Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in Goloka Vṛndāvana. He has also simultaneously expanded Himself in innumerable forms, beginning with Lord Rāma, Lord Nṛsiṁha, Lord Varāha and all the incarnations coming directly from Saṅkarṣaṇa. Saṅkarṣaṇa is the expansion of Baladeva, and Baladeva is the first manifestation of Kṛṣṇa. Therefore all these incarnations are known as kalā.

The word īśvarāṇām refers to all the Personalities of Godhead. As stated in Brahma-saṁhitā (5.39): rāmādi-mūrtiṣu kalā-niyamena tiṣṭhan. In the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam it is confirmed that all the incarnations are partial expansions, or kalā, of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. However, Kṛṣṇa is the original Supreme Personality of Godhead. One should not take the plural number of the word īśvarāṇām to mean that there are many Godheads. The fact is that God is one, but He exists eternally and expands Himself in innumerable forms and acts in various ways. Sometimes the common man is bewildered by all this and considers such activities contradictory, but they are not contradictory. There is a great plan behind all the Lord’s activities.

For our understanding, it is sometimes said that the Lord is situated in the heart of the thief as well as in the heart of the householder, but the Supersoul in the heart of the thief dictates, “Go and steal things from that particular house,” and at the same time the Lord tells the householder, “Now be careful of thieves and burglars.” These instructions to different persons appear contradictory, yet we should know that the Supersoul, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, has some plan, and we should not consider such activities contradictory. The best course is to surrender unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead wholeheartedly, and, being protected by Him, remain peaceful.

The first point that Prabhupāda is emphasizing is that the tiny human being cannot estimate the purpose and plans of the activities of the Lord.

*acintyāḥ khalu ye bhāvā*  
*na tāṁs tarkeṇa yojayet*  
*prakṛtibhyaḥ paraṁ yac ca*  
*tad acintyasya lakṣaṇam*

**“Anything transcendental to material nature is called inconceivable, whereas arguments are all mundane. Since mundane arguments cannot touch transcendental subject matters, one should not try to understand transcendental subjects through mundane arguments.” (Cc. Ādi 17.308, as quoted from Mahābhārata (Bhīṣma-parva 5.22))**

I was meeting with a gathering of young children in Kiev, and all their parents had told them that they should bring questions. Many of them were about five to eight years old. One of them asked, “Who created Kṛṣṇa?” It is one of those inconceivable conceptions—that Kṛṣṇa is anādi—He has no beginning and He is the beginning of everything. With our tiny brains, if we try to understand, it is inconceivable. We cannot use mundane arguments to understand transcendence. Although, Śrīla Prabhupāda many times would give us analogies to help us understand that which is difficult to understand with the mind. Prabhupāda once gave an analogy to explain why we use analogies: If one wants to see the movements of the moon in the sky at night, looking directly at the sky, it is very difficult to see it moving. However, if you look at the moon through the branches of a tree, then you can see how the moon is moving from one branch to the next, because the branches of the tree are closer to us and more recognizable. Therefore, to understand spiritual subject matter, sometimes it is not so easy to understand or to see with blunt material senses. However, this material nature is acting according to Kṛṣṇa’s direction, and therefore we can also use analogies in material nature, such as the sun and the moon, which help us to understand Kṛṣṇa.

*eka-deśa-sthitasyāgner*  
*jyotsnā vistāriṇī yathā*

(Viṣṇu Purāṇa)

Just as the sun is situated in one place and it spreads its energy throughout the entire universe, similarly Kṛṣṇa is sitting in one place in the spiritual world and pervades the entire cosmic manifestation through His multifarious energies. The sun is used as an analogy, because we can experience the heat and light of the sun here, even though the sun is millions of miles away. Thus, if the sun can spread its heat and light from millions of miles away, why can Kṛṣṇa not spread His energies from some other place beyond our imagination?Some things about Kṛṣṇa are simply inconceivable. Jīva Gosvāmī says, “Unless the Lord’s activities are accepted as inconceivable, they cannot be explained.”

*bhaktyā mām abhijānāti*  
*yāvān yaś cāsmi tattvataḥ*  
*tato māṁ tattvato jñātvā*  
*viśate tad-anantaram*

**“If you really want to understand Me in truth, the only way you are going to be able to understand Me is by devotional service. There is no other way you can enter in these mysteries of understanding Me.” (Bg. 18.55)**

Kṛṣṇa must reveal within the heart His transcendental nature, His transcendental qualities and His transcendental personalities.

*tarko ‘pratiṣṭhaḥ śrutayo vibhinnā*  
*nāsāv ṛṣir yasya mataṁ na bhinnam*  
*dharmasya tattvaṁ nihitaṁ guhāyāṁ*  
*mahājano yena gataḥ sa panthāḥ*

**Dry arguments are inconclusive. A great personality whose opinion does not differ from others is not considered a great sage. Simply by studying the Vedas, which are variegated, one cannot come to the right path by which religious principles are understood. The solid truth of religious principles is hidden in the heart of an unadulterated, self-realized person. Consequently, as the śāstras confirm, one should accept whatever progressive path the mahājanas advocate. (Mahābhārata, Vana-pārva (313.117))**

That which is inconceivable can be understood if one accepts that the Lord has inconceivable energies. Without surrendering to the Lord, it will always remain inconceivable, and will always remain a mystery. Those devotees who have completely surrendered their hearts to the service of the Supreme Lord can understand Kṛṣṇa, even though they may see apparent contradictions in His behavior. Kṛṣṇa is worshiped by millions and millions of goddesses of fortune. Yet He steals butter just like a poverty-stricken thief. This is seemingly a contradiction. Kṛṣṇa says:

*ajo ’pi sann avyayātmā*  
*bhūtānām īśvaro ’pi san*  
*prakṛtiṁ svām adhiṣṭhāya*  
*sambhavāmy ātma-māyayā*

**“Although I am unborn and My transcendental body never deteriorates, and although I am the Lord of all living entities, I still appear in every millennium in My original transcendental form.” (Bg. 4.6)**

A mundane logician will read these sections from scriptures, see these contradictions in different places and say, “How can I accept Kṛṣṇa? Here it says He is unborn, while elsewhere it says He is the son of Yaśodā and Nanda Mahārāja. I cannot accept these contradictory scriptures! Here it says that Kṛṣṇa is feared by fear-personified. Yet it says that Kṛṣṇa is afraid of the stick of Mother Yaśodā. Here it says that Kṛṣṇa knows everything—past, present and everything that is yet to come. However, when He is talking to Uddhava, he is asking him what He should do!”Devotees, however, understand Kṛṣṇa and how His contradictory behaviors can be reconciled. Kṛṣṇa’s greatest quality is that He is bhakta-vātsalya—completely controlled by the love of His devotees. Under this control, a devotee can cause Kṛṣṇa to act even in a way that appears to be completely contrary to His nature. If one knows how Kṛṣṇa is controlled by the love of the devotee, one will be able to understand Kṛṣṇa’s inconceivable potencies, which cannot be understood by ordinary, mundane logic. The mundane logicians will study Śrīla Prabhupāda’s books and try to apply their logic. But sooner or later, they have to accept that there is something that their mundane minds are not going to be able to fully comprehend and understand. Although there is still so much logic here that can satisfy even mundane logicians, until we convince them to place their heads at Śrīla Prabhupāda’s lotus feet, they will never be able to understand the acintya-śakti (inconceivable potencies) of the Supreme Lord. Thus, as Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī has said, unless the Lord’s activities are accepted as inconceivable, they cannot be explained.

## Kṛṣṇa’s Appearance

*janma karma ca me divyam*  
*evaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ*  
*tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma*  
*naiti mām eti so ’rjuna*

**“One who knows the transcendental nature of My appearance and activities does not, upon leaving the body, take his birth again in this material world, but attains My eternal abode, O Arjuna.” (Bg. 4.9)**

It is not such an easy thing to understand Kṛṣṇa’s transcendental appearance and His activities. Kṛṣṇa says in the Bhagavad-gītā:

*na māṁ karmāṇi limpanti*  
*na me karma-phale spṛhā*  
*iti māṁ yo ’bhijānāti*  
*karmabhir na sa badhyate*

**“There is no work that affects Me; nor do I aspire for the fruits of action. One who understands this truth about Me also does not become entangled in the fruitive reactions of work.” (Bg. 4.14)**

There is nothing that Kṛṣṇa has to do. Everything He does is by His desire or free choice. When Kṛṣṇa wants to create the material world, He does not have to personally do anything; everything happens automatically simply through His multifarious potencies, which all act very perfectly according to His will. Therefore, if Kṛṣṇa does not have to do anything, then why does He come to this world? Although Kṛṣṇa does not have to come, he says (Bg. 4.7-8): “Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice, O descendant of Bharata, and a predominant rise of irreligion—at that time I descend Myself in order to deliver the pious and to annihilate the miscreants, as well as to re-establish the principles of religion.”

It is also described in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam:

*ete cāṁśa-kalāḥ puṁsaḥ*  
*kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam*  
*indrāri-vyākulaṁ lokaṁ*  
*mṛḍayanti yuge yuge*

**“All of the different incarnations are either plenary portions or portions of the plenary portions of the Lord, but Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the original Personality of Godhead. All of them appear on planets whenever there is a disturbance created by the atheists. The Lord incarnates to protect the theists.” (Bhāg. 1.3.28)**

Kṛṣṇa does not have to come to destroy demons. He can already do that perfectly according to His multifarious potencies. Primarily, Lord Kṛṣṇa’s purpose for appearing in this world is to give pleasure to and to satisfy His devotees. The Lord appears to fulfill the internal desires of His devotees. Although He is independent in His will, He is always displaying His transcendental līlās (pastimes), which are full submission to the love of His devotees. Kṛṣṇa enjoys being submissive to the desires of His devotees. Because of the intense desire within the devotees’ heart to see the Lord, the Lord is very eager to appear before His devotees to give them pleasure and to fulfill their desires. His pastimes are called līlās because they are simply a display of His reciprocal relationships with His loving eternal associates. Although Kṛṣṇa says, “There is nothing I have to do, nor do I become implicated in whatever I do,” still we understand that Kṛṣṇa is always engaged in activities. But those are not the same activities that we perceive (the activities of this material world). Rather, they are divyam (transcendental). Although Kṛṣṇa has nothing that He has to do, He does what He likes to do. Such is the transcendental nature of His līlās, and especially the transcendental nature of His appearance.We can understand this by a mundane example: In this material world, there are so many activities that we are forced to do, and so many dictations or demands of the body that we must follow. If we neglect to do so, there will be many implications. However, although there are many things that we have to do, there are many other things that we would like to do. Prabhupāda explains in the Nectar of Devotion that these are the activities of bhoga and tyāga. For example, a businessman works hard all week to receive some salary. Then on the weekend, he goes off and does what he wants to do. However, the next week, he has to return to work. Thus, there are many things that we have to do, but still we all have a list of other things that we want to be able to do.Kṛṣṇa, however, is the supreme enjoyer. That is all He does. He never becomes implicated in not doing something, and never is He forced to have to do something that He does not want to do. Whatever He does is for His transcendental pleasure and also for the pleasure of His devotees. Therefore, when the Lord appears in this world, it is not under the influence of the three modes of material nature, but rather out of His free choice.

It is described in the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam how Lord Kṛṣṇa appeared in the womb of Devakī and took His birth in Mathurā. Prior to His appearance in this world, Kṛṣṇa had explained to Yogamāyā that she should take her birth before Him and make all the arrangements to transfer Lord Balarāma from the womb of Devakī into the womb of Rohiṇī, and then He would take His birth as the eighth child of Devakī.It is also explained in Jīva Gosvāmī’s Gopāla-campū that not only did Kṛṣṇa appear as the eighth child of Devakī, but He also appeared in His original svayam bhagavān form as the son of Mother Yaśodā. Mother Yaśodā was very eager to have a son, but she was unable to do so, even after performing many different vratas. Then one day she told her husband, Nanda Mahārāja, “Let us perform the dvādaśī-parama-vrata for one continuous year in an attempt to obtain a son.” Nanda Mahārāja agreed, and after one continuous year of performance of this vrata, one night, Nanda Mahārāja had a dream in which the Lord appeared and told him that He would appear as their son. In the dream, he also saw a young boy with a bluish complexion and a young baby-girl with a golden complexion flying through the sky, and they entered into the heart of Nanda Mahārāja, and from there, they entered into the womb of Mother Yaśodā. In this way, Yaśodā became pregnant.When Upananda and all the residents of Vṛndāvana heard how mother Yaśodā was pregnant, they all began to celebrate. Nanda Mahārāja also gave many cows in charity. He was also told by a tapasvinī who had come to their house that Yaśodā would very soon give birth to a son. When everyone heard that Yaśodā was going to give birth to a son, they became so happy, because that was Yaśodā’s desire. Everyone was pleased with this tapasvinī and they built a nice cottage for her in which to reside. In due course of time, mother Yaśodā gave birth to a child.The Gopāla-campū, which is the recitation of Snigdha-kānta and Madhu-kānta who are telling this whole story about Yaśodā giving birth, provides further details. Yaśodā first gave birth to a baby girl. All the gopīs were waiting all night, as they were very anxious to see the birth of the child. However, by the arrangement of the internal potency, Yogamāyā, they all fell asleep. Then mother Yaśodā gave birth to a second child, who was Kṛṣṇa in His original svayam bhagavān form. At the same time, Kṛṣṇa also appeared in His Vāsudeva form in Mathurā in the womb of Devakī. First, however, Kṛṣṇa had appeared in His original four-armed form before Vasudeva and Devakī to fulfill their desires, as they were very eager to have the Lord as their son. By first appearing before them in His four-armed form, they could actually have that realization that the Lord was appearing as their son. They were very fearful and concerned about the welfare of their son because of Kaṁsa. The Lord therefore changed from His four-armed form into His two-armed form. By the arrangement of the Lord’s internal potency, all the prison guards fell asleep, the locks to the prison house were opened, and Vasudeva took Vāsudeva-Kṛṣṇa to the home of Nanda Mahārāja in Vṛndāvana.Yogamāyā, who had appeared prior to Kṛṣṇa from the womb of Yaśodā, covered Vasudeva in such a way that he was not able to see that Kṛṣṇa had already taken birth from the womb of Yaśodā. Therefore, when Vasudeva put Vāsudeva-Kṛṣṇa down before Yaśodā, he did not see that there was another Kṛṣṇa who had already taken birth. Also Yaśodā did not see it, because she gave birth in such a way that she was not even aware that she had given birth to a son, and everyone else was also asleep. When Vasudeva put Vāsudeva-Kṛṣṇa down, that form of Kṛṣṇa merged into the other form of Kṛṣṇa (the svayam bhagavān form). In this way, we can also understand that Kṛṣṇa never leaves Vṛndāvana. He is always there, fulfilling the desires of His devotees who have relationships with Him, out of friendship, maternal affection, and conjugal love.Vasudeva then brought Yogamāyā back to Mathurā, and in this way, Kaṁsa was cheated. He was told that the eighth child of Devakī would be a son, but when he appeared in the prison house, he saw that the child was actually a daughter. Then when Kaṁsa attempted to kill that child of Devakī, the child, who was Yogamāyā, flew up into the air and said, “You fool! Don’t you know that the person who is going to kill you has already taken His birth elsewhere?!”Thus, the Lord’s internal potency acts in such a way to fulfill His desires. This internal potency of the Lord acts very perfectly according to His will. The Lord instructed Yogamāyā to appear in this world to make all the necessary arrangements for His appearance. Thus, the Lord appears to fulfill the desires of His confidential associates. We can therefore see that there is nothing that He has to do, but He is always very eager to satisfy the innermost desires within the core of the hearts of His devotees. Not only does the Lord satisfy the devotees by appearing in this way to reciprocate their desires to have Him as their son, but He also satisfies the devotees by appearing in this world so that His pastimes can be spoken about and constantly repeated.Queen Kuntī describes in her prayers in the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam that the Lord has many different purposes for His appearance. One of them is that the Lord comes into this world upon the request of Lord Brahmā to diminish the burden of atheistic kings. However, He also comes to rejuvenate the process of hearing, chanting and remembering the pastimes of the Lord. The Lord is eager to appear in order to satisfy His devotees’ desires.

*nāhaṁ tiṣṭhāmi vaikuṇṭhe*  
*yogināṁ hṛdayeṣu vā*  
*tatra tiṣṭhāmi nārada*  
*yatra gāyanti mad-bhaktāḥ*

(Padma Purāṇa)

He says to Nārada, “I am not in the Vaikuṇṭha planets nor am I in the hearts of yogīs. But I remain where My devotees engage in glorifying My activities. In that place you will always find Me.”

## The Lord in the Heart

*upadraṣṭānumantā ca*  
*bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ*  
*paramātmeti cāpy ukto*  
*dehe ’smin puruṣaḥ paraḥ*

**Yet in this body there is another, a transcendental enjoyer, who is the Lord, the supreme proprietor, who exists as the overseer and permitter, and who is known as the Supersoul. (Bg. 13.23)**

PURPORT

It is stated here that the Supersoul, who is always with the individual soul, is the representation of the Supreme Lord. He is not an ordinary living entity. Because the monist philosophers take the knower of the body to be one, they think that there is no difference between the Supersoul and the individual soul. To clarify this, the Lord says that He is represented as the Paramātmā in every body. He is different from the individual soul; He is para, transcendental. The individual soul enjoys the activities of a particular field, but the Supersoul is present not as finite enjoyer nor as one taking part in bodily activities, but as the witness, overseer, permitter and supreme enjoyer. His name is Paramātmā, not ātmā and He is transcendental. It is distinctly clear that the ātmā and Paramātmā are different. The Supersoul, the Paramātmā, has legs and hands everywhere, but the individual soul does not. And because the Paramātmā is the Supreme Lord, He is present within to sanction the individual soul’s desiring material enjoyment. Without the sanction of the Supreme Soul, the individual soul cannot do anything. The individual is bhukta, or the sustained, and the Lord is bhoktā, or the maintainer. There are innumerable living entities, and He is staying in them as a friend.

The fact is that every individual living entity is eternally part and parcel of the Supreme Lord, and both of them are very intimately related as friends. But the living entity has the tendency to reject the sanction of the Supreme Lord and act independently in an attempt to dominate nature, and because he has this tendency he is called the marginal energy of the Supreme Lord. The living entity can be situated either in the material energy or in the spiritual energy. As long as he is conditioned by the material energy, the Supreme Lord, as his friend, the Supersoul, stays with him just to get him to return to the spiritual energy. The Lord is always eager to take him back to the spiritual energy, but due to his minute independence the individual entity is continually rejecting the association of spiritual light. This misuse of independence is the cause of his material strife in the conditioned nature. The Lord, therefore, is always giving instruction from within and from without. From without He gives instructions as stated in Bhagavad-gītā, and from within He tries to convince the living entity that his activities in the material field are not conducive to real happiness. “Just give it up and turn your faith toward Me. Then you will be happy,” He says. Thus the intelligent person who places his faith in the Paramātmā or the Supreme Personality of Godhead begins to advance toward a blissful eternal life of knowledge.

In this chapter of Bhagavad-gītā, Kṛṣṇa is answering a question posed by Arjuna (Bg. 13.1): “I wish to know about prakṛti, puruṣa, and the field and the knower of the field, and of knowledge and the object of knowledge.”There are two knowers—the living entity and Paramātmā. Kṣetra is the field of activities and kṣetra-jñaḥ is the knower of the field of activities. Both the individual soul and the Supersoul (Paramātmā) are seated within the heart of this material body. This verse, which describes the existence of Paramātmā, is giving us information about one of the knowers of the field—the Superknower (Supersoul). The minute living entity is the knower of his own field of activities, while the Supersoul is considered to be that which is knowable or is to be known by the individual soul.It is described of the Supersoul (Bg. 13.14), “Everywhere are His hands and legs, His eyes, heads and faces, and He has ears everywhere. In this way the Supersoul exists, pervading everything.” Similarly, the sun is situated in one place in the sky, and is simultaneously over many people throughout a very wide tract, extending over five thousand miles. Many may simultaneously declare that the sun is over their head. In the same way, the example is also given of a reflection. The sun is situated in one place, yet its presence can be perceived in the reflection of various pots of water everywhere. It seems divided, but it is actually one.

Similarly, the Supersoul is situated within the heart of all living beings. The Lord’s function as the Supersoul is to witness and give sanction to the activities of all living entities according to their desires.

In one lecture, Śrīla Prabhupāda was answering a question of a devotee who was trying to understand where individuality and one’s own effort comes into play. That devotee quoted a verse from Bhagavad-gītā (18.61):

*īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ*  
*hṛd-deśe ’rjuna tiṣṭhati*  
*bhrāmāyān sarva-bhūtāni*  
*yantrārūḍhāni māyayā*

“The Supreme Lord is situated in the heart of all living beings and He is directing the wanderings of all the living entities, who are seated as on a machine, made of material energy.” The devotee was asking, “If Kṛṣṇa is directing the wanderings of everyone, do I have to surrender? Is Kṛṣṇa going to direct me?”Prabhupāda very clearly and concisely answered, “No, there is another verse in Bhagavad-gītā. Why don’t you remember that verse? Kṛṣṇa says (Bg. 4.11), ‘ye yathā māṁ prapadyante, tāṁs tathaiva bhajāmy aham—as they surrender unto Me, I will reward them accordingly.’ Kṛṣṇa is directing everyone. For those who are surrendered to Kṛṣṇa, He will direct them in such a way that they can come closer to Him. For those who are not surrendered to Kṛṣṇa, He will direct them in such a way that the living entity will have all the facilities by His sanction. Even if a living entity decides that he wants to go to hell, the Supersoul will direct him in such a way that he can achieve his desired goal.

Thus, direction is there for everyone. However there is a distinction between direction that is given for one who is surrendered, and for one who is not. It is compared to two birds sitting in a tree. One bird is enjoying the fruits, while the other bird is simply waiting for the bird who is enjoying the fruits to turn to him, and to follow the direction of how to come to him.

Similarly, the Supersoul is situated within the heart, witnessing the desires of the living entity and giving sanction. By the living entity’s persistence, the Supersoul says, “OK, by your persistence you can go ahead and do it at your own risk.” Kṛṣṇa also says in Bhagavad-gītā, “If you take shelter of Me, I will protect you.” Therefore, Kṛṣṇa takes a particular position according to our individual choice. However, not a blade of grass can move without His sanction. Thus, the Lord is directing everybody.Kṛṣṇa describes the position of the surrendered soul or one who is endeavoring:

*teṣāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ*  
*bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam*  
*dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ*  
*yena mām upayānti te*

**“To those who are constantly devoted to serving Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.” (Bg. 10.10)**

From within the heart, Kṛṣṇa destroys the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge. He directs the living entities on how to come to Him. Surrender has to be there. Every living entity is surrendering to either a superior dictation or an inferior dictation.

Prabhupāda explains that because the living entity has partial independence, he is given freedom of choice. To have freedom of choice, one must have the facility to choose that which is wrong or that which is right. If one chooses to surrender to that which is wrong, Kṛṣṇa becomes silent and observes. Sometimes the living entity knows he should not do a particular activity, but he is driven to do it by the modes of nature.Arjuna asked Kṛṣṇa in Bhagavad-gītā, “By what is one impelled to sinful acts, even unwillingly, as if engaged by force?” Kṛṣṇa replied that it is lust only, that is born of contact with the material mode of passion and later transformed into wrath, and which is the all-devouring sinful enemy of this world.

The living entity may suspect that he should not be doing a particular action, yet he still does it. Thus, Kṛṣṇa will dictate in such a way that the living entity can fulfill his various desires, but unfortunately because he is not surrendering to Kṛṣṇa, it means that he is surrendering to the modes of material nature and to its six whips—illusion, pride, envy, lust, anger and greed—which cause so much suffering to the living entity. A living entity who is not surrendered is driven by them, and the consequences are suffered in due course of time, because he has to reap the fruit of his desires. By neglecting Kṛṣṇa’s warning and His suggested direction, Kṛṣṇa allows us to pursue our material desires, at our own risk, which will lead to consequences such as suffering.

The living entity must surrender to some dictation—either the inferior dictation or the superior dictation.

*puruṣaḥ prakṛti-stho hi*  
*bhuṅkte prakṛti-jān guṇān*  
*kāraṇaṁ guṇa-saṅgo ’sya*  
*sad-asad-yoni-janmasu*

**The living entity in material nature thus follows the ways of life, enjoying the three modes of nature. This is due to his association with that material nature. Thus he meets with good and evil among various species of life. (Bg. 13.22)**

If we surrender to the inferior dictation, coming from the three modes of material nature, the consequence is that we have to take repeated birth and death in the material world. Śrīla Prabhupāda clearly states in his commentary that when the living entity turns towards Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa will dictate what we should avoid. We should try to listen. We may think that to hear the Supersoul means simply hearing Him say something positive: “Here I am. Just come to me!” and not that it includes any warnings He may give. We have to choose to surrender, which means to momentarily bend our will towards something that is being asked of us. Without that surrender, how can we get help from Kṛṣṇa? Kṛṣṇa says that if we take one step towards Him, He will take ten steps towards us. As we surrender unto Him, He will reward us accordingly.

If you try to tell a young child who wants something, that he cannot have it, he usually persists to get it, because his nature is preyas—wanting immediate gratification. Similarly, sometimes Kṛṣṇa may tell us not to do something, but we do not listen, not wanting to be told to avoid doing something that we want to do.Prabhupāda describes śreyas as that which is beneficial for the long term—such as when a child is told by the parents to go to school to pursue his future and get an education. Preyas is when the child does not want to do what he is told, not wanting to think of his long-term welfare. In one of his commentaries, Prabhupāda says that this spontaneity is the child-like mentality of the living entity, which in modern times is like the slogan: Just do it! In other words, we do not take heed of any good warnings, but instead just do it for immediate gratification. However, we have to learn to bend our will towards a superior dictation. Then Kṛṣṇa will help us from within, and will give us the understanding by which we can come to Him.

Prabhupāda says that the Lord will dictate in a different way, because He sees that the living entity is making the effort to move towards surrendering to the superior dictation coming from the Lord from within, and also coming from the instructions of the Vaiṣṇavas from without. Prabhupāda says (purport to Bg. 13.23), “The Lord, therefore, is always giving instruction from within and from without. From without He gives instructions as stated in Bhagavad-gītā, and from within He tries to convince the living entity that his activities in the material field are not conducive to real happiness.” He tries to convince us, but He has given us the independence to choose.

This is the position of the Supersoul in the heart. Prabhupāda describes that the Supersoul is all-knowing, the permitter giving sanction, and the supreme enjoyer. Therefore, this verse of the Bhagavad-gītā is helping us to understand that there is a distinction between the soul and the Supersoul, and our position is to embark upon the endeavor to follow the superior dictation so that we can ultimately achieve direction towards coming to Kṛṣṇa. Simply to perceive the presence of the Supersoul within the heart is not the ultimate goal.

*vadanti tat tattva-vidas*  
*tattvaṁ yaj jñānam advayam*  
*brahmeti paramātmeti*  
*bhagavān iti śabdyate*

**Learned transcendentalists who know the Absolute Truth call this nondual substance Brahman, Paramātmā or Bhagavān. (Bhāg. 1.2.11)**

These are the three phases of the Absolute Truth. Paramātmā is the feature of the Lord within the heart. Beyond that is the feature of the Supreme Lord, Bhagavān, who exists in the eternal transcendental realm, the spiritual world. Whatever the living entity makes as the object of his surrender, meditation and efforts to satisfy, that aspect of the Lord will help him. Prabhupāda explains that when we try to surrender to the superior direction of the Lord within the heart, which will begin by restricting us from certain things that we should not do, then gradually we also get dictation on how to come to Kṛṣṇa. In other words, we get dictation not only on what we should not do, but also on what we should do.The heart then becomes cleansed, becoming gradually free from all unwanted desires (anarthas) which are obstacles in the path of devotional service. These anarthas are difficult to overcome by our own efforts, but can be removed by the mercy of the Lord when we try to surrender to Him. Kṛṣṇa will eradicate them from within the core of our hearts and help us to overcome these obstacles. If we try to overcome them by our own endeavors, it will be very difficult. Even if we make a little effort to surrender to Kṛṣṇa, immediately we will see some resistance. The mind’s tendency will be to say, “Don’t think of Kṛṣṇa now.” Whatever effort we make to remember the Lord, the mind’s tendency is to find more and more distractions that will appear to oppose and fight, saying, “No, there are other things you should think about now besides Kṛṣṇa.” It is a constant battle.

To advance in spiritual life, one has to recognize that he must be prepared to struggle. If he does not struggle, then he will surrender to māyā. It is always a struggle from the beginning to more elevated stages of devotional service. To be struggling does not mean that one is in māyā. Struggle is good. It is when one gives up all struggles that he has succumbed to māyā.Aniṣṭhitā-bhakti means flickering, and it is the stage of devotional service where one is not very fixed. One of the symptoms of aniṣṭhitā-bhakti is vyūḍha-vikalpā, or indecisiveness, which is when one is always fluctuating between surrendering and not surrendering. One thinks that if he surrenders, he may get a certain benefit. However, he always looks for the example of those who have not surrendered to such a great degree, yet have benefitted in some way in devotional service. He then thinks that he cannot surrender and still hope to make progress in devotional service. This is vyūḍha-vikalpā—the inability to remain fixed upon an object or goal that one is trying to accomplish for the Lord’s pleasure.Another symptom of aniṣṭhitā-bhakti is viṣaya-saṅgarā—struggling with the senses. Struggle with the senses is an indication that one wants to satisfy his material desires, but he also wants spiritual advancement.Another symptom is niyamākṣamā—the inability to uphold vows. For example, one may vow to fast on every Ekādaśī and chant more than sixteen rounds. However, when Ekādaśī comes and he sees somebody eating something, this may lead him to decide to wait until next Ekādaśī to follow his vow. He is still struggling—trying to make vows, but unable to keep them. This is aniṣṭhitā (flickering). One will continue to display such symptoms until he actually comes to the stage of niṣṭhā—being fixed in his devotional service.Utsāha-mayī (false enthusiasm) is another characteristic of aniṣṭhitā-bhakti. This is when one becomes enthusiastic because he has a particular conception of himself as being qualified, and others recognize it. One gets his enthusiasm when others see that he has certain qualifications in devotional service. However, when one does not get the recognition, then he loses his enthusiasm. For example, one may have been trying to play karatālas for five years, and he thinks that he has finally mastered it and everyone is seeing how nicely he plays. However, when somebody tells him to stop since he is off beat, then his enthusiasm to play karatālas immediately goes away.The last symptom of aniṣṭhitā-bhakti is called taraṅga-rangiṇī—enjoying the benefits of devotional service. One may think that he has chanted Hare Kṛṣṇa for so many years and likes the respect he has gotten for being a Hare Kṛṣṇa for 25-30 years. He therefore tries to enjoy his position and all other benefits that may come from the respect that he may gain as a result of his devotional service.

Śrīla Prabhupāda explains that the Lord as the Supersoul, within the heart of every living being, is the supreme enjoyer of all of our endeavors and that everything is ultimately meant for His pleasure. We should not try to enjoy anything. Real enjoyment comes when the Lord gives it. That is the Lord’s nature, and that is how He reciprocates with His devotees. He becomes so purchased by the devotee’s efforts to please Him, without any reservation and conditions. Even though the devotee will not ask for anything, the Lord will demand that he accepts something from the Lord. That is how the Lord wants to reciprocate with the devotee who is really surrendered and always thinks exclusively of the His pleasure. This type of pleasure, given by the Lord, is unsurpassable. This type of pleasure or attainment goes beyond even satisfying the Lord within the heart. The Lord becomes so pleased when the devotee tries to surrender to what He says. He then starts dictating how we can go to Him. Although we may feel ourselves so unqualified, the Lord will come or send a devotee to bring us forth and accept us. That is how Kṛṣṇa reciprocates—coming from within and without—with the devotee who makes the effort to surrender to the superior dictation of the instructions given in Bhagavad-gītā.The story of Gopa Kumāra is given in Bṛhad-bhāgavatāmṛta. Gopa Kumāra relates his personal story of how he traversed through all the different spheres of existence, all the way to the topmost place—the spiritual world. He shows the object of his meditation, which was the result of having received the Gopāla mantra from his spiritual master. It is described how the living entity, specifically Gopa Kumāra, was not satisfied at any place he went, because within his heart, his meditation was on a cowherd boy, with whom he wanted to play, act spontaneously, and serve by gratifying the object of his meditation by his spontaneous devotional service. Even though he went to so many places that allowed for personal association with the Lord, within his heart, there was always some slight dissatisfaction. He began to continuously chant this Gopāla mantra and, effortlessly, he would traverse to the next higher abode and get the opportunity to associate with the Lord. Yet, that aspect of the Lord was not fully satisfying to him because his meditation as a cowherd boyfriend of Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana was the topmost abode.Gopa Kumāra is telling the story of his whole life to one Mathurā brāhmaṇa who was given the same mantra by the goddess Kāmākhyā. This brāhmaṇa was directed from within his heart to go to a specific forest of Vṛndāvana and to meet Gopa Kumāra, who was sitting, waiting for him to come. Gopa Kumāra was told by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī that on that particular day, a brāhmaṇa would come to this place. She said, “I want you to tell him this story. I want you to direct him on how he can achieve the fulfillment of his desires by chanting this mantra.”Gopa Kumāra therefore decided that he would tell the story of his own life to this brāhmaṇa. To convince the brāhmaṇa that he was worthy of being listened to, Gopa Kumāra told him exactly what was going on in his (the brāhmaṇa’s) heart. Because Gopa Kumāra knew what was going on in his heart, the brāhmaṇa immediately developed some faith in him. Such is the position of the spiritual master—he should understand the heart—because he is an external manifestation of the Supersoul. Normally while citing evidence, one should not speak about himself. Therefore, Gopa Kumāra had to get this faith from the brāhmaṇa first, before speaking about himself and telling his story about how he went to achieve friendship with Kṛṣṇa in the spiritual world.The brāhmaṇa very attentively heard the whole story, and the result of his association with Gopa Kumāra is that he also achieved perfection and assumed his original identity as a cowherd boy in Vṛndāvana. Gopa Kumāra’s name is Sarūpa in the spiritual world, but he was known as Gopa Kumāra before. The Mathurā brāhmaṇa, whose name was not given, also achieved his own svarūpa (eternal identity) as Janaśarmā, Kṛṣṇa’s cowherd boyfriend in the spiritual world, as a result of his association with Gopa Kumāra.This small summary illustrates that we should surrender to the Lord’s direction, which He is giving to help us and to remind us that He is watching everything. We may think we can hide something from somebody else, but we cannot hide anything from Kṛṣṇa. In due course of time, we are going to be reminded that we neglected the Lord within our hearts. Therefore, it is always best to remember Kṛṣṇa’s presence within our heart, and to try to satisfy Him. By that process of surrender, Kṛṣṇa will help us to achieve that which should become the real object of our meditation.When a devotee of the Lord associates with Vaiṣṇavas, the desire to achieve the same destination as those who have achieved spontaneous, loving devotional service to the Lord in the spiritual world will be awakened within his heart. For him, the relationship with the Supersoul is not sufficiently satisfying. If one wants to fully satisfy the soul, the Lord will help him by bringing him into the association of those Vaiṣṇavas who can instill within his heart the desire to achieve Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet in the spiritual world. That benefit is made available by this process of surrender.Therefore, Śrīla Prabhupāda concludes his commentary to Bhagavad-gītā 13.23 by saying: “Thus the intelligent person who places his faith in the Paramātmā or the Supreme Personality of Godhead begins to advance toward a blissful eternal life of knowledge.”

**Question: If an aspiring devotee has lusty desires due to his previous activities, and he is chanting, although not perfectly, how will Kṛṣṇa help?**

Kṛṣṇa explains that it is lust only which is the all-devouring sinful enemy of this world. Lust can be found in the heart and in the senses of every living being. Lust is the actual perversion of our original love for God, which is the cause of our bondage in the material world. To become free from all material contamination means to be free from lust. As long as the living entity is still within the material world, there will be traces or symptoms of this lust, which will manifest in various ways. However, Kṛṣṇa helps, because He sees how much we endeavor to please Him by chanting and hearing. These are the two very powerful processes of devotional service, in which the Lord will help from within the heart to cleanse desires for material enjoyment.

*śṛṇvatāṁ sva-kathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ*  
*puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ*  
*hṛdy antaḥ-stho hy abhadrāṇi*  
*vidhunoti suhṛt satām*

**“Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, who is the Paramātmā \[Supersoul\] in everyone’s heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who has developed the urge to hear His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted.” (Bhāg. 1.2.17)**

We need to cultivate the urge to hear. The nature of the material world is forgetfulness. Thus, to remember, we must be reminded. We may try to remember by our own efforts, but Māyā is always there, suggesting something else. We therefore have to develop an urge to hear His messages from those who speak in such a way that they impact us. When instructions impact us from within the heart, we realize that we have forgotten Kṛṣṇa and that we must remember Him. That is how a devotee is supposed to feel. He should never be complacent, thinking, “I have done as much as I can.” Complacency is a means of sliding down, and a sādhaka is one who is never complacent. He realizes that there is a goal, although he may feel that he is still far from it.

Kṛṣṇa explains to Uddhava:

“Having awakened faith in the narrations of My glories, being disgusted with all material activities, knowing that all sense gratification leads to misery, but still being unable to renounce all sense enjoyment, My devotee should remain happy and worship Me with great faith and conviction. Even though he is sometimes engaged in sense enjoyment, My devotee knows that all sense gratification leads to a miserable result, and he sincerely repents such activities.” (Bhāg. 11.20.27-28)

The devotee will voluntarily accept suffering by his repentance. The only way to be happy is to voluntarily suffer and repent. Kṛṣṇa therefore says, “Go on hearing about Me. By so doing, it demonstrates that you have awakened your faith in something higher. You have awakened your faith in Me. Because you have faith in Me, I will take these obstacles away, and I will eradicate the lust from within your heart.” In Bhagavad-gītā, Kṛṣṇa declares (Bg. 7.14): “This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross beyond it.”To overcome lust, we need help. Therefore, when a devotee is chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, he is praying to the internal potency of the Lord, “Help me. I cannot overcome this material energy. Unless You help me, how can I do it?” Śrīla Prabhupāda said type of chanting is like a child crying for his mother. By chanting in this way, we will feel that Kṛṣṇa is here, and hearing our prayers. Sometimes tears may even come to our eyes, lamenting in remembrance of the things we have done. But those tears are the price to pay if we want Kṛṣṇa’s help. He is ready, but we have to pay the price.

**Question: In the neophyte stage, it is not very easy to discriminate between the Supersoul’s dictation and māyā’s dictation. How can we understand the difference between the two?**

When we are not in the advanced stages of devotional service, the type of dictation that the Lord gives us is when he says, “Don’t do it.” This dictation is what we may consider as the conscience. Before we get the higher dictations of things that are positive, we should always be wary of doing those things that could lead us to pride, of accepting those things that can make us think that we are advanced, and of taking steps that could cause us to forget our subordinate position to the Lord. We should get a resounding confirmation before doing something that could potentially lead us to these kinds of dangerous situations. By such dictations, we will be conscious to avoid those things that are detrimental for our spiritual life. If we clearly see that something is detrimental, then even though our nature is to jump into it, we realize that the Supersoul is trying to caution us not to do it, as we are not ready yet.We are also always looking for the Supersoul to manifest His instructions externally by the blessings of Vaiṣṇavas who understand our hearts, who are our well-wishers and whom we perceive as representing Kṛṣṇa in some way in our lives. Śrīla Prabhupāda explains that when the living entity tries to surrender to the instructions of the spiritual master, the Lord will advise him in his heart about which direction to go. The Lord may not appear as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, because those who are not so advanced cannot actually see the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He will therefore appear in a different form to advise those who are first trying to follow the instructions of the spiritual master sincerely.Once, in New Vṛndāvana, there was a devotee, Janārdana Prabhu, who was telling Śrīla Prabhupāda about how he met a person who told him that the Supersoul speaks to him, and therefore he does not need to accept a spiritual master. It was a very heavy conversation between Śrīla Prabhupāda and this devotee. Śrīla Prabhupāda said that such a person who is speaking in this way is speaking nonsense. If one hears from him, the he is also nonsense. Kṛṣṇa speaks to those who are, twenty-four hours a day, dedicated in serving the instructions of the spiritual master.Therefore, we first try to serve the order externally. By prolonged effort to serve those orders, we get help within. How do we know if it is really positive direction? When a person is eating, how does he know if his hunger is going away? How does he know it tastes good or is satisfying? He knows. It is clearly confirmed. Until that confirmation is there, he should be careful.

**Question: Is the Supersoul and Kṛṣṇa the same? If we surrender to Kṛṣṇa, does that mean we are not satisfying the Supersoul?**

The Supersoul is non-different from Kṛṣṇa. One who loves Śrī Kṛṣṇa loves the Supreme Lord in His original form and recognizes the original form of the Lord that is manifest in his heart. For a person who is indebted to the Supersoul, he should not think that by surrendering to Kṛṣṇa, he is not satisfying the Supersoul. By going to the source (Kṛṣṇa), then all the expansions (including Supersoul) are satisfied as well.It is to be noted that while there is a loving relationship between the living entity and Kṛṣṇa, that kind of relationship does not exist with the Supersoul. Paramātmā’s function is to sanction and to oversee. Intimacy cannot exist in such a relationship where we are always asking, “Can I? Can I? Can I?” and where Paramātmā is answering, “Yes. Yes. Yes.” The relationship with Kṛṣṇa is not one where we ask, “Can I?” but rather one which is based on loving relationships.

**Question: If the spiritual master is the external manifestation of the Supersoul, with whom there cannot be the same kind of intimacy as there is with Kṛṣṇa, then what are the characteristics of the relationship with the spiritual master?**

The spiritual master is accepted as a friend, because he is our well-wisher. Kṛṣṇa says (Bg. 5.29): suhṛdaṁ sarva-bhūtānāṁ—“I am the well-wisher of all living beings.” It is also described in the Seventh Canto of the Bhāgavatam that the spiritual master is accepted as our best well-wishing friend. But as far as the intimacy is concerned, we will always have the position of a servant. It is the same in the relationship with Lord Caitanya, who is Kṛṣṇa Himself. While there are five different types of relationships of intimacy with Kṛṣṇa, in the case of Lord Caitanya, the predominant relationship is always that of servitude. However, only through the mercy of Lord Caitanya can we understand Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana.

*(ese) bṛndābane rādhā-śyāmer pa’be daraśan*  
*(gaura-kṛpā ha’le he)*

(Śrī Nām-Kīrtan, Verse 3)

One can understand the intimacy of pastimes of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana, but first he must get the mercy of Gaura, and before he gets the mercy of Gaura, first he has to get the mercy of Nityānanda. Nityānanda is the greatest servant of Lord Caitanya. The representative of Nityānanda is the spiritual master, because he prepares the soil, helping the living entity to become free from anarthas so that he can become qualified to establish his relationship with Lord Caitanya. Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura describes that even a proud person can get the opportunity to establish sambandha (relationship) with Lord Caitanya by the mercy of Lord Nityānanda or the spiritual master. Thus the spiritual master brings us into those intimate relationships.

**Question: Lord Caitanya is teaching how to invite Kṛṣṇa to sit in our heart rather than concentrating on following the dictation of the Supersoul. Should we therefore take the focus away from the Supersoul and just concentrate on trying to get Kṛṣṇa to sit in our heart? Or is that leap-frogging?**

No, it is not leap-frogging to get Kṛṣṇa in the heart. As Rūpa Gosvāmī says in Vidagdha-mādhava, “There is so much nectar in these two syllables, kṛṣ-ṇa. When I chant these two syllables kṛṣ-ṇa, I desire many, many tongues, because they are dancing on my tongue. Then when these two syllables, kṛṣ-ṇa, enter my ears, I desire millions of ears. And when those two syllables, kṛṣ-ṇa, dance within the courtyard of my heart, they conquer my mind, and my senses become inert.”

Those two syllables, kṛṣ-ṇa, are akhila-rasāmṛta-mūrti, the reservoir of all transcendental rasa, who is Kṛṣṇa within His original form. That is who we want dancing in our heart. The means for inviting Him into our hearts is to chant these syllables.

*kṛṣṇa-mantra haite habe saṁsāra-mocana*  
*kṛṣṇa-nāma haite pābe kṛṣṇera caraṇa*

(Cc. Ādi, 7.73)

The name of Kṛṣṇa is the means by which one can achieve the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. That is what we are trying to get by chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa.

## Kṛṣṇa’s Mercy

*arjuna uvāca*  
*senayor ubhayor madhye*  
*rathaṁ sthāpaya me ’cyuta*  
*yāvad etān nirīkṣe ’haṁ*  
*yoddhu-kāmān avasthitān*  
*kair mayā saha yoddhavyam*  
*asmin raṇa-samudyame*

**Arjuna said: “O infallible one, please draw my chariot between the two armies so that I may see those present here, who desire to fight, and with whom I must contend in this great trial of arms.” (Bg. 1.21-22)**

PURPORT

Although Lord Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, out of His causeless mercy He was engaged in the service of His friend. He never fails in His affection for His devotees, and thus He is addressed herein as infallible. As charioteer, He had to carry out the orders of Arjuna, and since He did not hesitate to do so, He is addressed as infallible. Although He had accepted the position of a charioteer for His devotee, His supreme position was not challenged. In all circumstances, He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hṛṣīkeśa, the Lord of the total senses. The relationship between the Lord and His servitor is very sweet and transcendental. The servitor is always ready to render service to the Lord, and, similarly, the Lord is always seeking an opportunity to render some service to the devotee. He takes greater pleasure in His pure devotee’s assuming the advantageous position of ordering Him than He does in being the giver of orders. Since He is master, everyone is under His orders, and no one is above Him to order Him. But when He finds that a pure devotee is ordering Him, He obtains transcendental pleasure, although He is the infallible master in all circumstances.

As a pure devotee of the Lord, Arjuna had no desire to fight with his cousins and brothers, but he was forced to come onto the battlefield by the obstinacy of Duryodhana, who was never agreeable to any peaceful negotiation. Therefore, he was very anxious to see who the leading persons present on the battlefield were. Although there was no question of a peacemaking endeavor on the battlefield, he wanted to see them again, and to see how much they were bent upon demanding an unwanted war.

In this verse, Arjuna has assumed the position of a person who is giving orders to Kṛṣṇa, telling Him where to bring the chariot. Prabhupāda explains that Kṛṣṇa takes greater pleasure in His pure devotee’s assuming the advantageous position of ordering Him than He does in being the giver of orders. Here we see how the Lord derives His pleasure—by becoming submissive and subordinate to His devotee.

When the devotee engages in hard labor with great effort to please the Lord, Kṛṣṇa bestows upon him His mercy. This mercy of Kṛṣṇa upon His devotee is His topmost quality, which illuminates all His other qualities. Upon its appearance, it makes the Lord’s heart very soft like butter.

We see this in the pastime where Mother Yaśodā is trying to bind Kṛṣṇa. After personally witnessing her endeavors to bind Him, Kṛṣṇa showed His mercy by allowing Himself to be bound, although prior to that point, all of Mother Yaśodā’s efforts were not able to bear fruit. This was the manifestation of Kṛṣṇa’s kṛpā-śakti, His mercy potency. The two fingers distance, which separated the ropes from being able to be tied was filled by bhakta-niṣṭhā and sva-niṣṭhā. Bhakta-niṣṭhā is the devotee’s tireless endeavors to please the Lord, and sva-niṣṭhā is Kṛṣṇa’s own niṣṭhā.

Kṛṣṇa’s niṣṭhā is acyuta (infallible), as described in this verse from Bhagavad-gītā, because He never fails in His affection for His devotees. As such, Kṛṣṇa did not hesitate to carry out Arjuna’s order. All of Kṛṣṇa’s potencies are infallible because they are emanations coming from Him. However, the specific infallible potency that is spoken of here is Kṛṣṇa’s determination to reciprocate with His devotee. In this endeavor, Kṛṣṇa never fails; He is always successful in satisfying His devotee. Such is His sva-niṣṭhā and the manifestation of His mercy upon His devotee.

We see here how Kṛṣṇa is being very merciful to Arjuna. Out of His causeless mercy, He was engaged in service to Arjuna as a friend, and thus very willingly accepted the position of being ordered by Arjuna, which gave Him great pleasure.

To all the devotees of the Lord, to varying degrees, Kṛṣṇa is always merciful to them. Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī describes in Śrī Bṛhad-bhāgavatāmṛta how Nārada Muni was on a search to find the greatest recipient of Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. In his search, he came upon many devotees of the Lord who he had been told were recipients of Kṛṣṇa’s mercy.

Nārada Muni happened to be present when one brāhmaṇa was rendering service to many sages who had gathered together in Prayāga. When Nārada Muni observed the characteristics of this brāhmaṇa, he could immediately understand that this brāhmaṇa was manifesting the quality of having received Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. He approached the brāhmaṇa and began describing his wonderful qualities and how he had received Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. However, the brāhmaṇa would not accept Nārada Muni’s statement as true. He felt that in comparison to a king in the southern part of India, he was very insignificant. He directed Nārada Muni, “If you want to really see somebody who has received Kṛṣṇa’s mercy, then you should go to one particular kingdom, to see the king who rules it.”

When Nārada Muni went to that kingdom and saw the king, the opulence in which he was living, and his service to the Deity, Nārada Muni could immediately appreciate the wonderful qualities that had been described previously to him by the brāhmaṇa. However, when he approached the king, the king described himself as the inadequate receptacle for Kṛṣṇa’s mercy, and as being very unqualified to receive it.

In this way, Nārada Muni was off on a journey from one devotee to the next, beginning from the brāhmaṇa, to the king, to Indra. After going to see Indra, he heard the glories of Lord Brahmā who also then denied that he had received the mercy of the Lord due to his lack of qualification, and said, “You must go see Lord Śiva. He is a recipient of this mercy.”

From there, Nārada Muni was sent to see Prahlāda Mahārāja who told him, “No, I am not a recipient of Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. I took birth in a family of demons. If you really want to see someone who has gotten Kṛṣṇa’s mercy, you should go see Hanumān in Kimpuruṣaloka.” Nārada Muni thus went to see Hanumān. However, from Hanumān he got the same response.

Each devotee was manifesting the symptoms of dainya or total humility, thinking themselves to be unfit and unqualified for Kṛṣṇa’s mercy, and always appreciating, recognizing and directing to someone whom they felt had much more mercy than themselves. No one said, “Yes you have come to that place where all your inquiries can be fulfilled by seeing me.”

Hanumān told him, “You should go see the Pāṇḍavas. They are there in Hastināpura, and the Lord often frequents their palace and spends intimate time with them.” Hanumān continued, “I do not get the opportunity to be with my Lord. I simply have to wait until He calls me. However, Kṛṣṇa personally goes to the Pāṇḍavas and spends time with them in their palace.”

Nārada Muni thus went to see the Pāṇḍavas in Hastināpura. However, again, the Pāṇḍavas denied their qualification. They said, “Better you go see the Yādavas in Dvārakā. They are the constant associates of the Lord, and the Lord is always merciful to them.”

Nārada Muni then went to see the Yādavas, and spoke to the senior members of the Yadu dynasty who then told him, “No. We have not received this mercy that you are talking about. You must go see Uddhava.” One by one the Pāṇḍavas each spoke to Nārada Muni. Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva all defeated him, saying, “Whatever you have said about me is not true.” They then produced the evidence and convinced Nārada that there was somebody superior to go and see who had really received Kṛṣṇa’s mercy.

One of the characteristics of a devotee who has received Kṛṣṇa’s mercy is that he never thinks he is qualified for it and has enough of it. He never thinks he does enough service for Kṛṣṇa, and he feels that he does not have enough love for Kṛṣṇa. This is one of the characteristics of bhakti or devotional service.

Nārada Muni was thus witnessing this in each of the devotees he approached. By the time he reached Uddhava, he was feeling great ecstasy from this saṅga. He went where Uddhava, Rohiṇī, Devakī, Balarāma, Satyabhāmā, Rukmiṇī, and many of the other queens of Dvārakā were sitting—just outside the room where Kṛṣṇa was. Their concern was that for the first time Kṛṣṇa was not coming out of His room. Kṛṣṇa did not even get out of bed that morning.

As we know, Kṛṣṇa in Dvārakā, as described in Kṛṣṇa book, gets out of bed every morning, performs His morning duties, and then goes to the Sudharmā assembly house. However, this particular morning, Kṛṣṇa had not come out of the room. These devotees were therefore sitting and discussing among one another what was wrong with Kṛṣṇa.

Nārada Muni, who was in great ecstasy and manifested on his body all the symptoms of ecstatic love, approached them and said, “I am looking for the greatest recipient of Kṛṣṇa’s mercy—Uddhava! I know that he is here, and I simply want to take the dust from his lotus feet.”

Nārada Muni had so many tears of ecstasy in his eyes that he could not see that Uddhava was standing right in front of him. However, as soon as Nārada Muni entered that place and manifested his disposition, all the devotees’ attention turned to him. They asked him, “Nārada, what has come over you? What has happened to you? Why are you behaving like this?” They began considering what they could possibly do to bring him back to a normal state of consciousness.

Nārada said, “I simply want to see Uddhava! I know he is the greatest recipient of Kṛṣṇa’s mercy!”

Seeing Nārada in this way, Uddhava clasped the lotus feet of Nārada Muni and took dust from them. He said, “Previously I thought that I had received Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. However, after going to Vṛndāvana and seeing the residents of Vṛndāvana, all of my pride has been crushed into dust!”

Uddhava had been sent to Vṛndāvana by Kṛṣṇa as a messenger, because Kṛṣṇa wanted him to see the unique love that the residents of Vṛndāvana have for Him, and Uddhava wanted to see the mercy that they had received from Kṛṣṇa and the type of service they render unto Kṛṣṇa. Uddhava said, “Now having been to Vṛndāvana, I understand who are the recipients of Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. However, Nārada, we should not enter too deeply into this subject now.” Uddhava and the other devotees could see that Nārada was already manifesting such ecstasy and losing consciousness, and if they would have entered too deeply into the subject, they would have never brought him back to consciousness.

However, Rohiṇī, who was also present, understood the inner meaning of Uddhava’s words, because she had been sent to Vṛndāvana by Vāsudeva. Although she was present there in Dvārakā along with Devakī, Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā and Balarāma, she still knew the ways of Vṛndāvana. Rohiṇī therefore began to speak about the symptoms that she had seen of the devotees of Vṛndāvana and the pain they were experiencing from separation from Kṛṣṇa. She described how they were simply drying up and almost at the point of death. The ecstasy of their separation from Kṛṣṇa may appear to look like suffering, but it is actually the highest form of pleasure. Although they feel that they are at the point of death, they do not die, because they know that if they do, it would make Kṛṣṇa very unhappy. They therefore maintain their lives simply for Kṛṣṇa’s pleasure.

After Rohiṇī spoke about how Kṛṣṇa had caused so much pain to these devotees in Vṛndāvana, Rukmiṇī then tried to defend Him, saying, “Actually, I hear how Kṛṣṇa is behaving every night. In His sleep, He calls out, one by one, the names of His cows, His cowherd boyfriends and His gopī girlfriends. Sometimes He even assumes the position of holding a flute, and bends His body into the three-fold bending form. And sometimes He will place His head on His pillow and will cry a lake of tears into it, calling out each of their names. How can anyone say Kṛṣṇa is not thinking of His devotees in Vṛndāvana? Although He is here with us in Dvārakā, He is always absorbed in thinking about them.”

Satyabhāmā then spoke up, saying, “What are you speaking about, Rukmiṇī?! You are speaking about how He behaves at night, but even during the day I see how He behaves! During the day He walks about as if He is in a dream-like state, simply meditating on these devotees. Don’t you realize that we are all His wives in name only?! Actually, He is always thinking about the gopīs in Vṛndāvana.”

Balarāma then spoke, describing how Kṛṣṇa is very clever in deception. He began describing how His brother had left all the devotees in great pain from separation, and how He (Balarāma) went to Vṛndāvana for two months, trying to assure them: “Don’t worry, Kṛṣṇa will come back! Kṛṣṇa will come back!” But alas He did not come. He simply sent a messenger who said, “Kṛṣṇa will come!” He gave them hope, but still Kṛṣṇa would not come.

Uddhava could see that the whole conversation was accelerating. Although he was trying to avoid this discussion from becoming too detailed, it all began manifesting among themselves. Meanwhile, Kṛṣṇa was in the other room, and when He heard this discussion going on, He came out. Kṛṣṇa was crying! He said, “It is true! I must have a heart as hard as a diamond because I have put all of these devotees into so much pain and suffering! What should I do?” He said to Uddhava, “Tell Me what I should do to rectify the situation.” Kṛṣṇa started thinking, “Maybe I should write a message?”

Uddhava said, “No, Kṛṣṇa, You already tried that before! Don’t do that again! They will only be satisfied when they see Your two lotus feet entering into Vṛndāvana!”

Kṛṣṇa then looked at Balarāma, and Balarāma looked at Kṛṣṇa. They were both feeling so overwhelmed by the situation that They began shedding tears! They embraced in each other’s arms and fell on the ground, having completely lost consciousness. When everyone saw this, they became very concerned and began to cry. Everyone else who heard the crying, started crying as well. All the ministers, kings and residents of the different palaces came and asked, “What is going on here?” When they saw Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, they too began crying, which was heard throughout the whole universe.

When Lord Brahmā heard it, he asked, “What is going on there in Dvārakā?!” Lord Brahmā went to that place to see what was happening and to see what he could possibly do to help the situation. He saw his father lying on the ground unconscious, with tears coming from His eyes. Seeing Kṛṣṇa in that condition, Lord Brahmā began crying. Then he realized, “I must do something to rectify this situation. How can devotees in Dvārakā tolerate this? For them, it is such an anomaly to see such an event and to see Kṛṣṇa manifesting such symptoms.”

Lord Brahmā realized he had to gather his wits and think of something to do. He had an idea. He tried to get the attention of Garuḍa who was nearby. However, Garuḍa was crying and crying and crying. Lord Brahmā tried to calm him down, and when he finally got his attention, he explained what needed to be done to bring Kṛṣṇa back to normal so that Dvārakā could also return to normal. He realized that he must bring Kṛṣṇa to a place called Nava-vṛndāvana, which is in between the Raivata forest and the ocean in Dvārakā, which Viśvakarmā had constructed. There, the setting was exactly the same as Vṛndāvana, except that the devotees could not be duplicated. Still, Viśvakarmā had constructed immovable images of all the residents of Vṛndāvana. These included images of Yaśodā, Nanda Mahārāja, the cowherd boys and the gopīs.

Having decided that he had to bring Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma to that place, Lord Brahmā told Garuḍa to place Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma on his back and carry Them to Nava-vṛndāvana. He then told all the residents of Dvārakā, “You must stay here, and don’t come with us!”

However, some of them could not restrain themselves. Padmavatī (Kaṁsa’s mother) had to go. Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā, Devakī and Rohiṇī wanted to go. Lord Brahmā understood that Rohiṇī knows the ways of Vṛndāvana and he thought that she should go as she may be helpful there. The others could not restrain themselves and also wanted to go. Therefore, they went to Nava-vṛndāvana, but hid behind trees so they could watch from a distance.

Garuḍa took Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma on his back and flew to Nava-vṛndāvana. Balarāma was gradually coming back to consciousness, while Kṛṣṇa remained completely unconscious. Being very expert in these matters, Balarāma very quickly started to understand the situation. By the time Garuḍa had landed in Nava-vṛndāvana and removed Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma from his back, Balarāma was fully conscious and was already in full motion. He immediately took a stick and placed it in Kṛṣṇa’s hand. He took a flute and placed it in Kṛṣṇa’s belt. He took a buffalo horn and placed it on Kṛṣṇa. He put a nice garland of kadamba flowers around His neck. He put guñjā-berry garlands around His ears. All these things were created by Viśvakarmā for Balarāma’s service to make Kṛṣṇa think that He was in Vṛndāvana. Balarāma then wiped all the dust off His own body.

Balarāma began shaking Kṛṣṇa, “Kṛṣṇa, wake up! Wake up! Get up! Get up, Kṛṣṇa! Look where You are!” Kṛṣṇa gradually came to consciousness. He looked up and immediately saw before Him the forms of Yaśodā and Nanda Mahārāja. Looking at Mother Yaśodā, He said, “O Mother! I was having a dream today. I dreamed I was in Madhupurī and that there were kings that were killed like Jarāsandha. There were also demigods who were saved.” He began describing everything that had been going on in Dvārakā, but then said, “There is too much that I can tell you right now, Mother. I will tell you all of this later.”

When He saw Nanda Mahārāja, He immediately got down and offered His obeisances. Then Rohiṇī, who had been standing there, said, “Just look at Your Mother! She was so concerned about You that she is standing motionless, unable to move, being distressed by the fact that You were staying in bed all morning.”

Kṛṣṇa then said to Balarāma, “I will tell You about My dream on Our way to the forest together.”

Balarāma said, “Yes, Kṛṣṇa, look, all the cowherd boys are going off to the forest now. They are taking the cows to the Yamunā. Quick! You should get up! Let’s go!”

Rohiṇī was thinking that when Kṛṣṇa goes to the forest and the pasturing grounds with His cowherd boyfriends, He usually takes something to eat. However, if Mother Yaśodā does not prepare anything for Him, then He will be completely disturbed and bewildered by this. She therefore immediately ran off to prepare something for Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma to take to the forest to eat. She told Kṛṣṇa, “Your Mother is just too distressed by the events this morning to cook anything for You today. I will have something ready for You.” Balarāma then said to Kṛṣṇa, “Let’s go off to the forest’s pasturing grounds!”

As Kṛṣṇa was leaving, He saw the gopīs standing there. Rādhārāṇī was not moving either. He said to Her, “You look so angry! You must know what I was dreaming about this morning. Don’t worry, I’ll come and see You later!” Taking a handful of flower petals, He showered them on Rādhārāṇī. Looking around to see if anyone was watching, He embraced and kissed Her. He then went off to join His cowherd boyfriends.

Everybody was watching from a distance. Padmavatī, Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā and all the others were standing and seeing Kṛṣṇa’s display of His beauty. They were crying, seeing how beautiful Kṛṣṇa is in His love for His devotees in Vṛndāvana. When Padmavatī and one other queen were going to run out to embrace Kṛṣṇa, Uddhava and Kālindī (who, although she is in Dvārakā, is also the Yamunā River and knows what goes on in Vṛndāvana) pulled her back and said, “No! You will ruin the whole thing! Get back!!” They were thus pulled back so as to not expose themselves and reveal that they were hiding behind the tree.

Meanwhile, Nārada Muni thought that he was the instigator of this whole thing. He was thinking, “Look what I started by my inquiry in Dvārakā!” Up in the sky, sitting in a lotus position, he was watching and relishing everything he was seeing, and did not want to go anywhere.

Kṛṣṇa continued down to the Yamunā River to meet His cowherd boyfriends and the cows. When He got there, He saw the size of this huge ocean, and then looked behind Him and saw this huge city. He said, “What is this?! Where am I?! Who am I?!” He was totally bewildered. He did not know where He was and who He was.

Balarāma had to immediately say something that would quickly bring Kṛṣṇa back to His normal consciousness. He said, “My dear Brother! Don’t You remember why You descended to this world?! You came to protect Your devotees! Because of their relationship with You, they are being persecuted by so many demoniac kings. You must give them protection!”

As Balarāma was speaking in this way, Kṛṣṇa immediately came back to His consciousness in Dvārakā: “Now I know who I am! What is this? What am I wearing?!” Balarāma could understand that He put Kṛṣṇa back in the right consciousness to return Him to Dvārakā to pacify everybody. Brahmā had been successful.

Uddhava said, “Yes, let’s all go back to Dvārakā.” Garuḍa carried Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa back.

All of Kṛṣṇa’s queens who were standing there began talking among themselves: “Actually, Kṛṣṇa’s greatest love is for His devotees in Vṛndāvana. We have personally seen it today. Certainly we are His wives in name only. Just see how much affection He has for His devotees of Vṛndāvana!”

Devakī said, “Just how great and glorious is Mother Yaśodā! She has been the greatest recipient of Kṛṣṇa’s mercy.”

Kṛṣṇa was hearing all of this and said, “Where is Satyabhāmā? Tell her she should come here.” When Satyabhāmā was brought to that place, Kṛṣṇa told them, “There is nothing that I will not do for these devotees! They have given everything to Me! They have given Me their lives! They have given Me their love! They sacrificed their families! They have sacrificed everything! I can never repay them!” From His own mouth, Kṛṣṇa began describing the glories of the residents of Vṛndāvana.

After having this discussion, they brought Nārada Muni back in. By this time, Nārada could understand that he had finally reached the pinnacle. He understood who had the greatest power to control Kṛṣṇa, and therefore understood who the recipients of the greatest mercy from Kṛṣṇa were. However, Nārada Muni felt very bad, because he thought that everything Kṛṣṇa went through was the result of his own provocation.

Kṛṣṇa told Nārada, “No! Do not think like that! You have performed the most wonderful service for Me. When a devotee always remembers his beloved within the core of his heart, even though he may be feeling great separation, anyone who reminds that person of his beloved or beloveds is most dear to him in rendering the greatest service to him. Please ask Me any benediction you like!”
