Nārada said, “O Lord, I ask for the benediction that for anyone who engages in Your devotional service, the nature of that devotional service should be that that devotee never thinks he has enough of Your mercy. He should never think that he serves You sufficiently. He should never think that he has enough love for You. I pray that You please give me this benediction.”

The Lord replied, “You are asking for a benediction that already exists! That is the nature of My devotional service.” He explained how all the devotees that Nārada Muni had previously visited were all recipients of His mercy. Each and every one of them felt that they did not have enough of Kṛṣṇa’s mercy, did not render enough service for Kṛṣṇa and did not have sufficient love for Kṛṣṇa. He said, “Every one of them are recipients of My mercy. I am simply reciprocating with them according to their love for Me. They are all perfect. They are all situated in premā. However, there are different levels of premā—ecstatic love for the Supreme Lord. According to their desire to serve Me in a particular way, I reciprocate. Therefore, since this benediction for which you have asked has already been fulfilled, please ask for some other benediction.”

Nārada Muni then asked, “I simply pray that I may wander throughout the three worlds chanting Your glories—the glories of Your pastimes that I have witnessed today. I pray that anyone who comes in contact with these pastimes—either by speaking about them, by hearing about them, or by touching them—and anyone who understands the importance of these pastimes will be given the benediction to be eternal servants in the dust of Your lotus feet. I pray for that benediction from You today.”

Kṛṣṇa said, “So be it!” and fulfilled this benediction.

Kṛṣṇa is always merciful to His devotees. However, there are different levels of devotees. The devotees who render service to Kṛṣṇa in the mood of the residents of Vṛndāvana have the greatest power to control Him, and their service gives Him the greatest pleasure.

Nārada Muni has received the benediction that anyone who comes in contact with these pastimes—either by hearing, by speaking, or by coming in contact in any other way—will also become recipients of that mercy and will be able to obtain the dust of service to Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet. This is Kṛṣṇa’s mercy.

## Qualities of the Lord

*adīna-līlā-hasitekṣaṇollasad-*  
*bhrū-bhaṅga-saṁsūcita-bhūry-anugraham*  
*īkṣeta cintāmayam enam īśvaraṁ*  
*yāvan mano dhāraṇayāvatiṣṭhate*

**The Lord’s magnanimous pastimes and the glowing glancing of His smiling face are all indications of His extensive benedictions. One must therefore concentrate on this transcendental form of the Lord, as long as the mind can be fixed on Him by meditation. (Bhāg. 2.2.12)**

PURPORT

In Bhagavad-gītā (12.5) it is said that the impersonalist undergoes a series of difficult programs on account of his impersonal meditation. But the devotee, due to the Lord’s personal service, progresses very easily. Impersonal meditation is therefore a source of suffering for the impersonalist. Here, the devotee has an advantage over the impersonalist philosopher. The impersonalist is doubtful about the personal feature of the Lord, and therefore he always tries to meditate upon something which is not objective. For this reason there is an authentic statement in the Bhāgavatam regarding the positive concentration of the mind on the factual form of the Lord.

Kleśo ’dhikataras teṣām, avyaktāsakta-cetasām (Bg. 12.5)—for those who try to meditate on the impersonal absolute, their advancement is very troublesome.

In his purport, Prabhupāda explains how the impersonalists have a difficult time because they have no transcendental object of meditation. Every object has four characteristics: name, form, qualities and activities. These characteristics of Kṛṣṇa are all transcendental. Therefore, the real transcendental object of meditation is to meditate upon the form, qualities, activities and pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains that in order to understand these characteristics of the Lord, one must first come in contact with the name of the Lord. Because Kṛṣṇa is very kind, He has manifested all of Himself within His name. When we talk about Kṛṣṇa’s self, we are not just talking about His name, but we are also talking about His form, His qualities and His activities. They are all manifested within His name.

*nāma cintāmaṇiḥ kṛṣṇaś*  
*caitanya-rasa-vigrahaḥ*  
*pūrṇaḥ śuddho nitya-mukto*  
*’bhinnatvān nāma-nāminoḥ*

(Cc. Madhya, 17.133)

Prabhupāda often quoted this verse to describe how Kṛṣṇa is the form of all transcendental mellows. Kṛṣṇa is not a material name under any circumstance. His name is no less powerful than Himself. Kṛṣṇa’s name is always eternally liberated and transcendental, and it never comes under the influence of the modes of material nature, because Kṛṣṇa and His name are non-different from each other.

For the benefit of the living entity in the material world, Kṛṣṇa has very kindly manifested Himself completely within His name.

*kali-kāle nāma-rūpe kṛṣṇa-avatāra*  
*nāma haite haya sarva-jagat-nistāra*

**In this Age of Kali, the holy name of the Lord, the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, is the incarnation of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Simply by chanting the holy name, one associates with the Lord directly. Anyone who does this is certainly delivered. (Cc. Ādi, 17.22)**

All the characteristics of the Lord—His qualities, form and activities—are all descriptions of His transcendental personality. However, the impersonalists do not know anything about the personality of the Supreme Lord in His dealings, in His personal relationships, and in His likes and dislikes.

In a lecture by Śrīla Prabhupāda in Los Angeles in 1968, he was saying that the impersonalists have no understanding of God as being a person who has likes and dislikes. We have everything in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. We not only know everything about the person, but we have His name, address, and phone number. We know how to reach Him. If we want to get in contact with any person, we have to know how to find him. Similarly, we have to know how to contact Kṛṣṇa. We know His address (Goloka Vṛndāvana), and we know His phone number. If we want to call Him, we just have to call out His name and can reach Him. He is always available, because He does not differ from His name, and He will immediately be there to answer our call.

Therefore, because the devotee has the Lord’s personal service, the devotee progresses very easily, whereas the impersonalist undergoes a series of difficult programs on account of his impersonal meditation. Understanding that the God is a person means understanding that He has particular qualities, activities and a transcendental form, which is described here as the glowing glancing of His smiling face.

In the previous verse (Bhāg. 2.2.11), it is said: “He is well decorated with an ornamental wreath about His waist and rings studded with valuable jewels on His fingers. His leglets, His bangles, His oiled hair, curling with a bluish tint, and His beautiful smiling face are all very pleasing.” These are all descriptions of His form.

His qualities are also explained by Lord Caitanya in Caitanya-caritāmṛta, where He describes all the qualities of the Supreme Lord. One of them is His compassionate nature, and how He is very kind in His dealings with His devotees. He is very merciful. These are again qualities of a person. His activities are most attractive because, as we see in His activities, the Lord is very inclined towards His devotees, and He reciprocates with them according to their attitude of love.

In the Tenth Canto of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, the gopīs question Kṛṣṇa: “What kind of a person are You? Do You have love for us? Are You indifferent towards us? Are You an enemy?” They wanted to know why Kṛṣṇa was dealing with them in the way in which He was—calling them into the forest in the dead of night by playing His transcendental flute. The gopīs rejected all the Vedic injunctions. They gave up their husbands, families and children. They were subjected to criticism from society. Upon hearing the sound of Kṛṣṇa’s flute, they gave everything up, thinking, “Kṛṣṇa is calling us because He wants to enjoy us.” Their meditation in everything that they did and in renouncing everything they had, was from thinking exclusively of Kṛṣṇa’s desires and pleasures.

Prabhupāda explains in his commentary on Caitanya-caritāmṛta that when the gopīs are decorating themselves and dressing themselves very nicely, they are thinking of how Kṛṣṇa is going to enjoy. Sometimes when a person is dressing himself, he thinks, “I want to try to attract others,” wanting to extract some pleasure from somebody else’s form or body. However, the gopīs do not think like that. They think, “Kṛṣṇa will be pleased by everything that we do, and because Kṛṣṇa is so pleased by seeing this body, the way we are dressing and our features, then He becomes even more attractive upon seeing us. When He becomes more attractive, we have a greater desire to please Him.”

These are the internal affairs of a devotee who actually has a desire to please or satisfy the Lord, knowing that the Lord is a person. This is the essence of what makes advancement on the path of devotional service more accessible for the living entity, because it is natural. What is very natural is that we have a natural desire to please and serve somebody. Prabhupāda explains that that is the innate characteristic of the soul.

Prabhupāda was talking about dharma in a lecture, saying that we cannot use the word religion as a translation for dharma. According to the dictionary, religion is a type of faith, and faith can change. One may have faith today as a Hindu, and tomorrow he can have faith as a Muslim or as a Christian. Thus, faith is something that can change.

However, dharma is something that cannot change, and it is the inherent characteristic or feature of the soul. Therefore, in the translation to the following verse, the wording used is occupational duties.

*ataḥ pumbhir dvija-śreṣṭhā*  
*varṇāśrama-vibhāgaśaḥ*  
*svanuṣṭhitasya dharmasya*  
*saṁsiddhir hari-toṣaṇam*

**The highest perfection one can achieve by discharging the duties prescribed for one’s own occupation according to caste divisions and orders of life is to please the Personality of Godhead. (Bhāg. 1.2.13)**

Prabhupāda explains that the dharma of the living entity is to serve the Lord. Everyone must serve. You cannot take heat and light away from fire. If you do so, then it is no longer fire. Heat and light are the very intrinsic qualities or characteristics of fire. Similarly, when we translate the word dharma we cannot use the word religion. It is not a sufficient translation. We have to try to understand that the essence of the living being is to serve.

The impersonalists have a very difficult time, unable to realize their innate qualities or characteristics, because they have no conception of God being a person who is worthy of our service. They are unable to meditate on how they can willfully and voluntarily do something that will please Him, even at the expense of possibly having to sacrifice their own personal pleasures.

*ramyā kācid upāsanā vrajavadhū-vargeṇa yā kalpitā*

(Caitanya-mañjuṣā)

This is a verse spoken by Lord Caitanya, where He considers the gopīs’ method of worship of the Supreme Personality of Godhead to be the highest method of worship. You will not find anyone who has a higher method of worshiping and serving the Supreme Lord, because theirs is always that of pleasing Kṛṣṇa. They gave up all personal considerations, although they were going to be subject to criticism; although they had to leave and face so much adversity from their family members; and although they had to make all kinds of personal sacrifices. The only thing that they were thinking was, “What does Kṛṣṇa want? What is Kṛṣṇa’s desire? What will give Him pleasure, even if it brings me displeasure? I don’t care. I want to satisfy Kṛṣṇa.”

This mentality of personal service to the Lord is the dharma of the living entity. We therefore have to practice by voluntarily making sacrifices for the satisfaction of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

In quoting the verse, ataḥ pumbhir dvija-śreṣṭhā varṇāśrama (Bhāg. 1.2.13), Prabhupāda said that the Lord, being a person, has particular desires, and a devotee who is on the platform of spontaneous devotional service is always attuned to them. Therefore, at every moment, for eternity, the devotee is constantly engaged on the spontaneous platform of pleasing the Lord.

The Lord reciprocates with that devotee and satisfies his innermost desires. The devotee then experiences all kinds of spiritual emotions, pleasures and ecstatic love, and the Lord’s love for the devotee continuously increases. On the platform of spontaneous devotional service, the devotee, being always attuned to what is pleasing to the Lord, never for a moment thinks of his own pleasure. Even if he experiences pleasure or ecstasy, he does not want it. In fact, even sometimes if he experiences it, he considers it to be a disturbance to his service to the Lord.

The example is given of Dāruka who was experiencing ecstasy when he was personally fanning the Lord. However, because that ecstasy was disturbing his service, he wanted to get rid of it. It was more important to him to serve and satisfy the Lord at that moment.

This desire to satisfy the Lord is the highest ecstasy. It brings the highest pleasure and satisfaction of the self. The devotee therefore gives up all kinds of personal motives and selfish desires, thinking exclusively of the pleasure of the Lord. This type of personal service to the Supreme Lord makes it very easy for the devotee to make progress.

Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī says in his Sandarbha: bhajanīya-parama-puruṣa-sukha-mātra-sva-sukhatvam. To the degree that one gives pleasure to the Lord, the living entity experiences pleasure. Because the Lord is so pleased that he is giving up consideration for his own happiness and he thinks of the Lord’s pleasure, the Lord gives pleasure to the devotee.

We chant every morning: aṅgāni yasya sakalendriya-vṛttimanti—the Lord’s senses are all completely transcendental. With any one of His senses, He can perform the activities of another sense. Prabhupāda explains that we should not think that the Deity form of the Lord cannot eat food offered to Him. Kṛṣṇa can eat with His eyes. He does not have to take food and put in His mouth. Simply by looking at it, He can enjoy it.

The devotee is therefore thinking of how he can please the Lord in his offering. He is not thinking, “How can I serve the Lord for my own pleasure? How can I get something by doing this service for the Lord?” Due to one’s selfish nature, having forgotten that God is a person, he will think, “I will simply do something for the Lord so that I can get my senses pleased.”

In the Seventh Canto of the Bhāgavatam, in his prayers to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, Prahlāda Mahārāja says, “O Lord, I am not going to be like a merchant. I am not going to serve You because I want something in return. I just want a relationship where You will be my master, and I will be Your servant, birth after birth after birth. I want no other relationship with You than this. I do not want to serve You just because You are going to offer me some benediction. I was born in a demonic family. I have a demonic mentality. Please do not tempt me by offering me something.” Prahlāda Mahārāja prays thusly, showing his selflessness.

A mercantile mentality will never enable one to experience the higher pleasure of devotional service. And if one does not have the higher pleasure of devotional service, then he will start looking for other forms of pleasures, question why he should serve the Lord, or try to please the senses of the Lord. He will think that he has more important things to do for experiencing pleasure in life. Having other aspirations in this life, he may temporarily do something to serve the Lord only so that he can get what he wants from the Lord. With such a mentality, he will never be able to advance on the path of devotional service. Kṛṣṇa knows our motives, desires, intentions, and what is in our heart. He knows if we are doing something to please Him or if we are doing something to please ourselves.

Bhajanīya-parama-puruṣa-sukha-mātra-sva-sukhatvam (as quoted in Bhāg. 2.3.10, purport)—to that degree that we actually have a desire to satisfy the senses of the Lord, then, viṣayā vinivartante, nirāhārasya dehinaḥ (Bg. 2.59)—we begin to experience the higher taste, our consciousness becomes fixed, our senses become controlled, and the lusty desires that are there within our heart become eradicated.

Further in his purport, Śrīla Prabhupāda speaks about the lusty desires in the heart:

PURPORT

The process of meditation recommended herein is bhakti-yoga, or the process of devotional service after one is liberated from the material conditions. Jñāna-yoga is the process of liberation from the material conditions. After one is liberated from the conditions of material existence, i.e., when one is nivṛtta, as previously stated herein, or when one is freed from all material necessities, one becomes qualified to discharge the process of bhakti-yoga. Therefore bhakti-yoga includes jñāna-yoga, or, in other words, the process of pure devotional service simultaneously serves the purpose of jñāna-yoga; liberation from material conditions is automatically achieved by the gradual development of pure devotional service. These effects of bhakti-yoga are called anartha-nivṛtti. Things which are artificially acquired gradually disappear along with the progress of bhakti-yoga. Meditation on the lotus feet of the Personality of Godhead, the first processional step, must show its effect by anartha-nivṛtti. The grossest type of anartha which binds the conditioned soul in material existence is sex desire, and this sex desire gradually develops in the union of the male and female. When the male and female are united, the sex desire is further aggravated by the accumulation of buildings, children, friends, relatives and wealth. When all these are acquired, the conditioned soul becomes overwhelmed by such entanglements, and the false sense of egoism, or the sense of “myself” and “mine,” becomes prominent, and the sex desire expands to various political, social, altruistic, philanthropic and many other unwanted engagements, resembling the foam of the sea waves, which becomes very prominent at one time and at the next moment vanishes as quickly as a cloud in the sky. The conditioned soul is encircled by such products, as well as products of sex desire, and therefore bhakti-yoga leads to gradual evaporation of the sex desire, which is summarized in three headings, namely profit, adoration and distinction. All conditioned souls are mad after these different forms of sex desire, and one shall see for himself how much he has been freed from such material hankerings based primarily on the sex desire. As a person feels his hunger satisfied after eating each morsel of foodstuff, he must similarly be able to see the degree to which he has been freed from sex desire. The sex desire is diminished along with its various forms by the process of bhakti-yoga because bhakti-yoga automatically, by the grace of the Lord, effectively results in knowledge and renunciation, even if the devotee is not materially very well educated. Knowledge means knowing things as they are, and if by deliberation it is found that there are things which are at all unnecessary, naturally the person who has acquired knowledge leaves aside such unwanted things.” (Part of the purport to Bhāg. 2.2.12)

Prabhupāda dissects everything and extracts it to the essence, explaining what happens if we do not have a desire to please the senses of Kṛṣṇa. A devotee, due to his personal service to the Lord, progresses very easily. However, if we do not develop or cultivate the mentality that God is a person, and if we do not become personally involved in serving the senses of the Supreme Lord, then we will become captivated by our own sense desires and anarthas, the greatest of which is the sex desire.

We gave the examples of how the gopīs’ method of worshiping and pleasing Kṛṣṇa’s senses was the highest, because everything they did was exclusively in thinking of what would be pleasing to Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa therefore gave them an ecstasy that is even millions of times greater than that which He experiences. For that reason, He had to come as Lord Caitanya to experience the love that they experience. He thought, “They are getting so much bliss by selflessly serving Me. How can I also taste that bliss?” That is how wonderful Kṛṣṇa is as a person. Because of the devotee’s selfless service to give Him pleasure, He gives back so much bliss and pleasure. Bhakti is Kṛṣṇa’s internal potency, and hlādinī-śakti is His internal pleasure potency, which gives pleasure both to the Lord and to the living entity. The living entity, by nature, is ānandamayo ’bhyāsāt—a pleasure-seeking being. However, if he does not look for pleasure in the Lord’s service, then he will attempt to look for pleasure in this world. It is so simple, yet we make it so difficult, because we do not want to clean away these unwanted desires within our heart.

**Question: If we attain the abode of Kṛṣṇa, will we ever fall under the modes of material nature?**

Kṛṣṇa says in many places in Bhagavad-gītā that when one comes under the influence of His daivim prakṛtim, His internal potency, he never comes under the influence of the modes of material nature. Tad dhāma paramaṁ mama (Bg. 15.6)—“One who attains My abode never has to take birth again.” When one goes there, he never has to come back. When a devotee comes under the protection of the Lord’s internal potency, he is protected. Kṛṣṇa explains how one can come under this protection:

*daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī*  
*mama māyā duratyayā*  
*mām eva ye prapadyante*  
*māyām etāṁ taranti te*

**“This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross beyond it.” (Bg. 7.14)**

Kṛṣṇa accepts that living entity under the protection of His internal potency, and thus he never again has to see māyā.

**Question: What is the difference between Kṛṣṇa’s internal energy and His external energy?**

*bhūmir āpo ’nalo vāyuḥ*  
*khaṁ mano buddhir eva ca*  
*ahaṅkāra itīyaṁ me*  
*bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā*

**“Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intelligence and false ego—all together these eight constitute My separated material energies.” (Bg. 7.4)**

The Lord’s internal energies (sandhinī, saṁvit and hlādinī) are sat, cit and ananda. His sandhinī potency is His eternal aspect; His saṁvit potency is His cognitive aspect; and the hlādinī potency is His pleasure potency. When we come under the protection of the Lord’s internal potency, we become captured by His energy, which is the protective potency for the living entity.

*kṛṣṇa—sūrya-sama; māyā haya andhakāra*  
*yāhāṅ kṛṣṇa, tāhāṅ nāhi māyāra adhikāra*

**“Kṛṣṇa is compared to sunshine, and māyā is compared to darkness. Wherever there is sunshine, there cannot be darkness. As soon as one takes to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, the darkness of illusion (the influence of the external energy) will immediately vanish. (Cc. Madhya 22.31)**

If the living entity is no longer in illusion about the false conception of his connection with his body, then he is under the protection of the Lord’s internal potency. Anyone who comes under the protection of His internal potency never has to come back again, as Kṛṣṇa very clearly says.

When we are chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, we are actually praying, addressing Kṛṣṇa’s internal potency (hlādinī or pleasure potency): “Rādhā, please engage me in Kṛṣṇa’s service. You are the most merciful manifestation. When anyone else is unable to please Kṛṣṇa, still You can. Thus, if You can engage me somehow in pleasing Kṛṣṇa, then certainly Kṛṣṇa will be pleased.”

We pray thusly to come under the protection of the Lord’s internal potency, and to not be captured by the glitter of the material world, which is external.

## Chapter 2 – Relationship with the Lord

## Serving a Person

Serving a person is the essence of devotion. Therefore, the impersonalists cannot have devotion. It is very difficult to be devoted to an inanimate object or to an impersonal void. Where is the quality or characteristic of devotion for an entity that has no life, no desires and no personality? When referring to service, Śrīla Prabhupāda refers to it as devotional service to enhance its real meaning. There is no question of service to God without devotion. Bhakti is therefore translated as devotional service.

An ideal devotee serves and pleases Kṛṣṇa to the highest degree, gratifying His transcendental senses and desires. As Kṛṣṇa is the supreme enjoyer, satisfying His desires is the way He relishes rasa or relationships. When He relishes that rasa with those who give pleasure to Him without any expectation of getting pleasure in return, then such devotees experience bliss, which is one of the byproducts of devotion.

By nature, every living being is ānanda-mayo ’bhyāsāt—meant to experience bliss. Unfortunately, we spend a lot of time looking for bliss in the wrong place and therefore never taste it. Or we may have gotten a slight glimpse of it by the mercy of Kṛṣṇa or His devotee. One may experience it at some point at a more elevated stage of devotion, but unlimited pleasure is the byproduct of devotion to Kṛṣṇa, because He is the reservoir of bliss and all pleasure. This enhances our understanding of Him being a personality.

“All purposes that are served by the small pond can at once be served by the great reservoirs of water. Similarly, all the purposes of the Vedas can be served to one who knows the purpose behind them.” (Bhāg. 4.13.25) After quoting this verse in a 1968 lecture in Los Angeles, Prabhupāda started talking about village life in India. He explained how in village life, the village girls go to one particular place for washing clothes, another place for washing dishes, another place for bathing, and so on. They have various small wells where they go to fulfill their purposes. Prabhupāda explained that as the river is continuously flowing, it cannot become contaminated. From a big reservoir of water, you can fulfill all your purposes. In the same way, if one wants to experience real pleasure or happiness, then he should go to Kṛṣṇa, who is the reservoir of all pleasure.

Kṛṣṇa is the Rasarāja, the King of all rasas and all relationships. He is the bestower of pleasure upon those who satisfy Him. He gives Himself to such living beings and He gives them unlimited bliss. He brings such living beings under the protection of His internal potency (daivī prakṛti), which consists of the sandhinī potency, saṁvit potency and hlādinī potency. These give the living being access to eternality, cognizance of his relationship with Kṛṣṇa, and unlimited bliss.

The embodiment of that hlādinī potency is Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī because She gives the greatest pleasure to Kṛṣṇa. The pleasure that She experiences by giving Kṛṣṇa pleasure is even greater than His pleasure. Therefore, Kṛṣṇa has to come as Lord Caitanya to taste the pleasure that Rādhārāṇī experiences. That is Kṛṣṇa’s personality.

Prabhupāda said, “To know you is to love you. If one wants to love somebody, then to the degree that we can know him we can love him.” Kṛṣṇa can never be fully known, but the more we know about Kṛṣṇa, the more it will increase our love or affection for Him. The essence of all our activities in devotional service is to revive our dormant love for Kṛṣṇa.

A phrase that we use very liberally sometimes is devotional service. We say, “This is my devotional service” or “I perform this devotional service” or “can I have some devotional service?” However, in devotional service, there must be some affection and absorption. Rūpa Gosvāmī explains that there are two characteristics of devotional service: svarūpa-lakṣaṇa and taṭastha-lakṣaṇa. The svarūpa-lakṣaṇa (primary characteristic) of bhakti is the intent to please Kṛṣṇa, and the secondary characteristic is freedom from any motivation, the desire for fruitive gain and the desire for liberation. When devotion, with the primary aim and desire to please Kṛṣṇa, is awakened within the heart, it is Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. Kṛṣṇa does not otherwise give devotion so easily.

*rājan patir gurur alaṁ bhavatāṁ yadūnāṁ*  
*daivaṁ priyaḥ kula-patiḥ kva ca kiṅkaro vaḥ*  
*astv evam aṅga bhagavān bhajatāṁ mukundo*  
*muktiṁ dadāti karhicit sma na bhakti-yogam*

**\[The great sage Nārada said:\] “My dear Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, the Supreme Personality of Godhead Kṛṣṇa is always ready to help you. He is your master, guru, God, very dear friend and head of your family. Yet sometimes He agrees to act as your servant or order-carrier. You are greatly fortunate because this relationship is possible only by bhakti-yoga. The Lord can give liberation \[mukti\] very easily, but He does not very easily give one bhakti-yoga, because by that process He is bound to the devotee.” (Bhāg. 5.6.18)**

Kṛṣṇa gives liberation very easily in comparison to bhakti, because when He gives bhakti, He has to give Himself. One of the characteristics of pure love or prema-bhakti given by Rūpa Gosvāmī is that it is the only means to control Kṛṣṇa and through which He becomes a plaything in the hands of His devotee.

None of us would like to become playthings in the hands of anyone, not wanting to sacrifice our individuality. However, Kṛṣṇa, although He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, likes to make Himself a plaything in the hands of His devotee, allowing the devotee to control Him and make Him dance!

In one pastime, by the transcendental sound of His flute, Kṛṣṇa called the gopīs to appear in the middle of the forest. Upon hearing the sound, they gave up everything. They performed the greatest sacrifice by going against Vedic injunctions and facing social criticism and ostracism. We cannot imagine the kind of criticism that would be there for leaving their families and husbands and going off into the forest in the dead of the night to answer the call of a charming blue boy who had captured their hearts. Their willingness to take that risk was not because they were driven by lust. Although Prabhupāda refers to the lusty desires of the gopīs, it is not lust as we know it. Their love is kāma-rūpa, which means lusty desires, but their lusty desire was to satisfy Kṛṣṇa’s desires, and never for a moment was there even the slightest thought of their own enjoyment. They only wanted Kṛṣṇa to enjoy. Prabhupāda explains in Caitanya-caritāmṛta that whenever the gopīs are decorating their bodies, putting on clothing or ornaments, the only thing they are thinking of is how Kṛṣṇa will be pleased.

People who do not understand anything about the nature of rasa or loving relationships on the transcendental platform think that Kṛṣṇa was immoral. They do not understand that there is no question of immorality, because everyone is meant for Kṛṣṇa’s enjoyment.

A man, in speaking to Śrīla Prabhupāda, was criticizing Kṛṣṇa, saying, “Why does Kṛṣṇa have to have so many wives?” Kṛṣṇa married over 16,000 wives to satisfy their desires, because they all wanted Him as their husband. Kṛṣṇa thus reciprocated accordingly and married them.

Prabhupāda responded to the man, “How many wives do you have?”

The man said, “I have one.”

Prabhupāda replied, “You have stolen one from Kṛṣṇa! You are immoral. Everyone is meant to be enjoyed by Kṛṣṇa.” Prabhupāda was so expert in dealing with everyone’s attitude.

There is no question of Kṛṣṇa’s immorality in the ways that He reciprocates love with His devotees. This is how Kṛṣṇa enjoys and there is no tinge of any mundane lust. He is the supreme reservoir of all pleasure and all living beings are meant to enjoy and experience that pleasure. The pleasure that Kṛṣṇa experiences with His devotees is completely spiritual, because He is never interested in anything mundane or material. Only something that is completely spiritual can give Kṛṣṇa pleasure. He is not interested in anything in the mundane world.

However, according to our own mundane conceptions, we project onto Kṛṣṇa our material or lusty desires for pleasure and enjoyment, thinking that He is immoral. Therefore, the materialists do not understand the affairs of Kṛṣṇa with the gopīs. As such, Śrīla Prabhupāda and Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura were always very emphatic that one should not delve too deeply into the loving affairs of Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs.

In one of Prabhupāda’s early lectures, he said, “If one hears Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes of the gopīs and thinks of mundane sex, then he should stop hearing them immediately! Do not enter there! Do not hear!” One must first be purified to hear these subjects.

We will discuss a section of the Bhāgavatam that describes Kṛṣṇa’s rāsa-līlā, but I will not delve deeply into the narrations of Kṛṣṇa’s pleasure with the gopīs. This section really helps us to understand how Kṛṣṇa is a reciprocator with all of His devotees, including sadhakas who are still in the material world, bound by the material body. It also illustrates how Kṛṣṇa reciprocates with everyone according to the degree of their love for Him. Furthermore, this section helps us understand Kṛṣṇa’s personality, emotions, and how Kṛṣṇa’s love, and the love experienced by His family, friends and lovers is the original form of spiritual emotions. The emotions that we experience in this world are simply perverted reflections of the emotions that are meant to be experienced in relationship to Kṛṣṇa.

Kṛṣṇa is a person and therefore Śrīla Prabhupāda uses the term Supreme Personality of Godhead to refer to the Lord. He wanted to emphasize that He is a person, because the usual tendency is to think of Him with an impersonalist conception.

Not only is Kṛṣṇa eternally the Supreme Person, but we are also eternally persons. Kṛṣṇa says:

*na tv evāhaṁ jātu nāsaṁ*  
*na tvaṁ neme janādhipāḥ*  
*na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ*  
*sarve vayam ataḥ param*

**“Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor all these kings; nor in the future shall any of us cease to be.” (Bg. 2.12)**

This is Kṛṣṇa’s emphasis to help us understand that we are eternally persons. If at some perfectional stage we lost our personality, or if previously we were impersonal and then became persons by accepting a material body, then Kṛṣṇa simply would have said, “Never was there a time when ‘I’ did not exist nor in the future will ‘I’ cease to be.” However, Kṛṣṇa specified the individuality of Arjuna and all the other kings present on the battlefield to emphasize the point that there never was a time when he, the kings, or any of us did not exist, nor in the future shall any of us cease to be.

Because we are persons, we have desires and we should know how to fulfill those desires. Whatever desires are within the core of the heart can be fulfilled much better by Kṛṣṇa than by our own efforts. Of course, if His devotee wants the fulfillment of some material desire, Kṛṣṇa will fulfill the desires in such a way that the devotee will not come back and ask for it again. Kṛṣṇa is very expert. He knows how to satisfy the desires of the devotee in such a way that the devotee ultimately gets the most valuable jewel. He says, “Why should I give My devotee material prosperity? Instead I shall induce him to take shelter of My lotus feet and make him forget these things.”

*samo ’haṁ sarva-bhūteṣu*  
*na me dveṣyo ’sti na priyaḥ*  
*ye bhajanti tu māṁ bhaktyā*  
*mayi te teṣu cāpy aham*

**Kṛṣṇa says, “I envy no one, nor am I partial to anyone. I am equal to all. But whoever renders service unto Me in devotion is a friend, is in Me, and I am also a friend to him.” (Bg. 9.29)**

Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura explains that the first half of this verse is referring to Kṛṣṇa as Supersoul—“I am equal to everyone. I am not envious of anyone.” However, Kṛṣṇa also says, “Whoever is a friend to Me, I am a friend to them.” How can He be equal to everyone, but still be friends with somebody? Our conception is that if we are friends with somebody, it means that we are not friends with someone else, which would mean that we are playing favorites.

Kṛṣṇa, on the other hand, says, “Whoever renders service unto Me in devotion is a friend, is in Me, and I am also a friend to him. If you want to be My friend, I will be your friend!” Kṛṣṇa does not have to worry about playing favorites. He is simply reciprocating according to the devotional attitude of His devotees.

Prabhupāda explains that it is very natural to reciprocate with those who are fully dependent on you. He gives the example that if the parent hears his child screaming in danger, immediately he recognizes and hears that voice above all other voices. That child does not know anyone except the parent. Similarly, Kṛṣṇa naturally reciprocates when a devotee is fully dependent on Him, saying, “Kṛṣṇa, I want to fully depend on You and I want to be friends with You!” Kṛṣṇa is svayaṁ bhagavān—He reciprocates with those who have spontaneous affection toward Him as a friend, parent, lover, etc. Kṛṣṇa reciprocates and answers according to their desires, and becomes completely subordinate to their desires to please and satisfy His senses.

When Kṛṣṇa played His flute, the gopīs left their homes and came before Him in the forest. He said, “Why did you all come? Don’t you know it is dangerous to come to the forest in the middle of the night? Why don’t you all go back home?” The gopīs continued standing there, making marks on the sand with their toes, and could not move away.

They said to Him, “Why have You done this? Why are You speaking to us in this way?”

Kṛṣṇa therefore enjoyed with the gopīs, and then at one point He left them. The gopīs became so mad in ecstasy and were looking around, asking everyone—the trees, creepers, flowers, deer, and all creatures in the forest—if they had seen Kṛṣṇa. They began imitating His activities and pastimes.

The gopīs, who were feeling pangs of separation, asked, “Why did Kṛṣṇa leave us? Where did Kṛṣṇa go?” They began wondering, “Maybe Kṛṣṇa went off with somebody else?” Upon seeing two sets of footprints someplace, they said, “Look! Kṛṣṇa must have left!” Eventually they saw only one set of footprints, and when they followed them, they found Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī sitting in one place, which meant that Kṛṣṇa had also left Her. This caused them all to be thrown into an ocean of lamentation, bereavement and suffering. The gopīs felt that Kṛṣṇa was killing them.

Later when Kṛṣṇa returned, they all wanted to find out how it was possible that Kṛṣṇa could do something like that to those who love Him so much. They started asking questions about Kṛṣṇa to Him in the form of riddles, trying to understand Him: “What kind of reciprocator are You? What kind of a personality are You?” They wanted to hear directly from Kṛṣṇa’s mouth what kind of a person He was.

**“The gopīs said: Some people reciprocate the affection only of those who are affectionate toward them, while others show affection even to those who are indifferent or inimical. And yet others will not show affection toward anyone. Dear Kṛṣṇa, please properly explain this matter to us.” (Bhāg. 10.32.16)**

The gopīs did not want to accuse Him directly. Therefore, they asked in such a way to make Kṛṣṇa responsible for His actions and have Him explain Himself. Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura explains:

Each of the gopīs personally considered within her mind, “Since Kṛṣṇa has put us, who are the crest-jewel of all His loving devotees, into such an unfortunate condition, we should ask Him why He did it.”

Other gopīs thought, “O Kṛṣṇa, do You have love for us, indifference to us, or enmity towards us? Even though there are these three possibilities, we cannot ascertain which is the fact. Moreover is Your love conditional or unconditional? It cannot be conditional! Because the person with conditional love gratifies those who help him to fulfill his desires, and therefore does not neglect them or subject them to misery. You however, have tried to kill us by burning us in the fire of separation from You. Neither is Your love unconditional, since You abandoned us in the dense, fearful forest in the middle of the night. Though seeing our suffering, You were not at all bereaved. In that we see some motive, so it cannot be unconditional.”

(Sārārtha-darśinī, commentary to 32.16)

The gopīs then say, “Indifference means to not care. Therefore, we can see that You are not indifferent, and we do not see enmity, because You tried to make us both happy and sad.”

When they speak about enmity, they speak of two types—either due to a permanent dislike towards somebody, or due to arousal by some contrary action by the other person. Therefore, they say, “Actually, we do not see that it is a kind of enmity due to some permanent dislike, as we just do not see that quality in You. Also, it could not have been anything that we provoked, because we have never done anything to cause You disturbance. Therefore, you are neither a conditional lover nor an unconditional lover. You are not indifferent. You neither have any permanent dislikes towards us, nor is there anything that was provoked.” They were asking such questions in the form of riddles, because they wanted to see Kṛṣṇa wriggle out of this one.

The gopīs then tell Kṛṣṇa:

“Rather, You serve as the example of a person who has that sort of perverted enmity, symptomized by the vicious desire to harm those who trust one. We should not state this openly with our own mouths.” (Sārārtha-darśinī, commentary to 32.16)

We can relate to these emotions of the gopīs, as they are based upon the emotions that we experience in relationships in this world. However, the emotions that we experience in this world are the perverted reflections of the emotions that the gopīs and the residents of Vṛndāvana are experiencing with Kṛṣṇa. The symptom of their love is that it is never diminished even though there is reason for it to diminish. It is one of the symptoms given by Rūpa Gosvāmī as the criteria of loving relationships between Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs. Although there is a reason for diminution of their love, it is never diminished. Rather, it is always increasing.

The gopīs continued:

“We should not state this openly with our own mouths, but we will ask such questions in the form of riddles, so that Kṛṣṇa Himself will give the appropriate answer, and thus the truth of this matter will become evident.”

Because the gopīs were feeling the same sentiment within each of their hearts, they all reflected in a similar way. Then these gopīs of similar mind spoke: “O most intelligent one, O Kṛṣṇa, please answer this riddle of ours. There are some people who only respect those who respect them. Their respect is conditional. They give respect expecting something, and if they do not get that, then they no longer give respect. This is conditional love. Quite to the contrary of this, there are those who give respect to those who do not respect them. They have unconditional respect. Not expecting any results for themselves, they have unconditional love.

“The third type of people are those who do not respect anyone, whether that person respects them or not. There is no question of conditional or unconditional love here. Those persons are indifferent. Hatred and enmity are also non-reciprocation, so persons who are hateful and inimical also fall in the category of non-respect.”

Though not clearly mentioned here, it will become somewhat evident in Kṛṣṇa’s answers. The gopīs said, “Kṛṣṇa, please say something to explain this matter as to who reciprocates with whom and who fails to do so? You should answer correctly without deviating from the subject.”

(Sārārtha-darśinī, commentary to 32.16)

This is essentially a summary of all the different types of reciprocators—whether it is unconditional love, conditional love or indifference. Kṛṣṇa is going to explain why it appeared that He did not reciprocate, but in fact, was reciprocating. This is what really brings out and enhances Kṛṣṇa’s personality—especially in the case of devotees—when it externally appears that Kṛṣṇa is invisible and is not reciprocating. When it appears that Kṛṣṇa is not reciprocating, He is actually reciprocating, because He is intensifying the affection and unconditional love that devotees have for Him. This is further elaborated upon within the commentaries of Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura.

Kṛṣṇa says to the gopīs, “For those who are actually situated on the platform of premā (pure love), I do not reciprocate with them because I want to intensify their attachment, love and affection for Me. Just like a person who once had a great wealth and later lost it, he does nothing after he lost it except think of how to get that wealth back again.”

I had a disciple in the Soviet Union who, when he became a devotee, was always thinking in the back of his mind, “I have so much money in the bank that I don’t have to be in anxiety. I will just leave it there.” When communism fell, though, the ruble lost its value by a significant amount. They even froze all the banks and would not give out any money, not knowing what it was worth. Therefore, all the money that this disciple had in the bank, on which he was thinking that he could live for a long time without anxiety, became worthless.

Thus Kṛṣṇa has used an example that we can directly relate with, and further explains:

“The reason I do not immediately reciprocate the affection of living beings even when they worship Me, O gopīs, is that I want to intensify their loving devotion. They then become like a poor man who has gained some wealth and then lost it, and who thus becomes so anxious about it that he can think of nothing else.” (Bhāg. 10.32.20)

The gopīs asked, “What class do you belong to? How is it different from the group (guru-druhaḥ) that You previously explained?” Guru-druhaḥ is an example of a person who does not reciprocate even though somebody is favorable towards him. Even though the spiritual master has always been favorably disposed and helping the disciple, that disciple is actually called the guru-druhaḥ. Thus, the guru-druhaḥ does not reciprocate with the guru even though the guru is always favorably disposed towards him. The guru-druhaḥ is also one who injures someone who is faithful.

Kṛṣṇa had also previously explained to the gopīs about the alpa-druhaḥ—those who have a reason for being inimical, and are of a lower class than the guru-druhaḥ. Those who show hatred toward one who renders protection are druhaḥ.

The gopīs say to Kṛṣṇa, “You are saying that You do not respond to anyone who acts favorably towards You. So how are You different from the guru-druhaḥ?”

Kṛṣṇa responds:

“For those surrendered souls who worship Me through nāma-kīrtana and other means, I do not respond in order to make their worship more perfect. O gopīs who cannot understand My real intention! Not seeing Me, those surrendered souls develop deep humility, feeling, ‘Alas, alas, everything I have done has been useless. Because I am an offender, Kṛṣṇa has not shown even the slightest favor toward me. Let me be damned.’

“By constantly thinking in this way, those who have not yet developed mature love for Me will become free from lust and anger and awaken pure devotion full of power and brilliance.”

(Sārārtha-darśinī, commentary to 32.20)

In this commentary, Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura is explaining how Kṛṣṇa does not reciprocate with those who respect and worship Him. Those who are engaged in kīrtana, chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, and to whom it appears that Kṛṣṇa is not reciprocating with them, they become humbled and pray in a particular way, saying, “Kṛṣṇa has not even shown the slightest favor toward me. I am an offender!” But they still continue to chant. They never think, “I am an offender! Kṛṣṇa is not reciprocating. Can Kṛṣṇa not see that I am sincere?”

Often we think, “Kṛṣṇa cannot see that I am sincere and that He should reciprocate.” Such thoughts are in the mood of conditional love. Conversely, the devotee’s understanding is: “It is because of me that Kṛṣṇa is not reciprocating. I have impurities! Let me be damned! I will still go on chanting Kṛṣṇa’s name!” Continuing to chant Kṛṣṇa’s name in this mood, Kṛṣṇa says, “His heart will become free from whatever contamination is in his heart. He will become free from lust, anger and greed. He will become a pure devotee. I am therefore reciprocating with him, and bringing him to the platform of pure devotion.”

In continuing to read these verses and commentaries about this pastime between the gopīs and Kṛṣṇa, we will see that the gopīs were ultimately defeated by Kṛṣṇa. They realized that nobody has loved them like Kṛṣṇa has, because He actually made Himself a debtor to the gopīs.

Kṛṣṇa said, “I cannot possibly repay you! You have done everything, sacrificing your family, society, Vedic injunctions and everyone else. I cannot properly reciprocate with what you have done! You have made Me a debtor!”

Kṛṣṇa therefore purposely left them to make Himself an eternal debtor to the gopīs. He said:

“I am not able to repay My debt for your spotless service, even within a lifetime of Brahmā. Your connection with Me is beyond reproach. You have worshiped Me, cutting off all domestic ties, which are difficult to break. Therefore please let your own glorious deeds be your compensation. (Bhāg. 10.32.22)

Kṛṣṇa said, “You left your mother, father, children, brothers and families! I have said in Bhagavad-gītā that as they surrender, I reciprocate accordingly—ye yathā māṁ prapadyante, tāṁs tathaiva bhajāmy aham, mama vartmānuvartante, manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ. (Bg. 4.11) Although you have given up your family, I am unable to give up Mine. How can I possibly adequately reciprocate with what you have done for Me? There is nothing that I can do to reciprocate in return. I cannot give up My mother, My father and My brother. I am therefore a debtor!”

The gopīs then considered in their minds, “Even though Kṛṣṇa, being the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is full of all transcendental qualities, devoid of the slightest trace of any fault and knows all about our love for Him, in order to establish the superiority of our love for Him, and to make Himself indebted to us, He has performed this act of giving us up.” (Sārārtha-darśinī, commentary to 32.22)

Kṛṣṇa performed this act for two reasons: 1) to make Himself indebted to the gopīs, and 2) to show everyone for all of eternity that no one has more love for Him than these gopīs. He put the gopīs in that intense suffering to show everyone how the love of the gopīs is the highest.

Kṛṣṇa came as Lord Caitanya to show everyone the gopīs’ love, by Himself embodying the love of the gopīs, headed by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. In doing this, He felt the same pain as the gopīs, returned that to His devotees with the ecstasies of His own love, and thus paid back the debt for having put the gopīs in that kind of separation.

The gopīs realized:

“In order to establish the superiority of our love for Him and to make Himself indebted to us, He has performed this act of giving us up. We, who wanted to defeat Kṛṣṇa and criticize Him for His conduct with our riddles, have been most immoral in our intent, whereas He desired only to establish our exalted position. We could never act like that! Thus in effect we have become conquered by Kṛṣṇa’s love.” (Sārārtha-darśinī, commentary to 32.22)

Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura describes these pastimes in much greater detail. What has been mentioned herein describes just a little bit about serving the Lord.

## Understanding Kṛṣṇa’s Personality

*na veda kaścid bhagavaṁś cikīrṣitaṁ*  
*tavehamānasya nṛṇāṁ viḍambanam*  
*na yasya kaścid dayito ‘sti karhicid*  
*dveṣyaś ca yasmin viṣamā matir nṛṇām*

**“O Lord, no one can understand Your transcendental pastimes, which appear to be human and are so misleading. You have no specific object of favor, nor do You have any object of envy. People only imagine that You are partial.” (Bhāg. 1.8.29)**

PURPORT

The Lord’s mercy upon the fallen souls is equally distributed. He has no one as the specific object of hostility. The very conception of the Personality of Godhead as a human being is misleading. His pastimes appear to be exactly like a human being’s, but actually they are transcendental and without any tinge of material contamination. He is undoubtedly known as partial to His pure devotees, but in fact He is never partial, as much as the sun is never partial to anyone. By utilizing the sun rays, sometimes even the stones become valuable, whereas a blind man cannot see the sun, although there are enough sun rays before him. Darkness and light are two opposite conceptions, but this does not mean that the sun is partial in distributing its rays. The sun rays are open to everyone, but the capacities of the receptacles differ. Foolish people think that devotional service is flattering the Lord to get special mercy. Factually the pure devotees who are engaged in the transcendental loving service of the Lord are not a mercantile community. A mercantile house renders service to someone in exchange for values. The pure devotee does not render service unto the Lord for such exchange, and therefore the full mercy of the Lord is open for him. Suffering and needy men, inquisitive persons or philosophers make temporary connections with the Lord to serve a particular purpose. When the purpose is served, there is no more relation with the Lord. A suffering man, if he is pious at all, prays to the Lord for his recovery. But as soon as the recovery is over, in most cases the suffering man no longer cares to keep any connection with the Lord. The mercy of the Lord is open for him, but he is reluctant to receive it. That is the difference between a pure devotee and a mixed devotee. Those who are completely against the service of the Lord are considered to be in abject darkness, those who ask for the Lord’s favor only at the time of necessity are partial recipients of the mercy of the Lord, and those who are cent percent engaged in the service of the Lord are full recipients of the mercy of the Lord. Such partiality in receiving the Lord’s mercy is relative to the recipient, and it is not due to the partiality of the all-merciful Lord.

When the Lord descends on this material world by His all-merciful energy, He plays like a human being, and therefore it appears that the Lord is partial to His devotees only, but that is not a fact. Despite such apparent manifestation of partiality, His mercy is equally distributed. In the Battlefield of Kurukṣetra all persons who died in the fight before the presence of the Lord got salvation without the necessary qualifications because death before the presence of the Lord purifies the passing soul from the effects of all sins, and therefore the dying man gets a place somewhere in the transcendental abode. Somehow or other if someone puts himself open in the sun rays, he is sure to get the requisite benefit both by heat and by ultraviolet rays. Therefore, the conclusion is that the Lord is never partial. It is wrong for the people in general to think of Him as partial. (Teachings of Queen Kuntī, Chapter 12)

In this verse from the Teachings of Queen Kuntī, we get a little glimpse of Kṛṣṇa’s personality, which is very difficult to understand.

*athāpi te deva padāmbuja-dvaya-*  
*prasāda-leśānugṛhīta eva hi*  
*jānāti tattvaṁ bhagavan-mahimno*  
*na cānya eko ’pi ciraṁ vicinvan*

**“My Lord, if one is favored by even a slight trace of the mercy of Your lotus feet, he can understand the greatness of Your personality. But those who speculate to understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead are unable to know You, even though they continue to study the Vedas for many years.” (Bhāg. 10.14.29)**

One requires some mercy to understand Kṛṣṇa’s personality. It is hidden to those who do not obtain that drop of mercy and who are not eager for that mercy. We know the Lord is very merciful and very kind, and this verse describes how the Lord is not partial to anyone. He is equally disposed, but it is dependent upon the quality of the receptacle and how one obtains the full mercy or partial mercy of the Supreme Lord.

A person who is suffering may look to the Lord for relief from that suffering, but he is only a partial recipient of the mercy of the Lord. He may get relief from his suffering, but then he thinks, “Because my suffering has gone, I no longer need a connection with the Lord.” Thus he does not get the full mercy of the Lord. To get the full mercy of the Lord, one must understand Kṛṣṇa’s personality, obtain pure devotional service, and establish his eternal relationship with the Supreme.

In the Bhāgavatam, Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja says, “Kṛṣṇa has become your friend; He has become your messenger, guru and God. But I see that you are very fortunate, because He has become your servant.”

While the Lord gives liberation very easily, He does not give devotional service so easily, because when He gives devotional service, He has to give Himself. However, although the subject matter of bhakti is very difficult to understand, in the Age of Kali, Lord Caitanya is so merciful that He has made it very easily accessible even to those who are unqualified for such mercy. Either way, mercy is required. The Lord is purchased and inclined to give His mercy to those who have unflinching faith in the process of pure devotional service. This was illustrated very nicely in the Tenth Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam in the pastime of Mother Yaśodā trying to bind Kṛṣṇa with ropes. He ultimately allowed Himself to become bound by her because of her pure love.

Furthermore, to obtain the mercy of the Supreme Lord requires great faith and persistence. This faith is described to be the characteristic or the eligibility for pure devotional service.

## Establishing our Relationship with the Lord

*prāyeṇa munayo rājan*  
*nivṛttā vidhi-ṣedhataḥ*  
*nairguṇya-sthā ramante sma*  
*guṇānukathane hareḥ*

**“The topmost devotees of the Lord, the paramahaṁsas, they derive the greatest pleasure by always speaking about Kṛṣṇa.” (Bhāg. 2.1.7)**

A devotee does not feel burdened to give Kṛṣṇa consciousness to others. Rather, he is very happy because it is an opportunity to render service to the Lord and to satisfy Him by his service.

To be dependent upon a devotee for Kṛṣṇa consciousness is not the same thing as being dependent upon a materialistic person in the material world, which is the utmost sign of misfortune. It is not a very auspicious relationship that exists between the dependent and the person who is burdened by the other person’s dependency. Just as a devotee is very happy to give Kṛṣṇa consciousness to others and does not consider such dependency of others as a burden, we should understand that the Lord is also very happy when His devotee is dependent upon Him.

It is described in the Fourth Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is very dear to those devotees who have no material possessions, and who are fully satisfied in possessing only devotional service to Kṛṣṇa. The Lord never thinks of His devotees’ dependence on Him as a burden.

When a devotee calls out Kṛṣṇa’s name, He relishes hearing it. When a devotee calls out “Kṛṣṇa,” the devotee is simply saying, “Kṛṣṇa, let me remember You. Kṛṣṇa, let me serve You. Kṛṣṇa, I don’t want anything from You. I simply want to satisfy You and remember You birth after birth after birth.”

Kṛṣṇa never thinks, “There are unlimited living entities in the universe who are already dependent on Me, and another one is now calling out to Me…this is such a burden.”

Although the living entities in the universe may be hanging onto the Lord in dependence, He does not personally get involved in their lives. Everyone has a relationship with the Lord, because He is situated within everyone’s heart as Supersoul and is simply witnessing and sanctioning the living entity’s unlimited desires. Through the agencies of the material nature and the Lord’s different energies, He gives His sanction, but there is no intimacy.

A pious person may turn to the Lord for some remuneration, but his only interest is that remuneration. Prabhupāda explains in Teachings of Queen Kuntī that such a person establishes only a partial or temporary connection with the Lord to fulfill a particular purpose. When the purpose has been fulfilled, the connection is no longer there. Even if there is gratitude, there is no intimacy. Intimacy requires a relationship and reciprocation, but there is no līlā when the Lord simply sits within the heart as Supersoul and witnesses and sanctions. Līlā only begins when the devotee has bhakti.

However, Kṛṣṇa relishes taking care of His devotees, and the devotees are always satisfied with whatever the Lord gives them.

*nārāyaṇa-parāḥ sarve*  
*na kutaścana bibhyati*  
*svargāpavarga-narakeṣv*  
*api tulyārtha-darśinaḥ*

**Devotees solely engaged in the devotional service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa, never fear any condition of life. For them the heavenly planets, liberation and the hellish planets are all the same, for such devotees are interested only in the service of the Lord. (Bhāg. 6.17.28)**

Whether in opulence or in poverty, it is all the same for the devotees, because they are simply thinking of Kṛṣṇa and calling out to Him: “Please, let me serve You and remember You!” Kṛṣṇa is therefore very happy to see to the comforts of His devotees. This is intimacy. The devotees dress Kṛṣṇa, supply food, and engage in serving Him. Because the devotee is only happy in serving Him, Kṛṣṇa sees to his happiness and gives him opportunities to serve Him, causing his pleasure to increase.

Viṣṇujana Swami tells a story to illustrate this point of intimacy. It is about a man who went to another lover besides his wife. When the wife found out that her husband was going to someone else, she tries to find out what it is that the other woman has that she does not.

The husband says, “Well, it is the way she dresses for me.”

The wife thinks, “He is my husband, and I certainly want to attract him in such a way that he won’t go to this other woman.” She therefore spends all her money on costly clothing and nicely decorates her body. When the husband returns home and sees his wife, he becomes so appreciative by her beauty and stays with her that night.

The following night, he does not come home. When he finally returns, the wife said, “I thought it is the way she dresses for you. Does she dress as beautifully as I dressed for you?”

The husband says, “Actually, it is the way she cooks for me.”

The wife then makes another plan to capture the heart of her husband. She goes out and collects so many ingredients and cooks him a huge feast—one like he has never had before. He returns home and sees the wonderful feast and enjoys the food. He expresses his gratitude to his wife: “I have never had a meal like this before.”

The following night, he again does not come home. When he does eventually return, the wife says, “I thought you said that it is the way she cooks for you. Did she cook like I cooked for you?”

“Well… No.”

“Then, what is it? Why did you not come back last night?”

“It is the way she kicks and bites me.”

To that, the wife responds, “Kicks and bites you? You want to be kicked and bitten? I can’t kick and bite you. I love you! If you want to be kicked and bitten, then go. You’ll have to go to her. I will not kick and bite you.”

Similarly, being kicked and bitten by the material nature is the kind of reciprocation we get for the fulfillment of all our material desires. It is temporary fulfillment, which ultimately leads to suffering. Kṛṣṇa, however, will never do that to His devotee. Rather, He will try everything to attract His devotee to that intimate relationship, saying, “All you have to do is to turn to Me. Depend upon Me. Call out My name. I am always very eager to hear My devotees who are calling My name with devotion, and who are always depending upon Me in all their activities.” Kṛṣṇa takes care of everything for such devotees.

Thus, if we want to relish this intimacy, we have to approach Kṛṣṇa in this way. Similarly, if we want to relish this intimacy with Kṛṣṇa’s devotees, we have to approach His devotees in this way. Devotees are always happy to give Kṛṣṇa to others. It is their pleasure, because it is so pleasing to Kṛṣṇa. If we approach devotees in this mood, then intimacy opens up due to reciprocation and love. Kṛṣṇa says, “When you approach Me with love, I reciprocate and I give love. I give the most valuable thing I have in My possession—I give My heart.”

Thus, Queen Kuntī is praying in this way: “Kṛṣṇa, we are fully dependent upon You. We are Your intimate friends. We are simply living by Your care and mercy. We have no shelter other than Your lotus feet. Therefore, kindly, do not leave us, and please, let us always be with You.” Such is the prayer of a devotee.

Śrīla Prabhupāda therefore says, “This is a symptom of a real Kṛṣṇa conscious person.” Kṛṣṇa is the supreme master and the devotee always feels in danger without Him. By taking shelter of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, the devotee always feels safe.

**Question: Can the different types of persons who approach Kṛṣṇa establish their relationship with Him and render devotional service?**

Śrīla Prabhupāda describes the four types of persons who approach Kṛṣṇa:

*catur-vidhā bhajante māṁ*  
*janāḥ sukṛtino ’rjuna*  
*ārto jijñāsur arthārthī*  
*jñānī ca bharatarṣabha*

(Bg. 7.16)

Those four types of persons who approach the Lord are: those who are distressed, those who are inquisitive, those who are in need of wealth, and those who are wise. Prabhupāda speaks about these different persons and how each of them gets mercy to a particular degree. However, he says that the pure devotee of the Lord does not have a mercantile consciousness, and his only desire is to bring about the satisfaction of the Supreme Lord.

Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura describes in his Bhaktyāloka that there are the karmī, jñānī and bhakta. They are all looking for some result from their sacrifices. For one who is engaged in karma-yoga, he is looking for the fruit of his sacrifice; he wants some result. The jñānī is also looking for some fruitive sacrifice; he wants liberation. The devotee is also looking for some fruit, but the fruit he is looking for is Kṛṣṇa’s pleasure. Sometimes it is seen that the sādhakas are engaged in devotional service, and after prolonged sādhana they give it up because they lose their faith. Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says that patience is required. To have patience means that a devotee must have firm faith that he will get Kṛṣṇa’s mercy—either now, one year from now, a hundred years from now, or a hundred lifetimes from now. With this faith that someday he will get Kṛṣṇa’s mercy, he continues to serve Him.

*athāpi te deva padāmbuja-dvaya-*  
*prasāda-leśānugṛhīta eva hi*  
*jānāti tattvaṁ bhagavan-mahimno*  
*na cānya eko ’pi ciraṁ vicinvan*

**“My Lord, if one is favored by even a slight trace of the mercy of Your lotus feet, he can understand the greatness of Your personality. But those who speculate to understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead are unable to know You, even though they continue to study the Vedas for many years.” (Bhāg. 10.14.29)**

The devotee must be very eager for mercy and have faith that perfection in Kṛṣṇa consciousness is obtainable. He must have hope against hope that some day, sooner or later, he will get that mercy by simply going on with faith, chanting Kṛṣṇa’s name, associating with Kṛṣṇa’s devotees and hearing about the pastimes of the Lord in the association of devotees of the Lord.

Therefore, in Bhakti-tattva-viveka, in reference to these four types of persons—those who are distressed, those who are in need of money, those who are inquisitive, and those who are wise—Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says that as long as one wants the fulfillment of these desires, he does not have the eligibility for śuddha-bhakti or pure devotional service.

These four types of devotees require sukṛtī. According to the teachings of Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, sukṛtī means to have the association of transcendental personalities. As a result of that association, the intense desire to serve Kṛṣṇa awakens within one’s heart.

For example, to be eligible for śuddha-bhakti, the desire to become relieved from distress has to be given up. In this regard, the example of Gajendra the elephant is given. Gajendra was in great distress, and he offered prayers to the Lord that he remembered from his previous birth. The Lord, who is the reliever of all distress, appeared to take away his distress. By his association with the Lord, Gajendra gave up his desire to become relieved from distress and thus became eligible for pure devotional service.

The example of the sages of Naimiṣāraṇya is given in reference to those who are inquisitive and approach the Lord. The sages had doubts that by karma-yoga (fruitive activities and sacrifices) alone, one could achieve perfection in this Age of Kali. They were very inquisitive and wanted to inquire from Sūta Gosvāmī. By such inquisitiveness, they got the association of Sūta Gosvāmī, and the result of that association was that their desire of an inquisitive nature was eradicated from their hearts and they became qualified for pure devotional service.

An example of one who wanted wealth was Dhruva Mahārāja. Dhruva Mahārāja, who wanted a kingdom, received instructions from Śrīla Nārada Muni on how to get the darśana of the Supreme Lord. He was told by his mother to go and look in the forest for the fulfillment of his desire. The Lord appeared by his severe austerities. His desire for that kingdom immediately disappeared: “I came here looking for a piece of broken glass, but I found the most valuable jewel.” He no longer had that desire for wealth and prosperity, and thus became qualified for pure devotional service.

The example given of jñānīs was the four Kumāras. They were nirviśeṣa-śūnyavādi (voidists and impersonalists). However, because they smelled the fragrance of the aroma of the Tulasī leaves emanating from the lotus feet of the Lord, they also became qualified by that association, and within their hearts, the intense desire to serve Kṛṣṇa arose.

These four examples demonstrate how sukṛti—association with the Lord or with a pure devotee of the Lord—awoke within their heart the intense desire to serve the Lord.

Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura quotes a verse from Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī that says that those who are neither too attached nor too detached, and who have developed some faith in devotional service of the Lord, can become qualified for pure devotional service. Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains that sometimes when one realizes the futility of material existence, because of prolonged endeavors to fulfill his desires, he realizes the futility of materialistic life. After prolonged endeavor to fulfill his desires, he either does not get them fulfilled or they do get fulfilled, but he realizes that that fulfillment of the desires cannot satisfy him. At that point, some detachment is awakened within his heart, and then by good fortune, if he gets an opportunity to associate with a devotee of Kṛṣṇa and he hears from Kṛṣṇa that the highest goal is to attain devotional service and the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, then he gains some faith in devotional service.

*jāta-śraddho mat-kathāsu*  
*nirviṇṇaḥ sarva-karmasu*  
*veda duḥkhātmakān kāmān*  
*parityāge ’py anīśvaraḥ*  
*tato bhajeta māṁ prītaḥ*  
*śraddhālur dṛḍha-niścayaḥ*  
*juṣamāṇaś ca tān kāmān*  
*duḥkhodarkāṁś ca garhayan*

**“Having awakened faith in the narrations of My glories, being disgusted with all material activities, knowing that all sense gratification leads to misery, but still being unable to renounce all sense enjoyment, My devotee should remain happy and worship Me with great faith and conviction. Even though he is sometimes engaged in sense enjoyment, My devotee knows that all sense gratification leads to a miserable result, and he sincerely repents such activities.” (Bhāg. 11.20.27-28)**

**Question: Is there a difference in the relationship with Kṛṣṇa and in the relationship with Lord Caitanya?**

As Prabhupāda explains, this subject matter of devotional service is very difficult to understand for non-devotees. Unless one establishes a relationship with Lord Caitanya, it continues to be very difficult to understand. It is explained in Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya:

That blissful place, which is transcendental to material nature, rests on Kṛṣṇa’s inconceivable and supremely magnanimous sandhinī energy. By that energy the dhāma has descended here in Nadia, for Kṛṣṇa’s real desire is to deliver the living entities. Materialistic persons cannot enter the dhāma, nor is there any material influence here. Māyā has eternally covered the dhāma with the film of dull matter. People who have no relationship with Kṛṣṇa Caitanya simply live on top of that cover, blind to the real truth. Though one is thinking, “I am in Navadvīpa,” Prauḍhā Māyā happily keeps that person far away from the dhāma. But if by some great fortune one receives the association of a devotee, that relationship, or sambandha, with Śrī Caitanya will be established.

This topic of sambandha is a deep thing (…), a treasure that conditioned souls cannot easily understand. Even if one calls out the name of ‘Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya’ with seeming affection, if that relationship is not established in his heart, he simply remains in the material realm. Such a person resides on top of the dhāma’s illusory covering and never attains pure bhakti. That person is the dharmadvajī, or hypocritically devout, who is especially duplicitous, who has no humility and is full of pride, yet still thinks he is fully qualified. (Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya, Chapter 18)

Thus, unless one gets the association of a devotee of the Lord, it will be impossible to establish his relationship with Lord Caitanya. He will simply stand on top of this covering, but will never understand that mystery of devotional service. Such persons have no humility, are full of pride, and still think that they are fully qualified.

By the mercy of a devotee, a person can give up his pride and perform devotional activities. One should think himself to be lower than the blade of grass, more tolerant than a tree. He should not desire respect for himself, but should expertly offer respects to all others. When one possesses these four qualities and sings the glories of Lord Kṛṣṇa, his relationship with Śrī Caitanya manifests within his heart. One must get sambandha, or relationship, with the Lord by coming in contact with a devotee.

In Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya, Lord Nityānanda is taking Jīva Gosvāmī on parikramā in Navadvīpa, and after completing Navadvīpa Maṇḍala Parikramā, He is instructing Jīva Gosvāmī. He says that there are five types of relationships with Kṛṣṇa: śānta (in neutrality), dāsya (in servitude), sākhya (in friendship), vātsalya (in parental affection) and mādhurya (in conjugal love). However, with Lord Caitanya, the relationship is primarily of dāsyaṁ or servitude, and thus one must actually think himself to be a servant of Lord Caitanya. By the mercy of a devotee of the Lord, one can establish that relationship with Lord Caitanya.

It is described that although Jīva Gosvāmī previously had contact with Lord Caitanya, he was instructed to go to Navadvīpa and take shelter of Lord Nityānanda. Lord Nityānanda took him on parikramā in Navadvīpa-dhāma and bestowed upon him His mercy. Lord Nityānanda said, “Now, having gone on parikramā, Lord Caitanya will bestow upon you the right to enter into Vṛndāvana.” One who takes shelter of Lord Nityānanda, who is the greatest devotee of Lord Caitanya, who develops or cultivates the consciousness of tṛṇād api sunīcena, and who always hears the glories of Kṛṣṇa, will establish his relationship with Lord Caitanya.

After instructing Jīva Gosvāmī, Lord Nityānanda told him, “Now you have the right to go to Vṛndāvana.” Yathā yathā gaura padāravinde (Caitanya-candrāmṛta, 88)—to the degree that one renders service to Lord Caitanya, he becomes qualified to understand Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes in Vṛndāvana.

Thus, Lord Nityānanda does the cleaning and the preparation work to make one qualified to establish his relationship with Lord Caitanya. Even the offenders were delivered by the mercy of Lord Nityānanda. Sometimes Lord Caitanya will not accept certain individuals, such as offenders. Lord Nityānanda, however, has no discrimination. He is so merciful that even the offenders can be delivered.

When Lord Nityānanda petitions Lord Caitanya, “Please, bestow Your mercy upon them,” Lord Caitanya cannot refuse when He sees Nityānanda begging with tears in His eyes, saying, “You have come to deliver the most fallen. Look at these two, Jagāi and Mādhāi. Certainly they are qualified for Your mercy.” Such was Lord Nityānanda’s mercy.

Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura describes in his Godruma Kalpataru and Dālālera-gīta that Lord Nityānanda is distributing the holy name of the Lord in the marketplace of the holy name. Simply for the price of one’s faith, one can purchase that pure holy name and establish his relationship with Lord Caitanya. Even for those who have no faith, Lord Nityānanda is so merciful that by His method of distribution, He awakens that faith in Gaurāṅga. With tears in His eyes, He falls on the ground begging, “Please, simply take this name.” He is not asking for anything else.

Lord Nityānanda then cleans away all the material desires within the heart. As long as there is pride and one does not feel himself to be lower than the straw on the street, unable to offer respects to everyone and unable to give up the foolish poison of wanting respect for oneself, he can never have a relationship (sambandha), and can therefore never understand Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana.

## Becoming Recognized as a Servant of the Lord

We should understand that we should have the aspiration within our hearts to become servants of Lord Caitanya. If we want to become His fully dedicated and recognized servants, then our hearts have to be cleaned. It is not a cheap expression to be recognized as a servant of Lord Caitanya; it is such an exalted position. It is so exalted that for most of us it is inconceivable, but we should at least aspire for it. Therefore, Lord Caitanya has very kindly appeared, and not alone, but with His associates, including His most confidential associate, Lord Nityānanda. Together They have appeared to dissipate the darkness of the ignorance of Kali-yuga.

By the mercy of Lord Caitanya’s devotees—Lord Nityānanda and His other associates—we can gain access to His service. To be recognized, the Lord has to give His attention.

Similarly, Lord Brahmā prayed to Lord Kṛṣṇa (Bhāg. 10.14.30): “My dear Lord, I therefore pray to be so fortunate that in this life as Lord Brahmā or in another life, wherever I take my birth, I may be counted as one of Your devotees. I pray that wherever I may be, even among the animal species, I can engage in devotional service to Your lotus feet.”

One person who always wanted to be recognized as a servant of Lord Caitanya was Advaita Ācārya.
