On the other hand, a nondevotee, though fully engaged in occupational duties, does not gain anything.” (Bhāg. 1.5.17)

“My dear Vyāsa, even though a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa sometimes falls down somehow or other, he certainly does not undergo material existence like others \[fruitive workers, etc.\] because a person who has once relished the taste of the lotus feet of the Lord can do nothing but remember that ecstasy again and again.” (Bhāg. 1.5.19)

Tasting the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet is the beginning of devotional service:

What is the value of a prolonged life which is wasted, inexperienced by years in this world? Better a moment of full consciousness, because that gives one a start in searching after his supreme interest. (Bhāg. 2.1.12)

One moment of full consciousness is far superior to living a long life devoid of knowledge of the Supreme. Everybody is struggling to live a long and happy life, but he who is struggling to get that one moment of full consciousness is a rare soul.

In the Mahābhārata, there is a story of the Pāṇḍavas, the five sons of Mahārāja Pāṇḍu, who were exiled to the forest. While in the forest one day, they all felt very thirsty. Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja told Nakula to go and find some water. Nakula went off and found a very beautiful, pristine lake, and realized that he could quench the thirst of all his brothers by taking some water from this lake and bringing it to them. As he was about to take some water from the lake, there was a voice from the sky that said, “Stop! That lake belongs to me. Don’t take the water. If you drink that water, you will immediately die.”

Nakula did not pay any attention to the voice from the sky and said, “No, I will take this water anyway.” He drank some water, and immediately died.

Because Nakula did not return, Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja turned to Sahadeva and said, “Go look for Nakula. Something must have happened.”

Sahadeva went and found this beautiful lake, and saw Nakula lying there on the ground. He also ended up being warned by the voice in the sky not to drink the water, but he did anyway and fell down on the ground.

Arjuna was then sent to find the two brothers. He saw his brothers lying on the ground, and then heard the voice in the sky say, “Your two brothers have died because they did not listen to me.” Arjuna was wondering who was speaking. Arjuna was a very powerful warrior and was thinking that he would immediately defeat this voice in the sky and avenge him for the death of his two brothers. He started firing weapons, but to no avail. He was not able to defeat the opponent.

After engaging in battle, he was thirsty and wanted to take some water from the lake. Again, the voice said, “That lake belongs to me. Don’t drink that water; otherwise you will follow the same path as your brothers.” Arjuna took the water anyway and died.

Then Yudhiṣṭhira and Bhīma were left. Yudhiṣṭhira told Bhīma, “Go find out what has happened to your three brothers. Bhīma went and saw this beautiful lake and his three brothers lying on the ground. By that time, he was so thirsty and he took some water.

He was also warned, “Don’t drink that water, or you will meet the same result.” Bhīma still took the water and fell down.

Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja was waiting, but none of his brothers returned. He therefore went to look for them, and came to the lake. The same voice came from the sky, “Your brothers have met their death because they did not listen to me. Do not take this water. It belongs to me.”

Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja responded, “All of my brothers are very powerful mahārathīs. They have the strength to defeat tens of thousands of warriors at once. It is not possible for them to have been killed or defeated by any ordinary person.” He then realized that the voice in the sky must be none other than Yamarāja, the Lord of death. Indeed it was Yamarāja.

Yamarāja said, “If you answer these questions for me, then I will give you a benediction. The first question he asked was, “What is the most amazing thing in the world?”

Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja’s answer was:

*ahany ahani bhūtāni*  
*gacchantīha yamālayam*  
*śeṣāḥ sthāvaram icchanti*  
*kim āścaryam ataḥ param*

**“Every day millions of living entities go to the kingdom of death. Still, those who are remaining aspire for a permanent situation here. What could be more wonderful than this?” (Mahābhārata, Vana-pārva, 313.116)**

Yamarāja was very pleased by his answer. He began asking him many other philosophical questions, to which Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja gave perfect answers. Then Yamarāja said, “Alright, I am satisfied by your answers and I want to give you a benediction. I will bring to life one of your brothers. Which one do you want?”

Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja said, “I ask for the benediction that you bring to life my brother Nakula.” Yamarāja was very curious to know why Nakula, because Arjuna and Bhīma were actually the sons of his mother, Kuntī, whereas Nakula and Sahadeva had taken birth from a different mother, Mādrī. Thus Yamarāja thought that Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja would have asked for one of his maternal brothers to be revived.

Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja’s said, “No, all my brothers are equal to me. Please bring to life my brother Nakula.”

Yamarāja was so pleased by Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja’s behavior that he said, “Because I am so impressed by your way of thinking, I will bring to life all of your brothers.” Yamarāja had actually appeared there simply to test Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja, and Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja displayed his integrity and qualification to be emperor of the whole world.

Thus Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja’s realization of the most amazing thing in the world was that every day we see so many living entities being sent to the kingdom of death—whether it is family, friends, society, insects, reptiles, animals, etc., they all have the same destination—yet those who remain here think that they will not have the same destination. However, Prabhupāda dispelled this illusion that there is shelter in the material world.

*dehāpatya-kalatrādiṣv*  
*ātma-sainyeṣv asatsv api*  
*teṣāṁ pramatto nidhanaṁ*  
*paśyann api na paśyati*

**Persons devoid of ātma-tattva do not inquire into the problems of life, being too attached to the fallible soldiers like the body, children and wife. Although sufficiently experienced, they still do not see their inevitable destruction. (Bhāg. 2.1.4)**

PURPORT

This material world is called the world of death. Every living being, beginning from Brahma, whose duration of life is some thousands of millions of years, down to the germs who live for a few seconds only, is struggling for existence. Therefore, this life is a sort of fight with material nature, which imposes death upon all. In the human form of life, a living being is competent enough to come to an understanding of this great struggle for existence, but being too attached to family members, society, country, etc., he wants to win over the invincible material nature by the aid of bodily strength, children, wife, relatives, etc. Although he is sufficiently experienced in the matter by dint of past experience and previous examples of his deceased predecessors, he does not see that the so-called fighting soldiers like the children, relatives, society members and countrymen are all fallible in the great struggle. One should examine the fact that his father or his father’s father has already died, and that he himself is therefore also sure to die, and similarly, his children, who are the would-be fathers of their children, will also die in due course. No one will survive in this struggle with material nature. The history of human society definitely proves it, yet the foolish people still suggest that in the future they will be able to live perpetually, with the help of material science. This poor fund of knowledge exhibited by human society is certainly misleading, and it is all due to ignoring the constitution of the living soul. This material world exists only as a dream, due to our attachment to it. Otherwise, the living soul is always different from the material nature. The great ocean of material nature is tossing with the waves of time, and the so-called living conditions are something like foaming bubbles, which appear before us as bodily self, wife, children, society, countrymen, etc. Due to a lack of knowledge of self, we become victimized by the force of ignorance and thus spoil the valuable energy of human life in a vain search after permanent living conditions, which are impossible in this material world.

Our friends, relatives and so-called wives and children are not only fallible, but also bewildered by the outward glamour of material existence. As such, they cannot save us. Still we think that we are safe within the orbit of family, society or country. The whole materialistic advancement of human civilization is like the decoration of a dead body. Everyone is a dead body flapping only for a few days, and yet all the energy of human life is being wasted in the decoration of this dead body. Śukadeva Gosvāmī is pointing out the duty of the human being after showing the actual position of bewildered human activities. Persons who are devoid of the knowledge of ātma-tattva are misguided, but those who are devotees of the Lord and have perfect realization of transcendental knowledge are not bewildered.

Ātma-tattva means knowledge of the self. People devoid of ātma-tattva do not inquire how to solve the real problems of life. They are not capable of making such inquiries, because they are too attached.

This verse refers to fallible soldiers. We usually think of soldiers as those who will give us protection. However, although they may fight on our behalf, they are all fallible in the great struggle against material nature. Therefore, they cannot actually give protection. Even though such persons, who are devoid of ātma-tattva, are sufficiently experienced, somehow they still do not see their inevitable destruction.

Prabhupāda said that this material world exists only as a dream, due to our attachment to it. We need to give up our identification with ātma-māyā and begin our identification with ātma-tattva. Of course, identification with ātma-tattva, even upon beginning, requires a continual process before full realization has taken place. Attachments are not easy to give up. Due to our attachments to this material world, it exists only as a dream. The Bhāgavatam states that every learned person knows that attachment to the material world is the cause of bondage for the living entity. When that same attachment is applied to the association of self-realized devotees, then mokṣa-dvāram apāvṛtam—the gate to liberation is opened.

It is one thing to have the gate open, but one has to actually enter through it. The more we are attached to this material world, the more we identify with it. However, the soul is different from the body. To the degree we identify with the body and perform activities in relationship to the body, to that degree we become increasingly absorbed in the body.

Similarly, no matter how fancy a car may be, it needs some maintenance—to be cleaned, oil changed, etc. Sometimes it gets scratched and then you want to paint it and fix the scratch. Gradually, different parts need to be replaced. People think, “That’s my car. If I don’t maintain it and take care of it, then so many things are going to start happening to it.” Thus, the more energy you invest in that car, the more attached you will become, and the more you will identify with it.

Prabhupāda gives the example of the soul and the Supersoul: A person has a car and is driving down the road. He picks up a stranger who needs a ride. The person is driving along, and all of a sudden somebody hits the side of the car. The driver immediately looks at his car, and his heart falls into his stomach. He begins to think about all the money he spent on the car and all the maintenance that he had put into it: “How am I going to get to work tomorrow? How much is it going to cost to repair it? How am I going to pick up my wife? How long am I going to be without the car?” All these thoughts start racing through his mind, but the passenger he picked up opens the door, gets out, and walks away. He doesn’t identify with the car. There is no absorption and he is not attached. However, the driver is attached because of all the absorption he has put into the car and because of his identification with the car.

Similarly the soul, who is the knower of the field of activities of this body, identifies with this body. However, the process is to become free from attachment so that we no longer identify with the body and the fallible soldiers. Attachments are not things that we can immediately give up. Even death is not the means for becoming freed from attachments, because the living entity carries his different conceptions of life from one body to the next, just as the air carries aromas from one place to the next.

Sometimes people foolishly think, “I’m suffering so much. I have to become free from the suffering. Let me take my own life so that I can end the suffering!” However, they do not know the stringent laws of nature. They do not know how the soul is eternal, and how the attachment that the soul has at the time of death carries him to his next body.

Therefore, becoming free from attachments is a gradual process. We have to decrease the degree of absorption that we put in connection with this body and increase the absorption in those activities that will free us from identification with this body.

*prasaṅgam ajaraṁ pāśam*  
*ātmanaḥ kavayo viduḥ*  
*sa eva sādhuṣu kṛto*  
*mokṣa-dvāram apāvṛtam*

**Every learned man knows very well that attachment for the material is the greatest entanglement of the spirit soul. But that same attachment, when applied to the self-realized devotees, opens the door of liberation. (Bhāg. 3.25.20)**

*vāsudeve bhagavati*  
*bhakti-yogaḥ prayojitaḥ*  
*janayaty āśu vairāgyaṁ*  
*jñānaṁ ca yad ahaitukam*

**By rendering devotional service unto the Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, one immediately acquires causeless knowledge and detachment from the world. (Bhāg. 1.2.7)**

This Kṛṣṇa consciousness is meant to awaken our real attachment. Every one of us wants to be attached to something. It is the very symptom of life. Sometimes people think that becoming free from attachments means rejecting everything, and they try to do so by renouncing their connections in this world. However, that is false renunciation. Real renunciation is to see everything connected to Kṛṣṇa.

Prabhupāda used to give the example of the Phālgu River. This river flows below the surface and you cannot see it. Although it is not visible, it is continuously flowing. It is said that if you put your hand deep into the sand, you will feel that the water is flowing. Similarly, if you put your hand on the heart of false renunciates, you will feel so many desires flowing even though they may not appear on the surface. This is because it is the nature of life to have desires. Nobody can give up desires. False renunciates are people who renounce this world saying that it is false. Such people try to give up all their attachments, but they do not know that it is the nature of life to be attached to something. They are therefore called phalgu-vairāgis, false renunciates—giving up everything in this world but not actually knowing that their hearts are still filled with attachments and desires.

*kṛṣṇa-bhakta—niṣkāma, ataeva ‘śānta’*  
*bhukti-mukti-siddhi-kāmī—sakali ‘aśānta’*

**Because a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa is desireless, he is peaceful. Fruitive workers desire material enjoyment, jñānīs desire liberation, and yogīs desire material opulence; therefore they are all lusty and cannot be peaceful. (Cc. Madhya 19.149)**

Even though it was just stated that everyone has desires, a devotee is desireless, or niṣkāma, because the devotee is one who has transformed his desire to please the Lord. He has transformed his absorption. The more he absorbs his consciousness in hearing about the activities and pastimes of the Supreme Lord, the more he becomes absorbed in that consciousness.

*anta-kāle ca mām eva*  
*smaran muktvā kalevaram*  
*yaḥ prayāti sa mad-bhāvaṁ*  
*yāti nāsty atra saṁśayaḥ*

**“And whoever, at the end of his life, quits his body, remembering Me alone, at once attains My nature. Of this there is no doubt.” (Bg. 8.5)**

To the degree we practice the absorption in spiritual activities, to that degree we can become detached from all the activities that are connected to the body. However, if everything we do is just a desire to fulfill the demands of the body and the mind, then we will become more absorbed in this body.

Devotional service is the cultivation of consciousness that simultaneously awakens a genuine attachment. The material world exists only as a dream due to our attachment to it, but it is a temporary manifestation that has no connection with reality. We identify with it and think it is real when it is happening. But when we wake up, we see it was only a dream. Human life is meant for us to wake up. We should take advantage of the intelligence and everything that has been given to us in this human form of life so that we can wake up. We should use whatever time we have left in these temporary material bodies for cultivating Kṛṣṇa consciousness. This is ātma-tattva—the actual purpose of the human form of life. Our nature is to be attached to something, and to the degree we realize that attachment means to become attached to Kṛṣṇa, we can be fearless at the time of death. For a devotee, death is simply the threshold to the spiritual world.

Our life should be utilized for the cultivation of this consciousness and to increase our attachment to hearing about transcendence, which will automatically decrease our attachment to this temporary physical world.

Caitanya-bhāgavata describes a pastime of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura who was a great devotee of Lord Caitanya. Every night he would have kīrtana in his house with the Lord and His associates. One night during the kīrtana, his son left his body, but the kīrtana was continuing. Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura could see that some of his relatives were becoming very disturbed because his son had departed from this world. Lord Caitanya was feeling so much ecstasy in the kīrtana that Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura did not want Lord Caitanya to see everybody feeling despondent about the departure of his son. He therefore went into the other room and quickly told all his family members not to experience this lamentation in their hearts in the presence of the Lord: “If the Lord senses your lamentation, it will break His ecstasy. We should think only of the pleasure of the Lord.” Thus the kīrtana continued. Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura simply continued to chant and dance even though his son had departed. It continued for another seven hours, and no one spoke about the passing of Śrīvāsa’s son. They tried not to manifest any despondency in their hearts.

Gradually Lord Caitanya realized that there was some despondency present. He inquired, “What is everyone despondent about?”

The devotees responded, “It’s because just some hours ago, the son of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura departed from this world.”

Lord Caitanya said, “Oh really? Where is he?”

They went into the other room where his son’s body was lying, and Lord Caitanya spoke to the departed son and asked, “Why did you leave?”

This living entity appeared back in the body and began speaking the science of transcendence—how he is an eternal soul who has a journey to continue upon: “I have temporarily appeared in this world as the son of my father and mother. But now it is time for me to leave and go on to my next destination.”

As all of the family members were hearing Śrīvāsa’s son speaking in this way, all their grief was dispelled from their hearts by this transcendental knowledge. The son folded his hands and said to the Lord, “My dear Lord, please let me go to my next destination now. Please forgive me for any offenses that I may have committed and let me depart.” He then left his body, and the grief that all the family members were experiencing was dispelled having heard this transcendental wisdom from the mouth of this soul.

Lord Caitanya then said to Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, “Śrīvāsa, how can I ever give up the association of somebody who does not even know grief for the death of his own son? You were only thinking about My pleasure and therefore you did not even know grief for the loss of your son. From this day on, I and Nityānanda will become your sons.” Such is the nature of devotional service. Such a devotee becomes very dear to the Lord. When we become absorbed in the Lord, and understand how merciful and compassionate He is to all living entities, it will gradually eradicate all the unwanted attachments to everything within this world, and it will open up the gate to the spiritual world.

**Question: How long will it take to purify our heart, and what are the contributing factors to make it happen faster?**

It is based upon our desire. Man proposes and God disposes. Everyone has to develop greed for Kṛṣṇa. In the Caitanya-caritāmṛta, in the conversation between Rāmānanda Rāya and Lord Caitanya, it is described that pure devotional service cannot be had by millions of births of pious activities. Pure devotional service can be had only by those who have the greed to attain it. Therefore, whenever one sees it, he should immediately purchase it without delay. Millions of births of pious activities will not bring us to that state of pure devotional service. To the degree that we develop greed to obtain it, that will hasten the process. We have to become greedy to serve and please Kṛṣṇa. If we do not have that greed, then wherever we see it, we should immediately purchase it.

When you want to buy something, you have to give something in return. Therefore, if you want to buy pure devotional service, you have to purchase it with your faith. To the degree that you place your faith, to that degree you will get some return for it. Advancement in devotional service is simply advancement to the degree of our faith, and that faith will be tested along the way.

**Question: There is a verse in the Third Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam that says that as soon as topics of Kṛṣṇa enter into our ears, immediately our attachment to family, which is otherwise so difficult to reject, is destroyed. How is this?**

It means that the seed is planted immediately. At the beginning, the seed is being planted in the heart. It is not immediately that all the attachments go away. It also refers to when one genuinely hears.

*nitya-siddha kṛṣṇa-prema ‘sādhya’ kabhu naya*  
*śravaṇādi-śuddha-citte karaye udaya*

**Pure love for Kṛṣṇa is eternally established in the hearts of the living entities. It is not something to be gained from another source. When the heart is purified by hearing and chanting, this love naturally awakens. (Cc. Madhya 22.107)**

When one hears from the right source, it immediately awakens the desire for Kṛṣṇa, and the seed for devotional service is planted in the heart, although, it may simply be lying dormant in the heart. Prabhupāda gives the example that although the potential for fire already exists in the wood, it has to be drawn out of the wood by a catalyst. In the same way, when we hear about Kṛṣṇa from the right source, it awakens our desire for Kṛṣṇa that is lying dormant in the heart. In other words, the seed has been planted within our heart. However, it needs to be nourished and watered.

Lord Caitanya explained to Rūpa Gosvāmī:

*brahmāṇḍa bhramite kona bhāgyavān jīva*  
*guru-kṛṣṇa-prasāde pāya bhakti-latā-bīja*

**According to their karma, all living entities are wandering throughout the entire universe. Some of them are being elevated to the upper planetary systems, and some are going down into the lower planetary systems. Out of many millions of wandering living entities, one who is very fortunate gets an opportunity to associate with a bona fide spiritual master by the grace of Kṛṣṇa. By the mercy of both Kṛṣṇa and the spiritual master, such a person receives the seed of the creeper of devotional service. (Cc. Madhya 19.151)**

Prabhupāda explains that there are many different types of bījas, or seeds. There is karma-bīja, jñāna-bīja, and all different types of mixtures of seeds. But when the bhakti-latā-bīja is planted within the heart, one should continue to water it. That bhakti-latā-bīja has to come from somebody who has bhakti in his heart. Once the seed is planted, and if one continues to water it, then everything else in this world is finished. That contact with Kṛṣṇa is so superior to the contact of anything else in this world, and the soul who has made that contact will never forget. Even though he may go on struggling externally, appearing to still be so attached to material desires, they will never satisfy him as much as that little seed that was planted in the heart. It is simply separated by time.

**Question: As we progress in spiritual life, what difficulties will we face, and how can we overcome them?**

The existence of anarthas within our heart is our cause of difficulty. Prabhupāda says that the process of devotional service is the process of purification. When we are becoming purified, the anarthas are gradually coming to the surface, and they become increasingly noticeable. Such anarthas are the desire for prestige; jīva-hiṁsa—which is envy and enmity for living entities; niṣiddhācāra—unacceptable behavior for those trying to attain perfection; kuṭīnāṭī—diplomacy; lābha—mundane profiteering; pūjā—adoration achieved by satisfying mundane people; and pratiṣṭha-ādi—becoming an important man in material calculations. These anarthas need to be cleaned out. This process is demonstrated in the pastime of the cleansing of the Guṇḍicā temple.

In the beginning, we can give up some of our external attachments, which are like big pieces of dirt. However, if we are not careful to go back in and clean out all the finer particles of dust, we will have a lot of problems in our spiritual life. Therefore, the recommended process is to clean the anarthas from the heart. At every stage of devotional service, chanting of the holy name of the Lord is the recommended process for cleaning. In the beginning, the Lord will overlook our offenses, but as we progress and learn a few more things, then we are held accountable for those offenses. If we are not careful about that, then those offenses will drag us down and cause us to lose our taste and determination. When one makes a little advancement in spiritual life, he has to come to the realization that it is time to clean out all the finer dust particles that will drag us down.

Tattva-vibhrama is a type of anartha, which means ignorance of the obstacles that prevent us from making advancement in devotional service. We should not stay in ignorance. We should know what the obstacles are.

If a person is driving on a very dangerous road, usually he will see signs posted, warning of any dangers on the road—such as “Dangerous curve ahead.” However, if the driver is not attentive and does not look at the signs, then he may drive right off the mountain. Thus, when we advance in spiritual life, we have to be careful about the important signs that the ācāryas have left for us: “Dangerous curve ahead! Slow down! Be more attentive! Don’t fall asleep at the wheel!” All the warnings are there, and if we do not listen to them, thinking, “I am a devotee and I can just go on chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa,” then we will miss the curve and drive off the mountain! Being aware of the obstacles, we should learn how to apply the proper instructions that are given to avoid those obstacles and dangers. One of the great dangers for a devotee is inattentive chanting.

## Nourishing the Seed of Devotion

Now Kuntīdevī says, “My dear Kṛṣṇa, if You think that we are well established now that we have our kingdom back, and if You therefore want to leave us, that is not a very good proposal. We are not free yet. Because we have killed so many kings, all their friends and relatives are planning to come fight with us again. So don’t think that we are free from all dangers. We are not. And we have no protection other than Your lotus feet. That is our position.” Thus she indirectly says to Kṛṣṇa, “Do not leave us. Don’t think that we are now safe. Without Your protection, we are always unsafe.”

This should be the position of a devotee. We should know that we are actually in danger in this material world. Māyā, illusion, may catch us at any time, as soon as we are a little inattentive, thinking, “Now I have done my duty. Let me take a little rest.” No, there is no rest. We must be always alert.

There is a verse in which Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī says, avyartha-kālatvam: \[Cc. Madhya 23.18-19\] a devotee should be very much careful to see whether his time is being spent unnecessarily. He should ask himself, “Am I now engaged in māyā’s service or Kṛṣṇa’s service?” This is a symptom of an advanced devotee. Nāma-gāne sadā ruciḥ: such a devotee is never tired of chanting, singing, or dancing. The word sadā means “always,” and ruci means “taste.” A devotee always has a taste for chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa: “Oh, very nice. Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare/ Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare.” This is taste. Of course, this taste takes time to awaken, but when Rūpa Gosvāmī was chanting he was thinking, “I have only one tongue and two ears. What can I appreciate of chanting? If I could have millions of tongues and trillions of ears, then I could relish something by chanting and hearing.” Of course, we should not imitate him, but the devotees of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement must at least be very careful to complete their sixteen rounds, their minimum amount of prescribed chanting. Nāma-gāne sadā ruciḥ: we have to increase our taste for singing and chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa.

Furthermore, we should also increase our inclination to live in a place where Kṛṣṇa lives (prītis tad-vasati-sthale). In the vision of higher devotees, Kṛṣṇa actually lives everywhere, but because we are in a lower condition, we should know that for us Kṛṣṇa lives in the temple. Because we do not see Kṛṣṇa everywhere, we should come to the temple to see Kṛṣṇa, who kindly appears there, by His mercy, in a manner in which we can see Him. (Teachings of Queen Kuntī, Chapter 20)

In this section of Teachings of Queen Kuntī, Kuntīdevī is saying, “We have no protection other than Your lotus feet. Without Your protection we are always unsafe.” This should be the position of a devotee. We should know that we are actually in danger in this material world because māyā can catch us at any time if we are a little inattentive. Prabhupāda says that we should be careful not to think that now we have finished our duty, so now we can rest from our duties. There is no rest, because Māyā does not rest, being always fully engaged in Kṛṣṇa’s service. As we make further advancement, Māyā will be there to give us more difficult tests to pass.

In Caitanya-caritāmṛta there is a story of the cleansing of the Guṇḍicā temple. When Lord Caitanya and His associates were cleaning the Guṇḍicā temple, they were sweeping and cleaning all the dirt that had been accumulated inside. Lord Caitanya gave everybody brooms for sweeping. With His broom, Lord Caitanya collected so much dirt and made a huge pile outside the Guṇḍicā temple. His pile of dirt surpassed all the dirt collected by all the other devotees. After fully cleaning the temple, He told everybody, “Now let’s go in one more time, and this time we should collect all the finer particles of dust that we could not collect the first time.”

Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura describes that Lord Caitanya was teaching us by His example how to clean our hearts. While cleaning the hearts, there will be finer and more subtle attachments that need to be cleaned out. These more subtle attachments are not so easily perceivable when one first begins the process of bhakti, because we are coming from a very gross platform in the material world, being absorbed completely in a materialistic way of life. However, as one begins the process of bhakti, he begins to perceive that there are more subtle attachments that need to be cleaned out of the heart.

Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura describes these more subtle attachments to be the anarthas that are within the heart, such as: kuṭināṭī, which is faultfinding or duplicity; jīva-hiṁsā, envy of other living beings; pratiṣṭhā, the desire for respect; pūjā, the desire for worship; and niṣiddhācāra, neglecting of the injunctions of the scriptures. These subtle attachments that are within the heart also need to be cleaned. Bhaktisiddhānta compares these to the finer particles of dust that Lord Caitanya went in the second time to clean out of the Guṇḍicā temple. Lord Caitanya was cleaning the Guṇḍicā temple because He wanted to make a very nice place for Lord Jagannātha to sit, as He was going to stay there for some time.

Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta says that we must similarly make our hearts a very nice place for the Lord to sit. Although the Lord is situated within everyone’s heart, the Lord is very much inclined towards a clean heart.

*śṛṇvatāṁ sva-kathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ*  
*puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ*  
*hṛdy antaḥ stho hy abhadrāṇi*  
*vidhunoti suhṛt satām*

**Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, who is the Paramātmā \[Supersoul\] in everyone’s heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who has developed the urge to hear His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted. (Bhāg. 1.2.17)**

If we try to clean our hearts ourselves, it will be a very difficult task. However, the Lord who is within the heart is inclined to help. He will do the cleaning if we express our desire for it to be cleaned. He knows our desire even better than we know it. Just as a person can understand the fragrance of the flower by being near the flower, in the same way, the Lord, who is the Supersoul within the heart of all living beings and the closest to us, understands our desires.

Ceto-darpaṇa-mārjanaṁ bhava-mahā-dāvāgni-nirvāpaṇaṁ. Ceta is the heart, darpaṇa is the mirror, and mārjanaṁ means cleaning. Thus Lord Caitanya says that the saṅkīrtana movement cleanses the heart of all the dust accumulated for years together. The dust is made of deeply rooted impressions that have been accumulating for so many births.

Kṛṣṇa explains in Bhagavad-gītā: “The living entity carries these different conceptions of life from one birth to the next just as the air carries aromas from one place to the next.” Thus these impressions are carried from one birth to the next. They are called bīja, the seeds of material desires. These seeds of material desires force the living entity to commit sinful activities, which then further manifest and are called prārabdha and aprārabdha-karma. Prārabdha-karma means that which is already manifested. Aprārabdha-karma is that karma which is lying as a seed waiting to manifest at some future time. These are accumulated within the heart, and will have to manifest. Aprārabdha-karma is also the desire to again commit the sinful activity. Even though one may suffer, since the sinful desires seed has not been uprooted within the heart, the living entity therefore commits sinful activity and then further implicates himself with prārabdha and aprārabdha-karma. This goes on birth after birth after birth.

*kecit kevalayā bhaktyā*  
*vāsudeva-parāyaṇāḥ*  
*aghaṁ dhunvanti kārtsnyena*  
*nīhāram iva bhāskaraḥ*

**Only a rare person who has adopted complete, unalloyed devotional service to Kṛṣṇa can uproot the weeds of sinful actions with no possibility that they will revive. He can do this simply by discharging devotional service, just as the sun can immediately dissipate fog by its rays. (Bhāg. 6.1.15)**

Śrīla Prabhupāda gives the example that we may try to get rid of weeds in the ground by turning over the soil. It then appears that there are no weeds, but the seeds are still in the ground and will come up again. If we want to get rid of weeds, we cannot simply turn over the soil. The intelligent person knows better. Similarly, Kṛṣṇa says that one who withdraws his senses from the sense objects, but whose mind dwells upon those sense objects within, deludes himself and is called a pretender. On the other hand, it is far superior to engage the active senses in works of devotion, because then the senses become spiritualized. The seeds of sinful desires then become destroyed at the root.

One has to burn the seeds of sinful desires, as the fried seed will not fructify. This can be done by discharging devotional service, just as the sun dissipates fog by its rays. Although there are many seeds of sinful desires still lying within the core of the heart, Kṛṣṇa states in the Bhagavad-gītā, “Out of compassion for them, I who am dwelling within their hearts destroy with the shining lamp of knowledge the darkness born of ignorance.”

Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī explains in Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu that the root cause of all sinful activities is ignorance. The first characteristic of ignorance is to accept that which is temporary to be eternal; to accept that which is impure to be pure; and to accept that which is not this body to be the body. The second characteristic of ignorance is to accept the objects of the senses as real. The third symptom of ignorance is called rāga or attachment, and is to be attached to happiness and to be averse to distress. The fourth symptom of ignorance is dveṣa, which means hatred towards suffering and anything that we see as the cause of our suffering. The fifth form of ignorance is called abhiniveśa, which means to instinctively cling to the idea that we can enjoy with this body, and the fear that death means no more enjoyment.

However, Kṛṣṇa will destroy with the shining lamp of knowledge the darkness which is born of ignorance. He cleans the heart of those who develop the urge to hear about Him and to chant about Him. When a devotee awakens his faith in hearing about Kṛṣṇa and chanting about Kṛṣṇa, then it is the beginning of bhakti.

## Faith in Devotional Service

Śraddhā is what gives the eligibility for pure devotional service.

*śṛṇvatāṁ sva-kathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ*  
*puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ*  
*hṛdy antaḥ stho hy abhadrāṇi*  
*vidhunoti suhṛt satām*

**Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, who is the Paramātmā \[Supersoul\] in everyone’s heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who has developed the urge to hear His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted. (Bhāg. 1.2.17)**

The devotee has faith that if he simply goes on hearing about Kṛṣṇa and chanting Kṛṣṇa’s glories, then all the residual desires within his heart will gradually become cleansed and purified. Whenever he sees that he has committed some sense gratification, he voluntarily suffers by his repentance.

*tat te ’nukampāṁ su-samīkṣamāṇo*  
*bhuñjāna evātma-kṛtaṁ vipākam*  
*hṛd-vāg-vapurbhir vidadhan namas te*  
*jīveta yo mukti-pade sa dāya-bhāk*

(Bhāg. 10.14.8)

One who seeks compassion and thus tolerates all kinds of adverse conditions due to the karma of his past misdeeds and who always goes on glorifying the Supreme Personality of Godhead, engaging his body, mind and words in devotional service, he certainly becomes a bona fide candidate for liberation. Mukti-pade sa dāya-bhāk—he gets his rightful inheritance. Simply by living, he will get the inheritance. In the same way, a devotee goes on with faith and simply wants to satisfy the Supreme Lord by strictly following the instructions of the spiritual master and continuing the process of hearing and chanting. Kṛṣṇa says, “Simply remain faithful and you will be happy.”

The devotee remains happy, because he voluntarily suffers by his repentance, and he knows that for Kṛṣṇa, who is very merciful to the devotee by His kṛpā-śakti, His heart will melt. Seeing that the devotee wants to please Him, the Lord will remove all obstacles.

*ananyāś cintayanto māṁ*  
*ye janāḥ paryupāsate*  
*teṣāṁ nityābhiyuktānāṁ*  
*yoga-kṣemaṁ vahāmy aham*

**“Those who always worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on My transcendental form—to them I carry what they lack, and I preserve what they have.” (Bg. 9.22)**

That endeavor to go on hearing and chanting the glories of the Lord in the association of devotees of the Lord is very pleasing to the Lord. That type of faith is required. That faith is bhakta-niṣṭhā, and is what actually allows the Lord to become bound by the love of His devotee.

Rūpa Gosvāmī explains in Nectar of Devotion:

*bhukti-mukti-spṛhā yāvat*  
*piśācī hṛdi vartate*  
*tāvad bhakti-sukhasyātra*  
*katham abhyudayo bhavet*

(Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu 1.2.22)

**“The material desire to enjoy the material world and the desire to become liberated from material bondage are considered to be two witches, and they haunt one like ghosts. As long as these witches remain within the heart, how can one feel transcendental bliss? As long as these two witches remain in the heart, there is no possibility of enjoying the transcendental bliss of devotional service.”**

When śraddhā takes birth in the heart of the living entity, it means the awakening of faith in the holy name and in hearing Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. Once a devotee has awakened his faith in this, he no longer has faith in anything else that he has to do in relationship to the body in this life. He knows those things cannot make him happy. He simply does whatever is necessary as a matter of duty, but his real attraction and his real faith is in hearing about Kṛṣṇa, because that is what cleans the heart. Kṛṣṇa cleans the heart and allows us go on hearing about Him in the association of devotees.

However, Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains in Śrī Bhaktyāloka that the firm faith in the goal is lost when one keeps bad association. To the degree that one associates with material desires and materialistic persons, his firm faith in the goal diminishes. Although faith can be awakened by the association with devotees, if one is not careful to protect that faith, it can be lost in the association of materialistic persons and materialistic desires. There are different types of saṅga.

Lord Caitanya says (Cc. Madhya 22.87): asat-saṅga-tyāga, ei vaiṣṇava-ācāra, ‘strī-saṅgī’—eka asādhu, ‘kṛṣṇābhakta’ āra. A devotee has to renounce the association of asat (that which is temporary). He has to renounce the association of materialistic persons—those who are attached to associating with the opposite sex. Prabhupāda explains that a devotee has to protect himself by building a fence, always keeping himself in the association of devotees.

Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says that there are different types of saṅga. He quotes the verse saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ (Bg. 2.62), and says another type of saṅga is when a person contemplates the objects of the senses. When he contemplates the objects of the senses, then attachment, lust, anger, delusion, and bewilderment of memory arise. Then intelligence is lost, and one falls into the material pool.

One type of saṅga is the association of materialistic persons, and the other type of saṅga is constant association with lusty desires. Both types of saṅga cause our faith in the supreme goal to be diminished. Therefore, one who has fragile faith has to associate with those who increase his faith. Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura therefore compares that faith to be like a newborn baby girl, which one has to protect. The guardians of devotional service protect that faith, just as the mother protects her child from dangerous creatures, or from extreme heat and cold. She also nourishes her child, giving the child strength. The more strength the child gets, the more the child will remain unaffected by the dangerous elements.

Thus the guardians of devotion help us by protecting us from kāma and jñāna, by pointing out what the anarthas are within our heart and by giving us the nourishment and spiritual strength. We cannot defeat these anarthas by our own strength. We need to get nourishment and strength by the association of those who have it. Nāyam ātmā bala-hīnena labhyo, na ca pramādāt tapaso vāpy aliṅgāt (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 3.2.4)—the Supreme Lord cannot be attained by those who have no spiritual strength, by those who are wild and careless (wild means they have no sense control), and by those whose austerities are inappropriate. The Supreme Lord reveals Himself to those who always strive to achieve Him by the right means. Such persons enter into the spiritual world. We cannot defeat lusty desires by our strength alone. We need to get strength from those who have it. By associating with those who have strength, it gives us strength and increases our faith. It gives us faith in the goal, and it gives us the strength to overcome all of these anarthas that are within the heart. We actually have to awaken the taste for hearing and chanting about Kṛṣṇa. Once we do, because of faith, then that taste will help us to make further advancement.

*viṣayā vinivartante*  
*nirāhārasya dehinaḥ*  
*rasa-varjaṁ raso ‘py asya*  
*paraṁ dṛṣṭvā nivartate*

**The embodied soul may be restricted from sense enjoyment, though the taste for sense objects remains. But, ceasing such engagements by experiencing a higher taste, he is fixed in consciousness. (Bg. 2.59)**

A higher taste is when one awakens the desire to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa. Just as when you are eating, you experience the taste, nourishment and strength. You see that your hunger is going away. Similarly, when we hear about Kṛṣṇa and chant Hare Kṛṣṇa with devotees, it will give us strength and taste. We will see our anarthas going away, having lost our attraction for materialistic things. Therefore, we have to seek out the association of devotees, hear from them and get strength.

*śuśrūṣoḥ śraddadhānasya*  
*vāsudeva-kathā-ruciḥ*  
*syān mahat-sevayā viprāḥ*  
*puṇya-tīrtha-niṣevaṇāt*

**“O twice-born sages, by serving those devotees who are completely freed from all vice, great service is done. By such service, one gains affinity for hearing the messages of Vāsudeva.” (Bhāg. 1.2.16)**

To awaken that taste, one must serve the Vaiṣṇavas who have that taste. You serve them by giving them something they want, and what they want are our ears so that they can go on describing Kṛṣṇa’s glories to somebody who has faith in hearing it.

*śṛṇvatāṁ sva-kathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ*  
*puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ*  
*hṛdy antaḥ stho hy abhadrāṇi*  
*vidhunoti suhṛt satām*

**Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, who is the Paramātmā \[Supersoul\] in everyone’s heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who has developed the urge to hear His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted. (Bhāg. 1.2.17)**

When properly heard and chanted, the holy name will act within the heart.

*nitya-siddha kṛṣṇa-prema ‘sādhya’ kabhu naya*  
*śravaṇādi-śuddha-citte karaye udaya*

(Cc. Madhya, 22.107)

Pure love for Kṛṣṇa is eternally situated within the heart of every living being. It does not come from any other source. However, when one hears about Kṛṣṇa from the right source, that love within the heart becomes awakened, and then we get strength. Bhakti is the awakening of desire, and when that desire is awakened within the heart, that is the birth of śraddhā. We should then be very careful to always keep ourselves in the association of devotees that help increase our faith in the holy name, the message of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and the association of Vaiṣṇavas. These are the most valuable gifts.

Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura describes the holy name as the prema rathana dhana—the most valuable jewel. When a devotee has this faith awakened, and goes on chanting and hearing with faith, then even though there are some other desires within the heart, Kṛṣṇa within the heart says, “He is hearing about Me! He wants to hear about Me! He wants to chant My name! I will help him. I will destroy that ignorance within his heart, and because he is always endeavoring, I will make it easier for him to come to Me.”

*teṣāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ*  
*bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam*  
*dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ*  
*yena mām upayānti te*

**“To those who are constantly devoted to serving Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.” (Bg. 10.10)**

Despite the upheavals of the material world, the devotee will not give up hearing and chanting about Kṛṣṇa. Such is his faith. When Kṛṣṇa sees the devotee determined to maintain that faith, then all the other subtle desires (the anarthas or finer particles of dust that we cannot so easily see and clean) will be cleaned out by Kṛṣṇa. He will uproot the weeds of these desires from within the heart, and will make the heart a very nice clean place that He will be very much inclined to sit in for quite some time. He will be very inclined to further dictate and help us to come to Him, until there is no longer any need for Him to stay in the heart. Instead, He will just smile and say, “Look at Me! I am no longer there within your heart.” He will welcome you with His embrace. You will smell the fragrance of His transcendental body. You will hear the transcendental sound of His flute. Everything will be revealed to such a devotee who has faith. Kṛṣṇa is prepared to give him everything; Kṛṣṇa will give Himself.

*jñāne prayāsam udapāsya namanta eva*  
*jīvanti san-mukharitāṁ bhavadīya-vārtām*  
*sthāne sthitāḥ śruti-gatāṁ tanu-vāṅ-manobhir*  
*ye prāyaśo ’jita jito ’py asi tais tri-lokyām*

**“Those who, even while remaining situated in their established social positions, throw away the process of speculative knowledge and with their body, words and mind offer all respects to descriptions of Your personality and activities, dedicating their lives to these narrations, which are vibrated by You personally and by Your pure devotees, certainly conquer Your Lordship, although You are otherwise unconquerable by anyone within the three worlds.” (Bhāg. 10.14.3)**

In this prayer, Lord Brahma is explaining that this is how Kṛṣṇa is conquered—by those who give their hearts and ears to hearing His transcendental narrations. When Kṛṣṇa is conquered, He gives Himself. Kṛṣṇa will stand there face to face with us and say, “You have conquered Me by your love.” Kṛṣṇa will embrace us and accept us back home, back to Godhead.

*satāṁ prasaṅgān mama vīrya-saṁvido*  
*bhavanti hṛt-karṇa-rasāyanāḥ kathāḥ*  
*taj-joṣaṇād āśv apavarga-vartmani*  
*śraddhā ratir bhaktir anukramiṣyati*

**In the association of pure devotees, discussion of the pastimes and activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is very pleasing and satisfying to the ear and the heart. By cultivating such knowledge one gradually becomes advanced on the path of liberation, and thereafter he is freed, and his attraction becomes fixed. Then real devotion and devotional service begin. (Bhāg. 3.25.25)**

Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura explains that first there is śraddhā, then rati, bhāva, bhakti, and prema. On the platform of prema, he hears in great ecstasy. On the platform of śraddhā, he hears with some faith. At every stage, all the way from śraddhā to prema, he goes on hearing. This is the most powerful medicine, as it will clean the heart and give us hope. Otherwise, we will have no qualification to go back home back to Godhead by ourselves. We have no other hope than the hope that Śrīla Prabhupāda and Lord Caitanya have given us of the path, which the mahājanas have left behind for us to follow. It is very simple. We should not complicate it. We should just be very determined to follow it, and success is guaranteed. Kṛṣṇa gives His assurance of this.

*aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā*  
*dharmasyāsya parantapa*  
*aprāpya māṁ nivartante*  
*mṛtyu-saṁsāra-vartmani*

**“Those who are not faithful in this devotional service cannot attain Me, O conqueror of enemies. Therefore they return to the path of birth and death in this material world.” (Bg. 9.3)**

PURPORT:

The faithless cannot accomplish this process of devotional service; that is the purport of this verse. Faith is created by association with devotees. Unfortunate people, even after hearing all the evidence of Vedic literature from great personalities, still have no faith in God. They are hesitant and cannot stay fixed in the devotional service of the Lord. Thus faith is a most important factor for progress in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. In the Caitanya-caritāmṛta it is said that faith is the complete conviction that simply by serving the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, one can achieve all perfection. That is called real faith. As stated in the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (4.31.14),

***yathā taror mūla-niṣecanena***  
***tṛpyanti tat-skandha-bhujopaśākhāḥ***  
***prāṇopahārāc ca yathendriyāṇāṁ***  
***tathaiva sarvārhaṇam acyutejyā***

“By giving water to the root of a tree one satisfies its branches, twigs and leaves, and by supplying food to the stomach one satisfies all the senses of the body. Similarly, by engaging in the transcendental service of the Supreme Lord one automatically satisfies all the demigods and all other living entities.” Therefore, after reading Bhagavad-gītā one should promptly come to the conclusion of Bhagavad-gītā: one should give up all other engagements and adopt the service of the Supreme Lord, Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead. If one is convinced of this philosophy of life, that is faith.

Now, the development of that faith is the process of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. There are three divisions of Kṛṣṇa conscious men. In the third class are those who have no faith. Even if they are officially engaged in devotional service, they cannot achieve the highest perfectional stage. Most probably they will slip, after some time. They may become engaged, but because they haven’t complete conviction and faith, it is very difficult for them to continue in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. We have practical experience in discharging our missionary activity that some people come and apply themselves to Kṛṣṇa consciousness with some hidden motive, and as soon as they are economically well situated, they give up this process and take up their old ways again. It is only by faith that one can advance in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. As far as the development of faith is concerned, one who is well versed in the literatures of devotional service and has attained the stage of firm faith is called a first-class person in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. And in the second class are those who are not very advanced in understanding the devotional scriptures but who automatically have firm faith that kṛṣṇa-bhakti, or service to Kṛṣṇa, is the best course and so in good faith have taken it up. Thus they are superior to the third class, who have neither perfect knowledge of the scriptures nor good faith but by association and simplicity are trying to follow. The third-class person in Kṛṣṇa consciousness may fall down, but when one is in the second class he does not fall down, and for the first-class person in Kṛṣṇa consciousness there is no chance of falling down. One in the first class will surely make progress and achieve the result at the end. As far as the third-class person in Kṛṣṇa consciousness is concerned, although he has faith in the conviction that devotional service to Kṛṣṇa is very good, he has not yet gained adequate knowledge of Kṛṣṇa through the scriptures like Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and Bhagavad-gītā. Sometimes these third-class persons in Kṛṣṇa consciousness have some tendency toward karma-yoga and jñāna-yoga, and sometimes they are disturbed, but as soon as the infection of karma-yoga or jñāna-yoga is vanquished, they become second-class or first-class persons in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Faith in Kṛṣṇa is also divided into three stages and described in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. First-class attachment, second-class attachment and third-class attachment are also explained in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam in the Eleventh Canto. Those who have no faith even after hearing about Kṛṣṇa and the excellence of devotional service, who think that it is simply eulogy, find the path very difficult, even if they are supposedly engaged in devotional service. For them there is very little hope of gaining perfection. Thus faith is very important in the discharge of devotional service.

This verse is about the faithless, but the purport is mainly about faith. Elsewhere in the Bhagavad-gītā, Kṛṣṇa talks about faithless people and faithful people:

“A faithful man who is dedicated to transcendental knowledge and who subdues his senses is eligible to achieve such knowledge, and having achieved it he quickly attains the supreme spiritual peace. But ignorant and faithless persons who doubt the revealed scriptures do not attain God consciousness; they fall down. For the doubting soul there is happiness neither in this world nor in the next.” (Bg. 4.39-40)

There are three types of faithless persons described in the Bhagavad-gītā (9.3). The first type is ajñaḥ, a fool. The second type is aśraddadhānaḥ, which are those who do not have sufficient faith in the revealed scriptures. When they look at the scriptures, they see that there are contradictions, and therefore they think, “Why should I follow the scriptures?” The third type is saṁśaya, which is the doubting soul. Although a person accepts the scriptures, when he reads them he has doubts if they are going to be effective in his case. Therefore, Kṛṣṇa says, “For the doubting soul there is happiness neither in this world nor in the next.”

In this verse, Śrīla Prabhupāda gives a lot of emphasis about the cultivation of faith. He says that faith is created by association of devotees. There are many examples in the scriptures of how faith took birth in the heart of a living entity as the result of association of the devotees. We see this in the story of Nārada Muni and how he became faithful as a result of the association of bhaktivedāntas.

There is the very important story in Caitanya-bhāgavata of how faith took birth in in the heart of Devānanda Paṇḍita as a result of his association with Vrakreśvara Paṇḍita. When Devānanda Paṇḍita saw the symptoms of ecstatic love of the Lord that Vrakreśvara Paṇḍita manifested, he wanted to serve him. Therefore, he began rendering various types of personal service to him. Sometimes when Vrakreśvara Paṇḍita would dance in ecstasy, Devānanda Paṇḍita would guard and protect him from others. He would also always stand nearby in case Vrakreśvara Paṇḍita would fall in the kīrtana, and he would try to catch him, protect him, and wipe the dust from his body. Simply by seeing him, faith took birth in the heart of Devānanda Paṇḍita. As a result of that association with Vrakreśvara Paṇḍita, Devānanda Paṇḍita’s faith in Lord Caitanya was also awakened.

There is also the story of Gadādhara Paṇḍita, whose faith in Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi was awakened by seeing him. Mukunda brought Gadādhara Paṇḍita to see Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi, who was a very exalted devotee. At that particular time and place, Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi was dressed very opulently, and externally he had the appearance of a materialist. Surrounded by opulence, he wore very opulent clothing, had his hair styled in a very opulent way, sat on opulent furniture, and was surrounded by opulent spittoons.

When Gadādhara Paṇḍita looked at him, he wondered, “Is this the saintly person I heard about?”

Mukunda could understand what was going on in Gadādhara Paṇḍita’s mind, and therefore began reciting verses from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. He recited a verse describing Kṛṣṇa’s kṛpā-śakti (mercy), and how merciful Kṛṣṇa was even to Pūtanā. Pūtanā came to offer poison on her breast to kill Him, yet Kṛṣṇa accepted that as service, accepted the milk, and gave her the position of being a mother in the spiritual world.

When Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi heard this verse, it stimulated in his heart such deep remembrance of and attachment to Kṛṣṇa that he lost external consciousness and began manifesting ecstatic symptoms. He did not know from where the verse came.

When Gadādhara Paṇḍita saw all the symptoms that were manifest in his body, faith in Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi took birth in his heart. He thought, “Previously I misunderstood him, but now I can understand that He is a very exalted person. The only way I can rectify myself from the offense I have committed is that I must accept him as my spiritual master and take mantra dīkṣā from him.”

Thus, faith is awakened by association. There are so many other examples from scriptures of how faith takes its birth in the heart of a person as a result of association with a devotee. Faith is the most important factor for progress in Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

*‘śraddhā’-śabde—viśvāsa kahe sudṛḍha niścaya*  
*kṛṣṇe bhakti kaile sarva-karma kṛta haya*

(Cc. Madhya, 22.62)

Śraddhā means confident, firm faith that simply by engaging in devotional service, automatically all of one’s subsidiary activities are performed. Such śraddhā is conducive for the advancement in Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

Such complete conviction in serving Kṛṣṇa is real faith. When water is given to the root of a tree, automatically all the branches, twigs and leaves are satisfied. Similarly, when faith is developed in Kṛṣṇa, then one surrenders himself to Him.

Of course, faith is increased in the association of devotees, but faith can also be diminished by association with non-devotees. Therefore, Lord Caitanya explained (Cc. Madhya, 22.87):

*asat-saṅga-tyaga,- ei vaisnava-acara*  
*‘stri-sangi’-eka asadhu, ‘krisnabhakta’ ara*

The devotee should renounce asat saṅga—the association with worldly minded persons who are attached simply to the opposite sex and material enjoyment. To the degree that one associates with worldly minded materialists, to that degree one’s firm faith in the objective will diminish. Thus association is the key principle in the cultivation of firm faith. Development of faith is the whole process of advancement in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, all the way from śraddhā to prema. There are different levels of faith. Therefore, advancement in devotional service means to increase one’s faith.

For devotees who are taking a position of helping others in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, the real fruit of our effort should be that their faith is increasing. That is the result that a devotee wants. If one tries to purchase the holy name with material desires or with material goods, then these things are not accepted as real currency in the marketplace of the holy name. The only valid currency is faith. Thus, a devotee should want to see that others are offering their faith; not something material, and that their faith is increasing.

For those who are just coming to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, their faith is very weak. Prabhupāda describes such persons as third-class devotees, as their faith is very pliable and they are easily impressed. If they see inconsistent behavior, then immediately it affects their faith, and they look for excuses to not surrender to Kṛṣṇa. They are still struggling with their senses, as they still have some faith in sense gratification. However, to make progress in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, one’s faith must become very firm.

We see that Bali Mahārāja is glorified because he had faith in surrendering to Vāmanadeva. Because Vāmanadeva asked him for three steps of land, he was determined to give it. Lord Vāmanadeva took everything with three steps—Bali Mahārāja gave everything in the Lord’s first two steps, and then gave himself for the Lord’s third step. Although the Lord took everything, Bali Mahārāja gained everything by that surrender, and he is thus glorified. He is one of the mahājanas that we follow.

If faith is there, then everything else will follow. We may create faith, but we also have to be very careful that we do not break faith. Faith creates faith. Those who have firm faith will awaken, support and nourish faith in others by their example.

If a person takes a position of helping others’ faith in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, but if by their own example they do not demonstrate that they have faith, then that breaks the faith of others. It is a very dangerous position to take someone’s faith and then break it. Faith is not created by words, but should also be demonstrated by one’s example—in how much faith they have in chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, in hearing Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and in speaking the message of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

In Godruma Kalpatavi, Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says that such persons who are distributors of the holy name demonstrate their faith even in private conversations by speaking about Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and not about the mundane topics like economic development. Śrīla Prabhupāda describes in the Fifth Canto of the Bhāgavatam that even impersonalists become attracted to devotional service by hearing the pastimes of the Lord in the association of devotees of the Lord. They are not interested in the discussions of psychology, sociology, economic development, etc. There will always be someone who wants to talk about these things, but the devotees are very eager to discuss the topics of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. The ability to do that depends upon their faith. Having firm faith in Kṛṣṇa, they will minimize their discussions of material, worldly activities, do only that which is necessary, and utilize the rest of their time for cultivating their own faith by seeking out the association of devotees who help to increase their faith.

Sometimes people come into the society of devotees, but they do not look to advance. Even if they are externally fulfilled very nicely, they will always remain incomplete, and it will only lead to suffering.

Kṛṣṇa says to Uddhava:

**“Having awakened faith in the narrations of My glories, being disgusted with all material activities, knowing that all sense gratification leads to misery, but still being unable to renounce all sense enjoyment, My devotee should remain happy and worship Me with great faith and conviction. Even though he is sometimes engaged in sense enjoyment, My devotee knows that all sense gratification leads to a miserable result, and he sincerely repents such activities.” (Bhāg. 11.20.27-28)**

Not only does the devotee have faith in chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, but he has faith in hearing about Kṛṣṇa, which is the stage when devotional service begins. He knows that sense gratification leads to suffering, but he goes on hearing about Kṛṣṇa with faith. He hears pastimes about Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi, Nārada Muni, Vrakreśvara Paṇḍita and Devānanda Paṇḍita. He also hears about mother Yaśodā’s intense love for Kṛṣṇa and the kṛpā-śakti that manifested to her. He has faith to go on hearing these pastimes again and again and again, because he knows that by so doing, his own faith increases, and he feels himself advancing in spiritual life.

There will always be some anxiety in the material world. However, one’s mind gradually becomes more peaceful when he has bhakta-niṣṭhā—firm faith that to continue to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa and hear about Kṛṣṇa in the association of devotees. All other activities are simply a support to hearing, chanting, and remembering about Kṛṣṇa.

Thus, Lord Kapiladeva says that we must seek out the association of devotees who put Kṛṣṇa consciousness first above everything else. Then our faith will increase and naturally we will feel ourselves advancing in our spiritual life.

The example was previously given that when we first develop some faith, it is like the birth of a newborn baby girl whom the parents are always very anxious to protect from severe heat and severe cold, from hunger and thirst and from dangerous creatures. These are compared to be like karma and jñāna, which are like two stocks of poison. When the living entity’s faith is awakened in the process of pure devotional service, he has to be protected from these influences of karma, fruitive activities, mental speculation and the desire for liberation. These are compared to be like two witches that haunt one like a ghost, and as long as these two witches are within the heart, one will never be able to taste the bliss of devotional service. Thus, the Vaiṣṇavas protect that faith in the heart of the living entity once it has been awakened. Just as a mother nurtures her newborn child and raises her and helps her to grow, in the same way, the merciful Vaiṣṇavas will give nourishment so that the seed of devotion that has been planted within the heart can grow into a very beautiful flower.

This is the importance of association of devotees. Even in the Age of Kali, the Supreme Lord does not appear as the Supreme Lord, but as a devotee of the Lord. He says (Cc. Ādi, 3.19):

*yuga-dharma pravartāimu nāma-saṅkīrtana*  
*cāri bhāva-bhakti diyā nācāmu bhuvana*

**“I shall personally inaugurate the religion of the age—nāma-saṅkīrtana, the congregational chanting of the holy name. I shall make the world dance in ecstasy, realizing the four mellows of loving devotional service.”**

Unless one practices devotional service himself, he cannot teach it to others. Therefore the Supreme Lord Himself said, “I will come and accept the role of the devotee, and I will teach it by practicing it Myself.” A devotee thus awakens devotion in the hearts of others on the strength of his own absolute faith in Kṛṣṇa consciousness and in the power of the holy name.

Just as a person who has some money will invest it to increase his wealth, similarly, if an intelligent person has received the beautiful gift of faith in the holy name of the Lord, then he will invest his faith in those who have faith, which will result in his own faith increasing.

Śrīla Prabhupāda wrote on the Jaladuta, “The only thing that I have is Your holy name and faith in that holy name, otherwise I have no qualification for giving this message. If You desire their deliverance, then they will be delivered.” Śrīla Prabhupāda had complete faith in the process and power of chanting the holy name of the Lord, and therefore went to Tompkins Square Park by himself with a little drum and chanted the holy names of the Lord.

Śrīla Prabhupāda wrote in his diary in February of 1966 that he has personally witnessed how Haridāsa Ṭhākura had said that even the wild animals and creatures will take up the congregational chanting of the holy name of the Lord. He said that this statement by Haridāsa Ṭhākura has been corroborated, because we can personally witness how these American boys and girls have taken up the chanting of Hare Kṛṣṇa.

Previously we had faith in so many things, but not in Kṛṣṇa. We had faith that sense gratification and worldly pursuits would make us happy. However, by the mercy of the devotee, that faith has been changed into faith in something sublime. Śrīla Prabhupāda has given us the seed and he is watering it. He has demonstrated by his example how even those who are totally in forgetfulness can be awakened to their constitutional position as an eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa. We should follow in his footsteps, and follow the example of the Supreme Lord Himself, who came to teach devotional service by practicing it Himself. We should chant Hare Kṛṣṇa in the association of devotees, follow the simple principles of Kṛṣṇa consciousness and continue this divine mission which Śrīla Prabhupāda has given to all of us to carry out for him.

Prabhupāda was even thinking of us when he came to the shores of the United States and wrote Mārkine Bhāgavata-dharma. We are all made of his mercy. The best way to reciprocate is through gratitude. If we are grateful for the wonderful gift that we have received by his mercy and we try to offer him something in return by increasing others’ faith in the power of devotional service and the pure holy name, then Kṛṣṇa consciousness will spread. We will all become carriers of that mercy. We should aspire for that, as it is the best way to return our debt to Śrīla Prabhupāda. If we can make Śrīla Prabhupāda smile and be happy by our efforts in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, that will be the success of our lives.

We can see how wonderful it is to have the opportunity to have received the association of a devotee of the Lord, because it is by that association that we have been given the only true choice—to develop our love for Kṛṣṇa.

**Question: Can we develop a relationship with Lord Caitanya if our faith is not strong?**

Prabhodānanda Sarasvatī said (Śrī Caitanya-candrāmṛta, 88):

*yatha yatha gaura-padaravinde*  
*vindeta bhaktim krta-punya-rasih*  
*tatha tathotsarpati hrdy akasmad*  
*radha-padambhoja-sudhambu-rasih*

In proportion to the service that one renders to Lord Caitanya, to that degree he becomes qualified to serve Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana. Ultimately we want to achieve that faith. However, we also have to understand the purpose for which Lord Caitanya and Lord Nityānanda appeared, which was to awaken that faith. Their method of distributing Kṛṣṇa consciousness was such that even if one did not have faith, They awakened it. We should not think that we had any previous qualification for coming in contact with devotional service. Somehow or other, faith was awakened within our hearts by association.

Although there is a small amount of faith, we have to increase our faith. It is described in the song Dalalera-gītā by Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura that Lord Nityānanda opened the marketplace of the holy name and distributed the holy name of the Lord for the price of one’s faith. He made no consideration of who was fit and who was not fit. He made no consideration of one’s position, power, strength and wealth. The only requirement was that there must be a little faith, and this little faith actually came from His method of distribution.

The ācāryas give the example that salespeople sometimes give out free samples of a product in the store or on the street so that you can realize its value and come back to purchase more. Lord Nityānanda thus distributed the holy name in this way. He gave out small samples, even before we had faith. He was simply anxious to distribute it, and He did not want anything except to satisfy Lord Caitanya. He would cry, roll on the ground with tears in His eyes and say, “Please chant Kṛṣṇa’s names! Just please chant!”

People would see Him and His intense desire to give, and it would awaken some faith: “Yes, I want to chant. I will chant.” The devotees distribute the holy name of the Lord in that way. In that marketplace of the holy name, there is no other currency except faith, and there is no other profit, except increasing the faith. If you try to purchase the holy name of the Lord with false currency, trying to get it by some material motivation, you will not get śuddha-nāma, the pure holy name. Thus, if we want to get the holy name, we have to associate with devotees who will increase our faith and attachment to the Lord.

Lord Caitanya came to give the holy name, and He wanted us to take it. Therefore, if we take it, we are serving Him. He said, “Please take it! I can’t distribute it alone! How many of these fruits of love of Godhead can I distribute by Myself? I order every man in this universe to please take it and distribute it!” By so doing, we can understand Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana. If we see others happy in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, then it gives us faith that maybe someday we can also be happy in Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

Once when I was in America, I was flying from Minneapolis to San Jose, California. Due to being a frequent flyer, I was upgraded to business class where there are usually a lot of wealthy people. I was getting ready to board the plane in Minneapolis and apparently there was a man who was looking at me.

I proceeded to board the plane and took my seat. Soon thereafter, the same man boarded the plane and realized his seat was next to mine. He sat down and did not say anything. A few minutes after the flight took off, he kindly turned to me and said, “Can I ask you a question? Do you know that your sweater does not match your clothes?”

I said, “No. I didn’t know. You are the first person who told me this.”

He said, “Well, I just thought I would tell you. Tell me something about yourself, will you?”

I told him a little bit about what I do and that I was traveling to California to meet some devotees. It was a four-hour flight. About thirty minutes after we were talking, he really started to open up. He started telling me all about himself—about his work, his family, how he is a multi-millionaire and how he made all his money. He travels back and forth between Canada and San Jose once a week. He also told me about problems he has in his family.

All of a sudden, he said, “I have never been able to talk to anybody like this before. Do you know that you are the first person I have been able to talk to like this? I can’t even talk to my wife like this. I can’t talk to my friends. I don’t know what it is, but there is something about you. What is it about you?”

I answered, “I don’t know what it is.”

He said, “I know what it is. You are happy! You don’t have any money. You don’t have a wife. You don’t have kids. You don’t have a job. You don’t have a place to live. However, you are happy! Not only that, but you weren’t even disturbed when I told you that your sweater doesn’t match! How did you get to be like that? Please tell me. I am a businessman. When I see something valuable, I want to know how to get it.”

I proceeded to tell him about Prabhupāda, how I met him, and about the Bhagavad-gītā. He was listening very attentively, and after some time, he said, “I want that book! You know, I am a businessman. \[He said that to me at least fifteen times\]. I know when I see something valuable, I want it. How do I get that book?”

I did not have a Bhagavad-gītā with me, so I took his email address and later wrote him a letter, telling him how to get the Bhagavad-gītā. We talked throughout the entire flight, from takeoff to landing, and then went to get our baggage together.

I could see from this conversation that if we have association with somebody who is happy in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, then it awakens our faith, and we will want to find out more about it. Satāṁ prasaṅgān mama vīrya-saṁvido—in the association of devotees, the discussions of the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa are very pleasing to the ear and to the heart. As one advances along this path, gradually he becomes detached and his attraction to Kṛṣṇa becomes fixed. Then real devotion and devotional service begins.

We need that association all the way from śraddhā to prema, and we should be always very eager to be in the association of devotees who awaken our faith in the Lord. If we do not have it, then we should pray for it every day. If we see it somewhere, we should immediately go for it.

Rāmānanda Rāya described in his conversation with Lord Caitanya that pure devotional service cannot be had by millions of births of pious activities. It can be had only by paying one price—the intense greed to purchase it. Wherever we see it, we must immediately purchase it without delay. We should be very eager to associate with those devotees who help increase our faith.

## A Higher Taste

*buddhir jñānam asammohaḥ*  
*kṣamā satyaṁ damaḥ śamaḥ*  
*sukhaṁ duḥkhaṁ bhavo ‘bhāvo*  
*bhayaṁ cābhayam eva ca*  
*ahiṁsā samatā tuṣṭis*  
*tapo dānaṁ yaśo ’yaśaḥ*  
*bhavanti bhāvā bhūtānāṁ*  
*matta eva pṛthag-vidhāḥ*
