At work, one has to be in the physical presence of many other persons—oftentimes very worldly-minded persons who are trying to oblige us in various ways to sell us something, to buy something from us, to obtain our services or to render some service. Such association and physical contact can have a debilitating effect on a struggling sādhaka.

This is not being said in a negative sense. It is understood that many people have to live like this. However, that does not necessarily have to be a disqualification for advancing in spiritual life. Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura describes in Śrī Bhaktyāloka that even though we may have to be in the physical presence of persons who are worldly-minded and always trying to oblige us in so called higher priorities than chanting the holy name of the Lord, it does not really become association if we have a strong attraction or affection for association with devotees, and as long as we are not attracted to the materialistic qualities of materialistic persons. If we think, “This person has so much wealth and such a big position. If I associate with him, I can gain wealth and position,” then our faith in chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa diminishes.

Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains in Bhaktyāloka that to the degree that we are attracted to worldly objectives, goals, or people, and we aspire for what they have, then our faith will simply decrease. However, as Kṛṣṇa says in Bhagavad-gītā, renunciation in the mode of goodness is when one performs their duties because they have to be done, but he is not attached to the results.

*anāśritaḥ karma-phalaṁ*  
*kāryaṁ karma karoti yaḥ*  
*sa sannyāsī ca yogī ca*  
*na niragnir na cākriyaḥ*

**The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: One who is unattached to the fruits of his work and who works as he is obligated is in the renounced order of life, and he is the true mystic, not he who lights no fire and performs no duty. (Bg. 6.1)**

A struggling sādhaka adopts some means by which he is doing something every day that is important for his spiritual life. Because it is important for his spiritual life, it is most important.

Prabhupāda gives the analogy that if one has a million dollars, then all his ten dollar debts are taken care of. Similarly, if our life is meant to be based upon that spiritual life, then it is to be based upon that which gives us Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa gives Himself personally to the person who approaches Him with faith and love. Yasmin vijñāte sarvam evaṁ vijñātaṁ bhavati—When Kṛṣṇa is known, then everything else that is knowable also becomes known. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 1.3)

When Kṛṣṇa gives Himself, then everything else comes with Him. Thus a sādhaka has faith that the means for obtaining Kṛṣṇa is chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa. He knows that whatever he may obtain in this world is temporary, and it will only provide some flickering pleasure. If one really wants to obtain the ultimate fruit, then he should be looking to develop his pure love of God.

Therefore, a sādhaka is one who everyday engages in some activity that is going to help him to develop his love for Kṛṣṇa. A sādhaka is a very auspicious position to be in. Chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa is the most powerful and effective means for developing one’s love for Godhead in this age. There are so many references from the scriptures which confirm this.

However, for one who has firm faith in the statements of the scriptures—especially statements that speak about the glories of the holy name of the Lord—then he has faith that by chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa every day, he can gradually cleanse the contamination within his heart and directly perceive the Supreme Personality of Godhead in this life. For one who has such conviction, Kṛṣṇa, within his heart, reciprocates and helps him. Kṛṣṇa says (Bg. 10.10): “I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.”

## Making our Chanting Relevant

Although one should aspire to chant the holy name of the Lord in pure consciousness—in full remembrance of Kṛṣṇa—for most, that stage is only an aspiration. Devotees therefore need to adopt a reasonable means to purify the heart for achieving the goal of fixing the mind in full recollection of the Lord’s pastimes. The best process is properly chanting the holy name itself. Purification manifests to the degree that one opens the heart to the holy name. Along with endeavoring to remember the Lord’s form, qualities and pastimes, it is helpful to meditate on one’s exclusive dependence upon the holy name.

Śrīla Prabhupāda often gave an example to show how that purification works: As an iron rod in fire makes the iron rod hotter, then similarly, by coming in contact with Kṛṣṇa in the form of His name, form, qualities and pastimes, one becomes progressively purified.

We have to fully open our heart to the holy name so that it enters deeply and cleanses the heart by its influence. The consciousness that I have been trying to cultivate while chanting, in order to open my heart, is the feeling of unworthiness to chant it purely; feeling the inability to be fully engaged in devotional service; and the feeling of insufficiency in love for Kṛṣṇa.

It is quite like the mood described by Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī in the Bṛhad-bhāgavatāmṛta. He describes that one of the characteristics of a devotee is that he always feels that he does not have enough of Kṛṣṇa’s mercy, that he does not do enough to serve Kṛṣṇa, and that he does not have enough love for Kṛṣṇa. A humble devotee is thus increasingly feeling the need for Kṛṣṇa’s mercy, His service, and ultimately the intense desire for more and more devotion.

That feeling of inadequacy, however, should not be done in a mood of self-indulgence. It should not come to the point where one is thinking himself so unqualified and fallen that he is totally focusing only on himself. Unless one can properly relate to the concept of being fallen, how can one feel the need for mercy? A devotee should think that the Lord is very merciful—more merciful that one can imagine, and because of that kindness, He is manifested in His name. One should meditate on verses such as the following:

*kali-kāle nāma-rūpe kṛṣṇa-avatāra*  
*nāma haite haya sarva-jagat-nistāra*

**In this Age of Kali, the holy name of the Lord, the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, is the incarnation of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Simply by chanting the holy name, one associates with the Lord directly. Anyone who does this is certainly delivered. (Cc. Ādi 17.22)**

The Lord is so merciful that He kindly enters the heart to purify His devotee. However, one must first consider himself in great need of that mercy and so dependent on Him that He is drawn to reciprocate those sincere feelings.

Śrīla Prabhupāda would say that we should chant as a child sincerely crying out to attract the mother’s mercy. Before meditating on different aspects of the Lord’s pastimes and features, while chanting, I try to absorb myself for a specific period of time on how much I need mercy, and why I am presently in need. I look at my inadequacies, all the unwanted things that are within my heart, and realize that unless I can get mercy, I have no hope.

The holy name is more effective when chanted with faith. Because the holy name has been given to us from the lips of Kṛṣṇa’s pure devotee, it is imbued with all the necessary potency to manifest kṛṣṇa-premā, pure love of God. I have that deep confidence and firm faith in Śrīla Prabhupāda’s empowerment to deliver the holy name. Kṛṣṇa-śakti vinā nahe tāra pravartana—unless empowered by Kṛṣṇa, one cannot propagate the saṅkīrtana movement. (Cc. Antya 7.11)

That confidence and faith in Śrīla Prabhupāda’s ability to give the pure holy name, which can cleanse our heart, is also an essential ingredient for the process to work. Without faith that the holy name is everything; that the holy name can clean our heart; and that the holy name can bestow full mercy upon us, it is very difficult to focus the mind on the holy name consistently and with confidence.

Therefore, we need to not only carefully chant the holy name, but we need to also hear the glories of the holy name from Śrīla Prabhupāda and from advanced Vaiṣṇavas. We need to read and hear about those glories repeatedly and also to discuss with others the truth and beauty of the Lord’s holy name, as described in the revealed scriptures, and from the mouths of the Vaiṣṇavas. There is no other way to taste the sweetness of the Lord’s holy name.

This type of meditation is definitely absorbing and instills within me a genuine feeling of humility and invokes the feeling of repentance. In turn, such contrition awakens a kind of emotion and an inner impetus to take shelter of the holy name. It is difficult to just go on thinking about one’s inadequacies and fallen nature without taking refuge in the remedy of the holy name.

I have faith that not only is the holy name extremely merciful and can deliver me, but it can also forgive me. That gives me hope and instills further faith. Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī says that the holy name is even more merciful than the form of Kṛṣṇa, because it is shelter in the holy name where one seeks forgiveness. It is true that the Lord and His name are non-different, but still there is a slight difference. The holy name is even more merciful than the form of Kṛṣṇa, which gives me hope and confidence, and serves to stimulate these types of emotions that inspire a strong need to chant more and more. This state of hopelessness and dependency is the best catalyst for deeper meditation.

In other words, by first looking at our own inadequacies and realizing our helpless dependence on the holy name, our chanting automatically becomes relevant and meaningful, because we can see the direct connection between our chanting and our heart, desires and needs. That deep desire in the heart for shelter is thus the main feeling that is immediately accessible to me when chanting. Although I pray to the previous ācāryas, Śrīla Prabhupāda and the Vaiṣṇavas, certainly they are all accessible by calling them. The mercy of Kṛṣṇa and Kṛṣṇa Himself is manifested most fully and completely in His name.

Chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa should be relevant. If we do not feel its relevance, the tendency is to think that we are chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa because we have to, or because we want to get initiation. One may be driven to do that, but although obedience is the first stage of love as described by Rūpa Gosvāmī in Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindu, it is not the highest stage. Therefore, chanting should be relevant. For it to be relevant, we have to feel a sense of dependence, which means that we actually have to feel a sense of inadequacy. This is so contrary to the modern—especially the American—way. It seems everybody is taught to be proud and independent, and that to be helpless and dependent is a sign of total inadequacy.

However, we see from the examples in the scriptures that persons who are fully dependent on the Lord become very powerful and they achieve and accomplish so much. The result is that people fall at their feet, worshiping them. We see this in the example of Parīkṣit Mahārāja who had the potency to counter-curse Śṛṅgi, the son of Śamīka Ṛṣi, but he did not. He accepted it as the will of the Lord. Being fully dependent upon the Lord, he accepted His decision and achieved perfection. He heard Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. He accepted the curse and was bitten by the bite of the snake-bird, but had achieved all perfection by having heard Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam from the lips of Śukadeva Gosvāmī in seven days. The Lord was constantly protecting him.

It is an illusion to think that helpless dependence on the Lord is a sign of weakness. Of course, we do not want to be helplessly dependent upon somebody else for our maintenance, as that is a sign of weakness and is an unfortunate position. However, to be fully dependent upon Kṛṣṇa is the safest and the most auspicious position to be in. Our chanting should therefore be done in that consciousness: “I must not have love of God, because when I chant, tears don’t come to my eyes. I am not losing consciousness of the external world. I am not seeing Kṛṣṇa fully manifested and I don’t see Him dancing on my tongue. I am not experiencing the aṣṭa-satvika-bhava—eight ecstasies of transformation of my body, with tears flowing from my eyes, eruptions on my skin, and hair standing on end. Something must be wrong.”

When we have this realization, and if we are at least faithful enough to know that it is not the holy name that is ineffective, but rather that there is still something within ourselves that is wrong, then we will become dependent upon the holy name to clear away the anarthas within our heart. As previously mentioned, the anarthas are compared to be like the clouds obstructing our vision of the sun, and the fog is compared to be like ignorance, which needs to be destroyed. We are thus dependent upon the holy name.

*nāmāparādha-yuktānāṁ*  
*nāmāny eva haranty agham*  
*aviśrānti-prayuktāni*  
*tāny evārtha-karāṇi ca*  
*(Padma Purāṇa)*

In the Padma Purāṇa it is stated that chanting of Hare Kṛṣṇa is recommended for those who are committing offenses while chanting, but if they go on chanting and endeavor to overcome these offenses or anarthas within the heart, then gradually they become free from these offenses. Such is the power of the holy name. We must feel dependent upon the holy name. We must also feel a sense of inadequacy that we are not chanting purely enough—as dependent as a child crying out loudly for his mother.

Śrīla Prabhupāda speaks about this mood in which we should be chanting:

Of course we have to control the mind, and I have already instructed you and all my students that the restless fickle mind can only be controlled by putting the mind to the lotus feet of Krsna, and that can best be done by chanting Hare Krsna mantra, and there is no alternative in this age. By chanting without offenses, the devotee cries to Radharani and Krsna to please lift him out of the material energy and put him into the spiritual energy, which is devotional service. (Letter to Govinda dāsī—Bhaktivedanta Manor, July 20, 1973)

In another letter, Śrīla Prabhupāda says:

Simply pray to Krishna that you may be able by His Grace to serve Him nicely. Our prayer of the Hare Krishna Mantra means addressing Radha and Krishna for being engaged in Their service. Hare Krishna means “Oh Hare, Oh Radharani! Oh Krishna! Please engage me in Your service so that I can get relief from the service of Maya.” Just like a person resigns from an inferior quality of service and accepts a superior quality of service, similarly, our prayer to Krishna is to give us relief from the inferior quality of service to Maya, and to be engaged in the superior quality of service to Krishna. Service we have to render, and the whole process is to accept the superior quality of service in Krishna Consciousness. (Letter to Subala dāsa—Los Angeles, July 8, 1969)

Śrīla Prabhupāda further explains what our prayer should be:

We are very small, very insignificant, so what can we do? Simply He wants to see that we are engaging our time and energy in His service. And you always remember to abide by the laws of Krishna as described by His bona fide Representative, and the passage of going back to Godhead is assured. This is Krishna’s Mercy. But pure devotees do not even want to go to Krishna’s abode. Simply our prayer should be, My dear Krishna, please remind me to always chant Your Holy Name, please do not put me into forgetfulness. You are sitting within me as Supersoul, so you can put me into forgetfulness or into remembering You. So please do not put me into forgetfulness. Please always remind me to chant, even You send me into the hell, it doesn't matter, just so long as I can always chant Hare Krishna. (Letter to Devānanda dāsa—Los Angeles, November 23, 1968)

This is such a powerful and wonderful prayer. Before beginning our chanting, we should try to pray for mercy. Pray for the opportunity to remember the holy name of the Lord. It will help make our chanting relevant, and to make us feel dependent upon the holy name.

## Overcoming Obstacles

There are many impediments or obstacles that we have to try to overcome when chanting. We may be thinking of all the things we have to do at home. We get caught up in our obligations and feel that unless we can get everything in order, we cannot chant. However, nothing is ever set in order. Sometimes the tendency is to think, “If I can make my mind peaceful, then I can chant.” However, chanting is supposed to be our shelter. It is supposed to bring about that peaceful state when we realize that we will never be able to work everything out perfectly on the subsidiary platform of all the things that we have to do. Even when they are done, there will be more that needs to be done; they are never ending. Until we have that realization, it will be very difficult to whole-heartedly take shelter in the holy name.

Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura thus says that there are three things that are required for making progress in chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa. The first is determination, the second is to free ourselves from distractions—both external and internal distractions—and the third is to try to chant with devotees who can chant more attentively than we can.

Chanting free from distractions also means to chant in a place that does not create remembrance of all the things we have to do. Sometimes devotees will chant in front of the computer or the television, or with the right hand in the bead-bag and the left hand on Newsweek magazine. Sometimes they will chant in the room where they do their work, and as soon as they open their eyes and see all their work, it stimulates thoughts of the work they have to do, or what they may have forgotten to do. Then, instead of taking shelter of chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, they start making a list of what they have to do, thinking that by so doing, their mind will be peaceful enough to chant. However, these thoughts will always come to the surface. This is due to insufficient faith that by taking shelter in the holy name, first and foremost in the beginning of the day, then these other obligations will be taken care of later in the day. Furthermore, by so doing, one will be able to do them in a Kṛṣṇa conscious way, rather than thinking that by doing them because they are important, then he can chant Hare Kṛṣṇa in a peaceful state of mind. However, due to lack of faith, this will never come about. If Kṛṣṇa sees that we are willing to make that sacrifice for Him, He will be happy to accomplish that which we feel we have to accomplish. As Prabhupāda always said, if we take one step to Kṛṣṇa, He will take one hundred steps to us.

When we chant Hare Kṛṣṇa, it gives us the realization that there is something to listen to besides our mind. Most people do not know that there is a higher state of consciousness beyond the mind. Prabhupāda says that chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa is beyond intelligence and beyond the mind; it is on the transcendental platform. Thus, when we begin chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, we have the option of taking shelter of something higher than the mind.

In the Bhagavad-gītā it is described that the senses are like horses, the mind is like reins, the intelligence is like the driver, and the spirit soul is the passenger. When the intelligence is strong, holding tightly onto the reins, then the senses are controlled. The intelligence is higher than the mind. With the intelligence, we can discriminate between what the mind is dictating and what our spiritual intelligence is telling us to do.

Thus we have an option. When we pray to Kṛṣṇa in our hearts, He is witnessing and He knows when we have taken that step to Him. We must try to free ourselves from distractions. Kṛṣṇa says that by constant practice and detachment, gradually we can learn to conquer the mind.

**“For one who has conquered the mind, the Supersoul is already reached, for he has attained tranquility. To such a man happiness and distress, heat and cold, honor and dishonor are all the same.” (Bg. 6.7)**

The most powerful weapon for conquering the mind is the holy name of the Lord. As Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta says, we should beat our mind in the morning with the shoe and in the evening with the stick (not literally).

Mālatī had once asked Prabhupāda what we should think about while we are chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa. Prabhupāda answered, “Think? No, we should simply hear. Don’t try to artificially think. Simply hear.”

On another occasion, Prabhupāda said:

Chanting japa should be done early in the morning with full concentration preferably during the Brahma Muhurta time. Concentrate fully on the sound vibration of the mantra, pronouncing each name distinctly and gradually your speed in chanting will increase naturally. Do not worry so much about chanting fast, most important is the hearing. A devotee should always be grave and silent which means that he only discusses topics relating to Krishna Consciousness. Yes, spend your time chanting and reading and taking Krishna Prasadam and automatically your tongue will come under control. If you sincerely engage 24 hours daily in devotional service according to the instructions of the Spiritual Master, chant daily 16 rounds, attend the arati ceremony of Lord Krishna, associate with the devotees and adhere strictly to the regulative principles then Krishna will reveal Himself personally to you. (Śrīla Prabhupāda’s letter to Radhaballabha dāsa—Bombay, January 6, 1972)

Another time, a devotee asked Śrīla Prabhupāda if it is offensive to think of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes while we are chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa. Prabhupāda said that not only is it not offensive, but it is necessary. He also said that these pastimes will gradually begin to manifest in a natural way. It is not that we should try to force ourselves to think of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, especially to try to superimpose ourselves into Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes while chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa. We have to control the mind.

Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura describes this as the budding of a flower. First there is the bud, then it gradually opens, and as the petals open, the flower gives off a fragrance. This budding of the flower is just like chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa. First, we simply chant Hare Kṛṣṇa, and then nāma, then form (rūpa), then guṇa (qualities) and finally līlā (pastimes) all gradually begin to unfold and become increasingly revealed the more we fix our consciousness on the chanting of the holy name of the Lord.

However, we should still pray and have the proper attitude or conception of the holy name of the Lord. There is nothing wrong, prior to beginning our chanting, to meditate on Kṛṣṇa.

There is a particular pastime from Bṛhad-bhāgavatāmṛta that I meditate on before beginning my chanting. It is one that displays how merciful Kṛṣṇa is to those who are so exclusively dependent upon Him. It gives me hope, because we are really dependent on mercy. This pastime creates at least a conception within my mind and within my heart that Kṛṣṇa is very merciful to the devotee who exclusively depends upon Him. Realizing that before I get into that pastime, understand that pastime, or even remember that pastime, I pray: “Please, make me exclusively dependent upon You. Help me to overcome all the obstacles that are there on the path.” I have to really pray for the mercy of Lord Nityānanda to enter into the heart and to eradicate all the obstacles along the path, so that there is hope that I can one day chant śuddha-nāma.

Most importantly, we should try to hear. The tendency of the mind is to always think about something else; to remember somebody else; to think about some obligation; or to feel some discomfort. Thoughts about our discomfort are very strong, especially when sitting down with the aim of chanting our rounds non-stop.

**Question: Between serving our personal deities or doing our regular service and chanting, which is more important for us to do?**

The perfection of our service to the deities is glorification of Them. Lord Caitanya told Sanatāna Gosvāmī that of all the nine processes of devotional service, the most important is the chanting of the holy name of the Lord. All other processes are dependent upon the chanting of the holy name of the Lord.

Rūpa Gosvāmī also explains that if one commits offenses to the Deity of the Lord, then there is no hope for rectification, except by the mercy of the holy name. Therefore, although there is no difference between Kṛṣṇa’s name and His form (arcā-vigraha), still there is a slight difference. That slight difference is mercy. The most merciful manifestation of Kṛṣṇa is His name—even more than the His form. Thus even if we cannot properly complete our worship of the Deity, if we take shelter and glorify the Deity by chanting His name, then we can still be forgiven for offenses or incomplete worship of the Deity. Chanting is most important.

**Question: How do we approach the holy name, even though we are full of faults?**

We have to have that faith that Kṛṣṇa will overlook our inadequacies. Prabhupāda gives the example of a child calling for his mother in a state of helplessness. When one actually has firm faith in that helpless state, then that gives confidence to continue endeavoring, which is one of the six requirements for advancing in devotional service.

Prabhupāda therefore says that before we begin chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, we should always precede it by chanting the pañca-tattva mantra, because They are more merciful and will eradicate the offenses committed in the chanting of Hare Kṛṣṇa. It is the same in worshiping the deities. We worship Lord Caitanya, because He will overlook our offenses. Therefore, we approach Lord Caitanya first, and then Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.

Thus, we should approach the holy name of the Lord by first approaching Lord Caitanya so that we can overcome our obstacles and offenses that are committed, and have that confidence and faith that Kṛṣṇa understands our purpose and intention. Being confident that we are helpless without Him to be able to chant properly, He will help.

**Question: Is it an obstacle if when we are chanting in unison with others we are unable to focus on our own chanting?**

It is an impetus to focus more on our own chanting. However, if we cannot focus more on our own chanting, we can focus on somebody else’s chanting. But focus must be there.

**Question: How do we maintain the feeling of intense prayer?**

You do not have to continuously evoke it. While chanting, it is a struggle enough to hear the sound vibration of the holy name. It will come. If we precede our chanting with that prayerful mood, it will come back and we will remember it during our chanting. When it comes, then we can again feel that helpless dependency and call for mercy. We should welcome that. However, if it is not there, then just continue to focus on the holy name.

It is difficult to maintain that feeling of intense prayer, repentance, and helplessness. Of course, the struggle to hear is in itself a state of helplessness. By the mere fact that we are endeavoring and struggling to hear is proof that we are helpless. If we had the strength to do it by ourselves, then there would be no difficulty. However, because Kṛṣṇa is in His holy name and He is independent and does as He wishes, He also has to agree to appear in His name. We can call out again and again and again, but He has to agree to appear in our minds. If we want to remember Him and hear Him, then we have to show Him that we have that desire. He will then help.

*ananyāś cintayanto māṁ*  
*ye janāḥ paryupāsate*  
*teṣāṁ nityābhiyuktānāṁ*  
*yoga-kṣemaṁ vahāmy aham*

**“But those who always worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on My transcendental form—to them I carry what they lack, and I preserve what they have.” (Bg. 9.22)**

If we are lacking the ability to remember, then Kṛṣṇa will appear and will carry what we lack. We will then feel a sense of gratitude, being unable to do it by our own efforts.

This reminds me of when I was in Māyāpura when the big Pañca-tattva deities were being installed. Everyone had an intense feeling and hankering to see Pañca-tattva. Finally when the curtains opened, the kīrtana reached a crescendo and devotees were chanting in tears, crying. I was feeling such ecstasy, and could not imagine that such ecstasy was accessible. I realized afterwards, “How can I feel so much pleasure, unless Śrīla Prabhupāda was pleased!? There is no way! There is nothing I did that qualified me to feel so much pleasure upon chanting the glories of Pañca-tattva, and upon beholding Their beautiful form. What qualifications do I have to experience this? Somehow, Prabhupāda must have been pleased by the effort that the devotees had made.”

*bhajanīya-parama-sukha-*  
*mātra-sva-sukhatvam*

(From Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī’s Sandarbha, as quoted in the Purport of Bhāg. 2.3.10)

As explained in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, we experience pleasure to the degree that Kṛṣṇa is pleased. Similarly, by pleasing the spiritual master, we feel some reciprocation. Thus, we should remember Kṛṣṇa and realize that Kṛṣṇa is so kind that He has enabled us to hear, even if only for a moment.

Similarly, when Nārada Muni was sitting in the forest and meditating upon the Lord within his heart, the Lord appeared to him and said, “O Nārada, this is the last time you are going to see Me in this life. The more you hanker for Me, the more that whatever residual desires are there within your heart will be burned away and destroyed.”

Thus Kṛṣṇa sometimes appears for a fleeting moment. We get some reciprocation, but then it disappears. However, it is meant to awaken within us that hankering. Without hankering, it is very difficult to maintain our endeavor on the path. Prabhupāda says in Caitanya-caritāmṛta that it is very difficult to advance unless one feels reciprocation from Kṛṣṇa within the heart.

Nārada Muni says to Vyāsa in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam:

**“One who has forsaken his material occupations to engage in the devotional service of the Lord may sometimes fall down while in an immature stage, yet there is no danger of his being unsuccessful. On the other hand, a nondevotee, though fully engaged in occupational duties, does not gain anything.” (Bhāg. 1.5.17)**

**“My dear Vyāsa, even though a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa sometimes falls down somehow or other, he certainly does not undergo material existence like others \[fruitive workers, etc.\] because a person who has once relished the taste of the lotus feet of the Lord can do nothing but remember that ecstasy again and again.” (Bhāg. 1.5.19)**

Prabhupāda explains that one little drop can inundate the whole world. Even though we may not be able to remember, if we go on endeavoring, then when that remembrance comes, we will feel some gratitude and satisfaction.

*bhaktiḥ pareśānubhavo viraktir*  
*anyatra caiṣa trika eka-kālaḥ*  
*prapadyamānasya yathāśnataḥ syus*  
*tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭiḥ kṣud-apāyo ’nu-ghāsam*

**“Devotion, direct experience of the Supreme Lord, and detachment from other things—these three occur simultaneously for one who has taken shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in the same way that pleasure, nourishment and relief from hunger come simultaneously and increasingly, with each bite, for a person engaged in eating.” (Bhāg. 11.2.42)**

Prabhupāda said in one letter:

Regarding your last question about the ecstatic symptoms of chanting Hare Krishna, you should know that the Hare Krishna Mantra has an equal effect upon all devotees. Just like the sunshine has an equal effect on everyone, but when it is covered, the sunshine has a different effect. Similarly, the influence of the Hare Krishna Mantra becomes manifest when one is no longer covered by the ten offenses to chanting. The more we become free from the ten offenses, the more the effect of chanting becomes manifested through us. Everyone can become a great devotee, being freed from the offenses 100%, simply by one's determination and effort. (Letter to Arundhatī dāsī—New Vṛndāvan, June 16, 1969)

Our sampradāya-ācārya has given us such powerful quotes on chanting. Kṛṣṇa reciprocates with our one hundred percent determination and effort. He says (Bg. 4.11): “As they surrender, I reward them accordingly.” By our one hundred percent surrender, we get reciprocation. With that reciprocation, we can enter into devotional service. However, we cannot enter into devotional service unless Kṛṣṇa very kindly manifests. By the flow of devotional service, He manifests down from Rādhārāṇī and comes down through the sampradāya and appears before us. We cannot enter into devotional service unless it comes down to us. We are therefore beggars for that achievement. We are not achievers.

Kṛṣṇa says:

*yoginām api sarveṣāṁ*  
*mad-gatenāntar-ātmanā*  
*śraddhāvān bhajate yo māṁ*  
*sa me yuktatamo mataḥ*

**“And of all yogīs, the one with great faith who always abides in Me, thinks of Me within himself, and renders transcendental loving service to Me—he is the most intimately united with Me in yoga and is the highest of all. That is My opinion.” (Bg. 6.47)**

Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains that the sādhaka wants Kṛṣṇa’s pleasure and Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. Feeling unqualified, he knows he is incapable of obtaining it himself. Therefore with one hundred percent determination and conviction, he accepts everything favorable for devotional service and rejects everything unfavorable. He calls out to Kṛṣṇa in the helpless state. Kṛṣṇa then assures his success.

**Question: What prayer should we offer to remove the fault-finding mentality?**

It is good to first offer prayers spoken by the ācāryas. However, devotees can also pray in their own words. For example, they can say something as follows:

“I am fallen. I am finding faults with Vaiṣṇavas. I know that if I continue to fault-find, You will remove me from their association. I can think of nothing more unfortunate than to be kicked away from the association of Vaiṣṇavas. Understanding my fallen condition, my Lord, I open my mouth and heart to You. Please teach me the ways of devotional service. Teach me how to become a Vaiṣṇava. Please enter into the core of my heart and uproot these sinful desires. Please protect me, so that I can always live in the association of Your devotees. Please help me to overcome these obstacles. By my own efforts I can achieve nothing. Only by Your mercy can I possibly overcome the obstacles to my spiritual life. And although I have no qualification to even ask this of You, still I have no other hope. If I cannot come to You and reveal my heart, then I have no other hope in my life and cannot make progress in devotional service. I therefore surrender myself to Your will, if You so desire to help me overcome these obstacles. Please enter into my heart and rip them out. I know when You begin to rip them out, it will be painful. But if that pain comes as a result of Your mercy, it will be my happiness. Please be merciful unto me.”

Pray like this before beginning your japa. Place yourself in a position of complete dependence on the holy name. Doing so is how a devotee overcomes obstacles in devotional service. The Lord’s holy name will act, being the most merciful manifestation of Kṛṣṇa

**Question: How can we tune our mind so that the chanting of japa does not become a secondary activity to our other duties?**

We must hear the glories of the holy name. By so doing, we will appreciate the great value of the holy name and develop the right attitude in chanting.

Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says that there are three requirements to be fulfilled if one wants to make progress in chanting: one should chant with devotees who have faith—with those who know the value of the holy name; one should chant in a place that is free from both external and internal distractions; and one should have great determination. A place free from external and internal distractions means that one should not chant in a place that is going to make him think about something else besides chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa. For example, one should not chant behind the steering wheel of the car, in front of the computer screen, while listening to radio, while watching television, or in one’s office where he works every day. One should chant in that place where there is no opportunity to distract him from his most important business of chanting. He should sit in one place and chant his rounds. He should not chant three rounds and then get up and do something else. Then a couple of hours later chant a few more rounds, and continue with this cycle.

Sometimes in the temple there are some duties that are unavoidable. However, the devotee should always be looking for the first opportunity to sit in one place and chant his rounds. He thus removes himself from both external and internal distractions. To remove those distractions from our chanting, determination is required. What saps away our determination and sucks it dry is the contemplation of the objects of the senses. The example is given in the Bhāgavatam that just like the reeds on the lake gradually suck up all the water from the lake and make it dry, similarly, when we sit in complete absorption in meditation upon all our material desires, it saps away our determination. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains in Bhaktyāloka that to the degree we associate with our material desires, to that degree we lose our firm faith in the goal of devotional service. Sometimes even after prolonged sādhana, a person will give it up having lost their faith due to their loss of determination. Determination is very important and comes from association. We are always dependent upon getting good association.

**Question: What is the best physical position for chanting japa?**

Girirāja Mahārāja told me that Prabhupāda told him that for chanting japa, the number one position is sitting down. The number two position, if you cannot stay sitting down, is standing. And the number three position is walking.

## Achieving Perfection

We will discuss positive absorptions in chanting the holy name. It is definitely easier to chant in the association of other devotees than to chant by oneself. Śrīla Prabhupāda has given the following jewel:

Regarding your question, about living alone, living alone is a general tendency for a person who wants to get disassociated with the materialistic persons. That is also recommended by the Goswamis in their instructions. It is better to remain alone than to mix with materialistic persons. But this is not applicable when we have the opportunity to get the association of pure devotees. Our program is negative and positive simultaneously. We want to negate the materialistic side and make positive the spiritual side, it is not one sided. If you have no positive standing, negating only will not make you successful. Therefore it is better to remain positively within the society of pure devotees. That is also recommended by the Goswamis. That one should be occupied in activities in the modes of goodness and associate with spiritualistic persons, that will make one's advancement very quick.

Persons who want to take advantage of cheap reputation they imitate great personalities like Haridasa Thakura, who was alone chanting 300,000 of Holy Names daily. By such chanting, lonely chanting he got so much spiritual power that he could convert even a harlot to become a great devotee whereas an ordinary person falls easily a victim to such allurement. So one should not imitate such great personalities but one should try to see how much taste he has developed for chanting, so that one can remain alone simply being engaged in chanting. If one can remain alone simply being engaged in chanting, that is very good, but it is difficult also. A conditioned soul in conditioned life it is very difficult to concentrate our mind in chanting absolutely. Better to be engaged in preaching work, that will make one gradually successful. Besides that, when we are actually engaged in with the preaching work, we gradually acquire our spiritual strength without failure. (Letter to Śivānanda dāsa—Los Angeles, November 11, 1968)

We should not imitate and chant alone. We should chant with other devotees. We should not try to get cheap adoration. We should try to see how much taste we have developed for chanting. Until we actually get that taste, we are very much dependent upon others in getting strength and help.

Therefore, it is often recommended for devotees to chant with others. However, Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura does say in Harināma Cintāmaṇi that it is very good to go to a secluded place and if necessary, to put a chādar over your head. If you are strong enough to remain fixed in your chanting, then certainly it is beneficial. If one has taste, he will not fall victim to distractions. However, without sufficient taste, this is very difficult and therefore it is superior for such devotees to acquire that taste by association.

Prabhupāda gives the example that it is very easy to break one stick. But if you take that one stick and bundle many other sticks with it, it is very difficult to break that one stick. Similarly, when we are performing our sādhana activities in a collective group, it gives us more strength and pressure.

Of course, we should also be very careful that we are not performing our sādhana simply for some reputation (pratiṣṭhā) or puja, which are anarthas. However, when we see everybody else is sitting and chanting, we find ourselves also sitting and chanting and tolerating the pain that might before have just caused us to walk out of the temple room and go talk to somebody, or to do something else. That kind of pressure is good and can be utilized for positive absorption.

Anything that will help us to take shelter and to become absorbed in the holy name should be accepted as favorable. The principle of surrender is to accept everything favorable for executing devotional service, and to reject everything unfavorable. Thus sometimes it is beneficial to chant in unison in a group with other devotees who have acquired some taste.

The following is the translation of a bhajana about the holy name, Keno Hare Kṛṣṇa Nām.

“Oh, why does my heart not weep from chanting the holy names Hare Kṛṣṇa?”

“The bird of my heart does not know what past sinful activities it has committed to cause this inability to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa properly.”

“O forest bird! I have kept something for you very carefully within the cottage of my heart—the holy name of Lord Hari, which is overflowing with pure sweet honey. O bird, you could learn the chanting of this name if you were taught.”

“A bird is easily able to speak all names; why then does this bird of my heart refuse to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa? Oh, why does my heart not weep from chanting the holy names Hare Kṛṣṇa?”

“O bird! Come, let us go to the spiritual world, the land of true and everlasting beauty. It is the place where the imaginary man of my mind will never again come and go on the revolving cycle of birth and death.”

“O bird! At the time of death, your body will simply be placed upon a funeral stretcher, lifted on the shoulders of four persons and carried to the cremation grounds.”

“Alas! The cremation fire will then enter your mouth and totally consume your tongue. There will be nothing you can do to save yourself, for at that time it is too late—you will be unable to speak any more.”

This bhajana speaks for itself. It is meant to impress upon us the importance of chanting. For a sādhaka, chanting is our lifeline.

Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains in Harināma Cintāmaṇi that there are two realities in this material world: the jīva and the holy name. Everything else is simply illusion. He explains that everything that exists as an object has four characteristics: name, form, qualities and activities. The holy name is the jīva’s first introduction or connection to Kṛṣṇa. Once we make that connection with the holy name, then gradually through the chanting of the holy name, everything else is revealed—the form, qualities, and activities of the Lord.

We do not have the eyes to see Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa tells Arjuna in the Bhagavad-gītā, “You see Me standing before you because I am giving you the eyes by which you can see Me. You cannot see Me any other way—not by austerities, not by studying the Vedas, and not by charity. These things are not sufficient in themselves to enable you to see Me. Only by undivided devotional service can I be seen as I am, standing before you. Thus you are entering into the mysteries of understanding Me.”

It is described in the Sixth Canto of the Bhāgavatam that the fundamental religious system for the Age of Kali is the chanting of the holy name of the Lord. This is the activity by which we can establish our link with Kṛṣṇa. There are many verses given in the scriptures that praise the importance of the holy name and its relevance, specifically for the Age of Kali. The following is one such verse:

*kaler doṣa-nidhe rājann*  
*asti hy eko mahān guṇaḥ*  
*kīrtanād eva kṛṣṇasya*  
*mukta-saṅgaḥ paraṁ vrajet*

**“My dear King, although Kali-yuga is an ocean of faults, there is still one good quality about this age: Simply by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, one can become free from material bondage and be promoted to the transcendental kingdom.” (Bhāg. 12.3.51)**

In this Age of Kali, the Lord descended to make the process so simple and easily accessible for those who have taken birth in the iron age, which is the age of quarrel, in which man is short lived, quarrelsome, lazy, misguided, unlucky, and above all always, disturbed.

*mandāḥ sumanda-matayo*  
*manda-bhāgyā hy upadrutāḥ*

(Bhāg. 1.1.10)

The Lord is the Kali-yuga avatara. Lord Caitanya came to make this chanting of Hare Kṛṣṇa the means for revealing not only Kṛṣṇa, but for attaining the topmost form of devotional service, which is ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.

Lord Caitanya says in Caitanya-caritāmṛta:

*yuga-dharma pravartāimu nāma-saṅkīrtana*  
*cāri bhāva-bhakti diyā nācāmu bhuvana*

**“I shall personally inaugurate the religion of the age—nāma-saṅkīrtana, the congregational chanting of the holy name. I shall make the world dance in ecstasy, realizing the four mellows of loving devotional service.” (Cc. Ādi 3.19)**

In this Age of Kali, Lord Caitanya has come to give the topmost form of devotional service. One gets the opportunity to render direct service to the Lord in the spiritual world, Goloka Vṛndāvana, according to his eternal relationship with the Lord. This is all revealed by nāma, the holy name, if one understands that he can capture just a fragment of its meaning, relevance and importance, and if one takes into consideration being bound in the material world, undergoing repeated birth, death, disease and old age.

Often, many anomalies of Kali-yuga are described, such as the ill omens, ill activities and the fallen condition of its residents. However, the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam glorifies Kali-yuga, because in Kali-yuga, Lord Caitanya has made the process for going back home, back to Godhead so simple. Simply by coming in contact with the holy name of the Lord, one can achieve all perfection in life.

The importance of achieving this perfection is that we not only attain liberation, but we can enter into the spiritual world.

*kīrtanād eva kṛṣṇasya*  
*mukta-saṅgaḥ paraṁ vrajet*

(Bhāg. 12.3.51)

Mukta, liberation, referred to here is not simply to become free from repeated birth and death. Such liberation can be achieved even by nāmābhāsa. However, in this Age of Kali, Lord Caitanya has come to distribute the holy name, which is imbued by ecstatic love of Godhead, which bestows the benediction of giving pure love of God to anyone who sincerely takes up this chanting, and comes to the platform of chanting the holy name of the Lord offenselessly. It is a life mission if one understands the fortune of seeing the importance of progressing along the path of chanting the holy name of the Lord. It is our lifeline; it is our connection and our means for achieving the topmost goal—kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ.

As Lord Caitanya describes in His Śikṣāṣṭaka.

*tṛṇād api su-nīcena*  
*taror iva sahiṣṇunā*  
*amāninā māna-dena*  
*kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ*

**“One should chant the holy name of the Lord in a humble state of mind, thinking oneself lower than the straw in the street; one should be more tolerant than a tree, devoid of all sense of false prestige, and should be ready to offer all respect to others. In such a state of mind one can chant the holy name of the Lord constantly.” (Śrī Śrī Śikṣāṣṭaka, Verse 3)**

We have such a great fortune and opportunity in this lifetime to achieve what in other lifetimes was practically impossible. Not only was it practically impossible, but it would take many lifetimes to achieve. In previous ages, it would have taken thousands and thousands of years in meditation (sixty to seventy thousand years). However, in this Age of Kali, it only takes one lifetime.

Prabhupāda was once asked the question: “Śrīla Prabhupāda, if we don’t go back to Godhead in this life, will you come back and get us?”

Prabhupāda said, “Yes, but don’t take advantage of it. Don’t make your spiritual master come back.” Therefore, we have to achieve it in this one life.

Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says, “It will be too late on the funeral stretcher. You will not be able to speak anymore.”

*kabe ha’be bolo se-dina āmār*  
*aparādha ghuci’, śuddha nāme ruci,*  
*kṛpā-bale ha’be hṛdoye sañcār*  
*kabe ha’be bolo se-dina āmār*  
*tṛṇādhika hīna, kabe nije māni’,*  
*sahiṣṇutā-guṇa hṛdoyete āni’*  
*sakale mānada, āpani amānī,*  
*ho’ye āswādibo nāma-rasa-sār*

\[Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura prays\]: “When, oh when will that day be mine? When taste for the Holy Name increasing, when my offenses will be ceasing, when in my heart will your mercy shine, when, oh when will that day be mine?

“When will I be humbler than a blade of grass, more tolerant than a tree. When will my mind attain that tranquility? Ready to give honor to everyone else, not expecting any honor for myself. When, oh when will that day be mine?” (Kabe Ha’be Bolo, verses 1-2)

Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura is describing intense hankering. If we do not hanker in this way, then it will be too late. Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says in Keno Hare Kṛṣṇa Nam:

“The bird of my heart does not know what past sinful activities it has committed to cause this inability to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa properly. O forest bird! I have kept something for you very carefully within the cottage of my heart—the holy name of Lord Hari, which is overflowing with pure sweet honey. O bird, you could learn the chanting of this name if you were taught. A bird is easily able to speak all names; why then does this bird of my heart refuse to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa? Oh, why does my heart not weep from chanting the holy names Hare Kṛṣṇa? O bird! Come, let us go to the spiritual world, the land of true and everlasting beauty. It is the place where the imaginary man of my mind will never again come and go on the revolving cycle of birth and death. O bird! At the time of death, your body will simply be placed upon a funeral stretcher, lifted on the shoulders of four persons and carried to the cremation grounds. Alas! The cremation fire will then enter your mouth and totally consume your tongue. There will be nothing you can do to save yourself, for at that time it is too late—you will be unable to speak any more.”

The conclusion of this bhajana speaks for itself. It is meant to try to awaken within us that impetus to dedicate each day of our lives to improving the quality of our chanting of Hare Kṛṣṇa. Such is a sādhaka—somebody who is trying to increase his faith. He keeps the association of devotees who help him increase his faith. He molds his life in such a way that he is not simply working to maintain the body for sense enjoyment.

As described in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, life’s desires should never be directed towards sense gratification. One should desire to live only because the human form of life enables him to inquire about the Absolute Truth. When we put the holy name as the center of our life, or as our connection or link to Kṛṣṇa, then everything else becomes a support—even our work that we perform each day, such as maintenance of the family. This is gauṇa-dharma. Gauṇa means secondary, but it is the support to our chanting of the holy name of the Lord.

Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura explains this in his Vaiṣṇava-siddhānta-mala. His description will help impress upon us this point about chanting constantly.

“Mahāprabhu’s order is simply this—that everyone should incessantly chant harināma. Incessantly chant harināma—the meaning of this command is not that people should always chant the holy name while completely desisting from all bodily activities, household duties, and dealings with others. By ceasing all actions of bodily maintenance, the body will be destroyed in a short while. In the context of this command, then, how should one engage in harinām? Since the Lord gave humanity the command to incessantly take the holy name, then the true meaning is that everyone, whether gṛhastha or sannyāsī, vānaprastha or brahmacārī, brāhmaṇa or kṣatriya, vaiśya or śūdra, low-born or mleccha, and so forth—all people should remain in their respective situations and chant harināma. Verily this is the only meaning. It is necessary to nicely remain in one’s own natural situation because that position facilitates the proper performance of one’s activities for bodily maintenance, and thus the body will not expire untimely. Bodily maintenance requires dealing with others. It is essential that all such actions be observed in a pure and undisturbed fashion. Then all of these things will be conducted very nicely…” (Vaiṣṇava-Siddhānta-Mālā, Chapter 3)

To incessantly chant Hare Kṛṣṇa—kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ—is the goal as described in the Bhāgavatam: The topmost transcendentalists who are situated on the topmost platform are always chanting the glories of the Supreme Lord. They have no other topic of discussion than chanting the holy name of the Lord.

Haridāsa Ṭhākura was chanting 300,000 names daily, which is 192 rounds. To chant constantly, as Haridāsa Ṭhākura did, we cannot imitate. Therefore, Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says that kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ means that whatever position one is in, he should see that the goal is to chant. Chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa is the most important. It is our connection to Kṛṣṇa, and the means for deliverance. Kṛṣṇa says:

*anta-kāle ca mām eva*  
*smaran muktvā kalevaram*

**“Anyone who at the time of death remembers Me alone, he at once attains My nature. Of this there is no doubt.” (Bg. 8.5)**

This is exemplified in the story of Ajāmila who called upon the name of Nārāyaṇa at the time of death. Although he called out the name Nārāyaṇa, referring to his son, having remembered this name of the Lord, he was delivered. The Viṣṇudūtas came and protected him from the Yamadūtas. A discussion ensued, and since the time for Ajāmila to be removed from the body had not come yet, he heard that discourse and became further purified. When the Viṣṇudūtas were successful in convincing the Yamadūtas to leave Ajāmila alone, Ajāmila was convinced to go to the sacred places of pilgrimage and to dedicate the rest of his life in worshiping and serving the Lord. He thus did this, and when the time of death came again, the same Viṣṇudūtas came back, but they came alone. The Yamadūtas did not come with them. All of this occurred simply because Ajāmila called out the name of Nārāyaṇa at the time of death. Such is the power of the holy name of the Lord.

Previously when Prabhupāda was publishing the Bhāgavatam, there were only 10,000 to 20,000 copies printed at a time. However, when the Sixth Canto came out with the story about Ajāmila, the first printing was approximately of 100,000 copies. Prabhupāda wanted that canto to go out en masse so that everyone could see the potency of the holy name of the Lord through the story of Ajāmila, who had led a very degraded life filled with sinful activities.

For one who understands the importance of the holy name, he maintains his body accordingly. With his eyes, he sees the form of the Lord. With his ears, he hears the hari-kathā about the Lord and the transcendental vibration from the lips of the devotees of the Lord. With his tongue he vibrates the holy name of the Lord. It may be a struggle, but at least every day he sees it as the most important. Therefore, everything else that he does in relationship to maintenance of the body is simply a support to its primary goal in life: to make progress along the path of devotional service.

Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura goes on to explain:

When Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu was preaching the first command of Śrīman Mahāprabhu, He spoke in the following manner:

*kohena prabhur ājñā ḍākiyā ḍākiyā*  
*“bolo ‘kṛṣṇa’, bhajo kṛṣṇa, loho kṛṣṇa nām*  
*kṛṣṇa mātā, kṛṣṇa pitā, kṛṣṇa dhana-prāṇ*  
*tomā sabā lāgiyā kṛṣṇer avatār*  
*heno kṛṣṇa bhaja, saba chāḍo anācār”*

Nityānanda and Haridāsa repeated the Lord’s command by calling out to everyone, “Chant Kṛṣṇa, worship Kṛṣṇa, and accept Kṛṣṇa’s holy name from others. Kṛṣṇa is your mother, Kṛṣṇa is your father, and Kṛṣṇa is the treasure of your life-breath. Kṛṣṇa has incarnated just for your benefit, so please worship this merciful Kṛṣṇa and give up all sinful activities.” (Śrī Caitanya Bhāgavata, Madhya 13.82-84, as quoted in Vaiṣṇava-Siddhānta-Mālā, Chapter 3)

Prabhupāda explains that one can work to maintain the body, but he minimizes his activities that are meant for sense enjoyment. He minimizes the demands of the body and he accepts what is necessary to maintain the body so that his life does not become too encumbered and he forgets that chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa must be performed every day.

If one understands that this is the most important activity, he will appreciate the value of chanting, and then when it comes time to sit down and chant japa, he will realize that he has to make quality time for it. Every morning when we wake up, we have the urge to eat so we can have sufficient strength. Similarly, we should understand that for spiritual strength, we need spiritual food. We should keep our life in spiritual focus, and not let ourselves become dragged down by all the other demands.

Prahlāda Mahārāja instructed his classmates that they should not wait until they get old to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa. Rather they should do it now when their body is young.

Prabhupāda also said, “At any moment when you realize the importance of the holy name—either now when your body is young, or at any other moment—you must take up to chanting. Otherwise life will pass you by.”

We have to be convinced and committed to this as an everyday affair. Even if one cannot complete sixteen rounds, he has to be convinced that every day he has to take shelter, and fix his mind despite all other thoughts and distractions. Those who are householders have a greater impetus. Sometimes devotees living in the temple, if they are not careful and are not actively engaged, can be idle. They might not understand and appreciate the great value or importance they have to be able to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa, without the pressures of living outside and maintaining life outside the temple. They can take it cheaply. As soon as one takes it cheaply, or becomes a little bit familiar and minimizes its importance, then he will find himself not having the facility to be able to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa. Whereas those who are living outside have the opportunity to realize that they have to make some quality time every day to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa and remember Kṛṣṇa.

Prabhupāda wrote in a letter:

You are a devotee, and so Krishna will protect you. Always think that Krishna is with you. He is present in His name, so you are always associating with Him. (Letter to Annada devī dāsī—Bombay, November 25, 1974)

He also wrote:

Every one of you should be thoroughly convinced of the power of the Hare Krsna mantra to protect you in all circumstances and chant accordingly at all times without offense. Then advancement will be swift and you will gradually come to see everything clearly so that you may act for the pleasure of the Lord without uncertainty. When one is spontaneously engaged in this way, always in the service of the Lord and anxious to avoid all mundane activities, he is actually experiencing the taste of bliss in Krsna consciousness. (Letter to Dāmodara dāsa—Allahabad, India, Janaury 10, 1970)

These activities are not meant to be mundane. The maintenance of the body is meant to be dovetailed so that one can utilize the human form of life to get the maximum benefit of being able to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa every day and make progress in the cultivation of his faith.

Therefore, one should chant in an environment that is free from distractions. There are many different types of distractions. Unfortunately devotees find themselves chanting in places that are not the most conducive, such as while driving. Sometimes it is unavoidable. I do not wish to demean devotees who have been reduced to having to chant in situations like that. However, if devotees understand the importance, then they can at least make the effort and cultivate the desire to chant in an environment free from distractions. Effort must be there, and the desire to have the facility to chant must be there. Kṛṣṇa is powerful and capable of reciprocating, and thus He can create a facility for us to chant in a distraction-free environment.

Chanting is something that we have to cultivate. Kṛṣṇa says in the Bhagavad-gītā (12.9): “My dear Arjuna, O winner of wealth, if you cannot fix your mind upon Me without deviation, then follow the regulative principles of bhakti-yoga. In this way develop a desire to attain Me.”

In Śrī Upadeśāmṛta, Śrīla Prabhupāda explains that devotional service is cultivation of the heart and of desire. That desire which is the eternal companion of the soul needs to be cultivated. Therefore there has to be prayer and the desire. Man proposes and God disposes. Kṛṣṇa gives us that opportunity. All of a sudden we will find that we have some opportunity to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa in a distraction-free environment. If we have not been praying for it, we might not be able to recognize it when the opportunity is there. When we do recognize it, we will chant with gratitude, and then the chanting will become more meaningful. First there is humility, and then dependence, faith and finally gratitude.

*yasyāham anugṛhṇāmi*  
*hariṣye tad-dhanaṁ śanaiḥ*

(Bhāg. 10.88.8)

Sometimes Kṛṣṇa is very merciful to somebody by taking everything away. This is seen in the example of Nārada Muni, whose mother was bitten by a snake. Nārada Muni was a five year old boy and was left with nobody to protect him. He took it as divine arrangement and wandered off into the forest looking for the Supreme Lord. Sometimes circumstances happen beyond our control, but we have to see that Kṛṣṇa is putting us in this situation to bring us closer to Him. We should see our good fortune in this and be grateful. Kṛṣṇa will not neglect or forget such a surrendered soul. Then our chanting becomes meaningful. If we are well-practiced and try to make an effort to create an environment that is free from distractions, then Kṛṣṇa will help.

## Higher Taste

Prabhupāda said that the most important instruction of the spiritual master is to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa. My understanding is that when the spiritual master gives us the holy name, he is giving us the means for achieving the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. As it is stated in Caitanya-caritāmṛta (Cc. Ādi 7.73):

*kṛṣṇa-mantra haite habe saṁsāra-mocana*  
*kṛṣṇa-nāma haite pābe kṛṣṇera caraṇa*

The holy name will bring one to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. This verse helps us to understand that the spiritual master who bestows the holy name is giving us the means by giving us the pure holy name. We have to have faith that in that name everything can be revealed.

In His instructions to Rūpa Gosvāmī, Lord Caitanya has given the example of the bhakti-latā-bīja, which is the seed that has been planted in the heart and requires watering. In the same way, while the holy name can bestow all perfection and bring one to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, in order to have the proper conception of the holy name, one has to continue to water the holy name. The watering is the process of hearing from the Vaiṣṇavas.

There is a verse in Caitanya-caritāmṛta, which says: “One must learn the truth and beauty of the Lord’s holy name by hearing the revealed scriptures from the mouths of Vaiṣṇavas. There is no other way to taste the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa’s name.” Once the holy name is given, we have to continue to water the holy name by hearing its glories from the mouths of Vaiṣṇavas. Therefore, we are dependent upon the spiritual master and the Vaiṣṇavas to bring us to the point of full fructification of what the holy name can deliver. We have to continue the watering process by hearing the glories of the name. If we do not hear the glories of the name from the mouths of the Vaiṣṇavas, then we begin to minimize the holy name, and we take it for granted. We would like to obtain the desired result by chanting, but if we are neglectful in our chanting, if we are not very mindful in our chanting, if we are not struggling to overcome anarthas, and if we stay on the platform of nāma-aparādha, then:

*bahu janma kare yadi śravaṇa, kīrtana*  
*tabu ta’ nā pāya kṛṣṇa-pade prema-dhana*

(Cc. Ādi, 8.16)

**One can go on chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra for millions of births, but he will never get love of Godhead, which is the ultimate goal of chanting.**

Thus we have to be able to have the proper conception of the holy name by hearing the glories of the holy name from the mouths of Vaiṣṇavas. We are dependent upon our spiritual master to continue the watering process, and to help us gain the proper conception of the holy name. Then we will not become too familiar with the holy name, and will always have faith by hearing the glories of the holy name.

**Question: What does it mean to become too familiar with the holy name?**

It means to be inattentive. One type of anartha is called tattva vibhrama—to be bewildered about the conclusions of tattva. According to the statements of the śāstra, one of the types of anarthas is to not be aware of the obstacles on the path of advancing in the chanting of the holy name of the Lord. We should not keep ourselves in illusion by being unaware of the obstacles we have to overcome. By knowing the different dangers, then we can avoid them.

Sometimes when devotees first begin chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa overlooks the offenses, because they do not know of them and therefore they taste some wonderful bliss. However, after some time, if they are not careful, they become a little familiar, and they do not take advantage of the knowledge that becomes available to them to learn more about the pitfalls. After some time, Kṛṣṇa does not overlook the offenses so easily and one loses his taste. When one loses his taste, it is very difficult to chant. Thus this familiarity leads one to not always endeavor to have the proper conception of the holy name of the Lord and to minimize the importance of chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa.

It is very important for us to know about the ten offenses to the holy name of the Lord. Even if one loses his taste for chanting, the holy name of the Lord can still bring one back to obtain a taste for chanting. The following from Mādhurya Kaḍambinī, Third Nectar Shower talks about a person who commits an offense and loses the mercy of the holy name:

The case of the offender losing the mercy of the name is similar to a subordinate who is offensive to his vastly wealthy and capable master. The master treats him indifferently and denies him proper care. As a result that servant comes to suffer poverty and distresses of all sorts. One should know that every master neglects a servant who is offensive and no one else is capable of helping him (karma, jñāna, yoga, etc.). If the offending servant again puts himself at the beck and call of his master, the master gradually shows mercy, and that person’s sufferings are step by step eliminated. In the same way, the offending devotee at first suffers some miseries. As he again does sincere service to the devotees, the śāstras, and guru, the name gradually manifests mercy and eliminates his evil tendencies. Thus one cannot argue against the gradual elimination of anartha.

Someone may argue that he has never made any aparādhas, so why is he not getting the full mercy of the name? He should not make such statements. Maybe he didn’t make the aparādhas recently. He may have done them in the past, but one can infer the existence of aparādhas by their effect. The effect is that a person will not manifest any symptoms of premā while doing nāma-kīrtana as described in the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam:

*tad aśma-sāraṁ hṛdayaṁ batedaṁ*  
*yad gṛhyamāṇair hari-nāma-dheyaiḥ*  
*na vikriyetātha yadā vikāro*  
*netre jalaṁ gātra-ruheṣu harṣaḥ*

**Certainly that heart is steel-framed which, in spite of one’s chanting the holy name of the Lord with concentration, does not change when ecstasy takes place, tears fill the eyes and the hairs stand on end. (Bhāg. 2.3.24)**

In other words, this is the symptom. Someone may say, “I have never made any aparādhas!” The effect is that a person will not manifest any symptoms while doing nāma-kīrtana as described in the Bhāgavatam.

Seeing the following verse in Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu on the subject of aparādha, another doubt arises:

*ke te’parādhā vipendra*  
*namno bhagavataḥ krtāḥ*  
*vinighnanti nṛṇāṁ kṛtyaṁ*  
*prākṛtaṁ hyānayanti hi*

“O foremost of brāhmaṇas, what are the offenses against the name of the Lord that can cancel the results of all one’s pious works and lead to a material conception even of spiritual topics?”

In other words, repeatedly hearing and chanting the Lord’s name, qualities and so on should give premā, serving the holy tīrthas should bestow perfection, and repeatedly tasting the ghee, milk, betel and other kinds of the Lord’s prasādam should destroy all desires for sense enjoyment. So what are the great offenses that cancel these fruits and cause all these spiritually potent activities to appear material? This very startling and unnerving question is being raised. If this is so, does it follow that a person who commits nāma-aparādha becomes averse to the Lord and thus cannot even take shelter of guru or perform other devotional service?

This is true. As during a high fever, losing all taste for food, a person finds it impossible to eat. So a person who makes serious aparādhas loses scope for hearing, chanting and other devotional service. There is no doubt about this. However if the fever lessens with time, some taste for food develops. Even then, nourishing foods like milk and rice cannot give their full nourishment to the person suffering from chronic fever. They bestow some benefit, but cannot relieve him of his wasted condition. Nevertheless, medicine and an invalid’s diet can, with time, restore his former health. Then the full potency of normal food can again be utilized by the body. In the same way, after a long period of suffering the effects of aparādha, the intensity reduces slightly and a devotee develops a little taste. Again a devotee becomes fit for bhakti. Repeated doses of hearing and chanting the Lord’s name and other such processes then gradually reveal everything in progression. (Mādhurya Kaḍambinī, Third Nectar Shower)

Thus sometimes a devotee may have previously chanted the name and experienced such a wonderful taste. However, due to offenses, he may have lost that taste. He comes to the point where he cannot even chant. After some time of suffering, he begins to realize that he needs some nourishment. After becoming restored to health by the association with Vaiṣṇavas who are preaching the glories of the holy name of the Lord, by chanting the holy name of the Lord with faith, by hearing the message of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam in the association of devotees, by honoring the Lord’s mahā-prasāda, by taking darśana of the deity of the Lord, he can once again get his hunger back and relish the taste of the holy name of the Lord again. Such is the all merciful nature of the holy name of the Lord. We should never feel hopeless; we should never feel that it is not possible for us to ever obtain the mercy of the Lord. The holy name is so merciful and so forgiving that it gives one access to come back again, even if it will be after some time of possible suffering. However, why should one unnecessarily suffer if he can avoid it?

It is stated in the Bhāgavatam that even though a devotee may fall down, he cannot become a fruitive worker again, because anyone who has gotten a higher taste of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet will not be able to forget it, although he may try again and again and again.

Rūpa Gosvāmī says that if anybody is interested in enjoying friends, family and society, they should not go and see the beautiful form of Govinda, standing on the bank of the Yamunā, because they will not be able to enjoy again. Thus, upon getting that taste, you will eventually realize that all these lower tastes are the source of great suffering, and Kṛṣṇa is going to drag you back to His Lotus feet. You will realize, “I need to chant. I need to take a sick man’s diet and some medicine and get myself healthy again and associate with devotees and chant with faith.” Then there is no prāyaścitta required. One is immediately reinstated in devotional service. Such is its power.

**Question: If one does not have a taste for chanting, what is the inspiration to chant?**

Always look for opportunities to be in the association of devotees who have some attraction for chanting and chant with them. Then we can imbibe their faith and their attraction. That is necessary. One also has to be very careful to avoid offenses, which are the cause of losing one’s taste.

Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura quotes the following verse in his Mādhurya Kaḍambinī:

*visayāviṣṭa cittānāṁ*  
*visṇvāveśaḥ sudurataḥ*  
*vāruṇī dig gataṁ vastu*  
*vrajannaindrīṁ kim āpnuyāt*

**One whose heart is absorbed in materialism is far from obtaining devotion to Viṣṇu. Can a man by going east, obtain something that is in the west?**

Prabhupāda gives the example: How can you make a fire by pouring water on it at the same time? Similarly, how can one get a taste for chanting if he is pursuing the flickering taste of the material world? It is like trying to ignite a fire by pouring water on it at the same time—it is impossible. Thus one has to be very careful to avoid those types of activities that cause us to lose our attraction and our taste for the holy name of the Lord. One of the offenses to the holy name of the Lord is to maintain material attachments even after hearing so many instructions on this matter. This will cause one to lose the taste. However, as previously explained, the holy name of the Lord is so merciful that it will still forgive after we suffer for some period.

## Importance of Saṅkīrtana

*saha-yajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā*  
*purovāca prajāpatiḥ*  
*anena prasaviṣyadhvam*  
*eṣa vo ‘stv iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk*

**In the beginning of creation, the Lord of all creatures sent forth generations of men and demigods, along with sacrifices for Viṣṇu, and blessed them by saying, “Be thou happy by this yajña \[sacrifice\] because its performance will bestow upon you everything desirable for living happily and achieving liberation.” (Bg. 3.10)**

PURPORT

The material creation by the Lord of creatures (Viṣṇu) is a chance offered to the conditioned souls to come back home—back to Godhead. All living entities within the material creation are conditioned by material nature because of their forgetfulness of their relationship to Viṣṇu, or Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The Vedic principles are to help us understand this eternal relation, as it is stated in the Bhagavad-gītā: vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ. The Lord says that the purpose of the Vedas is to understand Him. In the Vedic hymns it is said: patiṁ viśvasyātmeśvaram. Therefore, the Lord of the living entities is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu. In the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam also (2.4.20) Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī describes the Lord as pati in so many ways:

*śriyaḥ patir yajña-patiḥ prajā-patir*  
*dhiyāṁ patir loka-patir dharā-patiḥ*  
*patir gatiś cāndhaka-vṛṣṇi-sātvatāṁ*  
*prasīdatāṁ me bhagavān satāṁ patiḥ*

The prajā-pati is Lord Viṣṇu, and He is the Lord of all living creatures, all worlds, and all beauties, and the protector of everyone. The Lord created this material world to enable the conditioned souls to learn how to perform yajñas (sacrifices) for the satisfaction of Viṣṇu, so that while in the material world they can live very comfortably without anxiety and after finishing the present material body they can enter into the kingdom of God. That is the whole program for the conditioned soul. By performance of yajña, the conditioned souls gradually become Kṛṣṇa conscious and become godly in all respects. In the Age of Kali, the saṅkīrtana-yajña (the chanting of the names of God) is recommended by the Vedic scriptures, and this transcendental system was introduced by Lord Caitanya for the deliverance of all men in this age. Saṅkīrtana-yajña and Kṛṣṇa consciousness go well together. Lord Kṛṣṇa in His devotional form (as Lord Caitanya) is mentioned in the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (11.5.32) as follows, with special reference to the saṅkīrtana-yajña:

*kṛṣṇa-varṇaṁ tviṣākṛṣṇaṁ*  
*sāṅgopāṅgāstra-pārṣadam*  
*yajñaiḥ saṅkīrtana-prāyair*  
*yajanti hi su-medhasaḥ*

“In this Age of Kali, people who are endowed with sufficient intelligence will worship the Lord, who is accompanied by His associates, by performance of saṅkīrtana-yajña.” Other yajñas prescribed in the Vedic literatures are not easy to perform in this Age of Kali, but the saṅkīrtana-yajña is easy and sublime for all purposes, as recommended in Bhagavad-gītā also (9.14).

This verse and commentary by Śrīla Prabhupāda very clearly describe the essence of the meaning of saṅkīrtana. Saṅkīrtana is the congregational chanting of the holy names of the Lord, and is in essence the primary method of satisfying the Supreme Lord in this Age of Kali.

*kaler doṣa-nidhe rājann*  
*asti hy eko mahān guṇaḥ*  
*kīrtanād eva kṛṣṇasya*  
*mukta-saṅgaḥ paraṁ vrajet*

**Although Kali-yuga is an ocean of faults, there is still one good quality about this age: Simply by chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra, one can become free from material bondage and be promoted to the transcendental kingdom. (Bhāg. 12.3.51)**

Sacrifice means to perform activities for the satisfaction of the Supreme Lord, and it must be voluntary. So many people are voluntarily making sacrifices in this world to obtain various goals in life. The essence of the soul is desire. To fulfill one’s desires, he has to perform some type of sacrifice. It may appear that one has very easily fulfilled his desires in this life; however, it was achieved only by the result of performances of sacrifices in a previous life. It is possible that one performed many pious activities in the previous life and therefore in this life he gets a high birth, a lot of wealth, or some high position. According to the teachings of the scriptures, it is understood that whatever one achieves in this life is the result of activities performed in the previous life. Thus, whatever activities we perform in this life will determine our next life.

Kṛṣṇa explains in the Bhagavad-gītā that the living entity carries his different conceptions from one body to the next just as the air carries aroma from one place to the next. Thus, whatever conceptions of life we develop in this lifetime will determine what will be our destination in our next life.
