It is understood that the human form of life is a rare and valuable gift, because in the human form of life, we can voluntarily accept sacrifice, and by dint of those austerities or sacrifices, we can acquire a higher position in our next life.

Kṛṣṇa says in the Bhagavad-gītā (2.42-43): “Men of small knowledge are very much attached to the flowery words of the Vedas, which recommend various fruitive activities for elevation to heavenly planets, resultant good birth, power, and so forth. Being desirous of sense gratification and opulent life, they say that there is nothing more than this.”

Kṛṣṇa also says:

*vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyo*  
*vedānta-kṛd veda-vid eva cāham*

**“By all the Vedas I am to be known. Indeed I am the compiler of Vedānta, and I am the knower of the Vedas.” (Bg. 15.15)**

Thus, the goal of all sacrifices is ultimately to know who Kṛṣṇa is. One who understands this, voluntarily accepts this method by which he can please the Supreme Lord.

It is described in the Vedas that there are different sacrifices that need to be performed according to the different ages. In Satya-yuga, when the duration of life is very long (hundreds of thousands of years), the means to achieve perfection is by performance of meditation. In Tretā-yuga, when the duration of life is also many thousands of years, the prescribed method is the performance of big sacrifices. Dvāpara-yuga is the following age, for which the method for satisfying the Lord is by performance of elaborate temple worship. Finally, in Kali-yuga, which is the present age, the duration of life is very short and is becoming even shorter. It is therefore very difficult to perform elaborate types of sacrifices or to perform meditation for thousands of years such as were performed in Satya-yuga. Thus, as described in Caitanya-caritāmṛta, one of the purposes for which the Lord appeared was to introduce the method of congregational chanting in the Age of Kali as the primary sacrifice or yuga-dharma.

Lord Caitanya says:

*yuga-dharma pravartāimu nāma-saṅkīrtana*  
*cāri bhāva-bhakti diyā nācāmu bhuvana*

**“I shall personally inaugurate the religion of the age—nāma-saṅkīrtana, the congregational chanting of the holy name. I shall make the world dance in ecstasy, realizing the four mellows of loving devotional service.” (Cc. Ādi 3.19)**

Lord Kṛṣṇa appears once in the day of Lord Brahmā. One day of Lord Brahmā is a very long period of time.

The four ages (Satya-, Tretā-, Dvāpara- and Kali-yugas) all added together consist of one divya-yuga (4,320,000 years). Seventy-one of these divya-yugas is equal to a lifetime of Manu, who is the prajāpati of mankind. Fourteen of these Manus is equal to one day of Lord Brahmā, and an equal duration of time is Brahmā’s night. When Lord Brahmā goes to sleep, there is partial annihilation of the cosmic manifestation. Lord Brahmā has such days and nights for one-hundred years. At the end of 100 years of Lord Brahmā’s life, the entire cosmic manifestation is annihilated and there is an equal period of unmanifestation.

“In the beginning of creation, the Lord of all creatures sent forth generations of men and demigods, along with sacrifices for Viṣṇu, and blessed them by saying, “Be thou happy by this yajña \[sacrifice\] because its performance will bestow upon you everything desirable for living happily and achieving liberation.” (Bg. 3.10)

Thus, creation takes place in cycles. Creation occurs during the 100 years of Lord Brahmā, then there is no manifestation for an equal period, and then there is creation again. One name for Lord Brahmā is Aja or “one who is the first born.” When the Lord creates unlimited universes, He enters into each universe as Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu. From Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu’s navel sprouts a lotus stem, and atop this stem where the lotus flower is, Brahmā becomes manifest.

In this universe, when Lord Brahmā appeared from the stem of the lotus flower coming from the navel of Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, he was wondering, “Where am I?” It was only he that existed, and all he could see below him was water. He climbed down the stem of the lotus flower and stuck his head into the water; he wanted to see the source of his lotus seat. Upon sticking his head into the water, he heard the vibration ‘tapa’. He accepted that vibration to be of divine origin and accepted the true meaning of the word tapa. He climbed back up into his lotus seat and performed meditation for many thousands of years. Upon perfecting his meditation, the Lord appeared to him and revealed to him the extent of the Vaikuṇṭha planets and empowered him to create this universe.

There are unlimited universes, and in each universe, there is a Lord Brahmā. He is described as the secondary creator, as he creates the bodies of the living entities within the universe, though the seeds of creation come from the Lord who, through His transcendental glance, impregnates the living entities into the universe according to their bodies that are created by Lord Brahmā. The activities of the living entities then begin.

The purpose of this entire cosmic manifestation is twofold: For the living entities to satisfy their own individual desires for happiness and to perform sacrifice so that they can put an end to their material bondage and ultimately achieve the supreme destination. There are 8,400,000 different species of life. The human form of life is a very rare opportunity, because in this form, the living being can voluntarily perform sacrifice. The lower forms of life do not have the intelligence to perform sacrifice and thus act according to their sensual instincts. The human being is therefore supposed to cultivate the higher state of consciousness, which means to cultivate the desire to understand his eternal identity.

*kāmasya nendriya-prītir*  
*lābho jīveta yāvatā*  
*jīvasya tattva-jijñāsā*  
*nārtho yaś ceha karmabhiḥ*

**Life’s desires should never be directed toward sense gratification. One should desire only a healthy life, or self-preservation, since a human being is meant for inquiry about the Absolute Truth. Nothing else should be the goal of one’s works. (Bhāg. 1.2.10)**

Thus we should use the human form of life to its full potential.

If somebody gives you a gift of a brand new, expensive computer that is fast, powerful, and has many accessories, then the first thing you will do is look at the user manual to find out how to use it to its full potential. Without even asking, you will want to get the most out of the gift as it was bestowed upon you.

Similarly, it is to be understood that the human form of life is a rare and valuable gift. It is the gift that the living entity can utilize to its full potential. An intelligent person should ask himself how he can actually do so. It is said in the Bhāgavatam that we must not simply use it for sense gratification, but rather the goal of all of our work is to inquire about the Absolute Truth. Thus, the importance of the human form of life is to voluntarily restrict the tendency for sense gratification for a higher goal.

However, we find that when we try to simply restrict the senses, the desires are still there. Kṛṣṇa explains in the Bhagavad-gītā (2.59), “The embodied soul may be restricted from sense enjoyment, though the taste for sense objects remains. But, ceasing such engagements by experiencing a higher taste, he is fixed in consciousness.”

Thus, Lord Caitanya has appeared in this world and describes in His Śikṣāṣṭaka prayers that the saṅkīrtana movement provides us the nectar for which we are all hankering.

Locana dāsa Ṭhākura worships Lord Caitanya and Lord Nityānanda, who provided the means of congregational chanting of the holy names of the Lord, which are kevala ānanda-kāṇḍa—simply joyful:

*parama karuṇa, pahuṅ dui jana,*  
*nitāi-gauracandra*  
*saba avatāra-, sāra-śiromaṇi,*  
*kevala ānanda-kāṇḍa*

(Dhamali)

When it comes to restricting ourselves from sense enjoyment, it is not a very easy thing to do—especially in the Age of Kali where we lack so much qualification for voluntary restraint. Sometimes when we see yogīs performing very severe austerities, we understand that they are given the ability to do so by dint of their strong desire and determination.

However, Kṛṣṇa says in Bhagavad-gītā, “All that you do, all that you eat, all that you offer and give away, as well as all austerities that you perform, you should do it for Me.” The highest austerity is to please the Lord, and the method that Lord Caitanya has given us in this Age is kevala ānanda-kāṇḍa.

Our only qualification for attaining this type of kṛṣṇa-premā that Lord Caitanya came to give is our realization that we are not qualified. Our tendency, however, is to become proud of ourselves—our intelligence, beauty, wealth, etc. It is very difficult for a proud person to depend upon the Supreme Lord. Thus, in this Age of Kali, Lord Caitanya has made the method of sacrifice so easy by allowing us to qualify ourselves through the realization that we have no spiritual qualification for understanding our relationship with Kṛṣṇa. Lord Caitanya therefore says, “Simply chant the names of Kṛṣṇa, and thus you can achieve all perfection in life.”

Sometimes people wonder what the benefit is of chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, and why we spend so many hours doing it on the streets, even during the freezing cold conditions of the winter. However, we remember that chanting the holy name and distributing books is very pleasing to Śrīla Prabhupāda. Śrīla Prabhupāda followed in the footsteps of Lord Caitanya, who took the holy name to every town and village. Śrīla Prabhupāda introduced to us this method of sacrifice by which the devotees could satisfy Kṛṣṇa’s pure devotee and at the same time, voluntarily accept whatever was necessary to distribute the glories of the holy name of the Lord through chanting of the holy names and distributing Śrīla Prabhupāda’s books. This is the same principle as the sacrifices that were recommended in the beginning of creation.

We see how perfectly Śrīla Prabhupāda is as Lord Caitanya’s ambassador and how he has given us the means for satisfying the Lord. Śrīla Prabhupāda preserved everything that Lord Caitanya came to give. Just as Lord Caitanya came to give the holy name, Śrīla Prabhupāda started this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement in Tompkins Square Park in New York with one small drum and chanting the names of Kṛṣṇa. This whole Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement that has been transplanted in so many cities throughout the world all came from Śrīla Prabhupāda’s chanting of Hare Kṛṣṇa and his pure, unalloyed faith in the holy name of the Lord. We simply have to take this holy name and make it our prema-ratana-dhana—most valuable treasure.

*harer nāma harer nāma*  
*harer nāmaiva kevalam*  
*kalau nāsty eva nāsty eva*  
*nāsty eva gatir anyathā*

(Cc. Ādi 17.21)

**In this Age of Kali there is no other means, no other means, no other means for self-realization than chanting the holy name, chanting the holy name, chanting the holy name of Lord Hari.**

**Question: How important is it for devotees to participate in harināma saṅkīrtana?**

This is described in Prabhupāda’s commentary to the first verse of Śrī Śrī Ṣaḍ-gosvāmy-aṣṭaka—kṛṣṇotkīrtana-gāna-nartana-parau premāmṛtāmbho-nidhī—in which he is talking about the six Gosvāmīs:

They were practicing to teach us, āpani ācari’ prabhu jīvere śikhāya. Simply teaching will not do unless we practice. That is very important thing, practice, practical life. Simply quoting verses, like parrot, will not be very much beneficial. One must apply, jñānam vijñāna-sahitam. Jñāna means to know the thing, and vijñāna means to apply the things in practical life. Jñānaṁ vijñāna-sahitam. So we must know the vijñāna, how practically. That is taught by the Gosvāmīs, kṛṣṇot-kīrtana-gāna-nartana, always chanting the glories of Kṛṣṇa. Kīrtana, gāna, nartana, nartana means dancing. Dancing is very good. The more you dance, the more you become light; means the burden of material contamination becomes reduced. Dancing is so nice. Even if you don’t feel ecstasy, if you dance by force, that will also help us. Kṛṣṇot-kīrtana-gāna-nartanau-parau premāmṛtāmbho-nidhī. By dancing dancing, we shall develop our dormant Kṛṣṇa consciousness, love for Kṛṣṇa. This is a nice process. Kṛṣṇot-kīrtana-gāna-nartana-parau premāmṛtāmbho-nidhī. Then you will merge into the ocean of love for Kṛṣṇa. So this is the highest stage of ecstasy for Kṛṣṇa consciousness, always chanting Kṛṣṇa’s name, dancing in ecstasy, and to be merged in the ocean of love for Kṛṣṇa. These are the perfection.

Dhīrādhīra jana-priyau, in this way we shall become friendly to every people, dhīrādhīra. There are two classes of men. Dhīra, sober, and other class, rogue. So both of them will be pleased by kṛṣṇot-kīrtana. You have practical experience. When there is kṛṣṇa-kīrtana, people, all classes of people, become very much pleased, and they join. As soon as your kīrtana will be pure saṅkīrtana, not artificial, not professional... There are many professional dancer. That will not attract. But, even if you do not know the art of dancing, if you simply dance in ecstasy for Kṛṣṇa’s love, that will be appreciated by everyone. That will be appreciated by everyone. Kṛṣṇot-kīrtana-gāna-nartana-parau. These are the art. One does not require to become a Vedāntist. Simply if one chants Kṛṣṇa’s name, holy name, and in ecstasy dances, he’s more than a Vedāntist. Actually vedānti means one who knows the ultimate knowledge, veda. Veda means knowledge. And anta means ultimate, vedānta. Then what is that ultimate knowledge? Kṛṣṇa. Vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyam \[Bg. 15.15\]. That is ultimate knowledge. So one who has understood Kṛṣṇa and Kṛṣṇa’s love, he’s dancing, then what more vedānta can do? That is the first class realization of vedānta. Kṛṣṇot-kīrtana-gāna-nartana-parau. So we should always offer our respect to the Gosvāmīs, ei chay gosāi yāra tāra mui dāsa, Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says. Tāṅ-sabāra pada-reṇu mora pañca-grās. We should be so humble, respectful to the Gosvāmīs. Not only these Gosvāmīs, anyone who is serving the Gosvāmīs. The Gosvāmīs has also the mission.

(Śrīla Prabhupāda Lecture—The Nectar of Devotion—Bombay, January 8, 1973)

Prabhupāda very clearly says that for one who is chanting and dancing has achieved perfection, for he has understood Vedānta. Of course, this does not refer to professional chanting and dancing, but rather to prema-nāma-saṅkīrtana—chanting for Kṛṣṇa’s love.

**Question: How can we develop a deeper taste for the holy name in saṅkīrtana?**

In Chapter Three of Part Two of Bṛhad-bhāgavatāmṛta, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī describes the glories of nāma-saṅkīrtana as the topmost process for achieving prema, pure love of Godhead, and how it surpasses even meditation:

a) Kīrtana manifests from the tongue, influences the mind and enchants the ears. It not only satisfies oneself but satisfies other listeners as well.

b) Meditation is not possible unless one is in a solitary place. But one can chant the holy name of the Lord in both solitary and crowded places.

c) Of all kinds of kīrtanas Kṛṣṇa’s nāma-saṅkīrtana is the best because it generates love for the Lord very quickly.

d) Loud chanting pleases oneself and pleases others as well, whereas meditation simply satisfies oneself.

e) When one chants the holy name with eagerness then love automatically becomes manifest. Therefore saṅkīrtana and love of Godhead are nondifferent.

f) Meditation is possible both in His presence and absence.

To meditate upon the Lord is very difficult unless the mind is controlled and fixed. However, engaging in nāma-saṅkīrtana employs all the senses and enhances one’s meditation on the Lord.

Rūpa Gosvāmī prays in his Padyāvalī to be able to chant Kṛṣṇa’s name just as a lover reads aloud a letter from his beloved, from whom he has been separated for a long time. This is how we should feelingly chant Hare Kṛṣṇa: “Kṛṣṇa, I have been away from You for too long. When I am chanting Your name, it makes me think of You. It makes me remember You. It makes me want to be with You. When will that day come when I will see You again?” Thus a devotee’s kīrtana is to feelingly address Kṛṣṇa for his benefit.

Ruci is a very elevated platform when one has a taste for devotional service. It already surpasses the stages of śraddhā, sādhu-saṅgaḥ, bhajana-kriyā, anartha-nivṛttiḥ and niṣṭhā (when one is engaging in śravaṇaṁ and kīrtanaṁ and is no longer influenced by the tendency to fall asleep, by distractions, and by lust). Steady in his bhajana he develops ruci, which is the following stage.

Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura describes in Mādhurya-kādambinī that there are two types of ruci:

That which depends on excellence of elements, and that which does not. Excellence of elements refers to an excellence relating to such things as the Lord’s name, qualities, form.

For instance, a person may only experience pleasure from kīrtana if it is pleasing to the ear and artistically sung, or may only relish topics of the Lord if they are delivered skillfully with literary ornaments and qualities, or may only enjoy Deity worship if all the implements, place, and materials are of high standard.

The first type of ruci is in which a slight trace of impurity remains. Therefore if a person depends on the excellency of the material elements of kīrtana to experience a spiritual taste, one should understand that this is evidence of impurity in his heart.

A person with the second type of ruci will experience great pleasure wherever and whenever there is a performance of kīrtana. He does not depend on excellence of the elements because he has actual depth in his taste. One should understand that he has no trace of impurity in his heart.

Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura gives three criteria for the excellence of elements:

**1) In kīrtana**, one only experiences pleasure if it is pleasing to the ear and artistically sung with expert mṛdanga and karatāls.

**2) In hearing**, one only relishes topics of the Lord if they are delivered skillfully with literary ornaments and qualities; if the speaker can speak with so many different types of embellishments and in a very attractive way.

**3) In Deity worship**, one only enjoys it if all the implements, place, and materials are of high standard. He can engage in worship of the Deity and have taste for it only if it is a high standard of worship with all kinds of paraphernalia available for their worship.

Thus devotees who have this type of ruci are dependent on this excellence of elements for their taste. However, Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura explains that even on the higher platform of ruci, there are those who are not dependent on such excellence of elements; they have taste even if all opulent paraphernalia is not there.

We can understand this through the story of the South Indian brāhmaṇa who was worshiping the Deity in his mind. He was in poverty and had no paraphernalia to worship the Deity. Therefore, in his mind he would travel to all the places of pilgrimage, gather all the waters from the sacred rivers and bring them all in one place to bathe the Deity. After bathing the Deity with water from all the sacred rivers, in his mind, he would dress the Deity and place all kinds of gold and silver ornaments on its body. He had a taste for serving the Deity even though he did not have the paraphernalia. He even wanted to cook the most opulent sweet rice, but he did not have the ingredients. Therefore, in his mind he cooked sweet rice. When he tested it with his finger, his finger got burnt. When he came to external consciousness, he looked at his finger and his finger was actually burnt; not only in meditation. Thus we can see how he had a taste for rendering his service, even though he did not have any opulent paraphernalia.

As another example, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta would sometimes ask the disciple who had a terrible voice to lead the kīrtana. He explained that this devotee sings with devotion. Therefore it is not really a criterion for one to be an expert at playing instruments or a professional singer.

In one commentary to the prayers of the six Gosvāmīs, Prabhupāda specifically denounces that a devotee is not interested in being a professional dancer or a professional singer. Rather, the devotee simply dances for Kṛṣṇa’s love. Such chanting and dancing for Kṛṣṇa’s love is so attractive that it will attract both the gentle and the ruffians. Even those who are not inclined will be attracted by such chanting. What good will professional dancing do? It may gain the attraction of others, but it will not attract them towards Kṛṣṇa and devotional service, and it will not attract Kṛṣṇa.

## Chapter 7 – Spiritual Master

## Prabhupāda’s Calling

September 4, 2009 was the 50th anniversary of Śrīla Prabhupāda’s acceptance of the renounced order of life. This celebration is referred to as Viśvarūpa-mahotsava because Śrīla Prabhupāda accepted the renounced order on the anniversary of the day that Lord Caitanya’s brother, Viśvarūpa, accepted the renounced order of life. It was a very significant event in Śrīla Prabhupāda’s life, because he took it as a direct order from his spiritual master to take sannyāsa and go out and preach about Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

He actually received that order in 1922 when he had his first meeting with Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura. In one conversation with disciples in the early 1970s, he said that it seemed that every eleven years something very significant happened in his life. He said that in 1922, he met his spiritual master, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Mahārāja. In 1933, he took initiation from him. In 1944, he began the Back to Godhead magazine. In 1955, he left his family life, and in 1966 ISKCON was incorporated in America.

One devotee asked Śrīla Prabhupāda, “Therefore, 1977 will also be a very significant year, Śrīla Prabhupāda, won’t it?”

Śrīla Prabhupāda said, “Yes, perhaps it is significant that 1977 will also be a very relevant year.”

One devotee said, “Maybe that will be the year you finish Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Śrīla Prabhupāda.”

Prabhupāda said, “Yes, maybe,” and this concluded the conversation.

However, we know that 1977 was certainly a significant year, as it was the year when Śrīla Prabhupāda entered into Kṛṣṇa’s eternal līlā in Goloka Vṛndāvana and departed from our vision. For us who were left to remain here on this planet, 1977 was a very difficult year. We were left to ‘break our heads against the stone,’ as Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura describes in the song about the separation due to the disappearance or departure of Vaiṣṇavas.

In 1922 when Śrīla Prabhupāda had his first meeting with Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura on Ultadanga Road in Calcutta, it was as a result of his friend named Narendranath Mullik, who requested that Śrīla Prabhupāda come and meet this very saintly person. He forcibly brought Śrīla Prabhupāda. Śrīla Prabhupāda explained that in his youth, he was a very influential person, and when he would do something, many of his friends would follow his example. Therefore, Narendranath thought that if he brought Śrīla Prabhupāda to see this saintly person, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, then many of his other friends would also go to see him.

Śrīla Prabhupāda thus had his first meeting with Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, who defeated Śrīla Prabhupāda in his arguments about Caitanya Mahāprabhu’s mission. What was most significant is that when Prabhupāda, known as Abhaya at that time, and his friend came to the rooftop and offered their obeisances to the saintly Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, upon arising, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta immediately gave Śrīla Prabhupāda his life’s mission: “You both look like intelligent men. Why don’t you take up the mission of Caitanya Mahāprabhu and preach this message of Kṛṣṇa consciousness in English in the West?” Prabhupāda had not even heard anything from him yet. They had simply offered their obeisances, and already Prabhupāda had his order and life’s mission given to him by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura after simply offering his obeisances to him.

At that time, Śrīla Prabhupāda was a young householder, and he tried to offer some arguments: “Who will hear our message as long as we are a nation dependent upon the British? We must first get our independence, and then people will hear our message.”

Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Mahārāja told him that the message of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is so important and urgent that it cannot wait. He said that there is no question of independence; one power will be in control, and then after some time another power will be in control. He said, “What is the meaning of this so-called independence? Caitanya Mahāprabhu’s message is real independence. It is urgent, and it cannot wait because everyone is gliding down to hell to suffer repeated birth and death.”

1959 was therefore a significant year, because it was when Śrīla Prabhupāda accepted the renounced order of life and embraced it as the opportunity to facilitate his execution of that order which he had already received. Acceptance of the renounced order of life is not simply a matter of changing one’s dress. It is a matter of consciousness.

*mayy ananyena bhāvena*  
*bhaktiṁ kurvanti ye dṛḍhām*  
*mat-kṛte tyakta-karmāṇas*  
*tyakta-svajana-bāndhavāḥ*

**Such a sādhu engages in staunch devotional service to the Lord without deviation. For the sake of the Lord he renounces all other connections, such as family relationships and friendly acquaintances within the world. (Bhāg. 3.25.22)**

Śrīla Prabhupāda’s taking of sannyāsa is very relevant to this verse. Although he had actually given up his family even before he accepted sannyāsa, his acceptance of sannyāsa is when the dṛḍha-vrata (fixed determination) manifested to do so and when it began to fructify within his heart to execute and fulfill that order that Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta gave him in 1922.

When Śrīla Prabhupāda was a householder, he had many children and family responsibilities. He never really lived in any of the Gauḍīya Maṭhas, although he certainly was assisting his sannyāsī-god-brothers in various ways to spread Kṛṣṇa consciousness while he was a householder.

In the 1930s when Śrīla Prabhupāda was in Bombay, he was assisting his god-brothers, Bhakti-rakṣaka Śrīdhara Mahārāja and Bhakti Saranga Mahārāja, who were opening the temple there. Śrīla Prabhupāda helped them by organizing different programs and facilitating their preaching so that they could go out and raise funds for establishing the temple in Bombay.

One of his godbrothers actually suggested to Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura: “Abhaya is a very good organizer and a very good manager. Why don’t we make him the temple president of the Maṭha here in Bombay?”

Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura said, “No, don’t put him in that position. He will do everything in due course of time.” Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura knew that Prabhupāda had embraced the order that he had given to him in his heart and knew that everything would manifest in due course of time.

Śrīla Prabhupāda often said that Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta had marked him as somebody that would accomplish something very wonderful because he hears very nicely. In fact, one time Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura was taking his followers on parikramā in Vṛndāvana and visiting various places. Śrīla Prabhupāda decided to leave Allahabad and go to Koṣi where Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura was speaking on that particular day. The Śeṣaśāyī temple was nearby, and Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta had suggested that those who wanted to go take darśana at the Śeṣaśāyī temple could go, but that he was also going to be speaking that evening. Many of the devotees who were on parikramā therefore went to take darśana of the Deity at the Śeṣaśāyī temple, and only about twelve devotees remained to listen to Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta give his lecture that evening. Prabhupāda was one that remained. He said, “I am not going anywhere. I want to sit here and hear from my Guru Mahārāja.”

Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura took notice of Śrīla Prabhupāda and said, “Yes, he likes to hear.”

In 1968 Prabhupāda also said to a group of young devotees in Columbus, Ohio that if one hears nicely, then he will preach nicely. Śrīla Prabhupāda was speaking about śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ viṣṇoḥ smaraṇaṁ. He said that first there must be hearing, and we must be very, very eager to hear. He gave the example of how he was very eager to hear Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta in Koṣi when he was on parikramā. He said, “When one is hearing very nicely, then the very natural thing that will come after is that you will want to preach and tell others about Kṛṣṇa.”

Thus Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura had taken note of that capacity of Śrīla Prabhupāda for being very eager to hear from his Guru Mahārāja.

Prabhupāda was doing many things in various ways to try to assist his godbrothers in spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness. In 1944, Śrīla Prabhupāda also began the writing, publication, printing and distribution of the Back to Godhead magazine. Sometimes he would not even have enough money to pay the printer. The printer would say, “I have already printed so many magazines for you.”

Prabhupāda would plead with him, “Please print more. I will get the money in due course of time. I will pay all my debts back to you. Please just print.” The printer could not refuse. He accepted Prabhupāda’s request and would print the magazine for him. Then Prabhupāda would take these magazines and personally go and distribute them. He brought them to the tea stalls, bazaars, and people’s homes. The local residents knew every time that Prabhupāda was coming with a new Back to Godhead magazine, because they knew the sound of the bicycle that he rode on to distribute his magazines. It was an old, broken bicycle. Every time he pedaled, it would make loud noises.

We can see that Śrīla Prabhupāda was already engaged in assisting Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura in his preaching mission prior to leaving his family in 1955. Bhakti-rakṣaka Śrīdhara Mahārāja tells a story about how, when Prabhupāda was a householder in the mid-1950s, he came to him in the middle of the night at 1:30 a.m. Prabhupāda was pounding on his door. Śrīdhara Mahārāja awoke and opened the door. Prabhupāda told him, “Guru Mahārāja came to me in a dream tonight. I am not ready for this. I am a little bit hesitant. However, Guru Mahārāja appeared and told me, ‘Please, you must take sannyāsa.’”

At that time, Śrīdhara Mahārāja was living close to Prabhupāda. Śrīdhara Mahārāja said, “Let me think about it. I am not sure I can do that—to give you sannyāsa right now.” He said this because he had a connection with Prabhupāda’s wife’s family and knew all the family members. He thought that if he were to give him sannyāsa, he would get a little flak from the family. At that time, sannyāsa meant that for the service of the Lord, you sever all connections, such as friendly acquaintances and family relationships in this world.

Prabhupāda actually had that calling from Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta in a dream many times. The second time, at 1:00 in the morning, Prabhupāda went to Śrīdhara Mahārāja’s door and said, “Guru Mahārāja has come to me again and has said, ‘You must take sannyāsa and preach. Before I was hesitant, but now I am not hesitant. Now I am completely ready. Please, give me sannyāsa now!’”

Śrīdhara Mahārāja again said, “Do not rush. I suggest that first you try bahūdaka—live outside, away from your family for a little while. Maybe later you can formally accept sannyāsa.”

Therefore, again, Śrīla Prabhupāda did not take sannyāsa at that time. However, the very next day, even though Śrīdhara Mahārāja did not give him sannyāsa, Prabhupāda was gone. He just left everything behind and was gone. He was nowhere to be seen or found. That determination was there in his heart. He felt Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura calling him. Prabhupāda felt that the call was not only to take sannyāsa, but also to execute the order he received in 1922. Prabhupāda’s mind was fixed on executing that order. That is what his guru wanted him to do; he wanted Prabhupāda to write in English, print books in English, and to go to the West with the English books and preach to the western people.

In 1958, something very wonderful happened. This is described in a poem written by Śrīla Prabhupāda that year, entitled Vṛndāvana Bhajana. He wrote it while he was in Vṛndāvana, just before taking sannyāsa. It is long, but the following is a small section of it:

Verse 1:

I am sitting alone in Vṛndāvana-dhāma

In this mood I am getting many realizations.

I have my wife, sons, daughters, grandsons, everything,

But I have no money so they are a fruitless glory.

Kṛṣṇa has shown me the naked form of material nature,

By His strength it has all become tasteless to me today.

Yasyāham anugṛhṇāmi hariṣye tad-dhanaṁ śanaiḥ

“I gradually take away all the wealth of those upon whom I am merciful.”

How was I able to understand this mercy of the All-merciful?

Verse 2:

Everyone has abandoned me, seeing me as penniless,

Wife, relatives, friends, brothers, everyone.

This is misery, but it gives me a laugh. I sit alone and laugh.

In this māyā-saṁsāra, whom do I really love?

Where have all my loving father and mother gone to now?

And where are all my elders, who were my own folk?

Who will give me news of them, tell me who?

All that is left of this family life is a list of names.

This was Prabhupāda’s realization as he sat in Vṛndāvana in 1958, after he had already left his family. Prabhupāda mentions in this poem that the soul is eternal, and that while relationships are established temporarily in this world, everyone on the spiritual platform is your relative.

In 1968, Prabhupāda was speaking to a group of disciples in Seattle. He received a message that Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Mahārāja, who was the devotee who gave Prabhupāda sannyāsa, had departed from the world. Prabhupāda said to the devotees present that he wanted to write a condolence letter to all the disciples of Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Mahārāja. He said that Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta was actually speaking to him through Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Mahārāja to accept sannyāsa. Initially he thought, “Oh how horrible! I have to give up the formal connection with family.” However, Prabhupāda explained to the devotees in 1968 that anyone who gives up anything for Kṛṣṇa never loses. He said that he gave up his children, but now he has three hundred children.

Prabhupāda felt the urge rising in his heart to execute the order of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta, and he saw sannyāsa as the facility to execute that order. Sannyāsa is not simply a change of dress. It is an evolution of consciousness. Of course, we know that Prabhupāda was completely Kṛṣṇa conscious. He told us that there never was a time when he forgot Kṛṣṇa. Yet he still set an important example to follow—accepting the order of the spiritual master. No matter how troublesome it may be to execute that order and to go on for many years, it is necessary to carry out that order. In due course of time, Kṛṣṇa will facilitate that order in the heart of the sincere disciple.

There are some very interesting verses at the very end of Vṛndāvana Bhajana, which give us the essence of what Prabhupāda’s Vṛndāvana bhajana was. Sometimes we think Vṛndāvana bhajana means to go to Vṛndāvana and meditate on the pastimes of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, or to meditate on the pastimes of the residents of Vṛndāvana, and we perform our bhajana, trying to absorb our minds and consciousness in the transcendental līlās of Bhauma Vṛndāvana. That is Vṛndāvana bhajana, but for one who has actually meditated on that Vṛndāvana bhajana and has understood the necessity of executing the order of the spiritual master in that consciousness he sees things in a different perspective.

Prabhupāda said in his Vṛndāvana Bhajana:

Verse 26:

Śrī Dayitā dāsa prabhu gave this instruction

“Chant Hare Kṛṣṇa loudly, this is my initiation:

Kīrtana is not just drums and karatālas

The sound of kīrtana is not this modern system (broadcasting over the radio)

Anything favourable for devotional service is all Mādhava

And the only enjoyer of the three worlds is Yādava

Māyā’s pride and joy, the radio sound

Destroy them all by forceful kīrtana.

At that time in India, everybody listened to the radio; there were no televisions or computers.

Verse 27:

Māyā’s is all these newspapers

Preach that throughout the whole world.

Sitting alone in your room shouting, you may increase your bile’s secretion

But in ten million births Śrī Hari won’t be pleased.

Śrī Hari is no one’s father’s property

Come out of your cage, stop making objection

Everything belongs to Śrī Hari and Śrī Hari belongs to everyone.

Chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra loudly

By the performance of such saṅkīrtana there will come remembrance automatically

Then there will be nirjana bhajana manifested in the heart spontaneously.

Thus ends Prabhupāda’s Vṛndāvana Bhajana, written in 1958 when he was preparing himself for sannyāsa.

There was the big Bhag Bazaar Gauḍīya-Maṭha temple in Calcutta, and in April 1959, there was fighting among the members of the Gauḍīya Maṭha about who was actually the real Gauḍīya Maṭha. Śrīla Prabhupāda’s godbrother, Bhakti-Vilāsa-Tīrtha Mahārāja, held the legal documents of the Gauḍīya Maṭha at that time. Śrīla Prabhupāda thought, “Since Bhakti-Vilāsa-Tīrtha Mahārāja is representing the Gauḍīya Maṭha, if I write to him, certainly he will help me fulfill Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura’s order.”

He therefore wrote, “Please help me fulfill the order of Guru Mahārāja. Guru Mahārāja wants his Gauḍīya Maṭha (his institution) to spread throughout the world in the English-speaking language. Please facilitate this for me by giving me sannyāsa and sponsoring me so I can go to America. Help me to publish books in the English language so that I can take these books to America and preach there.”

Bhakti-Vilāsa-Tīrtha Mahārāja wrote back a letter to Prabhupāda, saying, “First you should become a member of our society. Then you can come and live in the temple, do some menial service, and become a servant of the Vaiṣṇavas. You will see that others are taking sannyāsa in due course of time, and in due course of time, you can take sannyāsa also.” He therefore wanted Prabhupāda to become an official member of the Bhag Bazaar Gauḍīya Maṭha temple and to live there. He said, “We will give you a very nice room where there is very nice light and has good air. You can sit down and write for our temple.” He was therefore saying that by so doing, in due course of time sannyāsa would come.

Prabhupāda received that letter, and then decided in May of the same year (1959) to write a second letter to Bhakti-Vilāsa-Tīrtha Mahārāja. He emphasized that now was the time to execute the order of Sri Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He was using all the arguments that Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura used to defeat him in 1922 when Prabhupāda said, “How will people hear our message if we are not an independent nation?”

In 1922, Prabhupāda was a member of Gandhi’s movement. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura told Prabhupāda and Narendranatha to take this message to the West and preach to the western people. However, Prabhupāda offered his arguments: “Who will hear our message when we are not even an independent nation, and still subjugated by British rule?”

Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura right away defeated Śrīla Prabhupāda soundly, saying, “The political views can always go from one side to the other. Things are always changing in this world. But one thing that will never change is the message of Caitanya Mahāprabhu, which is absolute. It is an emergency now.” He explained how establishing the message of Caitanya Mahāprabhu throughout the whole world was more important than getting liberated from British rule. At that time, he established how important it was to take this message throughout the world and to give Kṛṣṇa consciousness to others—especially in the English language, because it was the language of the world.

Śrīla Prabhupāda therefore presented all these arguments to Bhakti-Vilāsa-Tīrtha Mahārāja in his second letter. He begged him, “Please facilitate me. Please allow me to come and accept the renounced order of life. Facilitate this order of our Guru Mahārāja, sponsor me, allow me to go to the West, and help me print books in the English language.”

Bhakti-Vilāsa-Tīrtha Mahārāja wrote back a letter again and essentially said the same as before: “We have so many books that were given to us as priority by our Guru Mahārāja. We still have to print the Sandarbhas. We have to print so many other books. You can come and help us edit and write these books. In due course of time, we may help you to print books in the English language. However, now there are more important things to be done.”

When Prabhupāda received this reply from Bhakti-Vilāsa-Tīrtha Mahārāja, in his heart he could not reject the order that Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura had given to him. He felt that over-flooding in his heart was the desire to execute the order.

There is a story in this connection that very nicely exemplifies Prabhupāda’s intense desire. In the 1940s and 1950s, Prabhupāda used to go to Advaita Ācārya’s house in Śāntipura, where he would sit and chant his japa in the back. There was one pūjārī who noticed Prabhupāda who was in white cloth at that time. Prabhupāda would come approximately once every two months, sit there and chant very attentively. Sometimes the pūjārī noticed that while Prabhupāda was sitting and chanting, tears were coming from his eyes.

Prabhupāda stopped going to that place, and for many years the pūjārī did not see him. Many years later, in 1965, the pūjārī saw this man once again sitting there. He recognized that it was the same man that used to come in the 1940s and 1950s to sit and chant his japa. However, this time something was different; he was sitting in saffron cloth and he had a daṇḍa.

The pūjārī walked over to him and said, “What is your name, dear, kind sir?”

Prabhupāda said, “I am the menial servant of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Ṭhākura. My name is A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami.” Tears immediately flooded Prabhupāda’s eyes as he was sitting and chanting.

The pūjārī said, “I remember you used to come here before to sit and chant japa. Why are you crying like this?”

Prabhupāda says, “I am crying because tomorrow I am leaving to execute a virtually impossible instruction of my spiritual master—to go to the West, preach Kṛṣṇa consciousness to the western people, and make the Americans into Vaiṣṇavas. Therefore, I am crying to all the personalities who used to gather at this great sacred place, such as Advaita Ācārya, Lord Nityānanda, Haridāsa Ṭhākura and Lord Caitanya. I am begging them to please give me their blessings and mercy so that I may follow my Guru Mahārāja.

Prabhupāda then bowed down at the feet of the pūjārī and said, “I am also begging you to please give me your blessings.” Prabhupāda continued chanting there for some time and then left. The next day, he boarded the Jaladuta.

Many years later, in 1980, many western people dressed as Vaiṣṇavas were visiting Advaita Ācārya’s house—this same place where Prabhupāda had been chanting. One of them handed the pūjārī a Back to Godhead magazine and then left.

The pūjārī took the Back to Godhead magazine, opened it and immediately saw Prabhupāda’s picture and said to himself, “That’s the man!” He immediately went through the magazine and looked up the address of the closest temple. In 1980 he went to that temple, which was in Māyāpura. Upon arrival at the temple, he was anxious to speak to someone. He was overwhelmed with excitement and wanted to tell everybody his story.

He said, “You see this picture? This man is Bhaktivedanta Swami! Now I understand. Now I see so many westerners coming in Vaiṣṇava dress. He has done it! He has done it! He has done it!”

The devotees responded, “What are you saying?”

He then told them the whole story of how Prabhupāda used to come to the house of Advaita Ācārya and sit and cry, and that the last time that Prabhupāda came, he had told him about going to the West. He immediately made a connection in his mind as to why these westerners were coming dressed in Vaiṣṇava clothing. He realized, “Prabhupāda had gone to the West and executed that impossible order.”

He said, “I just had to come here and tell you the story that was flooding my heart.” All the devotees were completely overwhelmed upon hearing the story of Prabhupāda.

The pūjārī had therefore last seen Prabhupāda in sannyāsa cloth and with a daṇḍa, sitting and chanting japa. But how is it that he eventually received sannyāsa?

In 1959 after he had written the second letter to Bhakti-Vilāsa-Tīrtha Mahārāja, Prabhupāda decided that he would approach Bhaktiprajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja and ask him for his blessings to accept sannyāsa. Bhaktiprajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja told him, “You must accept sannyāsa. Yes, you have been given the order. We should do it immediately.”

In 1968, when Prabhupāda heard that Bhaktiprajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja had departed from this world, he recited one verse to send as condolences for the departure of his beloved godbrother who said that Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta was speaking through him when he ordered that Prabhupāda must take sannyāsa. Prabhupāda asked all his disciples to sign it, as he wanted to send a letter immediately to India to offer condolences for the departure of Bhaktiprajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja.

Earlier, Bhaktiprajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja was so emphatic that they did not even take time to schedule the sannyāsa ceremony. Instead, he said, “Very soon it will be the Viśvarūpa Mahotsava—the day when Viśvarūpa takes sannyāsa. It is a very auspicious day. You should therefore take sannyāsa on that day.” Therefore, no invitations were written and no one was invited. One other godbrother, Sanātana dāsa, also received sannyāsa and the name Muni Mahārāja.

The way the ceremony took place is very important. Since there were no invitations, the only people who were present were the brahmacārīs of the Maṭha and a few guests. They all spoke Bengali. During the sannyāsa ceremony, Bhaktiprajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja gave a short talk and told Prabhupāda, “Now you give a lecture.”

Prabhupāda immediately began giving a lecture in English. Nobody understood. The only ones who were present who understood English at that time were Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja, who performed the yajña, Bhaktiprajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja and Kṛṣṇadāsa Bābājī Mahārāja (a very close friend of Prabhupāda). Although nobody else understood what he was saying, Prabhupāda chose to give the whole lecture in English to establish the point of why he was taking sannyāsa. English was the language of the world, and to preach in English was the order he was given by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura.

Another very interesting thing happened during that sannyāsa ceremony. Kṛṣṇadāsa Bābājī Mahārāja and Prabhupāda were close friends. Bābājī Mahārāja would always come and see Śrīla Prabhupāda in Vṛndāvana. They would sit, talk and laugh. Bābājī Mahārāja was loved throughout the Gauḍīya Maṭha. At that time in the Gauḍīya Maṭha, there was a lot of friction between temples, and the devotees were fighting with one another about who was to be the next ācārya. Sometimes when one sannyāsī would go to another temple, he would not be allowed to speak. However, Bābājī Mahārāja was such a non-political person, because the only thing he did was chant Hare Kṛṣṇa. As soon as he would walk into any Gauḍīya Maṭha temple, immediately they would take the mṛdaṅga, put it over his shoulders and say, “Please, sing kīrtana.” Bābājī Mahārāja would then lead kīrtana and everybody would be in complete bliss. He was so attached to the holy name of the Lord.

During the sannyāsa ceremony of Śrīla Prabhupāda, Bābājī Mahārāja was sitting there and was very enthusiastically chanting, “Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa…” He was so happy to see his godbrother, Abhay Babu, taking sannyāsa.

One Vaiṣṇava was saying to Bābājī Mahārāja, “Shhh… Perhaps you should be a little bit softer. Don’t disturb the atmosphere. You are chanting a little bit too loudly.”

When Prabhupāda heard this, he immediately turned to Bābājī Mahārāja and said, “Chant louder, louder, louder.” Bābājī Mahārāja later told many of Prabhupāda’s disciples that when Prabhupāda said that, he knew that Prabhupāda would be the person who would take the holy name and spread it throughout the world. He saw the firm faith that Prabhupāda had in the holy name.

## Prabhupāda’s Meditation

On September 18, 1965, on board the Jaladuta ship, Prabhupāda wrote a bhajana called Mārkine Bhāgavata-dharma, just before stepping on American soil for first time. This bhajana very nicely reveals Prabhupāda’s inner mood when he was about to begin his preaching mission in the West, and before he had met anybody there. The contents of this bhajana demonstrate that the only personality that Śrīla Prabhupāda knew and had with him on his journey was Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa. He was therefore writing to Lord Kṛṣṇa in a very dependent mood. We can also understand from this bhajana what the mood of a preacher is—simply trying to act as a servant and representative on behalf of the Lord, attempting to induce others to take shelter of the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.

*baro-kṛpā kaile kṛṣṇa adhamer prati*  
*ki lāgiyānile hethā koro ebe gati*  
*āche kichu kārja taba ei anumāne*  
*nahe keno āniben ei ugra-sthāne*

*rajas tamo guṇe erā sabāi ācchanna*  
*bāsudeb-kathā ruci nahe se prasanna*  
*tabe jadi taba kṛpā hoy ahaitukī*  
*sakal-i sambhava hoy tumi se kautukī*

*ki bhāve bujhāle tārā bujhe sei rasa*  
*eta kṛpā koro prabhu kori nija-baśa*  
*tomāra icchāya saba hoy māyā-baśa*  
*tomāra icchāya nāśa māyār paraśa*

*taba icchā hoy jadi tādera uddhār*  
*bujhibe niścai tabe kathā se tomār*  
*bhāgavater kathā se taba avatār*  
*dhīra haiyā śune jadi kāne bār bār*

*rajas tamo hate tabe pāibe nistār*  
*hṛdayer abhadra sate ghucibe tāhār*  
*ki ko’ re bujhābo kathā baro sei cāhi*  
*khudra āmi dīna hīna kono śakti nāhi*

*athaca enecho prabhu kathā bolibāre*  
*je tomār icchā prabhu koro ei bare*  
*akhila jagat-guru! bacana se āmār*  
*alaṅkṛta koribār khamatā tomār*

*taba kṛpā ha’ le mor kathā śuddha habe*  
*śuniyā sabāra śoka duḥkha je ghucibe*  
*āniyācho jadi prabhu āmāre nācāte*  
*nācāo nācāo prabhu nācāo se-mate*

*kāṣṭhera puttali jathā nācāo se-mate*  
*bhakti nāi beda nāi nāme khub daro*  
*“ bhaktivedānta” nām ebe sārthak kor*

My dear Lord Kṛṣṇa, You are so kind upon this useless soul, but I do not know why You have brought me here. Now You can do whatever You like with me.

But I guess You have some business here, otherwise why would You bring me to this terrible place?

Most of the population here is covered by the material modes of ignorance and passion. Absorbed in material life, they think themselves very happy and satisfied, and therefore they have no taste for the transcendental message of Vāsudeva. I do not know how they will be able to understand it.

But I know Your causeless mercy can make everything possible because You are the most expert mystic.

How will they understand the mellows of devotional service? O Lord, I am simply praying for Your mercy so that I will be able to convince them about Your message.

All living entities have become under the control of the illusory energy by Your will, and therefore, if You like, by Your will they can also be released from the clutches of illusion.

I wish that You may deliver them. Therefore if You so desire their deliverance, then only will they be able to understand Your message.

The words of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam are Your incarnation, and if a sober person repeatedly receives it with submissive aural reception, then he will be able to understand Your message.

He will become liberated from the influence of the modes of ignorance and passion and thus all inauspicious things accumulated in the core of the heart will disappear.

How will I make them understand this message of Kṛṣṇa consciousness? I am very unfortunate, unqualified and the most fallen. Therefore I am seeking Your benediction so that I can convince them, for I am powerless to do so on my own.

Somehow or other, O Lord, You have brought me here to speak about You. Now, my Lord, it is up to You to make me a success or failure as You like.

O spiritual master of all the worlds! I can simply repeat Your message, so if You like You can make my power of speaking suitable for their understanding.

Only by Your causeless mercy will my words become pure. I am sure that when this transcendental message penetrates their hearts they will certainly feel engladdened and thus become liberated from all unhappy conditions of life.

O Lord, I am just like a puppet in Your hands. So if You have brought me here to dance, then make me dance, make me dance, O Lord, make me dance as You like.

I have no devotion, nor do I have any knowledge, but I have strong faith in the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. I have been designated as Bhaktivedānta, and now, if You like, You can fulfill the real purport of Bhaktivedānta.

In this personal prayer, Prabhupāda expresses his total dependence upon Lord Kṛṣṇa’s will in the execution of his mission to preach Kṛṣṇa consciousness in the West. Prabhupāda was questioning how the westerners would be able to understand the real mellows of devotional service, when most of the population is covered by the material modes of ignorance and passion. They are so absorbed in material life, thinking themselves to be very happy and satisfied. Prabhupāda understood that the people he would be preaching to have no taste for the message of Kṛṣṇa, but rather, being covered by the modes of passion and ignorance, are thinking themselves happy and satisfied with a lower taste.

Prabhupāda did not know what to expect. All he knew is that he had Kṛṣṇa’s will and the order of the spiritual master. Somehow he had to awaken within the hearts of the westerners some desire to render service to the Lord. In his very first prayer, when he says, “How will they be able to understand the mellows of devotional service?” he is talking both about the taste for devotion, and the ability to understand the very subtle qualities of devotional service.

Devotional service is very difficult for materialistic persons to understand, because if one tries to look externally to see how he is progressing in devotional service, he will be fooled; externally there is no evidence that one is making progress in spiritual life. People who are accustomed to material formulas look externally at how much wealth they have accumulated; what kind of position they have been able to obtain; etc. However, bhakti is an engagement of the heart, and the evidence of progress is not based upon one’s position, wealth or strength, but rather on the increase of one’s devotion.

There are many examples given in the śāstras of how materialistic persons, who are proud of wealth, position, etc., will often deride those who have devotion, because they think that they have nothing to show for all their hard labor.

Thus, Prabhupāda was thinking, “How will these people understand the mellows of devotional service? How will I be able to convince them? Everyone here is covered by lower modes and they have different gauges for progress.”

Prabhupāda is therefore praying for the potency to carry out the will of the Lord. There are many examples in the Bhāgavatam that describe Vaiṣṇavas who are praying to the Lord for potency. A Vaiṣṇava is one who knows that he cannot accomplish anything by his efforts alone.

It is described in the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam how Lord Brahmā was praying for creative potency: “How can I create an entire universe as is expected of me and not become entangled in my work?” Therefore he is praying to the Supreme Lord, “Please empower me. Make me Your instrument.” Similarly, Prabhupāda is also praying in this way: “O Lord, I am just like a puppet in Your hands. So if You have brought me here to dance, then make me dance, make me dance, O Lord, make me dance as You like.”

A preacher never thinks himself to be the doer. Kṛṣṇa explains in Bhagavad-gītā:

*prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni*  
*guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ*  
*ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā*  
*kartāham iti manyate*

**The spirit soul bewildered by the influence of false ego thinks himself the doer of activities that are in actuality carried out by the three modes of material nature. (Bg. 3.27)**

The bewildered soul is filled with ahaṅkāra (false ego), which means that he is thinking himself to be the doer of activities. Therefore Prabhupāda was not thinking, “I am a big preacher coming to the west to get disciples!” Rather, what Prabhupāda was thinking is so beautifully described in his prayer: “I have come here by Kṛṣṇa’s desire. Kṛṣṇa, You have brought me here for some reason. I am not even sure what it is! I know I have to try to convince people of Your message, but they have no taste.”

Prabhupāda quotes a very important verse from the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam:

*śrnvatāṁ sva-kathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ*  
*punya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ*  
*hṛdy antaḥ-stho hy abhadrāṇi*  
*vidhunoti suhṛt satām*

*naṣṭa-prāyeṣv abhadreṣu*  
*nityaṁ bhāgavata-sevayā*  
*bhagavaty uttama-śloke*  
*bhaktir bhavati naiṣṭhikī*

**Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, who is the Paramātmā \[Supersoul\] in everyone’s heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who has developed the urge to hear His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted.**

**By regular attendance in classes on the Bhāgavatam and by rendering of service to the pure devotee, all that is troublesome to the heart is almost completely destroyed, and loving service unto the Personality of Godhead, who is praised with transcendental songs, is established as an irrevocable fact. (Bhāg. 1.2.17-18)**

Thus, Prabhupāda was repeating the words of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam in his prayer, Mārkine Bhāgavata-dharma.

Once, when Śrīla Prabhupāda was speaking to a group of Indian people in India, he was speaking very strongly, calling persons who do not surrender to Kṛṣṇa as mūḍhāḥ, or asses. One man objected to Prabhupāda: “Swamījī, why are you speaking so harshly? Don’t you know that Kṛṣṇa says in Bhagavad-gītā that you should be sama-darśinaḥ? Why are you using such strong words as fools and rascals?”

Prabhupāda responded, “These are not my words; these are Kṛṣṇa’s words, which He uses in the Bhagavad-gītā.”

The man argued, “But Swamījī, you should be sama-darśinaḥ; you should see everyone as equal.”

Prabhupāda said, “Yes, I do see everyone as equal. I tell everybody exactly what Kṛṣṇa says in the Bhagavad-gītā. I do not discriminate. This is sama-darśinaḥ. I am not so advanced to be completely sama-darśinaḥ in the way that you think. But this is sama-darśinaḥ according to Kṛṣṇa’s teachings. I will tell everyone without discrimination. Kṛṣṇa says if you do not follow His instructions, then you are a rascal. Thus these are Kṛṣṇa’s words; not mine.”

Then the man responded, “But Swamījī, you are not doing anything yourself; you are simply repeating. Why don’t you say something of your own?”

Prabhupāda very strongly replied, “No, I am simply standing on the words of the disciplic succession. This is preaching Kṛṣṇa consciousness. This is sama-darśinaḥ. You also tell everyone you meet about what Kṛṣṇa says. We are simply humble servants of the disciplic succession.”

Prabhupāda would also preach very strongly to his disciples, saying that they should repeat the message of Lord Kṛṣṇa as spoken in the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and Bhagavad-gītā. This is how to preach Kṛṣṇa consciousness. One has to be fully dependent and have firm faith.

Prabhupāda also writes in Mārkine Bhāgavata-dharma, “I have no devotion, nor do I have any knowledge, but I have strong faith in the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. I have been designated as Bhaktivedanta, and now, if You like, You can fulfill the real purport of Bhaktivedanta.”

In the beginning of his prayers, when he says that he is useless, this is the genuine feeling of a devotee. Such a devotee feels as though he has no devotion or knowledge. However, he has firm faith in Kṛṣṇa and in the holy name.

Therefore, Prabhupāda writes further in his prayer that if Kṛṣṇa wants to make them hear, He can do so. He prays for the Lord’s mercy to be able to convince them about His message.

If a devotee thinks himself the doer, then he will think that his progress is shown through that which manifests externally. He will not be able to look at what is in his heart, and he will become proud, thinking that Kṛṣṇa is not involved in the affair. It is easy to forget Kṛṣṇa when one thinks himself to be the doer.

The ācāryas give the example of the summer season in India during which the grass has mostly dried up. When the ass is eating some grass in the summer season, he looks around and sees that there is very little grass. Therefore, he eats just a little grass, but when he looks around him and sees that there is no grass around, he thinks that he has eaten so much and he becomes fat. Whereas in the winter, there is so much grass everywhere. Thus the ass is eating so much, but when he looks around, still there is so much grass! Even though he was eating so much, he thinks that he has eaten nothing, and he gets skinny. To him, everything is based upon external factors.

Similarly, a foolish person thinks himself to be the doer if he looks externally at what he has done. He becomes very proud of his accomplishment. He may think that he has preached very nicely, made devotees, distributed so many books, etc. However, he is possessed of that false ego (ahaṅkāra), thinking himself to be the doer. But if he sits down, tries to deeply chant Hare Kṛṣṇa, remember the Lord, depend on the Lord, meditate on the Lord’s pastimes, meditate on the holy name of the Lord and how it is non-different from the Lord, he foolishly thinks: “I am not doing anything! Better that I accomplish something external. In that way, I can think that I am the doer.” However, in such a case, devotion will not rise in the heart, which is contrary to the goal of all our activities.

*bhaktiḥ pareśānubhavo viraktir*  
*anyatra caiṣa trika eka-kālaḥ*  
*prapadyamānasya yathāśnataḥ syus*  
*tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭiḥ kṣud-apāyo ’nu-ghāsam*

**Devotion, direct experience of the Supreme Lord, and detachment from other things—these three occur simultaneously for one who has taken shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in the same way that pleasure, nourishment and relief from hunger come simultaneously and increasingly, with each bite, for a person engaged in eating. (Bhāg. 11.2.42)**

This is how one should know that he is making progress; not by how much he has accomplished externally. Of course, however, Śrīla Prabhupāda encouraged us to produce results for spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Śrīla Prabhupāda encouraged both simultaneously. However, if he saw pride in our heart, he was always ready to cut it. If somebody was thinking that they could impress Prabhupāda by what they were doing, or by how much they were doing, Prabhupāda would say, “You are supposed to be a fool before your spiritual master. Yet you are coming before me and telling me how much you are doing!” He would cut the pride because he knew that real progress will come when there is the feeling of dependence in the heart, and when one is crying out, “Kṛṣṇa, please help me!” Therefore, Śrīla Prabhupāda would sometimes take the devotees (who were apparently producing so many results) out of that position and put them in a situation where they were completely helpless again.

Those who have substance can preach. However, those who think that they need all the external things to preach, such as position, prestige and facilities, cannot preach. The substance of Kṛṣṇa consciousness is what produces Kṛṣṇa consciousness in the hearts of others. We can thus see how Śrīla Prabhupāda was so successful. Prabhupāda appeared to have come with nothing—simply forty rupees and a trunk full of books. However, Prabhupāda had everything he needed—he had firm faith in the holy name, total humility, and complete dependence on the will of the Lord. This is the perfect formula for spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Prabhupāda is teaching us in this beautiful prayer that no matter what we are doing in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, we can take shelter of this prayer. It does not make any difference, whether we are preaching, distributing books, worshiping the deities, or building temples.

Everyone should try to do something to please the Lord, including chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, remembering Kṛṣṇa, and praying to Kṛṣṇa. It is a task that cannot be accomplished on our own. If we think we can become Kṛṣṇa conscious by our own efforts, we are very foolish.

Kṛṣṇa describes who the greatest yogī is:

*yogīnām api sarveṣāṁ*  
*mad-gatenāntarātmanā*  
*śraddhāvān bhajate yo māṁ*  
*sa me yuktatamo mataḥ*

**And of all yogīs, the one with great faith who always abides in Me, thinks of Me within himself, and renders transcendental loving service to Me—he is the most intimately united with Me in yoga and is the highest of all. That is My opinion. (Bg. 6.47)**

Such a person is the highest yogī because he knows that he cannot do anything himself. Those who are proud of their knowledge and wealth think that they can do everything themselves and do not need God. For those who are free from pride are always fully dependent upon the Lord, and they know that they cannot do anything by their own efforts: “How can I remember Kṛṣṇa unless Kṛṣṇa helps me to remember Him? Kṛṣṇa has to even agree to manifest himself in my mind.” Nobody can demand anything of Kṛṣṇa, except those who have pure love for Him, such as Mother Yaśodā, the cowherd boys and the gopīs. Kṛṣṇa says:

*teṣāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ*  
*bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam*  
*dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ*  
*yena mām upayānti te*

**“To those who are constantly devoted to serving Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.” (Bg. 10.10)**

To be constantly devoted is an internal endeavor—to remember Kṛṣṇa, to depend upon Him, and to pray to Him. To the degree that we make this internal endeavor, Kṛṣṇa will help us. Somehow or other we have to keep the desire to do something to please Kṛṣṇa burning in our hearts. We cannot let that fire go out. To do so, we must hear from those who inspire and encourage us to keep remembering that Kṛṣṇa consciousness is the goal, and who help us to remember Kṛṣṇa in all circumstances. We must take their help to make progress in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Our desire to become Kṛṣṇa conscious must always be greater than our desire to stay in this material world. We must check to see how much this devotion is manifesting in our heart. If we take inventory of our spiritual desires and they do not seem to be growing, then we need to associate with those who help us to make it grow. We have to have that intense eagerness to seek out the association of, and hear from, those who help us to make it grow.

Lord Kapiladeva says:

*ta ete sādhavaḥ sādhvi*  
*sarva-saṅga-vivarjitāḥ*  
*saṅgas teṣv atha te prārthyaḥ*  
*saṅga-doṣa-harā hi te*

**“O My mother, O virtuous lady, these are the qualities of great devotees who are free from all attachment. You must seek attachment to such holy men, for this counteracts the pernicious effects of material attachment.” (Bhāg. 3.25.24)**

The seed of desire that is planted in our heart will grow when it is properly watered. If it is not being watered, it will dry up. That watering process is continued hearing to keep that desire alive. Kṛṣṇa says:

*atha cittaṁ samādhātuṁ*  
*na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram*  
*abhyāsa-yogena tato*  
*mām icchāptuṁ dhanañjaya*

**“My dear Arjuna, O winner of wealth, if you cannot fix your mind upon Me without deviation, then follow the regulative principles of bhakti-yoga. In this way, develop a desire to attain Me.” (Bg. 12.9)**

The regulative principles of bhakti-yoga refer to regularly hearing about Kṛṣṇa. By so doing, one will develop a desire to attain Kṛṣṇa. We must want to become Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

Prabhupāda is showing us by his example in this prayer that whatever we are doing in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, we should pray in this way—especially for those who are preaching Kṛṣṇa consciousness. This will help to keep us free from pride. Kṛṣṇa says that if we act in false ego, we will be lost. However, if we remember Him, He will protect us. Not only does He promise this, but His devotees promise it, and we can therefore be assured of the Lord’s protection, as He always protects the words of His devotees.

Prabhupāda has made so many promises for us on Kṛṣṇa’s behalf: “Kṛṣṇa, somehow or other please let me convince them. I have implicit faith in Your holy name. I will try to give them Your message. Please, therefore, purify their hearts and make them devotees.” All of us have that benediction of Prabhupāda’s prayer! We should take advantage of that benediction and reciprocate with him by taking up his mood and mission to preach Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Become Kṛṣṇa conscious, and become happy in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. This is what Prabhupāda wanted to see for all of us.

Thus, on the Jaladuta on September 18, 1965, Prabhupāda prayed just like this for all of us. We should therefore chant this prayer and remember it. We should try to cultivate this mood in all of our efforts in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, and then certainly we can be successful in our spiritual life. It does not depend on our own efforts alone, but will come by the grace of the devotees of the Lord.

**Question: Śrīla Prabhupāda always felt full dependence on Kṛṣṇa. How can we learn to accept everything, including our suffering, as the mercy of Kṛṣṇa?**

When we are not suffering, we usually think that we are happy, and when we are suffering, we usually do not see Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. However, Kṛṣṇa is so kind that He will put us in a situation where we are seemingly suffering. However, to not be suffering is simply a false perception of happiness. Forgetting Kṛṣṇa is hell for a devotee, and that is the real definition of suffering. Kṛṣṇa does not want us to forget Him. For that reason, He sometimes puts His devotee in a suffering condition. Such is His mercy! By seeing Kṛṣṇa’s hand in our suffering, then mukti-pade sa dāya-bhāk—mukti (liberation from this material world) becomes our rightful claim, and devotional service to Kṛṣṇa becomes our rightful claim.

Thus, we should see Kṛṣṇa’s hand in our suffering, and accept it as His mercy. Additionally, Kṛṣṇa does not give that kind of mercy to everybody. He will not take away something from a nondevotee; māyā will do that. Kṛṣṇa does not have to get involved at all, as māyā does it perfectly. His energy acts very perfectly according to His will, and therefore He does not need to personally deal with the karmic reactions of the living entities. Yet when he does, the devotee is most fortunate. The Lord will only take from His devotees; not from the nondevotees. Such is His mercy!

**Question: How can we receive Śrīla Prabhupāda’s blessings?**

Gratitude is the essence of our practicing Kṛṣṇa consciousness. If we feel a sense of gratitude within our hearts for a great gift that has been given to us, it means that we have understood how valuable it is in our life. The more we realize how valuable it is, the more the gratitude increases. Such is the nature of this gift that Śrīla Prabhupāda has given us in the association of the Vaiṣṇavas. Each and every feeling of gratitude increases our opportunity to reciprocate by offering something in return, which is insignificant in comparison to what we are being given.

Śrīla Prabhupāda has actually given us the opportunity to experience a dynamic exchange of reciprocal love for Kṛṣṇa of which Śrīla Prabhupāda, of course, is the fountainhead. A devotee feels a sense of gratitude for him having touched our hearts and having given us an opportunity to take part in his mission.

In the early days of the movement, Śrīla Prabhupāda was pleased by the efforts of the devotees to establish Kṛṣṇa consciousness. They would work so hard just to see his smile. That smile was the most captivating experience, and the devotees did not want to lose it. Prabhupāda’s radiant smile seemed to go from ear to ear. For the devotees, that smile was life itself! The devotees had the opportunity to see it on a daily basis in reciprocation for their hard efforts that they made to please Śrīla Prabhupāda. They would struggle and perform greater austerities just for another smile.

Gratitude is something that is ever expansive and very deep, like a great ocean. It is the essence of our existence in bhakti-yoga. The more we appreciate how fortunate we are to have the opportunity to be in the association of such wonderful Vaiṣṇavas who know how to make Śrīla Prabhupāda smile, the more we will be able to dedicate our lives to assisting Śrīla Prabhupāda and all the wonderful devotees, and continuing Prabhupāda’s mission for spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness into every nook and corner throughout this entire world. Śrīla Prabhupāda smiles when he sees Kṛṣṇa consciousness expanding, even if it is by some small endeavor. Prabhupāda takes the desire of the devotee to do something to please him and offers it to Kṛṣṇa. His desire is to offer a garland of devotees and place it around Kṛṣṇa’s neck. Thus Kṛṣṇa smiles upon him, he smiles upon us, and all the devotees whom we assist in spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness will smile upon us.

This is all that is required to go back home, back to Godhead. Such is the kindness and mercy of Śrīla Prabhupāda. We have the opportunity to achieve the highest benediction that one could possibly accomplish in the human form of life—to enter into the transcendental līlā of Kṛṣṇa in Goloka Vṛndāvana, simply by taking part in this effort to make Śrīla Prabhupāda smile.

We have to struggle with many difficulties that need to be overcome, but Prabhupāda is pleased by these efforts that we make every day to go on and try to give Kṛṣṇa consciousness to others and to become Kṛṣṇa conscious ourselves.

The whole path of devotional service is an ongoing process of purification of the heart. The more the heart becomes purified and cleansed of its unwanted anarthas, the more we begin to experience the full glory of devotional service. Just as the sun is self-effulgent and there is no darkness in the sun, our experience of the sun is eclipsed by the presence of clouds or fog. Similarly, the holy name of the Lord is transcendentally blissful, nondifferent from Kṛṣṇa, and full of unlimited bliss. Yet we may not fully experience the complete bliss of the holy name of the Lord because of the existence of the clouds of anarthas and the fog of ignorance, which is obstructing our experience of the pure holy name.

The cumulative effect of our efforts in devotional service, which are always dependent upon the association of Vaiṣṇavas, is the cleansing of the heart. The more the heart becomes clean from unwanted desires, the more our experience of pure Kṛṣṇa consciousness becomes a tangible reality. Then, the more we will experience the greatness of Kṛṣṇa consciousness and that which Śrīla Prabhupāda has given to all of his followers for generations to come in the form of association of Vaiṣṇavas, the holy name of the Lord, and various other valuable gifts that Prabhupāda has contributed.

The more we realize the greatness of Kṛṣṇa consciousness, the more we realize and experience the taste of Kṛṣṇa consciousness, and the more we feel gratitude for the gift that we have been given. This will only increase more as our heart becomes cleansed. An expression of gratitude manifests to the degree that we realize how wonderful something that we have been given is.

Hearing descriptions of devotees’ experiences in Kṛṣṇa consciousness and their association with Prabhupāda in the early years is very precious to me. My heart dances when I hear of the exchanges they had with Śrīla Prabhupāda, the struggles and difficulties they had to endure, and the ingenious ways in which they took up Śrīla Prabhupāda’s order. Just hearing of these things increases my realization of what an extremely valuable gift has been bestowed upon this unworthy, unqualified person. I do not know how I came to Kṛṣṇa consciousness; sometimes it is bewildering to me! However, I know it was Śrīla Prabhupāda’s mercy. Hearing about the efforts of these devotees from the early days makes me feel that I too have been captivated by Kṛṣṇa consciousness by their mercy, because somehow they were so intimately interwoven with Śrīla Prabhupāda’s efforts to spread Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Somehow, some of that mercy must have flowed through them and captured me at some point in the early 1970s, and I was touched, unknown, by some efforts that they made to serve Śrīla Prabhupāda in the late 1960s and early 1970s.

I simply pray to be in the association of those who are hearing and chanting the glories of Śrīla Prabhupāda forever. Hearing about Śrīla Prabhupāda is hari katha. Prabhupāda said in his Caitanya- caritāmṛta, “Lord Caitanya sent Lord Nityānanda to Bengal to preach. He sent Rūpa and Sanātana to Vṛndāvana. However, He left the rest of the world to the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement.” This Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is a part of the pastimes of the Lord.

Prabhupāda once said: “Five plus five is equal to ten. Two plus two is equal to four. So Kṛṣṇa plus everything is Vṛndāvana. Do not forget Kṛṣṇa and you shall always be in Vṛndāvana.”

The residents of Vṛndāvana are selflessly motivated by every fiber of their transcendental spiritual bodies to satisfy Kṛṣṇa. The selfless efforts of the devotees to satisfy Śrīla Prabhupāda is nondifferent than the mood of Vṛndāvana. Those selfless efforts that have been made by the devotees to satisfy their spiritual master, Śrīla Prabhupāda, is actually the real meaning of bringing this mood of Vṛndāvana everywhere. To bring the mood of Vṛndāvana means to bring a selfless spirit of preaching Kṛṣṇa consciousness, as was done by those who executed Śrīla Prabhupāda’s desires as their life and soul.

Prabhupāda said in one of his purports in Bhāgavatam, “Do not think that you will find Kṛṣṇa simply by looking behind some bush in Vṛndāvana. You will find Kṛṣṇa by strictly following the order of the spiritual master. Kṛṣṇa will manifest Himself to you.” Thus, the devotees who are strictly following the orders of their spiritual master, simply trying to satisfy him, are creating this Vṛndāvana mood and giving it to others by spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness. That is what Śrīla Prabhupāda wanted from all of his followers—for them to taste this experience of selflessly sacrificing to please the spiritual master, and, having gained this experience, to go out and give it to others. Prabhupāda was so anxious to make others fortunate as well.

Prabhupāda said that if you hear nicely, then you can chant, and then there will be smaraṇaṁ, remembrance in the heart. The result of this process of śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ viṣṇoḥ smaraṇaṁ is ceto-darpaṇa-mārjanaṁ—it cleanses the mirror of the heart. This is what we want to accomplish by coming in the association of devotees.
