Sometimes there will be brahmacārīs who are involved in activities such as building maintenance and cleaning the temple, which are connected to Deity worship. These are the primary activities in the temple. All other activities are in the extended community. One does not have to get married if he cannot live in the brahmacārī-āśrama. If he lives outside the temple and is not married, then he is a congregational member. There is a whole community of devotees, and there are still other services he can do within the community. The devotee should not feel forced to get married. It is a lack of proper approach to force somebody to get married. However, he should understand that he has to do something besides living in the brahmacārī āśrama if he is unable to remain there. Sometimes devotees who live outside the āśrama work for some other devotee who has a business. They may live close to the temple, and still come to the morning program. They have a way to maintain themselves, and they become more specialized in their work. They can still associate with the devotees in the temple. However, they are not forced to get married.

**Question: What should be done if a brahmacārī knows the standards of the āśrama, but due to lack of surrender, he is still unable to follow them?**

One approach is to try to bring him back up to the high standard by the proper inspiration. Somebody else may have to help him to become more properly situated and instruct him on the steps that need to be taken to do so. That brahmacārī may need a major psychological adjustment.

The Bhāgavatam describes the Haryaśvas and the Savalāśvas—the sons of Prajāpati Dakṣa. Although Dakṣa wanted them to prepare for householder life, he wanted them to prepare themselves by undergoing austerities, and then to become householders and procreate. However, Nārada Muni inspired them all in the path of nivṛtti-mārga. Due to this inspiration, they did not have to get entangled in household life. Instead, they took to the path of renunciation.

However, for those who are unable to follow that path, there has to be somebody else who helps them in their transition to a different path, and to help them understand the responsibilities that still need to be upheld so that they can remain responsible devotees. The devotee should not feel that he has failed. That is very important. Household life is not failure—especially according to Vedic standards.

One should also be taking shelter from the instructions of the spiritual masters—not just one’s initiating spiritual master, but those Vaiṣṇavas whose instructions become the foundation of our spiritual life. A Vaiṣṇava is one who is actually sheltered. He has spiritual strength. With spiritual strength, he can overcome the obstacles of conditional life. One must hear from Vaiṣṇavas. There should be other devotees to help one to surrender to the essence of the spiritual master’s instructions.

There is the difference between bahirmukha-śiṣya and antarmukha-śiṣya. The bahirmukha-śiṣya simply sees the external instruction, but he has to understand the essence of the instructions.

**Question: How essential is it to have a brahmacārī counselor for the brahmacārīs, and to have a gṛhastha counselor for the gṛhasthas? Can one have a counselor from another āśrama?**

If the brahmacārī is finding that it is difficult for him to stay in the brahmacārī-āśrama, then certainly he should have a gṛhastha counselor to help him in his transition. However, it should be understood that he is making a transition. Otherwise, a gṛhastha should not be a counselor for brahmacārīs. A brahmacārī may go to a gṛhastha for some instructions, but his counselor should be a brahmacārī.

Similarly a brahmacārī can preach to gṛhasthas, but he should not be their official counselor.

**Question: How should a brahmacārī learn to surrender to the temple authorities? Should he simply accept everything he is told to do, even if he does not understand the purpose?**

To surrender means: tṛṇād api sunīcena, taror api sahiṣnunā, amāninā mānadena, kirtaniya sada hari—one must feel himself to be very humble, lower than the straw on the street; more tolerant than a tree; not wanting recognition for himself; being ready to offer all respects to everyone. Until one actually comes to this platform, there is no relationship with Lord Caitanya. One simply lives under the illusory energy. Therefore, if one really wants to cultivate an attitude of surrender, ultimately he has to surrender to the holy name. One must make the holy name his only shelter. When one actually feels sheltered by the holy name, which is non-different from the Lord, then everything else becomes revealed to him.

If one cannot achieve that platform of surrender, then he should at least know the direction towards which he wants to move. He should always seek those instructions which help him make progress on that path, and he should not blame others for his own misfortune.

**Question: Is there a shift in emphasis away from book distribution?**

There is a shift in emphasis, but is not away from book distribution. From my own experience, I saw what happened when book distribution was always preached as the top priority. Many brahmacārīs thought that they were so superior to everybody else because they distributed books. However, I watched them fall, one by one, because Lord Caitanya does not tolerate this kind of pride. Book distribution is still very important. The shift in emphasis is simply ensuring that the right motivation is there for distributing books. Thus, the shift in emphasis is in the attitude, not in the service.

**Question: If there is pressure on a brahmacārī to change his āśrama because it is better for the needs of the community, is it justified?**

Sometimes a brahmacārī is really not a brahmacārī. However he cannot be told that, because he will not hear it. Therefore, the authority may present it in such a way that it encourages the brahmacārī to see that it is a meaningful sacrifice for the needs of the community. However, it is not something that should be pressured. The authority is actually helping the person to understand that the symptoms he is manifesting are not going to provide for lifelong stability as a brahmacārī. Before the brahmacārī reaches thirty-five or forty, when it is really late to start married life, he may need to start thinking about taking that responsibility of figuring out how to maintain a family. The brahmacārī may perceive that suggestion as pressure, but actually it is well-wishing. It is only perceived as pressure because he cannot hear it in any other way. However, the authority should still try to think of the benefits of the devotees for their future. A caring counselor will also try to introduce that idea to such a person so that he does not just flounder for ten or fifteen years and then realize that he should have listened to his authorities fifteen years ago. Yet the point remains that he should not be pressured to get married.

## Gṛhastha-āśrama

*āśvāghānte ’vasāyibhyaḥ*  
*kāmān saṁvibhajed yathā*  
*apy ekām ātmano dārāṁ*  
*nṛṇāṁ svatva-graho yataḥ*

**Dogs, fallen persons and untouchables, including caṇḍālas \[dog-eaters\], should all be maintained with their proper necessities, which should be contributed by the householders. Even one’s wife at home, with whom one is most intimately attached, should be offered for the reception of guests and people in general. (Bhāg. 7.14.11)**

PURPORT

Although in modern society the dog is accepted as part of one’s household paraphernalia, in the Vedic system of household life the dog is untouchable; as mentioned here, a dog may be maintained with proper food, but it cannot be allowed to enter one’s house, what to speak of the bedroom. Outcastes or untouchable caṇḍālas should also be provided with the necessities for life. The word used in this connection is yathā, which means “as much as deserved.” The outcastes should not be given money with which to indulge in more than they need, for otherwise they will misuse it. At the present moment, for example, low-class men are generally paid quite amply, but instead of using their money to cultivate knowledge and advance in life, such low-class men use their extra money for wine-drinking and similar sinful activities. As mentioned in Bhagavad-gītā (4.13), cātur-varṇyaṁ mayā sṛṣṭaṁ guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśaḥ: there must be four divisions of human society according to the work and qualities of men. Men with the lowest qualities cannot do any work that requires higher intelligence. However, although such a division of men must exist according to their quality and work, it is suggested herewith that everyone must have the necessities of life. The communists of the present day are in favor of supplying the necessities of life to everyone, but they consider only the human beings and not the lower animals. The Bhāgavatam’s principles are so broad, however, that it recommends that the necessities of life be supplied to everyone, man or animal, regardless of good or bad qualities.

The idea of giving even one’s wife to the service of the public is that one’s intimate relationship with his wife or one’s excessive attachment for his wife, by which one thinks his wife to be his better half or to be identical with himself, must gradually be given up. As formerly suggested, the idea of ownership, even of one’s family, must be abandoned. The dream of material life is the cause of bondage in the cycle of birth and death, and therefore one should give up this dream. Consequently, in the human form of life one’s attachment for his wife should be given up, as suggested herein.

This verse describes the duties of one who is in household life. It says that is the responsibility of the householder to maintain even dogs, fallen persons and untouchables including caṇḍālas. Even one’s wife should be offered for the reception of guests and people in general in one’s home.

*puṁsaḥ striyā mithunī-bhāvam etaṁ*  
*tayor mitho hṛdaya-granthim āhuḥ*  
*ato gṛha-kṣetra-sutāpta-vittair*  
*janasya moho ’yam ahaṁ mameti*

**The attraction between male and female is the basic principle of material existence. On the basis of this misconception, which ties together the hearts of the male and female, one becomes attracted to his body, home, property, children, relatives and wealth. In this way one increases life’s illusions and thinks in terms of “I and mine.” (Bhāg. 5.5.8)**

This verse was spoken by Lord Ṛṣabhadeva. It explains the dangers that one can fall into if he is not careful in household life. One can become very much attached; and attachment to anything which is temporary is a cause of bondage for the living entity. Thus it is the duty of the householder to gradually give up the conception of “I and mine.”

*prasaṅgam ajaraṁ pāśam*  
*ātmanaḥ kavayo viduḥ*  
*sa eva sādhuṣu kṛto*  
*mokṣa-dvāram apāvṛtam*

**Every learned man knows very well that attachment for the material is the greatest entanglement of the spirit soul. But that same attachment, when applied to the self-realized devotees, opens the door of liberation. (Bhāg. 3.25.20)**

There is a tendency for one to become increasingly attached in his home, and the implications that come with such attachment are great sufferings.

Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam describes the story of the Avantī brāhmaṇa who was engaged in commerce and had great wealth. However, he was very miserly and was attached to increasing his wealth. He did not show proper respect to his family members and to the guests at his home. Gradually his family members became very disturbed with him and stopped showing him any affection.

The five presiding deities of the five sacrifices necessary to be performed by householders became very disturbed due to his neglect. Because they had become so disturbed, gradually he lost all his wealth. Some of the wealth of this so-called brāhmaṇa was taken away by his relatives, some by thieves, some by the whims of providence, some by the effects of time, some by ordinary men and some by the government authorities. He lost everything because he did not perform any sacrifices, thus dissatisfying the presiding deities of the five sacrifices known as pañca-mahā-yajña.

According to dharma-śastra, and also as mentioned by Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī in Tattva-sandarbha, it is the responsibility of every householder to perform these five sacrifices daily. These five sacrifices are meant to satisfy the demigods, forefathers, all human beings, all living entities and the sages. These sacrifices have to be performed. It is described that the householder performs these five sacrifices because he is implicated in five places in his home: at his stove for cooking, at the stone for grinding rice, with his broom, with his mortar and pestle, and with his water pot. These five places are described as slaughter houses, because so many living entities are being killed. Thus, to become freed from the reaction of causing suffering to these living entities, one has to perform these five types of sacrifices.

One of the sacrifices is for the benefit of all human beings, which means that the householder must receive guests in his home and give charity to them. The living entities are bhūtas. Another sacrifice, done for sages, is sacrifice without fire, which is the chanting of Vedic mantras. The five deities of sacrifices have to be satisfied by the performance of the respective sacrifices.

In the story of the Avantī brāhmaṇa, although he had great wealth, he did not satisfy the presiding deities of the sacrifices, and thus in due course of time everything was taken away from him. The more one becomes attached to things, the more painful it is for the living entity to have to lose them.

*kṛṣṇa—sūrya-sama; māyā haya andhakāra*  
*yāhāṅ kṛṣṇa, tāhāṅ nāhi māyāra adhikāra*

**“Kṛṣṇa is compared to sunshine, and māyā is compared to darkness. Wherever there is sunshine, there cannot be darkness. As soon as one takes to Kṛṣṇa consciousness, the darkness of illusion (the influence of the external energy) will immediately vanish. (Cc. Madhya 22.31)**

Therefore, one must give up his material attachments by becoming attached to Kṛṣṇa. Of course, this verse on which I am speaking (Bhāg. 7.14.11) describes how various types of sacrifices help one to become free from attachment. One of the primary duties of the householder is to give in charity, as it helps him to become free from the conception that he is simply accumulating it all for himself or for his family.

In the Bhāgavatam, Śrīla Prabhupāda explains that such a home where the brāhmaṇas and Vaiṣṇavas are never invited and where there is never any water to wash their feet is compared to be like a tree where a serpent is living. Sometimes a venomous serpent will take shelter of the sandalwood tree because its body is very hot and the sandalwood tree is cooling. That tree thus becomes its home. Similarly, any home which does not welcome guests, brāhmaṇas and Vaiṣṇavas, and does not receive them to bathe their feet is simply like this tree that is the home of the snake.

The Bhāgavatam also gives the example of King Rantideva. Rantideva lived very simply. He did not endeavor for economic development, but simply accepted whatever providence provided for him. Even though he lived so simply, had so little, and his body would shiver because of lack of sufficient food, still he would give profusely to any guest that came to his home.

One time, Mahārāja Rantideva had performed a forty-eight day fast and was about to break his fast with some water and foodstuffs made with milk and ghee, which he had received that morning. At the moment when he and his family members were going to break their fast, a brāhmaṇa came to his home. Because Mahārāja Rantideva had such spiritual vision, he could see the Supreme Personality of Godhead within the heart of everyone, and therefore he saw this brāhmaṇa as a representative of the Supreme Lord. When the brāhmaṇa entered his home, he gave a portion of his food to him, and the remainder he divided amongst his family members.

After he divided the remainder of food amongst his family members, a śūdra entered his home. Of course, Mahārāja Rantideva also saw the Lord within the heart of this śūdra. He therefore gave him a portion of his portion of food. After so doing, a man came to his home with many dogs. Mahārāja Rantideva took all the remaining food from his portion and gave it to this man and his dogs. All he had left was some water.

As he was about to break his fast with the water, one caṇḍāla entered into his home and said, “O my dear king, I am very thirsty. Could you please give me some water?”

Whatever water was left, Mahārāja Rantideva gave to the caṇḍāla, and was then left with nothing. However, he began offering words of glorification to the Lord, and began describing how he became so fully satisfied because he was satisfying the Supreme Personality of Godhead by seeing the Supreme Lord as the Supersoul in the heart of all living beings, and therefore he no longer felt any thirst or hunger. The Lord was so satisfied by his sacrifices.

Actually, all of these persons who came to his house were demigods who had come to show the real glories of Mahārāja Rantideva, who saw the Supreme Lord present within the heart of everyone, and was ready to give whatever he had in charity.

There is another example for this point. It is a story about Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura. Once, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta went with many of his household disciples to the temple of Sākṣi-gopāla. In front of the temple, there were many beggars. The householders decided amongst themselves to not give in charity to the beggars, but instead to give to God.

However, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura chastised them: “You are not giving to the beggars. You must understand that the Supersoul is within their hearts. When you are giving charity, you are giving to the Lord within the heart.” He went on to explain that even in the temple, whenever a guest comes and whoever he may be, he should be given some food. This is the atithi-nārāyaṇa principle (respecting the uninvited or unscheduled guest as if he were God). However, one should not give food regularly to the same beggars, because then they will simply come for food. Thus we must see the Supreme Personality of God within the hearts of all living beings.

Even Śivānanda Sena also gave food to a dog. Thus there are many examples in śāstra which describe giving in charity, which is the essence of this verse. The dogs, fallen persons and untouchables including caṇḍālas should all be maintained with proper necessities which should be contributed by the householders.

There is a very nice quote by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī where he describes how one should live in his house. The following is an excerpt:

It is good to live in one’s own house with the desire to serve the Lord; then one can serve the Lord properly. But this is not possible for the illusioned householder attached to money, the opposite sex, and name and fame. One should enter into his house resolving to serve Kṛṣṇa. That is much better than false renunciation. Nothing good can come from false renunciation. If one’s household life is favorable for devotional service then that is acceptable. On the contrary, if it is unfavorable for devotional service then such a deep, dark pit called “home” should be given up. But if one wants to show off his desire for renunciation and artificially show some detachment then that is not beneficial. Such an immature renunciate will fall from his position in a few days.

The tendencies of the illusioned house-holders can only be destroyed by associating with the devotees of the Lord. Those who enter into household life following the rules of the external world will be more and more absorbed in the illusioned condition. Just as some devotees of the Lord need to enter into the sannyāsa-āśrama (the lifestyle of a renunciate), in the same way some need to enter into the gṛhastha-āśrama (the lifestyle of a householder). The festival known as gṛha-praveśa (the ceremony of entering a house for the first time) should be celebrated only by a devotee householder, not a non-devotee householder. When a devotee enters his house we should know that he has actually entered his temple. For a devotee, there is no difference between entering his house and entering a temple. But there is a heaven-and-hell difference between a devotee’s entering his house and a non-devotee’s entering his house.

One should enter one’s house only to always engage oneself in the service and thoughts of Kṛṣṇa, and to have everything favorable for that. The householder should always stay away from bad association and gossip. He should nurture with great care qualities such as enthusiasm, determination, and patience, and devotional practices such as hearing and chanting, śravana-kīrtana. To serve Hari, guru, and Vaiṣṇava, to chant śrī nāma, to associate with sādhus, and to hear about the Lord are the essential duties of householders. If all their endeavors are directed toward the service of the Lord they will definitely benefit, they will be protected, and their lives will be fulfilled.”

**Question: There are many responsibilities in household life— taking care of the spouse, taking care of the child, performing household activities, working, etc. When we sit to chant, all these things remain on our mind. In Kṛṣṇa consciousness, how can we prevent all of these activities from affecting our consciousness, especially while chanting the holy name?**

Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says that three essential ingredients are required for our development in our chanting of Hare Kṛṣṇa. The first is that we should always try to chant in the association of devotees who have taste.

Lord Kapiladeva tells His mother, Devahūti:

*mad-āśrayāḥ kathā mṛṣṭāḥ*  
*śṛṇvanti kathayanti ca*  
*tapanti vividhās tāpā*  
*naitān mad-gata-cetasaḥ*

*ta ete sādhavaḥ sādhvi*  
*sarva-saṅga-vivarjitāḥ*  
*saṅgas teṣv atha te prārthyaḥ*  
*saṅga-doṣa-harā hi te*

**“Engaged constantly in chanting and hearing about Me, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the sādhus do not suffer from material miseries because they are always filled with thoughts of My pastimes and activities. O My mother, O virtuous lady, these are the qualities of great devotees who are free from all attachment. You must seek attachment to such holy men, for this counteracts the pernicious effects of material attachment.” (Bhāg. 3.25.23-24)**

The second ingredient is removing oneself from all distractions externally and internally. Internal distractions are the different anarthas within our heart. We can recognize those anarthas as obstacles on the path of devotional service. Desiring to overcome these anarthas becomes an impetus for prayer while we are chanting. To deal with external distractions, we should try to chant in a place which is separate from our daily business. We should try to chant in a place which does not evoke memories of the things that we are ordinarily busy with.

For example, if a man is busy all day working on the computer, then obviously he should not chant his rounds in front of the computer or in his office, because everything he sees immediately stimulates his thoughts of his external duties, and very easily become a distraction to his japa. For householder women at home, they should try to chant when their children are sleeping. They should try to chant in a place that evokes thoughts of Kṛṣṇa, such as before the Deity or Tulasī-devī. They should chant in an environment which will not stimulate thoughts about their other duties that consume the better part of their day.

The third essential ingredient for chanting the holy name is to have very firm determination. If one practically applies these three ingredients, he will be successful in his chanting.

**Question: What should be the mood of a married woman so that she and her husband advance spiritually? To what extent should she dedicate herself to serving her husband, children, and the temple?**

A wife’s duty is to serve her husband and children. Why be married if you do not serve your husband and children? If you do not serve your children when they are young, you will really regret it later.

In a letter from Prabhupāda, he told one devotee that his (the devotee’s) devotional service is raising his child properly. Prabhupāda told him that his most important service is to take responsibility and raise his child properly. Other services can be performed in relationship to the temple. However, one should be very careful to not neglect his household duties; otherwise it will simply disturb the marriage. One should not think that disturbances in the marriage are simply a product of Kali-yuga. A wife should serve her husband and children, and a husband should help the wife advance spiritually by setting the proper example and inspiring her in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Thus everyone has their particular duties to perform.

**Question: How can one engage his family life in service so as to make spiritual advancement?**

The principle is to put Kṛṣṇa in the center. One performs his household affairs as a matter of duty. Prabhupāda gives the example that when a wife has a paramour, she is more attentive to her household duties so that her husband never suspects she has a paramour. In the same way, a person who is engaged in household life performs those duties which need to be performed, but is focused on the Lord.

Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira inquired from Nārada Muni: “O my lord, O great sage, kindly explain how we who are staying at home without knowledge of the goal of life may also easily attain liberation, according to the instructions of the Vedas.”

Nārada Muni replied: “My dear King, those who stay at home as householders must act to earn their livelihood, and instead of trying to enjoy the results of their work themselves, they should offer these results to Kṛṣṇa, Vāsudeva. How to satisfy Vāsudeva in this life can be perfectly understood through the association of great devotees of the Lord.

“A gṛhastha must associate again and again with saintly persons, and with great respect he must hear the nectar of the activities of the Supreme Lord and His incarnations as these activities are described in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and other Purāṇas. Thus one should gradually become detached from affection for his wife and children, exactly like a man awakening from a dream.” (Bhāg. 7.14.1-4)

Nārada Muni explains that it is a gradual detachment; not an abrupt detachment. Gradually one has to become detached by the association with saintly persons. As he explains, the most important duty for householders is to offer the fruits of their work and to hear the pastimes of the Lord in the association of saintly persons.

PURPORT

The Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement has been established to give gṛhasthas all over the world an opportunity to hear Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and Bhagavad-gītā specifically. The process, as described in many ways, is one of hearing and chanting (śṛṇvatāṁ sva-kathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ \[Bhāg. 1.2.17\]). Everyone, especially the gṛhasthas, who are mūḍha-dhī, ignorant about the goal of life, should be given opportunities to hear about Kṛṣṇa. Simply by hearing, by attending lectures in the different centers of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, where topics of Kṛṣṇa from Bhagavad-gītā and Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam are discussed, they will be purified of their sinful inclination for constant indulgence in illicit sex, meat-eating, intoxication and gambling, which have all become prominent in modern days. Thus they can be raised to the status of light. Puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ. Simply by joining the kīrtana—Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare/ Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare—and by hearing about Kṛṣṇa from Bhagavad-gītā, one must be purified, especially if he also takes prasāda. This is all going on in the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement.

Another specific description here is śṛṇvan bhagavato ‘bhīkṣṇam avatāra-kathāmṛtam. It is not that because one has once finished Bhagavad-gītā he should not hear it again. The word abhīkṣṇam is very important. We should hear again and again. There is no question of stopping: even if one has read these topics many times, he should go on reading again and again because bhagavat-kathā, the words spoken by Kṛṣṇa and spoken by Kṛṣṇa’s devotees about Kṛṣṇa, are amṛtam, nectar. The more one drinks this amṛtam, the more he advances in his eternal life.

The human form of life is meant for liberation, but unfortunately, due to the influence of Kali-yuga, every day the gṛhasthas are working hard like asses. Early in the morning they rise and travel even a hundred miles away to earn bread. Especially in the Western countries, I have seen that people awaken at five o’clock to go to offices and factories to earn their livelihood. People in Calcutta and Bombay also do this every day. They work very hard in the office or factory, and again they spend three or four hours in transportation returning home. Then they retire at ten o’clock and again rise early in the morning to go to their offices and factories. This kind of hard labor is described in the śāstras as the life of pigs and stool-eaters. Nāyaṁ deho deha-bhājāṁ nṛloke kaṣṭān kāmān arhate vid-bhujāṁ ye: \[Bhāg. 5.5.1\] “Of all living entities who have accepted material bodies in this world, one who has been awarded this human form should not work hard day and night simply for sense gratification, which is available even for dogs and hogs that eat stool.” (Bhāg. 5.5.1) One must find some time for hearing Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and Bhagavad-gītā. This is Vedic culture. One should work eight hours at the most to earn his livelihood, and either in the afternoon or in the evening a householder should associate with devotees to hear about the incarnations of Kṛṣṇa and His activities and thus be gradually liberated from the clutches of māyā. However, instead of finding time to hear about Kṛṣṇa, the householders, after working hard in offices and factories, find time to go to a restaurant or a club where instead of hearing about Kṛṣṇa and His activities they are very much pleased to hear about the political activities of demons and nondevotees and to enjoy sex, wine, women and meat and in this way waste their time. This is not gṛhastha life, but demoniac life. The Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, however, with its centers all over the world, gives such fallen and condemned persons an opportunity to hear about Kṛṣṇa.

In a dream we form a society of friendship and love, and when we awaken we see that it has ceased to exist. Similarly, one’s gross society, family and love are also a dream, and this dream will be over as soon as one dies. Therefore, whether one is dreaming in a subtle way or a gross way, these dreams are all false and temporary. One’s real business is to understand that one is soul (ahaṁ brahmāsmi (38)) and that his activities should therefore be different. Then one can be happy.

*brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā*  
*na śocati na kāṅkṣati*  
*samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu*  
*mad-bhaktiṁ labhate parām*

“One who is transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman and becomes fully joyful. He never laments nor desires to have anything; he is equally disposed toward all living entities. In that state he attains pure devotional service unto Me.” (Bg. 18.54) One who is engaged in devotional service can very easily be liberated from the dream of materialistic life.

Śrīla Prabhupāda’s purport captures the essence of this verse and of all the instructions which are given in this chapter, titled Ideal Family Life.

Contrary to public opinion, there is an ideal family life. Sometimes when people talk about family life, especially those who have had so many difficulties and problems with family life, they think that there is no such thing as an ideal family life. However, we cannot challenge the conclusions of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and neither should we challenge the instructions of Śrī Nārada Muni, who has given those conclusions here in this chapter. All of our previous ācāryas have established their teachings on the principle that there is such a thing as ideal family life.

Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura and Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura have given extensive instructions about ideal family life. Lord Caitanya has also given instructions about family life. Śrīla Prabhupāda, of course, in his Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, has also given so many instructions about ideal family life. Lord Caitanya not only gave instructions, but He also demonstrated by living as an ideal householder. Although He took sannyāsa at the age of 24 and gave up His household life at a very young age, one should not utilize that as an excuse to renounce his responsibilities in family life unless he can have the same or similar effect in his preaching as Lord Caitanya did by accepting sannyāsa.

\[Nārada Muni continues\]: “While working to earn his livelihood as much as necessary to maintain body and soul together, one who is actually learned should live in human society unattached to family affairs, although externally appearing very much attached.” (Bhāg. 7.14.5)

Here, Nārada Muni is talking about a householder man—he has so many responsibilities to fulfill in relationship to family and society. Therefore, externally it has to appear as if he is very much attached, but internally he has to be detached by doing just as much as is necessary to maintain body and soul together for himself and for his family members.

“An intelligent man in human society should make his own program of activities very simple. If there are suggestions from his friends, children, parents, brothers or anyone else, he should externally agree, saying, ‘Yes, that is all right,’ but internally he should be determined not to create a cumbersome life in which the purpose of life will not be fulfilled. (Bhāg. 7.14.6)

“One may claim proprietorship to as much wealth as required to maintain body and soul together, but one who desires proprietorship over more than that must be considered a thief, and he deserves to be punished by the laws of nature.” (Bhāg. 7.14.8)

These are Nārada Muni’s instructions to Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja. Householders should live by simply keeping Kṛṣṇa at the center. They should hear regularly the pastimes of the Lord in the association of saintly persons. They should perform their duties in relationship to maintaining their household. However, they have to cultivate the spirit of detachment. The best way to do that is by regularly hearing Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam in the association of Vaiṣṇavas. By doing that, natural detachment will awaken within the heart. It is not recommended that one simply give up his duties and become a monkey renunciant.

Lord Caitanya did not want Raghunātha Dāsa to renounce his family duties. Lord Caitanya told him, “Do not become a monkey renunciant by externally renouncing your duties, while within your heart remaining attached to so many things. Go back and perform your duties with your family. You should appear externally as a pounds and shillings man—someone who is attached to his wealth—but within your heart you should always remember the Lord, and the Lord will gradually remove all these obstacles on the path.”

Thus, a householder must perform his duties, and not renounce them simply because they are too troublesome. Kṛṣṇa says that one who renounces his duties because they are too troublesome is doing so in the mode of passion, and it will always lead to suffering. Real renunciation must be awakened in the heart.

A householder man maintains his family members and satisfies his wife. A wife, as described in Bhāgavatam, is like the husband’s fortress, because she protects him. Therefore, she also has to satisfy her husband and must always be very chaste. They should raise their children in a responsible way. If they want their children to become Vaiṣṇavas, then they have to be an example for them. Śrīla Prabhupāda explains that the first impressions that the child gets are the most lasting impressions.

Prabhupāda explains that in his childhood, he was given a Deity to worship, which later became his worshipable Deity when he became older. He said that he gives all credit to his father for raising him with a desire to make him a servant of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. He further explains that it is the responsibility of the parents to see that their child gets very good impressions (saṁskāras) right from birth. Of course, proper saṁskāras must be there before birth (for conceiving the child), but then also for raising the child.

Lord Ṛṣabhadeva says (Bhāg. 5.5.18): “One who cannot deliver his dependents from the path of repeated birth and death should never become a spiritual master, a father, a husband, a mother or a worshipable demigod.”

These are the responsibilities that a person must follow in household life and should not renounce them because they are too troublesome. However, one must perform them in the spirit of detachment. The most important connection that one should keep, however, is with the temple. The temple is the place where one must go to hear the message of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and thus cultivate detachment.

Prabhupāda therefore said that temples should be established all over the world for the gṛhasthas so that they can come and hear. If a gṛhastha does not have a place to go and hear regularly about Kṛṣṇa, then he will fall victim to sinful activities in Kali-yuga.

If householders mold their life in such a way that they have association with saintly persons by hearing the transcendental narrations of the Lord, and hearing and chanting the glories of the holy name of the Lord, then gradually they will awaken from their attachments and affection to family members, just as a person gradually awakens from a dream. The goal certainly is to awaken from the dream.

Śrīla Prabhupāda explains that in family life, those who are gṛha mūḍha-dhī, or those who have forgotten the goal of life, form a society of friendship and love. He says that in a dream, a person may form this kind of society, but when he awakes, he sees that it does not exist. Similarly one’s gross society of family and love is also a dream. It will be over as soon as one dies. Therefore whether the dream is a subtle dream or a gross dream, both of them are temporary. One’s real business is therefore to understand his eternal identity as a soul. We have to awaken from this dreamlike state. When we go about our daily activities, even in the association of devotees, we may actually be dreaming. We have to find the time every day to hear about Kṛṣṇa.

Ideal family life is a life that is molded around spiritual activities. Sometimes even though one may be in the physical proximity of devotees, or one may be working with devotees, it is very easy to create another dream and fall again into this sleeping condition of life. Just as a materialistic person is gṛha mūḍha-dhī, it is also possible to be wearing a saffron or white dhotī, or wearing a sārī, and forget the goal of devotional service. We may create another society, but if that society is not based on the principles of ideal family life, then it is also a dream. Ultimately, we have to awaken from the dreamlike state and realize that we actually have activities and an identity beyond our connections with friends, family and society. If one does not mold his life upon hearing such transcendental subject matters about the Lord and chanting the holy name of the Lord, it is very difficult to awaken from that dream, especially at the point of death. One’s consciousness at the time of death will determine his destination in his next life. When death is approaching, it is not easy to extract his identity from this material body and all its connections. It is a very fearful condition.

If one learns how to gradually awaken from the dreamlike condition, then the time of death is not so abrupt. One who has been sufficiently trained throughout his life by hearing about transcendental topics and connections with the Lord prepares himself for giving up this body by fixing his consciousness on full remembrance of the Lord. One will remember at the time of death those topics which he has heard throughout his life. That is what forms our consciousness. Sound vibration is extremely powerful. If we do not hear śabda-brahma, transcendental sound vibration, which enters into the ear and then into the heart, then, based upon the sound vibration that we hear throughout this life, that will mold our consciousness.

*āyur harati vai puṁsām*  
*udyann astaṁ ca yann asau*  
*tasyarte yat-kṣaṇo nīta*  
*uttama-śloka-vārtayā*

**Both by rising and by setting, the sun decreases the duration of life of everyone, except one who utilizes the time by discussing topics of the all-good Personality of Godhead. (Bhāg. 2.3.17)**

A householder has a duty to discuss the activities of this world. He has domestic responsibilities, and there has to be discussions in connection to these things about economic development. However, they have to be done in such a way that it is minimal, in order to live, by accepting only the basic necessities of life. Therefore, by maintaining his body, his life, and his family members, then every day he has to find time to practice changing his consciousness. Otherwise he will continuously live in a dream.

**Question: How can we balance family responsibilities and devotional life?**

There is always a balancing act that every devotee has to perform. One has to establish the criteria for distinguishing between what he really needs and what he simply wants. If he does not establish that criteria, he will think that just because he wants something, then he must need it. When we can actually discriminate between what we need and what we want, then balance will come.

*yāvad bhriyeta jaṭharaṁ*  
*tāvat svatvaṁ hi dehinām*  
*adhikaṁ yo ’bhimanyeta*  
*sa steno daṇḍam arhati*

**One may claim proprietorship to as much wealth as required to maintain body and soul together, but one who desires proprietorship over more than that must be considered a thief, and he deserves to be punished by the laws of nature. (Bhāg. 7.14.8)**

One only needs as much as necessary to maintain body and soul together. However, practically speaking, everybody has a very difficult time establishing that line. Therefore, Lord Caitanya has so mercifully come to help establish that line. He said to Kūrma brāhmaṇa, “Take the higher taste of chanting My names, hearing about Me, and telling others about Me. If you live like this, then there will be no obstacles in your life.” Kūrma was a householder and wanted to give everything up and just join Lord Caitanya. However, Lord Caitanya instructed him to go back and live his householder life, but at the same time to take up His order.

*yāre dekha, tāre kaha ‘kṛṣṇa’-upadeśa*  
*āmāra ājñāya guru hañā tāra’ ei deśa*

**“Instruct everyone to follow the orders of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa as they are given in the Bhagavad-gītā and Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. In this way become a spiritual master and try to liberate everyone in this land.” (Cc. Madhya 7.128)**

By following these instructions of Lord Caitanya, one will develop taste, and then he will actually have the strength to discriminate between what he needs and what he wants. However, without taste, we will always be thinking that we need more of what we want in order to get that taste. However, we will never be successful. We will just keep gasping for air. Lord Caitanya is so merciful and so kind, as He has made it so easy in this age. We just have to take up His order. By so doing, there will be no obstacles in household life.

## Chapter 12 – Festivals

## Nityānanda Trayodaśī

Lord Caitanya and Lord Nityānanda appeared in this world to fulfill the same purpose—to deliver the process of self-realization, which is kevala ānanda-kāṇḍa, a joyful process. Lord Caitanya appeared to distribute the holy name of the Lord and to answer the call of Advaita Ācārya. Lord Nityānanda appeared to assist Lord Caitanya.

Lord Caitanya is none other than Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself. Brajendra-nandana jei, śacī-suta hoilo sei, balarāma hoilo nitāi. Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura has described in his Prārthanā that Lord Caitanya is none other than the son of the King of Vraja, and Lord Balarāma is Nitāi. They are the same Supreme Personality of Godhead. The Lord appears in many forms to fulfill many purposes.

*pañca-tattva—eka-vastu, nāhi kichu bheda*  
*rasa āsvādite tabu vividha vibheda*

**Spiritually there are no differences between these five tattvas, for on the transcendental platform everything is absolute. Yet there are also varieties in the spiritual world, and in order to taste these spiritual varieties one should distinguish between them. (Cc. Ādi 7.5)**

This verse describes the Pañca-tattva, which is comprised of Lord Caitanya, Lord Nityānanda, Advaita Ācārya, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura and Gadādhara Paṇḍita.

*pañca-tattvātmakaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ*  
*bhakta-rūpa-svarūpakam*  
*bhaktāvatāraṁ bhaktākhyaṁ*  
*namāmi bhakta-śaktikam*

**“I offer my obeisances unto the Supreme Lord, Kṛṣṇa, who is nondifferent from His features as a devotee, devotional incarnation, devotional manifestation, pure devotee and devotional energy.” (Cc. Ādi 1.14)**

These are five features of the Supreme Lord. Although Lord Caitanya is Kṛṣṇa Himself, still He appeared in the Kali-yuga as the channa-avatāra or hidden incarnation—not as the Supreme Lord, but as a devotee of the Lord. His first expansion is Balarāma, who is none other than Nityānanda. Balarāma assists the Lord in various ways—both in the spiritual world as well as in the matter of creation. Just as Balarāma appeared to assist Lord Kṛṣṇa in His pastimes as His elder brother, that same Balarāma appeared as Nityānanda to assist Lord Caitanya in His pastimes. Balarāma also appeared as Lakṣmaṇa to assist Lord Rāmacandra in His pastimes. Although Nityānanda is the Supreme Lord, He appears in the mood of a servant of the Lord. Thus a distinction is made.

On the transcendental platform, the five tattvas are eka-vastu—all one, and absolute. However, we understand from our Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava siddhānta that although there is oneness, there is also difference. Lord Caitanya appeared to establish acintya-bhedābheda-tattva—inconceivable and simultaneous oneness and difference.

Although on the transcendental platform the five tattvas are all one, there is also variety in the spiritual world, and in order to taste that variety, one has to see the difference. There is no taste in oneness. If one wants to become one with the Supreme Lord or thinks himself to be the same as the Supreme Lord, then there is no relationship, which is the whole basis of rasa, or taste. When there is a relationship, there is a manifestation of reciprocal love between the lover and the beloved. The lover desires to please the beloved. There is also competition between the beloved and the one who desires to serve and to please the beloved. The Lord is the beloved and the supreme, most worshipable object. The Lord also desires to serve and please His devotees. When we read Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Caitanya-bhāgavata, Bhakti-ratnākara, and all the other literatures which describe the pastimes of Lord Caitanya, Lord Nityānanda and Advaita Ācārya, we see these loving relationships between Them.

The mentality that Lord Nityānanda has when He appears in this world is that He is the servant of the Supreme Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He serves Lord Caitanya as His guru, as His friend, and as His servant, just as Lord Balarāma played with Lord Kṛṣṇa in these three different moods in Vraja. In all these ways, He is absorbed in the mentality of serving. Every fiber and every atom of His existence is in complete absorption of serving Lord Caitanya.

Before Caitanya Mahāprabhu’s appearance in this world, Lord Nityānanda appeared in Ekacakrā as the son of Hāḍāi Ojhā and Padmāvatī. He enjoyed His childhood pastimes with His friends, playing and imitating many of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s childhood pastimes.

Lord Nityānanda stayed in Ekacakrā for twelve years, and then traveled to various places of pilgrimage for another twenty years until it was time to meet Caitanya Mahāprabhu in Navadvīpa.

Lord Nityānanda knew the purpose for which Lord Caitanya descended into this world, which was to propagate the congregational chanting of the holy name of the Lord and to induce the fallen conditioned souls to become lovers of God. Even though he knew the purpose, He did not preach while He was on pilgrimage. In Caitanya-bhāgavata, Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura explains that Lord Nityānanda waited to get the order to do so from Lord Caitanya. Lord Nityānanda thus established this relationship as a servant by demonstrating that only by first receiving the order from Lord Caitanya would He take up the initiative to display His pastimes of delivering the fallen souls.

When Lord Caitanya appeared in Navadvīpa, Nityānanda was in Rāḍhadeśa. At the moment of Caitanya Mahāprabhu’s appearance, Nityānanda gave out a loud roar, which could be heard throughout the entire universe. It was so loud that even the residents of other planets were wondering where the sound was coming from. It was the sound of Nityānanda’s ecstasy due to His worshipful Lord having appeared in this world. Later when Nityānanda went to Navadvīpa, He stayed in the house of Nandanācārya and waited for Lord Caitanya to come and meet Him.

Lord Nityānanda was a servant to the superior order given by Lord Caitanya. When Lord Caitanya gave Nityānanda the order to preach, Lord Nityānanda then displayed His pastimes of traveling all over Bengal, inducing the conditioned souls to take up the worship of Lord Gaurāṅga.

Lord Nityānanda was given the order by Lord Caitanya to go out and tell everyone He met to worship Kṛṣṇa, chant Kṛṣṇa’s name and make Kṛṣṇa their life. However, Lord Nityānanda could not fully take up that order, because He was more inclined to tell everybody: Bhaja gaurāṅga kaha gaurāṅga laha gaurāṅgera nāme—“Please just worship Gaurāṅga, always speak about Gaurāṅga, and take the name of Lord Gaurāṅga with all devotion. Anyone who adores My beloved master Gaurāṅga is more dear to Me than My own life.”

Of course, Gaurāṅga is Kṛṣṇa. However, Nityānanda has a very confidential service, and if one actually wants to be able to approach Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana, first they have to get the mercy of Nityānanda. Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura writes:

*āra kabe nitāi-cāṅdera karuṇā karibe*  
*saṁsāra-vāsanā mora kabe tuccha habe*  
*viṣaya chāḍiyā kabe śuddha habe mana*  
*kabe hāma heraba śrī-vṛndāvana*

**“When will Lord Nityānanda have mercy upon me so that I can realize the uselessness of material pleasure? When will my mind be cleansed of all material dirt so that I will be able to feel the presence of spiritual Vṛndāvana?” (Prārthanā)**

Having received the mercy of Lord Nityānanda, one becomes free from the desire for sense gratification. Unless one is free from material desires, it is not possible to understand Vṛndāvana-dhāma or the conjugal pastimes of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Therefore, it is understood that Lord Nityānanda is the original spiritual master, as He does the cleaning work and makes one qualified to enter Vṛndāvana-dhāma. The bona fide spiritual master is also understood to be the representative of Lord Nityānanda.

For the inner circle of devotees, those who enter into Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes in Vṛndāvana and assist the Lord in His conjugal pastimes, their guru is Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. She is guru because She trains up the devotees in their loving service to assist the gopīs in pleasing Lord Kṛṣṇa. Nobody can serve Kṛṣṇa better than Rādhārāṇī. She knows how to give Kṛṣṇa pleasure. Although She is the guru for this inner circle of associates of the Lord in His pastimes in Vṛndāvana, She will only accept those persons who are recommended to Her by Lord Nityānanda. Thus They work together. When Lord Nityānanda certifies one as being free from material desires and is a fit candidate for recommendation to Rādhārāṇī, it is due to His manifestation of mercy by having cleaned these desires from within the heart.

Such is the work of the spiritual master. Lord Nityānanda thus assists the Lord by manifesting Himself as the original spiritual master, who is also nondifferent from Lord Balarāma and who is the source of all spiritual strength.

*nāyam ātmā bala-hīnena lābhyo*  
*na ca pramādāt tapaso vāpy aliṅgāt*  
*etair upāyair yatate yas tu vidvāṁs*  
*tasyaisa ātmā viśate brahma-dhāma*

**The Supreme Lord is not attained by one who has no spiritual strength, who is wild or careless, or whose austerities are not appropriate. The Lord appears before a person who strives by right means to attain Him. Such a person enters the spiritual world. (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 3.2.4)**

Therefore Lord Nityānanda, being nondifferent from Lord Balarāma, also infuses spiritual strength within the heart of that devotee who gets His mercy and He also reveals His identity to such a person.

Kavirāja Gosvāmī says (Cc. Ādi 5.1): “Let me offer my obeisances to Lord Śrī Nityānanda, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose opulence is wonderful and unlimited. By His will, even a fool can understand His identity.”

Lord Nityānanda used to ornament Himself with all kinds of costly jewels, such as diamonds, gold, silver, emeralds, rubies and sapphires. He was also wearing very costly silks. He was literally a treasure house. Those who had material vision thought that these jewels were Lord Nityānanda’s only treasure. However, the devotees of the Lord understand that Lord Nityānanda’s real treasure is His love for Lord Caitanya. Because His love for Lord Caitanya is so great, He can control the Lord so much that even if Lord Caitanya wants to punish somebody or even kill them, Nityānanda’s begging for the Lord to deliver them cannot be refused. Such is Lord Nityānanda’s power. Furthermore, His method of distributing love of Godhead is such that He can induce anyone, even the offenders, to become lovers of God.

Lord Nityānanda was ornamented with all these jewels, because once when He was wandering about Vṛndāvana as an avadhūta, He gave His mercy to one Vaiṣṇava in Govardhana. In return, this Vaiṣṇava wanted to give Him very costly ornaments. However, Lord Nityānanda said, “Not now.” However, at a later time, He wanted to accept the offering of this devotee. He thus told this devotee and other devotees to bring whatever ornaments they wished to bring to Him. They then brought all of their costly jewels and ornaments, which Lord Nityānanda placed on His body.

There was a thief who was in charge of a big band of thieves. He was thinking that Lord Nityānanda’s treasure house consisted of all the jewels that He was wearing. He and all the other thieves were worshiping goddess Durgā, as they desired to obtain material opulence’s. The leader told the band of thieves, “Our worship of goddess Durgā has now bore fruit. We no longer have to travel everywhere to find costly things to steal. By our worship of goddess Durgā, she has taken everything and put it all in one place. Just see how merciful she is!”

They then devised a plan to steal these jewels from the body of Nityānanda. At that particular time, Lord Nityānanda was staying at the home of Hiraṇya Paṇḍita. While He was there, He was fully absorbed in congregational chanting of the holy names of the Lord and taking prasādam with the Vaiṣṇavas. The thief decided that he would go to the home of Hiraṇya Paṇḍita at the appropriate time with his band of thieves and steal all of the ornaments from Nityānanda’s body.

He sent a spy to see what they were doing. The spy reported back: “Right now, Nityānanda is eating. Everybody else is awake. It would not be a very good time for us to go and take the ornaments.”

The leader of the thieves said, “OK, we will wait until nighttime, when everybody is sleeping, and then we will go in and steal all the ornaments.”

Waiting for the night to come, all of the thieves sat together on the outskirts of Navadvīpa. However, by the influence of the Lord’s yogamāyā potency, all of them fell asleep. The next thing they knew, they were hearing the sound of crows. The morning had come and it was broad daylight.

Despite their planning, it was too late, and nothing had been taken. They had even planned which ornaments would go to which person. They then began fighting amongst themselves, blaming each other for having fallen asleep.

The head thief said, “What are we arguing about? There are many more nights to come. Why are we arguing about one night? Goddess Durgā arranged that we would all fall asleep because we did not worship her last night. Tonight we will worship her with wine and meat, and we will be successful.”

That night, they worshipped goddess Durgā, and then each thief cleaned his weapon, put on dark clothes so as to not be seen in the darkness of the night, and made their way to the house of Hiraṇya Paṇḍita. When they arrived nearby, they saw that it was being protected by many huge guards. They calculated that each guard was capable of killing a hundred thieves. The guards were ornamented with tilaka, wearing garlands, carrying weapons, and chanting the holy names of the Lord.

The thieves then started arguing amongst themselves again: “I’ve heard that this Nityānanda has a very special personality. These guards that we didn’t know about must be protecting Him.”

Someone else said, “I’ve heard that they call Him Gosāi.”

Another said, “How could He be Gosāi—a controller of the senses? I’ve seen how much He eats. And why would He wear such costly jewels if He was a Gosāi?”

The commander of the thieves then said, “Maybe some important dignitary is visiting the house of Hiraṇya Paṇḍita and they brought their own personal guards with them. Whatever the reason, these guards are there and we cannot attack now. Let’s wait for some nights to pass. The guards will go away, and then we will be able to steal the ornaments. Let’s come back in ten days.”

They went about their business, and ten days later they banded together again, each thief carrying five to ten weapons. This time, there were no guards around the house, and they felt sure they were going to steal all of Nityānanda’s ornaments. They started approaching the house. All of a sudden, it became pitch black and nobody could see anything. They began stumbling around in the dark. One thief fell into a big ditch and started getting bitten by mosquitoes and leeches. Another thief fell into a garbage pit, and was bitten by mosquitoes and scorpions. Another thief fell into thorns and his body was pierced all over. Another thief fell into a canal, and another thief came down with an extremely high fever and his body was burning up.

Nobody could make any progress towards the house. Just at that moment, all the clouds which had appeared in the sky began inundating them with torrential, freezing rain. The thieves could not move, and their bodies were freezing. They were ready to die. The rain turned into hail and they started being beaten by big hailstones. They were practically on the verge of death. The head thief began to think, “This Nityānanda cannot be an ordinary personality.” He started thinking about how all the events unfolded in the past—how they all fell asleep on the first night and therefore could not steal the jewels, and how the all the guards were protecting the house and they could not steal that night either.

He thought, “This Nityānanda could be no one other than the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. My only redemption will be to take shelter of His lotus feet.” In his heart, he prayed to Nityānanda: “When a person falls down onto the ground, he must take shelter of the earth. Similarly when a person offends You, he must take shelter of You by meditating on Your lotus feet.” While he was meditating on the lotus feet of Lord Nityānanda, all of a sudden the rain and hail stopped. Light appeared and they were able to find their way out. Although they were on the verge of death, they all came back to life, simply by the thief’s meditation on the lotus feet of Nityānanda.

The head thief decided to immediately go and take shelter at the lotus feet of Nityānanda. He went into the house of Hiraṇya Paṇḍita, and fell on the ground with tears flowing from his eyes. He got up, began dancing, and then again fell at the feet of Nityānanda.

All the devotees were carefully watching this thief, because they all knew who he was. One devotee warned, “He is pretending. Do not trust him. Although he may look like he is surrendering to Nityānanda, he actually has a scheme.”

Another devotee said, “No, we cannot minimize the potency of Nityānanda Prabhu. Certainly He can deliver even the most fallen.”

Nityānanda said to the thief, “Tell me. What is it that you are experiencing? Why are you behaving in this way? Have you received the mercy of Lord Kṛṣṇa?”

The thief was lying on the ground, clasping the lotus feet of Nityānanda. He said, “I have offended You. I deserve to die. Whether I live or die does not make any difference. I have come to take shelter of Your lotus feet. You can kill me, or You can let me live—whatever You like. I have realized that I have committed a great offense to You. I wanted to rob Your jewels.” He then summarized everything that happened leading up to the point of his surrender. He then said, “I have offended You, and for this I should no longer maintain life in this body. I have simply come to beg forgiveness, and now I should do what needs to be done. I am going to take my life by drowning myself in the Gaṅgā.”

Lord Nityānanda said to the thief, “I can understand, having heard of how much you have suffered, that you must be a servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa, and therefore you must have received the mercy of Lord Kṛṣṇa.”

Śrīla Prabhupāda, on a morning walk in Tehran, also explained that one will not be recognized as a great devotee of Kṛṣṇa until he has been severely tested by Him. Prabhupāda gave the examples of Prahlāda Mahārāja, Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Bali Mahārāja, and the Pāṇḍavas, who were all severely tested and therefore known as great devotees.

It was obvious that the thief had received Kṛṣṇa’s mercy, because the outcome is that he took shelter of Lord Nityānanda and fully meditated upon His lotus feet. Lord Nityānanda took the garland from around His neck and placed it on the body of the thief. The thief then became completely free from all material contamination, became infused with ecstatic love for the Lord, and began crying again. Lord Nityānanda placed His lotus foot on the thief’s head and told him, “You do not need to take your life. You were the king of thieves. They all know who you are. You should go and meet all of these thieves and tell them about Lord Caitanya’s mercy. If you do this, then your life will be completely successful.”

Thus, by Lord Nityānanda’s will, even the greatest fool can understand His identity. Lord Nityānanda makes His identity known to whomever He gives this mercy. If He sees one tear when someone is chanting the name of Gaura, He is very much inclined to give His mercy to that person.

Prabhupāda says in the Bhāgavatam that a man displays two types of tears: When he is suffering, his tears will be hot, and when he is happy, his tears will be cold. When a Vaiṣṇava is happy due to receiving the mercy of Lord Nityānanda, his tears will be cold.

Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura ends this pastime in Caitanya-bhāgavata by saying that anyone who hears this pastime of Lord Nityānanda and His distribution of mercy to the thieves, with faith, will see Lord Caitanya face-to-face in this life. That is the price one must pay. Lord Nityānanda is so merciful that when you pay with your faith He gives it all back to you so that you can come back and buy more. If you pay with śraddhā, then sādhu-saṅga will come, then bhajana-kriyā, anārtha-nivṛtti, ruci, āśakti, bhāva and finally prema.

Lord Nityānanda has come in this most merciful form to assist His worshipful Lord in rescuing the fallen conditioned souls of this Age of Kali. Both Nitāi and Gauracandra have arisen on the horizon of Gauḍadeśa to distribute this mercy—pure devotional service to Kṛṣṇa. Lord Nityānanda is very eager to make us qualified by removing all material obstacles on the path of devotional service so that we will become free from the desire for sense gratification. Only then, when our minds are completely purified, freed from material desires and anxieties, will we be able to understand Śrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma and the pastimes of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana. Only then will our devotional service be successful. Thus we should pray for this mercy from Nitāi.

In his commentary to Gaurāṅga Bolite Habe, Śrīla Prabhupāda says:

“Āra kabe nitāicand koruṇā karibe. We are all asking about the mercy of Lord Nityānanda. Nityānanda is supposed to be the original spiritual master. So we have to approach Gaurāṅga, or Lord Caitanya, through the mercy of Lord Nityānanda. So what is the symptom of a person who has achieved the causeless mercy of Lord Nityānanda? Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says that one who has actually received the causeless mercy of Nityānanda, he has no more any material desire. That is the symptom. Āra kabe nitāicand koruṇā karibe saṁsāra-vāsanā mora kabe tuccha. Saṁsāra-vāsanā means desire for material enjoyment, when it will become very insignificant.

## Gaura-pūrṇimā

*vairāgya-vidyā-nija-bhakti-yoga-*  
*śikṣārtham ekaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ*  
*śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-śarīra-dhārī*  
*kṛpāmbudhir yas tam ahaṁ prapadye*

**“Let me take shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who has descended in the form of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu to teach us real knowledge, His devotional service and detachment from whatever does not foster Kṛṣṇa consciousness. He has descended because He is an ocean of transcendental mercy. Let me surrender unto His lotus feet.” (Cc. Madhya 6.254)**

*kālān naṣṭaṁ bhakti-yogaṁ nijaṁ yaḥ*  
*prāduṣkartuṁ kṛṣṇa-caitanya-nāmā*  
*āvirbhūtas tasya pādāravinde*  
*gāḍhaṁ gāḍhaṁ līyatāṁ citta-bhṛṅgaḥ*

**“Let my consciousness, which is like a honeybee, take shelter of the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who has just now appeared as Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu to teach the ancient system of devotional service to Himself. This system had almost been lost due to the influence of time.” (Cc. Madhya 6.255)**

PURPORT

As Lord Kṛṣṇa states in the Bhagavad-gītā (4.7):

*yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata*  
*abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṁ sṛjāmy aham*

“Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice, O descendant of Bharata, and a predominant rise of irreligion—at that time I descend Myself.”

This is also the case with Caitanya Mahāprabhu’s appearance. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu appeared in this world as a disguised incarnation of Kṛṣṇa, but His appearance is confirmed in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, the Mahābhārata and other Vedic scriptures. In this Age of Kali almost everyone has become attached to fruitive and ritualistic activities and mental speculation. Consequently there was a great need to revive the system of devotional service. The Lord Himself personally came down disguised as a devotee to teach the fallen souls in this material world the process of devotional service, and so that they might take advantage of His example.

At the conclusion of the Bhagavad-gītā, Lord Kṛṣṇa advised complete surrender unto Him, promising all protection to His devotee. Unfortunately, people are so fallen that they cannot accept the instructions of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Therefore, Kṛṣṇa returned with the same mission, but He executed it in a different way. As Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, He ordered us to surrender unto Himself. However, as Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, He taught us how to surrender to Kṛṣṇa. Therefore, He is praised by the Gosvāmīs: namo mahā-vadānyāya kṛṣṇa-prema-pradāye te. Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is certainly the Personality of Godhead, but He is not as magnanimous as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Lord Kṛṣṇa simply gave orders for one to become His devotee (man-manā bhava mad-bhaktaḥ), but Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu actually taught the process of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. If one wants to become a devotee of Kṛṣṇa, he must first take shelter of the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, following in the footsteps of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and other exalted devotees.

In these verses, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya is glorifying Lord Caitanya as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was previously defeated by Lord Caitanya. He was accustomed to dry logic and argument, and he was very much attached to the study of scripture. However, he was unable to recognize Lord Caitanya as the Supreme Lord. Therefore, Lord Caitanya devised a plan to rectify Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.

First, the Lord sat and listened to Vedānta from Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya for seven continuous days, even though Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya presented the knowledge of Vedānta in an impersonal way. After many continuous days, Sārvabhauma became a little frustrated that Lord Caitanya had given no response to anything he had to say. Finally, he asked the Lord to say something just to confirm that He had understood a little about what he was speaking.

Lord Caitanya responded, “I can understand the scriptures that you are speaking from, but unfortunately you have clouded the essence of these scriptures with your interpretation, and that I cannot hear.” Lord Caitanya simply tolerated Sārvabhauma’s recitation. Later, Lord Caitanya defeated Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya by His explanation of Vedānta. He also explained to him the meaning of the ātmārāma verse of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. Although previously Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was accustomed to logic and argument, by Lord Caitanya’s mercy, he realized that logic and argument was not going to give him what he needed to fully realize the absolute truth. He also realized that he needed to accept everything he heard from Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and therefore he fully submitted himself to the Lord. Lord Caitanya then revealed to Sārvabhauma His wonderful form. First He manifested a four-armed form, and then He showed His two-armed form. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya prostrated himself before the Lord and completely surrendered to Him.

Sometime shortly after this revelation, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya composed one hundred verses in glorification of Lord Caitanya known as Sārvabhauma-śataka. He was very expert in composing verses and could do it spontaneously in perfect grammar. After composing Sārvabhauma-śataka, he also composed the two previously-quoted verses on two palm leaves. He gave these verses to Jagadānanda and Dāmodara Paṇḍita along with a large quantity of mahā-prasādam he had collected from Lord Jagannātha’s offerings. At this time, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was already recognized as a great devotee. Gopīnātha Ācārya, his brother-in-law, was also very happy to see that Sārvabhauma had become a great Vaiṣṇava. He asked Dāmodara Paṇḍita and Jagadānanda to deliver these verses and the mahā-prasādam to Lord Caitanya.

Just before entering into the house where Lord Caitanya was staying, Mukunda saw these palm leaves. After he read what was on each palm leaf, he knew what Lord Caitanya would do. Therefore, he wrote these two verses on the wall on the side of the house. He then sent the two verses to Lord Caitanya along with the mahā-prasādam. When Lord Caitanya saw these two verses on the palm leaves, as expected by Mukunda, the Lord immediately ripped up these leaves.

Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was very bold. In both verses he said, “Let me take shelter of Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” It took some fearlessness to compose these verses to offer to the Lord, because externally Lord Caitanya would become displeased by such statements. He did not want to hear that He was the Supreme Personality of Godhead. That was not His mood, as He appeared as the channa-avatāra, in the mood of a devotee of the Lord.

There is confirmation of this point in the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. One such reference is Prahlāda Mahārāja, who in his prayers to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva says:

“My Lord, You appear in various incarnations as a human being, an animal, a great saint, a demigod, a fish or a tortoise, thus maintaining the entire creation in different planetary systems and killing the demoniac principles. According to the age, O my Lord, You protect the principles of religion. In the age of Kali, however, You do not assert Yourself as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and therefore You are known as Triyuga, or the Lord who appears in three yugas.” (Bhāg. 7.9.38)

In the Satya, Tretā, and Dvāpara yugas, the Lord appears as the Supreme Lord. But in Kali-yuga, the Lord is hidden (channa-avatāra).

Prabhupāda explains that previously when the Lord appeared as Kṛṣṇa, He established the condition that we must first surrender unto Him. However, as Caitanya Mahāprabhu, He took that condition away. Instead of surrender, He said to simply take that which He has come to offer. He did not display Himself as the Supreme Lord, but always as a devotee of the Lord.

It is also explained that when the Lord appeared as Lord Kṛṣṇa, He taught this principle of surrender in a theoretical way. He said: “Always think of Me, become My devotee, worship Me and offer your homage unto Me. Thus you will come to Me without fail. I promise you this because you are My very dear friend. Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.” (Bg. 18.65-66) This lists all the components of surrender. However, Kṛṣṇa taught it in a theoretical way, and therefore He had to come again to teach by His example, which is more powerful. The devotee who is always thinking of Kṛṣṇa the most, always serving Him, and always speaking about Him is Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. Thus, Lord Caitanya appeared and adopted the mood of Rādhārāṇī.

Lord Caitanya did not like it when devotees would refer to Him as the Supreme Lord. He would block His ears. Or sometimes He would simply go away.

One time, in Śāntipura, Advaita Ācārya said to all the assembled devotees, “Let us have a kīrtana and simply chant the names of Gaurāṅga.” When all the devotees heard this, they became afraid, knowing that Lord Caitanya would not like it. However, Advaita Ācārya was the foremost of all Vaiṣṇavas. It was He who called the Lord to descend, and thus became one of the purposes for the Lord’s descent—to answer the prayers of Advaita Ācārya.

Advaita Ācārya had made many statements about forcing the Lord to appear. He knew that only the Lord could deliver the residents of Kali-yuga. Thus, Advaita Ācārya showed that He had the power to control the Lord by His prayers. He worshiped a śilā with Ganges water and tulasī and called out to the Lord.

Previously, all the Vaiṣṇavas who appeared before Lord Caitanya would gather at the house of Advaita Ācārya, have kīrtana, hear Vedānta from Advaita Ācārya, and would always present it in terms of devotional service. However, they could not do anything to change the mentality of the materialistic people.

In fact, Advaita Ācārya told all these assembled devotees how concerned He was by the state of affairs in Kali-yuga. He saw the mentality of the people—how they were so absorbed in materialism, and that although He is the Supreme Lord Mahāviṣṇu—still He could not convince them to give up their materialistic ways.

Advaita Ācārya told all the devotees who were feeling great lamentation, seeing all these living entities who were going to suffer and go to hell, “I will bring the Lord personally. Only He can deliver them. If He does not come, then I will personally sever their heads from their bodies.” He made such a strong statement because He knew the Lord would hear His prayers, and that He had the power to invoke Lord Caitanya to appear.

Thus, the two external reasons for the Lord’s appearance were to answer the call of Advaita Ācārya and to disseminate the congregational chanting of the holy names of the Lord. His internal reason for taking this position of a devotee of the Lord was to understand the topmost devotee (Rādhārāṇī), and to understand the transcendental mellows about Himself, which He could not otherwise understand. He wanted to taste that bliss that Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī Herself was tasting.

We will elaborate on his external reasons for appearing as Caitanya Mahāprabhu. In Śāntipura, when Advaita Ācārya told all the devotees to chant the name of Gaurāṅga, one of the prayers He was chanting was: “Glory glory to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya who is nondifferent from the forest-flower-garlanded Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana. He has come to taste Kṛṣṇa-bhakti-rasa, devotional service to Himself.”

When all the devotees saw that Advaita Ācārya was fearless in chanting the names of Gaurāṅga, they all got caught up in His mood and also started chanting the names of Gaurāṅga. They were chanting so many different names of Lord Caitanya, describing Him as nondifferent from Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

Lord Caitanya, from a distance, heard the loud kīrtana, but He could not hear exactly what they were chanting. He decided to come closer. When the devotees saw Lord Caitanya approaching, they all looked to Advaita Ācārya and asked what they should do.

Advaita Ācārya started chanting louder and was dancing in ecstasy. The devotees could see how fearless He was. By that example, the devotees also became fearless and did the same thing that He was doing. The chanting got louder, and as Lord Caitanya came closer, He asked, “What are you doing?” However, they did not answer. They simply looked at Him. Due to Advaita Ācārya’s transcendental provocation, all the devotees gathered around Lord Caitanya, chanting, “Gaurāṅga! Gaurāṅga! Gaurāṅga!”

Lord Caitanya became embarrassed and returned to His house. He closed the door, but all the devotees followed Him with the kīrtana. Lord Caitanya went into His room and lay down as if to go to sleep. He then said to Govinda, “Alright, let the Vaiṣṇavas in,” and then He went to sleep.

All the Vaiṣṇavas entered Lord Caitanya’s room, and Lord Caitanya awakened. Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita was in front. Lord Caitanya asked, “Śrīvāsa, tell me what is this? What is this that you are singing about?”

Śrīvāsa made a gesture with his hand as his answer. Lord Caitanya asked, “What do you mean by that gesture?”

Śrīvāsa replied, “What I mean is that I have taken my hand as if trying to block the sun. However, it is impossible to block the sun with my hand. Similarly it is impossible for You to hide yourself as the Supreme Lord. We know who You are. Even if I could block the sun with my hand, which I cannot, You could never hide who You are from the devotees. Even if You lie in the milk ocean, You cannot hide Yourself. How do You think You can come into this world full of human beings and hide Yourself amongst us? Everyone will recognize who You are. All living entities in the creation—from the lowest planet to the highest planet—will be chanting Your glories. How will You be able to punish all of them? We know who You are, and therefore we are chanting these names. Although You do not reveal Yourself to everyone, still, by Your mercy, everyone can see who You are.”

This appears to be a contradiction, as the Supreme Lord does not reveal Himself to just anyone. In fact, He even said that to the brāhmaṇa who was worshipping Gopāla: “I do not reveal Myself to everybody. Persons who are not My servant cannot see My form.”
