However, Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita is saying, “On one hand, You do not reveal Yourself to everybody. However, by Your mercy, You reveal Yourself to everybody. Therefore, You are very merciful.”

When Kṛṣṇa appeared as the Supreme Lord, not everybody recognized who He was. However, when the Lord appeared as a devotee of the Lord, He was hidden and was not asserting Himself as the Supreme Lord, but His mercy was so great that everyone could understand who He really was. He would cry, serve the devotees, glorify the devotees, wash their clothes, bow down and take the dust from their lotus feet.

However, we know that there was a time in Lord Caitanya’s youth when He was not behaving like a devotee. All the devotees used to pray, “If only Nimāi would become a devotee, I would completely surrender myself to Him.”

In the Lord’s youth, He behaved as an arrogant young paṇḍita who was very much accustomed to logic and argument. He was much inclined towards defeating others on the basis of scripture. He was always looking for someone to engage in debate with. He would defeat them, they would admit defeat, and then He would defeat His own argument that He used to defeat them. After defeating His own arguments, they would be astounded, saying, “How is it possible that you defeated such conclusive truths?” By defeating His own arguments, He would establish a new conclusion, and they would be compelled to accept it.

People would see Him getting into so many arguments, trying to defeat others because He was trying to attract a lot of followers. All the devotees who had descended before Lord Caitanya in Navadvīpa to assist Him in His pastimes were lamenting. When they would see such a display of arrogance, they would say, “If only He would become a devotee. With His knowledge of scripture and His ability to defeat others, He could make everybody a Vaiṣṇava.”

Sometimes Nimāi would even meet the devotees on the street, and they would run away, fearful that if He caught them, He would get into an argument with them. Thus they prayed for Nimāi to become a devotee.

In his childhood, He also displayed many mischievous pastimes similar to those of Kṛṣṇa in Gokula. Nimāi would go down to the Ganges and steal the garments of people who were taking their baths. On other occasions, when people would go to service their bodies, Nimāi would lock them in so that they could not get out.

While the men and women were taking bath in the river, the men would be on one side, and the women would be on the other side. Nimāi would come and switch the clothes, putting all of the men’s clothes on the women’s side and all of the women’s clothes on the men’s side. They would come out of the water after taking their bath, and the men would find sārīs, and the women would find dhotīs and kurtās.

Sometimes when the men were in the water and were chanting the Gāyatrī mantra, Nimāi would jump in, and while He was under the water, He would pull their legs out from underneath them. Sometimes, when they would come out of the water, Nimāi would walk up to them and spit on them.

They said, “I just took a bath so that I could do my pūjā, and this mischievous child is coming and spitting on me and contaminating me! I have to go back into the water and take my bath. I am so contaminated by His spitting!”

Finally, all of them got together one day and decided to go to Jagannātha Miśra to complain about Nimāi. They said, “Do you know what your son does? Sometimes I am sitting on the banks of the Gaṅgā, and I am ready to do my pūjā. However, He takes all the paraphernalia off the altar and sits down on the altar Himself. Your son says to me, ‘Don’t you know that all this paraphernalia is meant to be offered to Me?’ What kind of a son are you raising?” There were so many complaints being made to Jagannātha Miśra about all the things Nimāi was doing at the river.

Then all of the girls would come and complain to Śacīmātā: “Do you know what your son does? He comes up to us and says, ‘Marry Me.’ How could He say something like that? Can’t you control your son? Sometimes He throws seeds in our hair and our hair gets all stuck together with these seeds.”

Nimāi was just like child-Kṛṣṇa performing mischievous pastimes in Gokula. In Gokula, all the gopīs would say to mother Yaśodā: “We are not angry with your son. How can we become angry with Him? However, we just came to tell you about some of the things that He was doing.” Kṛṣṇa would steal yogurt and butter. When He would go into the homes of the cowherd women, sometimes He would pour water in the ears of the children. He would untie the calves, which would then go and drink all the milk from the cows before they could be milked.

In the morning all the women used to decorate the walls of the house with nice white-colored lime and Kṛṣṇa would take mud and throw it all over the walls. The gopīs would then complain to Nanda Mahārāja and mother Yaśodā about Kṛṣṇa’s behavior. However, then they would say, “Actually we are not angry. Your son just enchants us by His behavior. We cannot stop thinking about Him and speaking about Him.” Thus Kṛṣṇa and Nimāi both performed mischievous activities to attract attention.

In this incarnation as Caitanya Mahāprabhu, He did not present Himself as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He wanted to remain hidden, never wanting to disturb His mood of being a devotee of the Lord. However, by the mercy of the Lord, anyone who came in contact with the Lord could understand that He was in fact the Supreme Lord. Such was the magnanimity of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

*namo mahā-vadānyāya*  
*kṛṣṇa-prema-pradāya te*  
*kṛṣṇāya kṛṣṇa-caitanya-*  
*nāmne gaura-tviṣe namaḥ*

**“O most munificent incarnation! You are Kṛṣṇa Himself appearing as Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu. You have assumed the golden color of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, and You are widely distributing pure love of Kṛṣṇa. We offer our respectful obeisances unto You.” (Cc. Madhya 19.53)**

He was the most merciful incarnation of the Lord, because He freely distributed what no other incarnation before would—the highest ecstasy of loving devotional service in the mood of the residents of Vṛndāvana.

Kṛṣṇa appeared and displayed His pastimes with His eternal associates, and became conquered by His devotees in the various moods of servant, friend, parental affection and conjugal love. He came and displayed His pastimes as the Supreme Lord, stayed for as long as He wanted, and then disappeared. Sometime after His disappearance, He thought to Himself, “For a long time I have not bestowed upon the people of this world pure unalloyed devotional service, which is experienced by the devotees in Vṛndāvana. Without such loving attachment to Me, then this whole universe is useless.”

*yuga-dharma pravartāimu nāma-saṅkīrtana*  
*cāri bhāva-bhakti diyā nācāmu bhuvana*

**“I shall personally inaugurate the religion of the age—nāma-saṅkīrtana, the congregational chanting of the holy name. I shall make the world dance in ecstasy, realizing the four mellows of loving devotional service.” (Cc. Ādi 3.19)**

He then quoted verses from Bhagavad-gītā:

*yadā yadā hi dharmasya*  
*glānir bhavati bhārata*  
*abhyutthānam adharmasya*  
*tadātmānaṁ sṛjāmy aham*

**“Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice, O descendant of Bharata, and a predominant rise of irreligion—at that time I descend Myself.” (Bg. 4.7)**

*paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ*  
*vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām*  
*dharma-saṁsthāpanārthāya*  
*sambhavāmi yuge yuge*

**“To deliver the pious and to annihilate the miscreants, as well as to reestablish the principles of religion, I Myself appear, millennium after millennium.” (Bg. 4.8)**

*yad yad ācārati śreṣṭhas*  
*tat tad evetaro janaḥ*  
*sa yat pramāṇaṁ kurute*  
*lokas tad anuvartate*

**“Whatever action a great man performs, common men follow. And whatever standards he sets by exemplary acts, all the world pursues.” (Bg. 3.21)**

Thus, first the Lord came as Kṛṣṇa, but had to come again to teach by His example so that the fallen people of this age could learn by seeing an example. Prabhupāda used to say that example is more important that precept. Therefore, one of the great responsibilities for a preacher is to teach by his example. Thus, Lord Caitanya came to teach by showing what is man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru (Bg. 18.65). He demonstrated this by always being absorbed in thoughts of Kṛṣṇa. He therefore did not like it when devotees would offer prayers glorifying Him as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He simply wanted to be absorbed in the mood as a devotee of the Lord.

In this mood, the Lord demonstrated the merciful nature of a devotee, which can be even more merciful than the Lord.

*samo ’haṁ sarva-bhūteṣu*  
*na me dveṣyo ’sti na priyaḥ*  
*ye bhajanti tu māṁ bhaktyā*  
*mayi te teṣu cāpy aham*

**“I envy no one, nor am I partial to anyone. I am equal to all. But whoever renders service unto Me in devotion is a friend, is in Me, and I am also a friend to him.” (Bg. 9.29)**

*ye yathā māṁ prapadyante*  
*tāṁs tathaiva bhajāmy aham*  
*mama vartmānuvartante*  
*manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ*

**“As all surrender unto Me, I reward them accordingly. Everyone follows My path in all respects, O son of Pṛthā.” (Bg. 4.11)**

In other words, if somebody does not surrender, there is no relationship. The Lord is equal to everyone. However, especially in this age, nobody is inclined to surrender to the Supreme Lord. A devotee of the Lord, however, understands the purpose of the Lord, and therefore he can be even more merciful because he will preach. Even though somebody is not inclined to surrender, the devotee will give him the opportunity to do so by bringing him in contact with Kṛṣṇa.

Therefore, who could be more merciful than Lord Caitanya? He is both a devotee and Kṛṣṇa, and has come to preach. He is most munificent. The Lord may sometimes be neutral. However, Lord Caitanya is not neutral, neither is He indifferent to others suffering. Lord Caitanya has come as a devotee to teach the highest principle and the highest ecstasy of how to love the Lord.

For anyone who would see His love and His devotion, their hearts would melt. Tears would flow from their eyes, as they wanted to surrender. The result of that surrender is described as follows:

*yathā yathā gaura-padāravinde*  
*vindeta bhaktiṁ kṛta-puṇya-rāśiḥ*  
*tathā tathotsarpati hṛdy akasmād*  
*rādhā-padāmbhoja-sudhambu-rāśiḥ*

**“One who is extremely fortunate may get the mercy of Caitanya Mahāprabhu. As much as one can devote his full attention to the lotus feet of Lord Caitanya, to that extent he will be able to taste the nectarean service of the lotus feet of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī in Vṛndāvana.” (Caitanya-candrāmṛta 88)**

We therefore offer our obeisances unto Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu:

**“May the Supreme Lord who is known as the son of Śrīmatī Śacī-devī be transcendentally situated in the innermost core of your heart. Resplendent with the radiance of molten gold, He has descended in the Age of Kali by His causeless mercy to bestow what no incarnation has ever offered before: the most elevated mellow of devotional service, the mellow of conjugal love.” (Cc. Ādi 3.4)**

## Nṛsiṁha-caturdaśī

*oṁ namo bhagavate narasiṁhāya namas tejas-tejase*  
*āvir-āvirbhava vajra-nakha vajra-daṁṣṭra karmāśayān*  
*randhaya randhaya tamo grasa grasa oṁ svāhā;*  
*abhayam abhayam ātmani bhūyiṣṭhā oṁ kṣraum*

**“I offer my respectful obeisances unto Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, the source of all power. O my Lord who possesses nails and teeth just like thunderbolts, kindly vanquish our demonlike desires for fruitive activity in this material world. Please appear in our hearts and drive away our ignorance so that by Your mercy we may become fearless in the struggle for existence in this material world.” (Bhāg. 5.18.8)**

PURPORT:

In Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (4.22.39) Sanat-kumāra speaks the following words to Mahārāja Pṛthu:

*yat-pāda-paṅkaja-palāśa-vilāsa-bhaktyā*  
*karmāśayaṁ grathitam udgrathayanti santaḥ*  
*tadvan na rikta-matayo yatayo ‘pi ruddha-*  
*srotogaṇās tam araṇaṁ bhaja vāsudevam*

“Devotees always engaged in the service of the toes of the Lord’s lotus feet can very easily become free from hard-knotted desires for fruitive activities. Because this is very difficult, the nondevotees—the jñānīs and yogīs—cannot stop the waves of sense gratification, although they try to do so. Therefore you are advised to engage in the devotional service of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Vāsudeva.”

Every living being within this material world has a strong desire to enjoy matter to his fullest satisfaction. For this purpose, the conditioned soul must accept one body after another, and thus his strongly fixed fruitive desires continue. One cannot stop the repetition of birth and death without being completely desireless. Therefore Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī describes pure bhakti (devotional service) as follows:

*anyābhilāṣitā-śūnyaṁ*  
*jñāna-karmādy-anāvṛtam*  
*ānukūlyena kṛṣṇānu-*  
*śīlanaṁ bhaktir uttamā*

\[Cc. Madhya 19.167\]

“One should render transcendental loving service to the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa favorably and without desire for material profit or gain through fruitive activities or philosophical speculation. That is called pure devotional service.” Unless one is completely freed of all material desires, which are caused by the dense darkness of ignorance, one cannot fully engage in the devotional service of the Lord. Therefore we should always offer our prayers to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, who killed Hiraṇyakaśipu, the personification of material desire. Hiraṇya means “gold,” and kaśipu means “a soft cushion or bed.” Materialistic persons always desire to make the body comfortable, and for this they require huge amounts of gold. Thus Hiraṇyakaśipu was the perfect representative of materialistic life. He was therefore the cause of great disturbance to the topmost devotee, Prahlāda Mahārāja, until Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva killed him. Any devotee aspiring to be free of material desires should offer his respectful prayers to Nṛsiṁhadeva as Prahlāda Mahārāja did in this verse.

Certainly, we cannot speak about Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva without speaking about His devotee, Prahlāda, because they are inseparable. Prahlāda Mahārāja demonstrated by his ideal example the characteristic of pure devotion to the Lord, and the Lord demonstrated His supreme position, always giving protection to a devotee who has fully surrendered to Him.

We offer prayers to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva every day at the end of the ārati in the Namas te narasiṁhāya prayers, and also in the prayers of Jayadeva Gosvāmī (Daśāvatāra-stotra), which is “tava kara-kamala-vare nakham.” In the beginning of our movement, Śrīla Prabhupāda incorporated these prayers for protection as a part of our daily worship. These prayers were even chanted by Lord Caitanya Himself.

As described in Caitanya-caritāmṛta, before going to take darśana of Lord Jagannātha in Jagannātha Purī, Lord Caitanya would first go to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, bow down, offer His full obeisances, chant prayers to Him, and begin to dance. He would chant: śrī-nṛsiṁha, jaya nṛsiṁha, jaya jaya nṛsiṁha, prahlādeśa jaya padmā-mukha-padma-bhṛṅga. He also did this when He was traveling to South India and visited the temple of Jiyaḍa-nṛsiṁha. When Lord Caitanya appeared in that place, He began chanting and dancing very ecstatically, and began reciting prayers from Nṛsiṁha Purāṇa: namas te narasiṁhāya, prahlādāhlāda-dāyine. Lord Caitanya showed by His own example that He worshipped Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva.

Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva is the Lord of Prahlāda Mahārāja, who just like a honeybee is always beholding the lotus-like face of the goddess of fortune. At Jagannātha Purī, Lord Caitanya would also offer another prayer, which is a verse from Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī’s commentary on Śrīmad Bhāgavatam (7.9.1):

*ugro ’py anugra evāyaṁ*  
*sva-bhaktānāṁ nṛ-keśarī*  
*keśarīva sva-potānām*  
*anyeṣāṁ ugra-vikramaḥ*

**“Although very ferocious, the lioness is very kind to her cubs. Similarly, although very ferocious to nondevotees like Hiraṇyakaśipu, Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva is very, very soft and kind to devotees like Prahlāda Mahārāja.”**

When Lord Caitanya was in Jagannātha Purī, He would regularly hear the pastimes of Prahlāda Mahārāja. Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura described that Lord Caitanya would listen to these pastimes about Prahlāda Mahārāja and Dhruva Mahārāja at least one hundred times while hearing Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

Lord Caitanya came to teach devotional service by His example, including worshipping, praying to and meditating upon Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva and Prahlāda Mahārāja. Similarly, Śrīla Prabhupāda also established the worship of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, as the Lord in this form is meant to give protection to His devotees.

One time in 1973, about fifteen of us went on harināma in Harvard Square, in front of The Harvard Coop, and a gang of six or seven motorcyclists from the Hell’s Angels came before the harināma party with chains. We did not know what we were going to do. They stood before us, looking very menacing. Not knowing what else we could do, we started chanting prayers to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva. We kept them at bay for some time. However, at one point, it did get a little rough. They started attacking us, and some of the devotees had to defend themselves. However, they eventually stopped attacking us, seeing that we were continuing with our chanting.

The Lord’s protection, of course, is not simply physical protection; He is also protecting His devotee from within the heart. Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī quotes one verse in his commentary to the Seventh Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam: “Let me offer my obeisances unto Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, who is always enlightening Prahlāda Mahārāja within his heart and who always kills the nescience that attacks the devotees. His mercy is distributed like moonshine, and His face is like that of a lion. Let me offer my obeisances unto Him again and again.” Furthermore, as described earlier in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 5.18.8, Prahlāda Mahārāja also prays to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva to vanquish our demonlike desires for fruitive activity in this material world, and to appear in our hearts and drive away our ignorance so that by His mercy we may become fearless in the struggle for existence in this material world.

Hiraṇyakaśipu is classified as the ideal example of a demon, because he was a person who had an interest in enjoying his senses to the utmost degree.

Hiraṇyakaśipu was previously one of the gatekeepers of Vaikuṇṭha. The gatekeepers’ names were Jaya and Vijaya. These gatekeepers had obstructed the four Kumāras from entering Vaikuṇṭha. The four Kumāras were very disturbed by this, and thus decided to curse them. When the Lord appeared, He was very sympathetic with the four Kumāras. He said that when a wrong act is committed by a servant, it leads people in general to blame his master, just as a spot of white leprosy on the body spoils all of the skin. The Lord said, “Please, forgive Me for the behavior of these two servants (these persons who claim to be My servants).”

When Jaya and Vijaya understood that they were about to be cursed by the four Kumāras, they immediately fell down at their feet and begged to not be punished too severely. Jaya and Vijaya were given the choice of two forms of punishment—to take seven births in a favorable relationship with the Lord, or to take three births as demons. They chose the latter so that they could resume their services in Vaikuṇṭha as quickly as possible. After accepting this curse, Jaya and Vijaya fell to the material universe and took births as the two demons, Hiraṇyākṣa and Hiraṇyakaśipu.

Śrīla Prabhupāda explains that the Lord has unlimited desires, including the desire to fight. However, with whom can He fight in the spiritual world? Therefore, sometimes by His will, the devotees may descend and accept a birth as a demon so that He has somebody to fight with in the material world. Since this fighting propensity is within the Lord, and no ordinary living entity can fight with the Lord, by His will, He arranged for this curse to take place by the four Kumāras, so that these two gatekeepers would serve Him in the material world and fight with Him as demons.

Hiraṇyākṣa was killed by Lord Varāha, causing Hiraṇyakaśipu to consider Lord Viṣṇu as the enemy, and to become very determined to avenge the death of his younger brother. By performance of his austerities, he wished to usurp the position of Lord Brahmā and become the lord of the universe. Furthermore, he wanted to stop all sacrifices to Lord Viṣṇu, the personality whom he considered to be his greatest enemy, having killed his brother Hiraṇyākṣa, and he wanted to seek vengeance. In his attempt to become powerful, he also wanted to receive the benediction that he could enjoy eternally, or to be immortal.

With this motive, he performed very severe austerities to appease Lord Brahmā. By dint of his austerities, such as standing on one foot and controlling his breath, he became extremely powerful, and disseminated heat throughout the entire universe by his control.

All the demigods were feeling the impact of these austerities, and they appealed to Lord Brahmā to find out what Hiraṇyakaśipu wanted. He had actually performed these austerities for such a long time that an anthill formed around his body and the ants consumed the flesh and blood from his body. However, Hiraṇyakaśipu was sustaining his life in his bones by dint of his austerities and determination.

When Lord Brahmā appeared before Hiraṇyakaśipu, he poured some nectar on his head and restored Hiraṇyakaśipu’s body. Hiraṇyakaśipu then requested the benediction of immortality. Lord Brahmā said, “How can I do that? I myself am not immortal. I cannot give you something that I do not possess.”

Hiraṇyakaśipu then tried to ask for various other benedictions, which in essence, as he considered, would produce the same result. He asked to be killed in neither day nor night, neither by man nor by beast, neither inside nor outside, and so on. Lord Brahmā fulfilled all of these requests.

Hiraṇyakaśipu desired immortality, because he wanted to defy the existence of God and to usurp that position by becoming what he considered to be the supreme enjoyer of the universe and having lasting enjoyment. However, the type of enjoyment that he was addicted to was taking intoxication, accumulating wealth and power, and enjoying beautiful women.

Śrīla Prabhupāda explains that Hiraṇyakaśipu personified the materialistic person perfectly by his desires. However, any materialistic person who is demoniac in this way certainly cannot tolerate a person who is a devotee of the Lord. A devotee of the Lord shows by his own example and preaches strongly with firm faith that ultimately the Supreme Lord is the supreme controller; everything must be offered to Him; nothing is meant for our enjoyment; everything is meant for His enjoyment; and life’s perfection is to satisfy the Supreme Lord by dint of all of our activities, which are meant to be offered for His pleasure.

Hiraṇyakaśipu considered anyone with such a mentality to be siding with the enemy, Lord Viṣṇu. Somehow or other, Prahlāda, with such a mentality and devotion to the Lord, had taken birth in Hiraṇyakaśipu’s family as his son.

When Hiraṇyakaśipu had gone off to perform his austerities for one hundred celestial years, he had become very powerful, and the demigods wanted to try to get back their kingdom (the upper planetary system), which the demons had taken under their control. Therefore, the demigods, led by Indra, attacked to get back that which had been usurped by Hiraṇyakaśipu. Indra personally wanted to take the wife of Hiraṇyakaśipu within whose womb the seed (Prahlāda) had been left by Hiraṇyakaśipu. He wanted to kill her, and thus destroy Prahlāda whom he thought would be another unacceptable demon.

Nārada Muni showed up and said to Indra, “Stop! You cannot kill this woman!”

Indra replied, “What do you mean? I must kill this woman. Do you not know that the evil seed of Hiraṇyakaśipu is in this womb? That seed will lead to the destruction of everything. He must be killed.”

Nārada Muni said, “Don’t you realize that this woman has no husband to protect her? She should be protected. Not only that, but the child within her womb is a great, sinless devotee of the Lord. You cannot possibly kill him even if you wanted to. Therefore, you should leave her alone and allow me to take her.” It is explained that one of the reasons for Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva’s appearance was to uphold this statement by Nārada Muni, as well as the Lord’s statement to Arjuna in the Bhagavad-gītā: kaunteya pratijānīhi, na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati (Bg. 9.31)—“O son of Kuntī, declare it boldly that My devotee never perishes.”

Thus, Nārada Muni did not allow Indra to take Kayādhu. Instead, Nārada Muni took her to his āśrama and allowed her to render service there. While she was performing service, Nārada Muni would speak the message of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and Prahlāda Mahārāja heard everything from within the womb of his mother and remembered everything.

As described in the Harivaṁśa, and also as explained by Jīva Gosvāmī in his Bhakti Ṣaṇḍarbha, in his previous birth, Prahlāda Mahārāja was one of five sons of a great brāhmaṇa named Vāsu Śarma and his wife, Suśilā. His name was Vāsudeva, and he was the eldest of the five sons. Four of the sons were very good brāhmaṇas and devotees of the Lord. However, Vāsudeva was very degraded as a result of his association with a prostitute.

One time, he and the prostitute got into a big argument, resulting in them both deciding to fast that day and stay up all night. It just so happened that that night happened to be Nṛsiṁha-caturdaśī. It was the same tithi when Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva appears. Because of fasting completely on that day and staying up during the night, Vāsudeva became a great devotee (Prahlāda Mahārāja) of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva in his next life.

Hiraṇyakaśipu adored and loved Prahlāda, and wanted to train him so that he would adopt the same mentality as his own. Yet, somehow or other, this devotional experience continuously manifested in Prahlāda, which was displayed before his father.

Ṣaṇḍa and Amarka, the sons of Śukrācārya, were the teachers of Prahlāda and all the other sons of demons. One day, Hiraṇyakaśipu asked Prahlāda, “Please, give me the essence of what you have learned.”

Prahlāda Mahārāja replied: O best of the asuras, King of the demons, as far as I have learned from my spiritual master, any person who has accepted a temporary body and temporary household life is certainly embarrassed by anxiety because of having fallen in a dark well where there is no water but only suffering. One should give up this position and go to the forest \[vana\]. More clearly, one should go to Vṛndāvana, where only Kṛṣṇa consciousness is prevalent, and should thus take shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (Bhāg. 7.5.5)

Of course, Hiraṇyakaśipu expected to hear something else. His immediate suspicion was that somehow or other some Vaiṣṇava or worshipper of Viṣṇu had infiltrated into the school. He blamed Ṣaṇḍa and Amarka: “How did you let the enemy come into the school and contaminate my son like this? Obviously, somebody has come into the school and has influenced him in this way.”

Ṣaṇḍa and Amarka replied, “We are not aware of anybody who has done this.”

Hiraṇyakaśipu said, “Take my son back. Chastise him. Do whatever is necessary, and make sure he is properly trained to be a first-class demon!”

Thus Ṣaṇḍa and Amarka chastised him first, and then asked, “Why are you speaking in this way? How did this happen? Where did you learn all these things?” They dedicated themselves to seeing that he became trained in all kinds of diplomacy, knowing about friends and enemies, how to protect one’s material interests, and everything that was required to become a successful king who would eventually be able to take over the throne of Hiraṇyakaśipu.

After very intensive study, Prahlāda Mahārāja went back to Hiraṇyakaśipu. Hiraṇyakaśipu asked him, “Please give me the essence of what you have learned from your teachers.”

Prahlāda Mahārāja spontaneously responded (Bhāg. 7.5.23):

*śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ viṣṇoḥ*  
*smaraṇaṁ pāda-sevanam*  
*arcanaṁ vandanaṁ dāsyaṁ*  
*sakhyam ātma-nivedanam*

He said that devotional service rendered by the devotee consists of the nine processes of devotional service, beginning with hearing and chanting about the glories; remembering the pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead; serving the lotus feet of the Lord; worshipping the Lord with all kinds of paraphernalia; offering prayers to the Lord; becoming His servant; befriending the Lord; and surrendering everything to the Lord.

When Hiraṇyakaśipu heard this from Prahlāda Mahārāja, he became extremely angry, and took out his anger on Ṣaṇḍa and Amarka: “What have you been teaching my son?”

Ṣaṇḍa and Amarka fearfully said, “Please do not punish us. We have not taught him any of these things in any way. We have only been teaching him that which you have instructed us to teach him. We do not know from where all of these things he is saying are coming.”

Prahlāda Mahārāja reveals his disposition and from where he has gotten all of this devotion to the Supreme Lord.

Prahlāda Mahārāja replied: “Because of their uncontrolled senses, persons too addicted to materialistic life make progress toward hellish conditions and repeatedly chew that which has already been chewed. Their inclinations toward Kṛṣṇa are never aroused, either by the instructions of others, by their own efforts, or by a combination of both.

Persons who are strongly entrapped by the consciousness of enjoying material life, and who have therefore accepted as their leader or guru a similar blind man attached to external sense objects, cannot understand that the goal of life is to return home, back to Godhead, and engage in the service of Lord Viṣṇu. As blind men guided by another blind man miss the right path and fall into a ditch, materially attached men led by another materially attached man are bound by the ropes of fruitive labor, which are made of very strong cords, and they continue again and again in materialistic life, suffering the threefold miseries.

Unless they smear upon their bodies the dust of the lotus feet of a Vaiṣṇava completely freed from material contamination, persons very much inclined toward materialistic life cannot be attached to the lotus feet of the Lord, who is glorified for His uncommon activities. Only by becoming Kṛṣṇa conscious and taking shelter at the lotus feet of the Lord in this way can one be freed from material contamination.” (Bhāg. 7.5.30-32)

Prahlāda Mahārāja is alluding that whatever devotion he has received is a result of having gained the association of his spiritual master, Nārada Muni, when he was in the womb of his mother at the time when Hiraṇyakaśipu was performing his austerities.

Prahlāda displayed great devotion to the Lord and fearlessness in the face of his father who made so many attempts to punish him and even to kill him. Hiraṇyakaśipu tried to throw him off a mountain; poison him; have him be trampled by elephants; put him into a vat of burning oil; have him be tortured by demons; and have him bitten by venomous snakes. Despite his attempts, he could not kill his son. The Lord protected him, because Prahlāda Mahārāja had such deep conviction in the Supreme Personality of Godhead, even in the face of his father’s attempts to kill him.

Hiraṇyakaśipu said, “My son’s mind is just like a dog’s tail. When you try to straighten a dog’s tail, as soon as you let go, it immediately curls back. Similarly, every time I try to get my son to bend from his worship of Lord Viṣṇu, I cannot divert his mind from that worship.”

Hiraṇyakaśipu became so tormented by the fact that his son was a worshipper of Lord Viṣṇu that finally, in his anger, he decided that he was going to personally kill him himself. He asked Prahlāda Mahārāja, “From where do you get the strength to fight my strength? Don’t you know I am the most powerful being in the universe?”

Prahlāda said, “I’m getting my strength from the same place you got your strength. The only difference is that I know it and you do not.” Prahlāda Mahārāja got his strength by his firm faith in the Lord. Therefore, although Hiraṇyakaśipu had made so many previous attempts to have his son killed, now he decided he would personally sever Prahlāda’s head from his body and kill him.

Hiraṇyakaśipu asked, “Where is your Lord?”

Prahlāda said, “My Lord is everywhere.”

“Is He in this pillar?” Śrīla Prabhupāda in one lecture said that when asked this, Prahlāda Mahārāja looked up and saw that Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva was sitting on top of the pillar, and the Lord actually winked at him.

Prahlāda replied, “Yes, father!”

Hiraṇyakaśipu then took his sword and smashed the pillar. Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva thus took His birth from that pillar, which was His father for this particular appearance. He appeared because of the strength of the devotional service of Prahlāda, to protect him. The Lord manifested a most ferocious form, appearing to protect His devotee and his statement, and to uphold the benediction given to Hiraṇyakaśipu by Lord Brahmā—that he will be killed neither at day or night, nor by any created being of Lord Brahmā, nor by any man or beast, not indoors or outdoors, and so on.

A description of the Lord’s anger is given:

In the scriptures the Lord’s form as Nṛsiṁha is described as having a frightening face and filling His enemies with fear. The word bhisana, ‘frightening’, which occurs in Lord Nṛsiṁha’s mantra is explained in the following words of Nṛsiṁha-tāpanī Upaniṣad. “Why is the Lord called ‘frightening’? Because when all the demigods, all the worlds and all the living entities see His form, they all flee in fear. He fears no one. Out of fear of Him the wind blows and the sun rises. Out of fear of Him fire, the moon, and death all flee. (Kṛṣṇa Ṣaṇḍarbha)

Hiraṇyakaśipu studied the form of the Lord, trying to decide who the form of Nṛsiṁhadeva standing before him was. The Lord’s form was extremely fearsome because of His angry eyes, which resembled molten gold; His shining mane, which expanded the dimensions of His fearful face; His deadly teeth; and His razor-sharp tongue, which moved about like a dueling sword. His ears were erect and motionless, and His nostrils and gaping mouth appeared like caves of a mountain. His jaws parted fearfully, and His entire body touched the sky. His neck was very short and thick, His chest broad, His waist thin, and the hairs on His body as white as the rays of the moon. His arms, which resembled flanks of soldiers, spread in all directions as He killed the demons, rogues and atheists with His conchshell, disc, club, lotus and other natural weapons. (Bhāg. 7.8.19-22)

Upon defeating Hiraṇyakaśipu, Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva sat down and continued to manifest His ugra-nṛsiṁha form. It was a very fearsome form, and all the demigods, including Lord Śiva, Lord Brahmā, and even goddess Lakṣmī, were offering prayers, attempting to pacify the Lord. However, the Lord continued to manifest this ferocious form. Everyone was becoming fearful, and did not know how to deal with this form. They realized that the only way they could have any hope of the Lord becoming pacified was to ask Prahlāda to approach the Lord. Prahlāda then displayed, as he did through the entire līlā, how he had such firm faith in the Lord and His protection. He immediately went and prostrated himself before the fearsome form of the Lord, offering prayers unto Him. The Lord thus became so pacified. He took Prahlāda on His lap and petted him.

This form of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva is an eternal form. It is eternally situated in the spiritual world, but descends to fulfill a particular pastime. In addition to coming to prove the truthfulness of the statement of Prahlāda (that He is everywhere); the statements of Brahma (the benediction bestowed upon Hiraṇyakaśipu); and the curse of the four Kumāras, He also came to protect His devotee Prahlāda Mahārāja.

Not only does the Lord protect His devotee in the ways described in the pastime of Prahlāda, but also from within the heart by enlightening it. Śrīdhara Svāmī thus offers the prayer: “I offer my obeisances to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, who always enlightens Prahlāda from within his heart. He always protects His devotees from attacks of nescience.” This attack of nescience is, as described here, the demon-like desires for fruitive activities to enjoy the material world to the utmost.

Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura describes in Bhajana-rahasya that a devotee must make an effort to become free from these anarthas or unwanted desires within the heart. If a devotee makes no effort to become free from anarthas, then it is not possible for him to advance in devotional service, because he will not get the mercy of the holy name of the Lord. Even by repeated attempts, he will not be able to become free. Only when the devotee falls down before the lotus feet of the holy name of the Lord and cries with tears in his eyes can he actually be helped. For a devotee praying in this way, He will help from within the heart to remove these anarthas. These demon-like desires within the heart are destroyed by the Lord Himself. The Lord acts from within the heart for those devotees who develop the urge to hear and chant about Him.

*śṛṇvatāṁ sva-kathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ*  
*puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ*  
*hṛdy antaḥ stho hy abhadrāṇi*  
*vidhunoti suhṛt satām*

**Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, who is the Paramātmā \[Supersoul\] in everyone’s heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who has developed the urge to hear His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted. (Bhāg. 1.2.17)**

However, as Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says, if one makes no effort to become free from the desire for material enjoyment, then how can he expect these unwanted desires to go away? Unless he understands the danger of these unwanted desires, he will never consider the necessity of wanting them to go away. Prahlāda Mahārāja very emphatically in his teachings to his classmates describes the dangers of what happens to those who are addicted to sense enjoyment, and how they waste their lives in the pursuit of sense enjoyment:

“Every human being has a maximum duration of life of one hundred years, but for one who cannot control his senses, half of those years are completely lost because at night he sleeps twelve hours, being covered by ignorance. Therefore such a person has a lifetime of only fifty years. In the tender age of childhood, when everyone is bewildered, one passes ten years. Similarly, in boyhood, engaged in sporting and playing, one passes another ten years. In this way, twenty years are wasted. Similarly, in old age, when one is an invalid, unable to perform even material activities, one passes another twenty years wastefully. One whose mind and senses are uncontrolled becomes increasingly attached to family life because of insatiable lusty desires and very strong illusion. In such a madman’s life, the remaining years are also wasted because even during those years he cannot engage himself in devotional service.” (Bhāg. 7.6.6)

Being addicted by material desires, one becomes bound by the ropes of their fruitive labor, made of very strong cords, and they undergo repeated births and deaths in material world. However, Prahlāda Mahārāja demonstrated that by his devotional service and firm faith in Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, the Lord appears to give protection. The Lord protected him because his only desire was to dedicate his full life and everything he had for the service of the Lord.

After killing Hiraṇyakaśipu, and upon being pacified by Prahlāda Mahārāja, the Lord wished to grant him benedictions.

Although Prahlāda Mahārāja was only a boy, when he heard the benedictions offered by Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva he considered them impediments on the path of devotional service. Thus he smiled very mildly and spoke as follows.

Prahlāda Mahārāja said: “My dear Lord, O Supreme Personality of Godhead, because I was born in an atheistic family I am naturally attached to material enjoyment. Therefore, kindly do not tempt me with these illusions. I am very much afraid of material conditions, and I desire to be liberated from materialistic life. It is for this reason that I have taken shelter of Your lotus feet.

“O my worshipable Lord, because the seed of lusty desires, which is the root cause of material existence, is within the core of everyone’s heart, You have sent me to this material world to exhibit the symptoms of a pure devotee.

“Otherwise, O my Lord, O supreme instructor of the entire world, You are so kind to Your devotee that You could not induce him to do something unbeneficial for him. On the other hand, one who desires some material benefit in exchange for devotional service cannot be Your pure devotee. Indeed, he is no better than a merchant who wants profit in exchange for service.

“A servant who desires material profits from his master is certainly not a qualified servant or pure devotee. Similarly, a master who bestows benedictions upon his servant because of a desire to maintain a prestigious position as master is also not a pure master.

“O my Lord, I am Your unmotivated servant, and You are my eternal master. There is no need of our being anything other than master and servant. You are naturally my master, and I am naturally Your servant. We have no other relationship.

“O my Lord, best of the givers of benediction, if You at all want to bestow a desirable benediction upon me, then I pray from Your Lordship that within the core of my heart there be no material desires.

“O my Lord, because of lusty desires from the very beginning of one’s birth, the functions of one’s senses, mind, life, body, religion, patience, intelligence, shyness, opulence, strength, memory and truthfulness are vanquished.

“O my Lord, when a human being is able to give up all the material desires in his mind, he becomes eligible to possess wealth and opulence like Yours.

“O my Lord, full of six opulences, O Supreme Person! O Supreme Soul, killer of all miseries! O Supreme Person in the form of a wonderful lion and man, let me offer my respectful obeisances unto You.”

The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: “My dear Prahlāda, a devotee like you never desires any kind of material opulences, either in this life or in the next. Nonetheless, I order you to enjoy the opulences of the demons in this material world, acting as their king until the end of the duration of time occupied by Manu.” (Bhāg. 7.10.1-11)

The Lord was instructing Prahlāda to replace his father on the throne and to take the position of the king. Prahlāda Mahārāja, of course, would never have become contaminated by this position, as the Lord had given him this benediction. Prahlāda finally said:

“O Supreme Lord, because You are so merciful to the fallen souls, I ask You for only one benediction. I know that my father, at the time of his death, had already been purified by Your glance upon him, but because of his ignorance of Your beautiful power and supremacy, he was unnecessarily angry at You, falsely thinking that You were the killer of his brother. Thus he directly blasphemed Your Lordship, the spiritual master of all living beings, and committed heavily sinful activities directed against me, Your devotee. I wish that he be excused for these sinful activities.” (Bhāg. 7.10.15-17)

Prahlāda Mahārāja was selfless and did not want anything for himself. He only wanted that his heart be freed from material desires, and for his father to be forgiven for all of the sinful acts he had committed against him and the Lord. We see how the Lord protected him from being attacked by the nescience of material desires by enlightening him within his heart. He personally protects those devotees who remember these prayers and pastimes and who make the effort each day to pray to the Lord to protect them from the onslaught of the material world. Devotees should thus sincerely pray to the Lord for protection, because only by the mercy and grace of the Lord can one possibly overcome the obstacles of conditional life.

Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura has also provided wonderful prayers for receiving the mercy of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva. These prayers are certainly assurance to all sincere devotees that the worship of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva is purely in the line of aspiring love and devotion to Śrī Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. His prayers are as follows:

“Within my sinful heart the six enemies headed by lust perpetually reside as well as duplicity, the desire for fame, plus sheer cunning. At the lotus feet of Lord Nṛsiṁha I hope that He will mercifully purify my heart and give me the desire to serve Lord Kṛṣṇa.

“Weeping, I will beg at the lotus feet of Lord Nṛsiṁha for the benediction of worshiping Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Navadvīpa, perfectly safe and free from all difficulties. When will this Lord Hari, Whose terrible form strikes fear into fear itself, ever become pleased and show me His mercy?

“Even though Lord Nṛsiṁha is terrifying toward the sinful souls, He offers great auspiciousness unto the devotees of Lord Kṛṣṇa headed by Prahlāda Mahārāja. When will He be pleased to speak words of compassion unto me, a worthless fool, and thereby make me fearless?

“He will say: ‘Dear child, sit down freely and live happily here, in Śrī Gaurāṅga-dhāma. May you nicely worship the Divine Couple and may you develop loving attachment for Their holy names. By the mercy of My devotees, all obstacles are cast far away. With the purified heart just perform the worship of Rādhā Kṛṣṇa, for such worship overflows with sweet nectar.’

“Saying this, will that Lord delightedly place His own divine lotus feet upon my head? I will experience the sublime love for the Divine Couple Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa and undergo the ecstatic transformations called sāttvikā. Falling on the ground I will roll about at the door of Śrī Nṛsiṁha’s temple.” (Śrī Navadvīpa-bhāva-taraṅga, Verses 36-40).

The chanting of prayers to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva is our prayer for protection, what to speak of the holy name of the Lord, which is even more merciful than a form of the Lord or of the Deity, because if one commits offenses to the Deity, he can never be redeemed. The only way he can be redeemed by his offenses to the Deity is by chanting. If we petition the holy name of the Lord and chant very sincerely with the desire to eradicate the sinful desires within the core of our heart, and to forgive us for our past sins, then the Lord will protect us. This is also the protection which is being spoken of in Śrīla Prabhupāda’s purport to the prayer of Prahlāda Mahārāja to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 5.18.8.

## Rādhāstami

*mo-viṣaye gopī-gaṇera upapati-bhāve*  
*yoga-māyā karibeka āpana-prabhāve*  
*āmiha nā jāni tāhā, nā jāne gopī-gaṇa*  
*duṅhāra rūpa-guṇe duṅhāra nitya hare mana*

**“The influence of yogamāyā will inspire the gopīs with the sentiment that I am their paramour. Neither the gopīs nor I shall notice this, for our minds will always be entranced by one another’s beauty and qualities.” (Cc. Ādi 4.29-30)**

PURPORT

In the spiritual sky the Vaikuṇṭha planets are predominated by Nārāyaṇa. His devotees have the same features He does, and the exchange of devotion there is on the platform of reverence. But above all these Vaikuṇṭha planets is Goloka, or Kṛṣṇaloka, where the original Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, fully manifests His pleasure potency in free loving affairs. Since the devotees in the material world know almost nothing about these affairs, the Lord desires to show these affairs to them.

In Goloka Vṛndāvana there is an exchange of love known as parakīya-rasa. It is something like the attraction of a married woman for a man other than her husband. In the material world this sort of relationship is most abominable because it is a perverted reflection of the parakīya-rasa in the spiritual world, where it is the highest kind of loving affair. Such feelings between the devotee and the Lord are presented by the influence of yogamāyā. The Bhagavad-gītā states that devotees of the highest grade are under the care of daiva-māyā, or yogamāyā: mahātmānas tu māṁ pārtha daivīṁ prakṛtim āśritāḥ (Bg. 9.13). Those who are actually great souls (mahātmās) are fully absorbed in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, always engaged in the service of the Lord. They are under the care of daivī-prakṛti, or yogamāyā. Yogamāyā creates a situation in which the devotee is prepared to transgress all regulative principles simply to love Kṛṣṇa. A devotee naturally does not like to transgress the laws of reverence for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, but by the influence of yogamāyā he is prepared to do anything to love the Supreme Lord better.

Those under the spell of the material energy cannot at all appreciate the activities of yogamāyā, for a conditioned soul can hardly understand the pure reciprocation between the Lord and His devotee. But by executing devotional service under the regulative principles, one can become very highly elevated and then begin to appreciate the dealings of pure love under the management of yogamāyā.

In the spiritual loving sentiment induced by the yogamāyā potency, both Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and the damsels of Vraja forget themselves in spiritual rapture. By the influence of such forgetfulness, the attractive beauty of the gopīs plays a prominent part in the transcendental satisfaction of the Lord, who has nothing to do with mundane sex. Because spiritual love of Godhead is above everything mundane, the gopīs superficially seem to transgress the codes of mundane morality. This perpetually puzzles mundane moralists. Therefore yogamāyā acts to cover the Lord and His pastimes from the eyes of mundaners, as confirmed in the Bhagavad-gītā (7.25), where the Lord says that He reserves the right of not being exposed to everyone.

The acts of yogamāyā make it possible for the Lord and the gopīs, in loving ecstasy, to sometimes meet and sometimes separate. These transcendental loving affairs of the Lord are unimaginable to empiricists involved in the impersonal feature of the Absolute Truth. Therefore the Lord Himself appears before the mundaners to bestow upon them the highest form of spiritual realization and also personally relish its essence. The Lord is so merciful that He Himself descends to take the fallen souls back home to the kingdom of Godhead, where the erotic principles of Godhead are eternally relished in their real form, distinct from the perverted sexual love so much adored and indulged in by the fallen souls in their diseased condition. The reason the Lord displays the rāsa-līlā is essentially to induce all the fallen souls to give up their diseased morality and religiosity, and to attract them to the kingdom of God to enjoy the reality. A person who actually understands what the rāsa-līlā is will certainly hate to indulge in mundane sex life. For the realized soul, hearing the Lord’s rāsa-līlā through the proper channel will result in complete abstinence from material sexual pleasure.

In these verses, the Lord is describing the nature of His internal potency, yogamāyā. One must understand the difference between the internal potency and the external potency.

*viṣṇu-śakti parā prokta kṣetrajñākhya tathā parā*  
*avidyā-karma-saṁjñānyā tṛtīyā śaktir iṣyate*

(Viṣṇu Purāṇa)

It is described that the potencies of the Supreme Lord are summarized in three categories: the spiritual energy, which is full knowledge; the living entities, who although belong to the spiritual energies can come under the influence of the third energy, which is Māyā, and is visible in fruitive activities.

The Supreme Lord has unlimited potencies. In the Lord’s internal potency, He manifests the sandhinī potency, saṁvit potency and the hlādinī potency.

The sandhinī potency is that potency which sustains every living existence. The predominating Deity of the Lord’s sandhinī potency is Lord Balarāma, from whom comes all the forms in the spiritual world.

The saṁvit potency is Kṛṣṇa’s potency of knowledge or cognizance. It is that potency displayed in the spiritual world, which brings the living entities to know what their relationship is with Kṛṣṇa. This is also known as sambandha (relationship). In the spiritual world, Balarāma knows Kṛṣṇa as His brother; Kṛṣṇa knows Rādhārāṇī as His paramour; and Yaśodā knows Kṛṣṇa as her son. This is the perfection of the saṁvit potency—the knowledge that establishes that relationship with Kṛṣṇa.

The hlādinī potency, which is personified by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, is Kṛṣṇa’s pleasure potency. Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme enjoyer, and when He wants to enjoy, He is not interested in anything of this material world. Only that which is completely spiritual can give Kṛṣṇa pleasure.

*etad īśanam īśasya*  
*prakṛti-stho ’pi tad-guṇaiḥ*  
*na yujyate sadātma-sthair*  
*yathā buddhis tad-āśrayā*

**This is the divinity of the Personality of Godhead: He is not affected by the qualities of material nature, even though He is in contact with them. Similarly, the devotees who have taken shelter of the Lord do not become influenced by the material qualities. (Bhāg. 1.11.38)**

Therefore, Kṛṣṇa cannot be influenced by anything material. If we want to awaken Kṛṣṇa’s pleasure, we must understand that only His internal potency can do this.

Prahlāda Mahārāja explains that the Lord is pleased only when one has unflinching, unalloyed devotion to Him. You cannot please the Supreme Lord—whether you become an expert brāhmaṇa, or become advanced in etiquette or vast learning. Neither can you please Him by austerities or vows, nor by chastity or great sacrifices. Kṛṣṇa is pleased only when one has unflinching, unalloyed devotion to Him. Without such sincere devotional service, everything else is simply a show. Only a His devotee can influence Kṛṣṇa. The person who can best influence Kṛṣṇa, make Him bewildered, drive Him mad, make Him dance, and make Him fall at Her feet is Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. She is the personification of that hlādinī potency that gives pleasure to the Lord.

Yogamāyā creates a situation where Rādhārāṇī and the other gopīs, who are married women, are going to meet with Kṛṣṇa and have conjugal loving affairs with Kṛṣṇa. It appears that they have given up their chastity. Even though they have husbands and children, when Kṛṣṇa plays His flute, they leave them all behind and go to the forest and meet with Kṛṣṇa. They are under great pressure, because they always have to hide their deep affection for Kṛṣṇa, as it is certainly immoral to go and meet with a man other than one’s husband.

Prabhupāda explains that the mundane moralists simply cannot understand these affairs in the spiritual world. They can never understand who Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is, and how She pleases the Lord. Real chastity means knowing that every living being belongs to Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa is the husband, and everyone is the wife of Kṛṣṇa and meant to be enjoyed by Kṛṣṇa alone.

There is a pastime that exemplifies this true meaning of chastity. Once, Kṛṣṇa became very ill and lost consciousness. Mother Yaśodā was in great anxiety. She wanted to find a way to immediately revive her son. Kṛṣṇa therefore appeared at the home of mother Yaśodā in another form, as a mystic physician. He said, “I am a physician and I can see that your son is very ill. The only thing that can cure your son is water from the Yamunā, which is carried in a porous pot, full of holes. This pot can only be carried by a completely chaste woman.”

Mother Yaśodā frantically began to think, “Who are the most chaste women in Vṛndāvana?” Then she remembered that Kuṭilā and Jaṭilā are always talking about the unchastity of all these other young girls in Vṛndāvana. Therefore, they themselves must be chaste. Jaṭilā is the mother of Abhimanyu, who is apparently the husband of Rādhārāṇī, and Kuṭilā is Jaṭilā’s daughter. They are always suspecting that there is something not right going on between the young gopīs and Kṛṣṇa. Yaśodā therefore thought to first try asking Jaṭilā to go and get some water to cure her son.

When asked, Jaṭilā was not very inclined to do it. However, out of her maternal affection for Kṛṣṇa, mother Yaśodā was very desperate and very convincing to Jaṭilā. Jaṭilā therefore took the porous pot and went to the Yamunā. However, when she tried to fill it with water, the water immediately escaped through the holes.

Seeing that Jaṭilā could not do it, she decided to ask Kuṭilā. However, Kuṭilā refused, not wanting to get involved. However, due to mother Yaśodā’s desperation, she defeated Kuṭilā. Kuṭilā therefore took the porous pot, placed it into the Yamunā River, and when she picked it up, all the water came out through the holes.

Seeing mother Yaśodā’s increasing desperation, the physician said to mother Yaśodā, “I know someone who is very chaste. You should ask Rādhārāṇī to go to the river and get the water.”

They therefore went to Rādhārāṇī and asked Her to bring the water from the Yamunā in the porous pot. As She was walking to the Yamunā, Her mind was completely absorbed in thoughts of Kṛṣṇa. She was praying, “Kṛṣṇa, please allow Me to get this water so that I can cure You.” In Her mind, She was pleading with Kṛṣṇa to give Her the ability to get this water to cure Him. When She placed the pot in the Yamunā, Kṛṣṇa, present in the Yamunā, touched the pot. When She lifted it, none of the water came out. This water was brought by Rādhārāṇī back to the physician. It was given to Kṛṣṇa, and He was immediately cured and returned to consciousness. Kṛṣṇa thus showed who the most chaste person was.

Sometimes the mundane moralists think that by chastity, or by accepting vows, one can please the Supreme Personality of Godhead. However, we can understand from this pastime that real chastity means to be prepared to do anything to please Kṛṣṇa—even if it means disobeying the laws and rules of the scriptures, or even if it means losing respect or prestige from the village people. The gopīs, headed by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, are the manifestation of the pleasure potency of the Lord, and they are the ones who give the Lord the greatest pleasure.

Rādhārāṇī is the full embodiment of that pleasure potency, hlādinī śakti, of the Supreme Lord. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta has explained how the energies of the Lord are simultaneously one and different from the Supreme Lord. In Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Svarūpa Dāmodara also says that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are one in Their identity. The loving affairs of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are eternal manifestations of the internal potency of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Although They are one, They have separated Themselves eternally as Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.

Rādhārāṇī is Kṛṣṇa’s second self, and just as Kṛṣṇa is eternal, Rādhārāṇī is also eternal. However, as described by Jagadānanda Paṇḍita in the Prema Vivarta, we should never question who came first. Just as Kṛṣṇa has no beginning, Rādhārāṇī also has no beginning. Jagadānanda Paṇḍita also explains that when Rādhārāṇī and Kṛṣṇa unite to become Lord Caitanya, still we should not question whether it was Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa who came first, or Lord Caitanya who came first. They are all beginningless and our conception of time cannot be imposed on the eternal pastimes of the Supreme Lord, which are ever-present. Although we sometimes use the word ‘when’ in describing the Lord’s pastimes, such as, “When Kṛṣṇa became united with Rādhārāṇī and became Lord Caitanya,” Jagadānanda Paṇḍita explains that as soon as we try to impose the principles of this material world on transcendence, it will not be possible to conceive. We should not try to approach transcendental subject matter through mundane logic. We can only understand it when the Lord reveals Himself. We will then see how Lord Kṛṣṇa and Rādhārāṇī are eternal.

Although Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is eternal, the nature of Her appearance in this world is nicely described. King Vṛṣabhānu was very anxious to have a child. Once, when he went down to the Yamunā River, he saw an all-effulgent light coming from the water. In the whorl of a lotus in the river, he found a very beautiful young girl. However, She was blind. King Vṛṣabhānu brought this young girl home and accepted Her as his daughter.

Nanda and Yaśodā were very close with King Vṛṣabhānu, and when they heard that he had a daughter, they wanted to go and congratulate him. Thus, they went together with their young son, Kṛṣṇa, to the home of King Vṛṣabhānu. While they were talking among themselves, Kṛṣṇa crawled over to the cradle where Rādhārāṇī was lying with Her eyes closed. As soon as Kṛṣṇa looked into the cradle, Rādhārāṇī’s eyes immediately opened, and the first thing She saw was Kṛṣṇa’s beautiful form. Rādhārāṇī showed that She came to this world to see Kṛṣṇa alone and to display the perfect symptoms of love for Kṛṣṇa.

Just as the devotees feel separation from Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa also feels separation from His devotees. Once, Kṛṣṇa was in the pasturing grounds with His cowherd boyfriends, and He told Subala, “I am missing Rādhārāṇī. I must see Her right away. I am feeling such great separation. She must come right now. Please go get Her and bring Her here.”

Subala said, “But it is broad daylight now. How am I going to bring Rādhārāṇī here? Certainly somebody will see.”

Kṛṣṇa replied, “I will not be able to live a moment longer unless Rādhārāṇī comes. Please go find some means to bring Her here to relieve My separation.”

Subala therefore went to Rādhārāṇī and said that Kṛṣṇa will immediately die if He does not see Her right now.

She said, “What can I do? How can I leave? I will be seen if I leave the house now.”

Subala had very beautiful features, very similar to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī’s. He proposed, “Why don’t we exchange clothes? You can wear my cowherd boy dress and go to Kṛṣṇa. I will wear Your clothes and stay here.”

Rādhārāṇī agreed, and they exchanged clothes. While She was leaving the house, everybody called out, “Subala, what are you doing here? Why have you come to the house?”

Dressed as Subala, She was carrying a calf in Her arms. She said, “The cow is mooing, missing her young calf. I am bringing the young calf back into the forest to its mother.” Rādhārāṇī was really carrying the calf to cover Herself so that She would not be recognized.

Rādhārāṇī had a hint about where Kṛṣṇa was at that time in the forest, and thus proceeded there. Kṛṣṇa saw Her, and said, “Subala, what have you done? You have come back without Rādhārāṇī! How can I live? I must have Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī now!” Kṛṣṇa obviously did not recognize Rādhārāṇī in Her disguise.

Rādhārāṇī, in the dress of Subala, said, “If You would like, I can go get Candrāvalī. Maybe she will bring you some pleasure.”

Kṛṣṇa said, “No. One who has thirst for milk cannot be satisfied by curd.”

Rādhārāṇī then immediately opened Her arms and embraced Kṛṣṇa. She said, “Oh, You cannot recognize Me?” Immediately Kṛṣṇa’s separation from Rādhārāṇī was pacified.

Kṛṣṇa’s devotees experience four types of separation from Kṛṣṇa. The first type of separation is called pūrva-rāga, which is when one has heard about Kṛṣṇa, seen a picture of Him, or seen Him from a distance, but has not yet met Him. Of the four types of separation, this is the only one that we can experience, as we have not yet seen Kṛṣṇa. Those who feel separation in pūrva-rāga, thinking that they have not yet met Kṛṣṇa, are very anxious to meet and see Him.

Once, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī was shown a picture of Kṛṣṇa, and She was seeing how beautiful He is and was thus very anxious to meet Him. She was told to go and stand at the top of a tower so that She could see Him going out to the pasturing grounds with His cowherd boyfriends and the cows. However, the nature of this pūrva-rāga is that even though Rādhārāṇī has met Kṛṣṇa, She forgets, thinking that She has not yet met Kṛṣṇa. Thus every time she meets Kṛṣṇa, it is ever-fresh, and She feels as though it is the first time she is meeting Him.

The second type of separation is māna, or separation in anger. For example, sometimes when Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī becomes angry with Kṛṣṇa, She will have some feelings of separation. Kṛṣṇa then has to come before Her and plead, “Please allow Me to be with You.” He petitions Her in various ways, trying to break that anger. One time, He even took His flute and placed it before Rādhārāṇī’s lotus feet, or He would go to touch Her lotus feet to relieve Her anger.

The third type of separation is called prema-vaicittya, which is when Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are feeling separation from each other, although They are actually together. One example is when Kṛṣṇa was sitting with Rādhārāṇī, and a bee came buzzing around Them. Kṛṣṇa wanted to get rid of the bee, and therefore had Madhumaṅgala chase the bee out of the kuñja. Madhumaṅgala did so, and when he came back, he said, “Madhu is gone,” referring to the bee. Rādhārāṇī was sitting there, looking at Kṛṣṇa. However, She could not actually see Kṛṣṇa, because She was so absorbed in ecstasy, thinking that Kṛṣṇa (also known as Madhu) was gone. Thus, in prema-vaicittya, They are present, but feeling separation.

The fourth type of separation is pravāsa. There are two types of pravāsa: When Kṛṣṇa is going away for a short time, and when Kṛṣṇa is leaving for a long time. An example of the former is when Kṛṣṇa goes out to the pasturing grounds with His cowherd boyfriends for a short time. Mother Yaśodā feels so much separation. An example of separation felt when Kṛṣṇa is going for a longer time is when Kṛṣṇa was going to Mathurā to kill Kaṁsa, and He told all the gopīs that He would be coming back soon.

In Lalita-mādhava Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī reveals another beautiful pastime which further elaborates upon these feelings of separation. Akrūra came to take Kṛṣṇa from Vṛndāvana and bring Him to Mathurā. The gopīs were feeling the extreme fire of separation watching Kṛṣṇa leave. Rādhārāṇī began manifesting symptoms of udghūrṇā, or complete divine madness. She began speaking citrajalpa, or speaking like a mad woman. She was feeling such intense separation from Kṛṣṇa that finally it got to the point where She could no longer tolerate it. Therefore, both Rādhārāṇī and Viśākā jumped into the Yamunā River and drowned themselves.

The Yamunā River is the daughter of Sūryadeva. One of the greatest servants of Sūryadeva is Satrājit. Sūryadeva took Rādhārāṇī and gave Her to Satrājit, and then She entered into the body of Satyabhāmā, the daughter of King Satrājit. While She was there in Mathurā, She was feeling great intense separation from Kṛṣṇa. Because She was feeling so much separation from Kṛṣṇa, She requested Viśvakarmā to build a place called Nava-vṛndāvana, which is a replica of Vṛndāvana. Rādhārāṇī, in the body of Satyabhāmā, would go to this place, and would regularly worship the Deity of Kṛṣṇa that Viśvakarmā had also made.

Sometimes, when Kṛṣṇa was in Dvārakā, He would also feel separation from Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, and therefore He would also go to Nava-vṛndāvana. Kṛṣṇa was noticing that this girl was coming every day and worshiping a Deity of Kṛṣṇa. He said to Madhumaṅgala, “This girl is coming every day. She is offering everything to this Deity so feelingly with tears in Her eyes. I want to find out who She is. Let us take this Deity and move it away. In its place, I will stand there in the form of the Deity so that I can see who this girl is that is coming to worship.”

When Satyabhāmā came, Kṛṣṇa thought, “I feel that this girl has the same sentiment as Rādhā. I am feeling, in Her presence, just as I do in the presence of Rādhārāṇī. Viśvakarmā has done a very wonderful job here in Nava-vṛndāvana!”

Meanwhile, Satyabhāmā was looking at Kṛṣṇa standing there, and said, “Look at this Deity! It looks so life-like! Viśvakarmā has done such a wonderful job in this Nava-vṛndāvana that he has made a Deity that looks like My Kṛṣṇa!”

She began speaking to the Deity of Kṛṣṇa, “O My dear Kṛṣṇa, how are You feeling? Is everything auspicious for You?”

Kṛṣṇa was thinking, “Only for someone like My Rādhārāṇī could I have this sentiment. But She is not here. She drowned in the Yamunā. How can I feel what I am feeling right now?”

He answered back to Her, “Yes, everything must be auspicious, because I am feeling just like I am having Rādhārāṇī in My presence. How could there be anything inauspicious?”

Kṛṣṇa then began crying because He was feeling the absence of Rādhārāṇī. Tears were coming down His face, and Rādhārāṇī was crying. She was wiping the tears from Kṛṣṇa’s face and thinking, “This is a Deity, but it is such a life-like Deity by Viśvakarmā.” She could not realize that it was Kṛṣṇa. Such is prema-vaicittya—in the presence, but feeling separation. Kṛṣṇa and Rādhārāṇī were present together in Nava-vṛndāvana, which was non-different from the real Vṛndāvana, yet They were feeling intense separation for one another.

Lord Caitanya came to display such feelings of separation during His appearance in this world. He also displayed divine madness when He manifested His pastimes in Jagannātha Purī. The Lord came as Caitanya Mahāprabhu to teach by His example how to always be absorbed in thoughts of Kṛṣṇa in the mood of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. We cannot imitate these feelings of separation. But from His example, we should learn to hanker for Kṛṣṇa by serving Him in separation.

## Kārttika

In the Nectar of Devotion, Śrīla Prabhupāda quotes one verse from Padma Purāna. Paraphrasing the text from Chapter 12, it is stated that those persons who go to Mathurā or Vṛndāvana and render regulated devotional service during the month of Kārttika, even if they have some material motivation in the execution of their devotional service, will desire only pure devotional service. Prabhupāda comments that ordinarily an insincere person will not be able to obtain devotional service. Even if those who are insincere render regulated devotional service during the month of Kārttika in Mathurā or Vṛndāvana, they are given the opportunity to render personal service to Kṛṣṇa. Such is the power of rendering devotional service for the pleasure of Lord Dāmodara in that sacred place.

Of course, regulated devotional service begins with regular hearing and chanting the glories of the Supreme Lord. For those who are not rendering regulated devotional service in Mathurā and Vṛndāvana physically, still, by regularly hearing and chanting the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa or Dāmodara during the month of Kārttika, wherever they may be, it can be as good as being in Vṛndāvana. Therefore, we should desire to absorb our consciousness in Vṛndāvana by worshipping Lord Dāmodara during the month of Kārttika.

Generally, we do that by offering the Dāmodarāṣṭaka prayers composed by Satyavrata Muni. We should try to understand the meaning of those prayers. Dāmodarāṣṭaka describes two different moods: that of Lord Dāmodara, who is Yaśodā-Dāmodara, the son of mother Yaśodā, and that of Rādhā-Dāmodara.

Before elaborating on the Dāmodarāṣṭaka prayers, the mood must be set for understanding the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana. These pastimes are a very high subject matter. They are not merely stories that we are reading. Rather, they are eternal līlās of the Supreme Lord when He manifests Himself in this world once in each day of Lord Brahmā in each and every universe. These pastimes are eternally displayed in the transcendental realm of Goloka Vṛndāvana. When Kṛṣṇa appears in each universe, He displays His loving reciprocal relationships with His eternal associates to attract the conditioned souls to His eternal transcendental realm.

Sometimes our conception of God is with an incomplete understanding of how God is manifest in His most complete form. Sometimes people have a conception of God as being the controller, an all-powerful living being, or the most opulent being. Of course, Kṛṣṇa does display six opulences: wealth, fame, intelligence, beauty, strength and renunciation. However, the most complete understanding or conception (as described in Cc. Madhya 14.219) is that the Lord manifests all of His opulences in full only in the transcendental realm of Vṛndāvana, which is like an unlimited ocean. However, the opulence of Vaikuṇṭha and Dvārakā cannot be compared to even a drop of that ocean. In the realm of Vaikuṇṭha, the Lord is worshiped in great opulence, wealth and majesty. In Vaikuṇṭha, there are many palaces, kingdoms and transcendental planets where the Lord is the Supreme predominating being. The residents of those planets worship the Lord in awe, being struck by His powerful position. Yet, the Lord is most complete in His display of opulences in Vṛndāvana.

Brahmā-saṁhitā describes the opulences of Vṛndāvana—natural forests, natural minerals, leaves, flowers, and kāma-dhenu cows, which provide an unlimited supply of milk that is desired by everyone. These are considered to be real opulence. The forest simply provides flowers for decorating the body of the Supreme Lord and His devotees. The minerals are also used for decorating the Supreme Lord. Peacock feathers ornament His head dress. The Lord wears guñjā and vaijayantī garlands around His neck. The soil or the surface of Vṛndāvana is described as a transcendental touchstone and the source of all the cintāmaṇi jewels, which are the source of all opulence in the world. The gopīs in Vṛndāvana are considered to be far superior to the goddesses of fortune who are manifest in Vaikuṇṭha. These form the real opulence of Vṛndāvana.

The Lord, the possessor of all opulence, displays His full opulences most completely in Vṛndāvana because He displays Himself as subordinate to the love of His eternal associates—His greatest opulence, known as bhakta-vātsalya. He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, worshipped with great awe and reverence, and worshiped by millions of prayers given in the Vedic literatures. Although He is worshiped in this mood, He displays His greatest opulence by allowing Himself to be controlled by the love of His eternal associates, the residents of Goloka Vṛndāvana, and subordinates Himself completely to them. He is completely controlled by their loving attitude towards Him—as a friend, parent or lover. This greatest manifestation of opulence in the transcendental realm of Goloka Vṛndāvana is manifested in each and every universe.

Each universe is compared to be like a mustard seed in a bucket of mustard seeds, which is very insignificant. Yet, Kṛṣṇa, from His transcendental body, is emanating unlimited universes. In each universe the predominating deities are present: Lord Brahmā, the creator of the universe; Lord Viṣṇu, the maintainer and expansion of Kṛṣṇa; and Lord Śiva, the destroyer of each universe. The Lord’s portions or plenary portions appear to protect His devotees whenever there is disturbance created by the atheists.

Lord Kṛṣṇa is parameśvara (or paramaḥ īśvaraḥ), the supreme controller, the original and primeval person, and sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam, the cause of all causes. He is infallible, the original Supreme primeval Person, navayauvanaṁ (an ever-fresh youth), His body is endless (not subject to decay), and His body is the beginning of everything.

His pastimes, qualities and characteristics are inconceivable to our mundane mind, but they can be realized when we purify the mind and the senses through the transcendental sound vibration of chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa and by hearing the transcendental sound vibration which is emanating originally from the Supreme Lord Himself. By hearing the transcendental sound vibration, gradually the heart is cleansed. When the heart is cleansed, the senses become purified, and then one gradually achieves transcendental realization. Kṛṣṇa removes the illusory curtain that has caused us to forget our eternal relationship with Him and has caused us to look at this world as seemingly real.

In a conditioned state, when one hears the descriptions of pastimes of the Supreme Lord, then he may think that they are simply narrations or are fictional. However, a Vaiṣṇava or one whose faith has been awakened in hearing the narrations of the Supreme Lord by the process based on hearing the sound vibration gradually starts to achieve realization.

Thus, having introduced the nature of the pastimes of the Lord, we will elaborate on the dāmodara-līlā.

Mother Yaśodā’s meditation is always completely absorbed in satisfying Kṛṣṇa—whether she is preparing milk on the stove, preparing butter, or preparing milk sweets. She even churns the yogurt into butter herself, even though it is not necessary for her to do that as a queen. However, she does so, wanting to offer it to Kṛṣṇa. Furthermore, this butter is made from very aromatic milk that she acquires from cows grazing at a particular place on Govardhana, where the grass is very aromatic and fresh. While making that milk into yogurt, and then churning it into butter, she was singing poetry that she had composed about her son and His activities. Such was her mood of absorption. Her every thought was of Kṛṣṇa, her every action was for Kṛṣṇa, her every word was for Kṛṣṇa, whatever she would hear was always in relationship to Kṛṣṇa, and she would never think of preparing anything that was not for His pleasure.

Śukadeva Gosvāmī describes mother Yaśodā’s characteristics:

Dressed in a saffron-yellow sari, with a belt tied about her full hips, mother Yaśodā pulled on the churning rope, laboring considerably, her bangles and earrings moving and vibrating and her whole body shaking. Because of her intense love for her child, her breasts were wet with milk. Her face, with its very beautiful eyebrows, was wet with perspiration, and mālatī flowers were falling from her hair. (Bhāg. 10.9.1-2)

This verse presents the ideal of motherly affection for Kṛṣṇa. Anyone interested in cultivating vātsalya-bhāva, or parental love, should meditate upon the bodily form, qualities, features and affection of mother Yaśodā described here. In other words, this is the nature of mother Yaśodā’s love.

Although mother Yaśodā is laboring intensively for Kṛṣṇa, still He goes and steals butter elsewhere. Nonetheless, mother Yaśodā does not at any time think that because Kṛṣṇa is going and stealing someone else’s butter, that she should not make any more butter for Him. Her love for Kṛṣṇa is unalloyed. Sometimes she says to Him, “Why are You creating so much disturbance elsewhere? Why don’t You just stay home? Whatever You are doing can be accepted if it is in Your own home. But when You do it in others’ homes, it causes so much disturbance. Just stay home, Kṛṣṇa!”

However, Kṛṣṇa would still go to others’ homes and cause disturbance. Such is the nature of His pastimes. Even though He does whatever He wants, everybody is naturally satisfied by His activities.

Once, while mother Yaśodā was laboring to make butter for Kṛṣṇa, He was sleeping in another room. He awoke from His sleeping state, and came to mother Yaśodā, trying to get her attention. He grabbed the churning rod, and held onto it so that she could not churn yogurt into butter. Seeing that Kṛṣṇa wanted motherly attention from her, mother Yaśodā placed Him on her lap, and offered her breast milk to Him—one of her manifestations of motherly affection.

She then noticed that the milk on the stove, which she was preparing for Kṛṣṇa, was boiling over. Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura says:

How could Yaśodā show so much interest in the boiling milk that she left Kṛṣṇa unsatisfied and hungry? Yaśodā was so concerned for what Kṛṣṇa would eat and drink that she could temporarily ignore Kṛṣṇa.
