Only those who are under the sway of premā can understand or talk about the remarkable actions of one who is impelled by pure love for Kṛṣṇa. No one else can understand these matters. (Sārārtha-darśinī, ṭīkā by Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura to Bhāg. 10.9.5)

Mother Yaśodā was thinking, “That’s Kṛṣṇa’s milk on the stove! I can’t let Kṛṣṇa’s milk boil over on the stove! I can put Him down for a moment, get the milk, come back and continue.”

However, this was another way for Kṛṣṇa to capture attention by His mischievous behavior. Although Kṛṣṇa is the personification of peace, He became angry, in His display of His bhakta-vātsalya.

When mother Yaśodā went to get the milk, Kṛṣṇa became angry, thinking, “Why did she put Me down? I am not fully satisfied!”

He therefore picked up a stone and broke open the clay pot in which mother Yaśodā was churning the yogurt into butter. Then He went into the other room where the butter was stored, and took down the pots of butter. He began mischievously distributing the contents of the pot to His friends and to the monkeys. He went and sat on a grinding mortar, and called all His friends and the monkeys to come over. Sitting there, He was constantly looking around to make sure that nobody was running up to catch Him—especially His mother, as she often does.

Mother Yaśodā, who had gone to attend to the milk on the stove, came out of the house and saw all the mischief that had been caused—the broken pot and the contents all over the ground. She went into the other room and saw all the other pots either broken or thrown on the ground. She saw footprints everywhere on the ground, caused by Kṛṣṇa running through the butter.

Then she looked outside and saw her son sitting on the grinding mortar, distributing the butter. Seeing this, she approached Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa saw her and immediately got down from the grinding mortar and began running in fear. Mother Yaśodā picked up a stick and began chasing Him. While she is chasing Him, Kṛṣṇa says to her, “Mother, what are you doing? Stop right there! Don’t come closer! If you think I am engaged in mischief, just watch what kind of mischief I will do if you get any closer!”

Mother Yaśodā said, “If You are so scared of being punished, then why did You break the pot?”

Kṛṣṇa replied, “Oh I promise that I will never do it again!” Of course, He has said this so many times before, and mother Yaśodā knows it. Every time she catches Him, He either claims that He did not do anything, or he promises that He will not do it again. Kṛṣṇa does this because it enhances the motherly affection of Yaśodā. She wants to have a child whom she can punish; whom she can nurture; whom she can feed; and whom she can take care of. It just so happens that Kṛṣṇa is her child. Because she is so absorbed in vātsalya-prema, whenever Kṛṣṇa is in difficulty, or performing some mischievous acts, she thinks like a mother. It would not be possible for her to chase after Kṛṣṇa and punish Him if she has to consider that He is God. Such is the opulence of Kṛṣṇa, which is displayed in full in Vṛndāvana, where there is no awe and reverence; only unalloyed love according to one’s particular relationship with Kṛṣṇa.

Satyavrata Muni prays:

To the Supreme Lord, whose form is the embodiment of eternal existence, knowledge, and bliss, whose shark-shaped earrings are swinging to and fro, who is beautifully shining in the divine realm of Gokula, who (due to the offense of breaking the pot of yogurt that His mother was churning into butter and then stealing the butter that was kept hanging from a swing) is quickly running from the wooden grinding mortar in fear of mother Yaśodā, but who has been caught from behind by her who ran after Him with greater speed—to that Supreme Lord, Śrī Dāmodara, I offer my humble obeisances. (Śrī Dāmodarāṣṭaka, Verse 1)

Kṛṣṇa has committed an offense by breaking the pot of yogurt that His mother was churning into butter. Kṛṣṇa is a mischievous child. We would think that Kṛṣṇa would be fully satisfied with whatever His mother was offering to Him. However, because He is the Supreme autocrat, sometimes for His pleasure pastimes, He displays such pastimes as this. He derives His satisfaction by going elsewhere for His butter, which increases His pleasure, the pleasure of mother Yaśodā and all the residents of Vraja.

Mother Yaśodā was thinking, “If I do not tie Him up, He is going to get Himself into big trouble.”

All the other gopīs also used to come regularly and complain about Kṛṣṇa’s activities, such as stealing the butter and disturbing the children. They would say, “Look at your son right now, standing there, looking so innocent as if He has done nothing. When He is in front of you, He makes Himself look so innocent. But when He is in our houses, He yells at us, lies to us, and creates so much mischief. He unties the calves and they take all the milk from the cows. He throws dirt over our freshly painted houses. Look at Him now, looking so innocent!”

Hearing these accusations, Kṛṣṇa would say to mother Yaśodā, “Mātā, these gopīs are lying to you! Actually, I go to their houses every morning because I am simply thinking of them! Therefore, I want to see them and their sons! But now they are making up all these lies and telling you all these things. They are not telling you the truth! Truthfully mother, I am not doing any of these things.” Thus, the Supreme Absolute Truth was lying to His mother.

When Nanda Mahārāja would come in and asked what was happening, Kṛṣṇa would turn to him and say, “Mother is punishing Me for something I didn’t do!”

Nanda Mahārāja would then begin chastising mother Yaśodā, “For taking sides with the gopīs, you should be punished. Why are you punishing Kṛṣṇa? Look at my Kṛṣṇa. He is so innocent. He could not have possibly done all these things they are accusing Him of!”

Kṛṣṇa would then climb up on Nanda Mahārāja’s lap, throw His arms around him and embrace him. Nanda Mahārāja would then say to mother Yaśodā, “See? You are in hot water!” Kṛṣṇa is such an instigator. Such is His līlā and how He impacts His presence in everybody’s mind so that they think about Him.

When Kṛṣṇa is covered over by the prema of His devotees, He forgets His divinity. Thus, He was so absorbed in mother Yaśodā’s mood that He actually began crying out of fear of her stick when she was chasing Him. While reciting the prayers of Queen Kuntī, Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura explains that Kuntī was totally bewildered when she saw Kṛṣṇa crying. Kuntīdevī has aiśvarya-jñāna—knowledge of Kṛṣṇa’s divinity and His majestic features. If Kṛṣṇa was pretending to cry, she would not be bewildered, because it would all make perfect sense that He was doing so to give pleasure to mother Yaśodā. However, Kuntī’s bewilderment is due to the fact that Kṛṣṇa was not pretending. He was genuinely afraid and crying out of fear.

Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura compares this to the bee that enters into the lotus flower. The petals of the lotus flower cover it and keep it trapped inside all night long. However, the bee is not at all disturbed, because there is so much nectar inside that lotus flower, and it is perfectly happy to be trapped there. Similarly, Kṛṣṇa is perfectly happy to be trapped and covered in the hearts of His devotees, because there is so much nectar for Him to relish.

One may ask, if Kṛṣṇa is covered, then how would He let Yaśodā bind Him? He must have been conscious of what was going on, as He let her bind Him to the wooden grinding mortar after her many attempts. Mother Yaśodā got all the ropes out of the house and tied them end to end, but the rope was always two inches too short to bind Kṛṣṇa.

The other elderly gopīs were standing around watching and laughing, enjoying this little treat. They said to Yaśodā, “This morning you just tied that belt around Kṛṣṇa’s waist so perfectly, and now you can’t even tie a rope?” Even after using all the ropes from the whole village, still Yaśodā could not tie Him.

Kṛṣṇa’s internal potencies act according to His will. When mother Yaśodā was attempting to bind Him, He was thinking, “I don’t want to be bound now. I still have many things that I want to do. I want to steal yogurt and I want to play with My friends.” Because that was His desire, two potencies manifested in His body: vibhūti-śakti—the power which displays the Lord’s opulence, and satya saṅkalpa śakti—the power that fulfills each and every desire of the Lord.

Due to His desire to not be tied, and due to these potencies, mother Yaśodā could not tie the rope. However, Kṛṣṇa is finally bound by the ropes of love of Yaśodā. Yogamāyā makes all the arrangements for Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. She creates the perfect facilities to fulfill His desires, and the desires of His devotees. She knew that it was Kṛṣṇa’s desire to be bound by love, and thus she facilitated Yaśodā’s inability to bind Kṛṣṇa with rope.

Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura describes that Kṛṣṇa and His pastimes in Vṛndāvana are predominantly mugdha, or bewildering. Sometimes, however, He is all-knowing, or He displays His majestic features in Vṛndāvana to protect His devotees. His behavior can appear to be contradictory. However, it is reconciled by the Lord’s quality of bhakta-vātsalya, and the nature of His kṛpā-śakti, mercy potency, upon the devotees. By understanding this quality of the Lord, and ultimately understanding the absolute nature of the Lord, we can transcend any apparent contradictions that we may think exist in His character. That absolute nature of the Lord is that He becomes completely subservient to the desires of His devotees. He even appears to risk His own reputation for the sake of His devotee.

Devotees worship the Lord because of this most attractive quality of Kṛṣṇa. Even though He is God, and supreme controller, proprietor and enjoyer, He completely renounces that position to satisfy the innermost desires present within the core of the hearts of His devotees. Therefore, we can glorify Kṛṣṇa in this way.

Of course, we may glorify the Lord for manifesting these qualities, but we should know that we can never imitate the Lord. He says that those who try to imitate Him are bringing upon their destruction. By hearing these pastimes of the Lord, we should also never think that we can place ourselves in that līlā, without qualification, just as one cannot enter the spiritual world without the proper qualification. One cannot imitate those who take part in the Lord’s pastimes, without the proper qualification. Hearing about these pastimes is simply meant to awaken within our hearts the desire to become qualified. That desire to become qualified is increasingly enhanced by continuous hearing.

Our qualification also depends upon bhakta-niṣṭhā. Niṣṭhā is very firm faith. Its symptom is the desire of the devotee to tirelessly endeavor to serve and to worship the Lord, even to the point of total fatigue, as was manifested by mother Yaśodā in her attempt to bind the Lord.

Sva-niṣṭhā, on the other hand, is the steady quality in Kṛṣṇa, which brings forth His kṛpā (mercy), when He sees that His devotee is making great endeavor, even to the point of fatigue, to selflessly serve Him. By mother Yaśodā’s love, the two qualities or bhakta-niṣṭhā and sva-niṣṭhā manifested, causing the two potencies of the Lord of satya-saṅkalpa-śakti and vibhūti-śakti to disappear. Thus, bhakta-niṣṭhā and sva-niṣṭhā filled in the two inches that were missing from the end of the rope of mother Yaśodā, and which allowed her to bind Kṛṣṇa. Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura explains that whenever there is competition between the devotee and the Lord, the determination of the devotee always prevails. Such is the power of the Lord’s devotee.

In the second verse of Dāmodarāṣṭaka, Satyavrata Muni says:

“Seeing the whipping stick in His mother’s hand, He is crying and rubbing His eyes again and again with His two lotus hands. His eyes are filled with fear, and the necklace of pearls around His neck, which is marked with three lines like a conch-shell, is shaking because of His quick breathing due to crying. To this Supreme Lord, Śrī Dāmodara, whose belly is bound not with ropes but with His mother’s pure love, I offer my humble obeisances.” (Śrī Dāmodarāṣṭaka, Verse 2)

Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura explains that when a thief is punished by the Lord, he is forced to cry. Similarly, Kṛṣṇa, who is a thief and is being punished by His mother, is being forced to cry. This can only be understood by a devotee. God is feared by fear-personified. Of course, false gods may wish to challenge Kṛṣṇa, thinking they have no cause for fear. However, they are always proven unsuccessful, because Kṛṣṇa cannot be defeated by anything but His devotee’s love. It makes the Lord a plaything in the hands of His devotee. Just as a child has complete control over the plaything in his hands, the devotee has complete control over the Lord. Of course, the devotee’s control over the Lord is never based upon the desire to control the Lord. Rather, a devotee who controls the Lord has no conception whatsoever of Kṛṣṇa being the Lord.

Sometimes foolish people may try to approach the Lord and force Him to reciprocate in a particular way. However, the Lord is not willing to become a plaything in their hands. He only becomes subdued by unalloyed love. This is explained in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam:

*nāyaṁ sukhāpo bhagavān*  
*dehināṁ gopikā-sutaḥ*  
*jñānināṁ cātma-bhūtānāṁ*  
*yathā bhaktimatām iha*

**The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, the son of mother Yaśodā, is accessible to devotees engaged in spontaneous loving service, but He is not as easily accessible to mental speculators, to those striving for self-realization by severe austerities and penances, or to those who consider the body the same as the self. (Bhāg. 10.9.21)**

Thus, Kṛṣṇa is accessible to those who are engaged in spontaneous devotional service and who have no conception of the Lord’s divinity. We cannot imitate this consciousness. We should never think that we are qualified to chastise the Lord or to control Him. Such mentality brings about ruination. The qualification for entering into that role is bhakta-niṣṭhā—firm determination to serve and worship the Lord tirelessly, so much so that the kṛpā-śakti, the mercy, comes and lifts us up.

We cannot force our entry into Kṛṣṇa’s līlā. One is an intruder if he attempts to do so and will be punished. We must simply become so determined to selflessly and tirelessly serve the Lord that the kṛpā-śakti of the Lord and His devotee will bring us up. We should always think ourselves unqualified to enter.

We see in the example of Sudāmā Brāhmaṇa and Śuklāmbara that they were thinking themselves unqualified to serve the Lord. However, the Lord accepts the personal service of His devotees, even though the devotee feels himself unqualified. Feeling oneself unqualified and totally dependent on mercy, a devotee can advance.

Satyavrata Muni continues with the third verse of the Dāmodarāṣṭaka prayers:

“By such childhood pastimes as this He is drowning the inhabitants of Gokula in pools of ecstasy, and is revealing to those devotees who are absorbed in knowledge of His supreme majesty and opulence that He is only conquered by devotees whose pure love is imbued with intimacy and is free from all conceptions of awe and reverence. With great love I again offer my obeisances to Lord Dāmodara hundreds and hundreds of times.” (Śrī Dāmodarāṣṭaka, Verse 3)

There is a verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, which illustrates further this particular point:

*darśayaṁs tad-vidāṁ loka*  
*ātmano bhṛtya-vaśyatām*  
*vrajasyovāha vai harṣaṁ*  
*bhagavān bāla-ceṣṭitaiḥ*

**To pure devotees throughout the world who could understand His activities, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, exhibited how much He can be subdued by His devotees, His servants. In this way He increased the pleasure of the Vrajavāsīs by His childhood activities. (Bhāg. 10.11.9)**

Commentary by Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura:

Not only Kṛṣṇa’s relatives, but all the Vrajavāsīs enjoyed unlimited bliss from His childhood pastimes, wherein He allowed Himself to come under their control. Kṛṣṇa showed this aspect of Himself, being controlled by His devotee’s love directly, to those external devotees like Lord Brahmā or Lord Śiva, who were captivated by Kṛṣṇa’s potency of majestic opulence, because He cannot be understood merely by explanations.

Satyavrata Muni describes in the third verse of the Dāmodarāṣṭaka prayers how the residents of Gokula were drowning in pools of ecstasy by the childhood pastimes of Kṛṣṇa, such as the dāmodara-līlā. Kṛṣṇa only reveals such pastimes to those devotees whose pure love is imbued with intimacy and is free from all conceptions of awe and reverence. As Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura explained in the commentary, sometimes it is not sufficient to simply hear, but one has to see for themselves. The devotees like Brahmā and Śiva were described as external devotees, because they were captivated by Kṛṣṇa’s potency of opulence. Therefore, Kṛṣṇa shows this aspect of Himself—being controlled by His devotees. He cannot be understood simply by explanations.

Ultimately, a devotee’s heart has to be completely pure, and furthermore, the desire within the heart has to be awakened for such intimate relationships with Kṛṣṇa. Until those desires awaken within the heart, explanations by themselves will not fully reveal the nature of these pastimes. Sometimes when we hear such wonderful pastimes, we catch glimpses of how wonderful Kṛṣṇa and the spiritual world are. It stimulates our mind, and it awakens greed and attraction within our heart. However, our consciousness does not stay there, as our heart is not yet fully cleansed.

Hearing is meant to awaken that attraction, which then brings about the desire to hear more. Then the distinction between that consciousness and forgetting about all those pastimes becomes more pronounced. We go back to our routine consciousness, and we forget that there is a whole transcendental world that has no connection whatsoever to this material world, and that we are meant to be part of that.

We have duties to perform in relationship to this world. However, the attachment is what is still binding us to this world. Therefore, attachment has to be reverted back to our original attachment. The more we hear about Kṛṣṇa’s eternal pastimes with His devotees, the more it awakens the original attachment within the heart. If someone has been awakened, then it obviously means that he was sleeping. However, sleeping is not the natural state of the soul. The natural state of the soul is to be awake in Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

**Question: When mother Yaśodā was having difficulty tying Kṛṣṇa with rope, did it not cross her mind that maybe Kṛṣṇa is God? Or did Kṛṣṇa forget that He was God?**

Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura describes that Kṛṣṇa is so inconceivable that He can simultaneously forget that He is God and be fully conscious of everything. He forgets His divinity in the presence of His devotee. What then of those devotees who are worshipping Kṛṣṇa in that same affection throughout the entire creation? Kṛṣṇa has to be able to hear them and be aware of them when they are worshipping Him in that way. Therefore, in the presence of His eternal associates in the spiritual world, He becomes covered and actually forgets His divinity.

When Kṛṣṇa first jumped off the grinding mortar, He started rubbing His eyes and started feigning fear. However, when mother Yaśodā came after Him with a stick and was getting closer, real tears started flowing from His eyes. He was genuinely afraid. How could she think that He is God? Thus, although He was genuinely afraid, He was always conscious of His devotees throughout the entire creation. He reciprocates with their prayers in relation to the way that they approach Him. Therefore, He is simultaneously bewildered and all cognizant.

Similarly, when mother Yaśodā looked in Kṛṣṇa’s mouth to see the dirt He had eaten, she was stunned for a moment by His divinity, seeing the entire creation in His mouth, but she was immediately covered over. She had started wondering if He was some kind of powerful demigod. For the devotees who have ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa, their spiritual emotions are continuously manifesting. Such is the nature of prema that it is not devoid of emotion.

Emotions that we experience in this world are perverted reflections of transcendental emotions, which are manifested in the transcendental realm of Goloka by the residents in relation to their love with Kṛṣṇa. Their emotions are continuously manifesting in different types of ecstatic feelings they have, such as anubhāva, or they begin to experience sāttvika-bhāva, in which the body begins to tremble and perspiration comes with emotions of love of God.

The analogy is given that if you put a blade of grass in a pot of milk that is continuously boiling, then sometimes the blade of grass will come to the surface. However, because the milk is continuously boiling, you will no longer see the blade of grass on the top. Similarly, sometimes when these devotees are experiencing these emotions for Kṛṣṇa, they remember His divinity for a moment, but it does not last. An example of this is when Yaśodā and Nanda Mahārāja had heard from Gargamuni at the name-giving ceremony of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma that Kṛṣṇa is not an ordinary child, but rather as good as Nārāyaṇa. Therefore, for a moment they are aware of His divinity, but their emotions come to a rolling boil.

Thus, mother Yaśodā never questions Kṛṣṇa’s amazing activities. Rather, she simply thinks that her son’s activities are very wonderful.

**Question: What are the scriptural injunctions relating to how hard it is to enter into the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa?**

One example from Bhagavad-gītā is where Kṛṣṇa says that is very difficult to overcome māyā, but one who surrenders unto Him can easily overcome it. Our means of surrender, especially in this age, is surrendering our ears and our tongue. The Lord is so merciful that He has come in this age to distribute vraja-prema. He has made Himself and the service to Him accessible through chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, by personally manifesting Himself in His name. The Lord has made Himself very easily accessible in the Age of Kali, which under normal circumstances is very difficult to obtain, through the process of chanting. Whereas, in Satya-yuga it was achieved by performances of great austerities; in Tretā-yuga by great fire sacrifices; and in Dvāpara-yuga by very elaborate Deity worship. Thus chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa is described as an easy process. It only becomes difficult if one is not careful in his chanting, as he will commit offenses. Because of offenses to the holy name, one loses his taste. However, the holy name is the most merciful manifestation of the Lord, and is thus so accessible. Anyone who has a tongue can chant Kṛṣṇa’s name, but it requires some faith. If we want to make it easier for ourselves to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa, then we will keep ourselves in the association of devotees who have faith. However, if we want to make it more difficult for ourselves, then we will surround ourselves with persons who have no faith. To the degree that we become attached to the association of devotees, to that degree our faith in Kṛṣṇa and His name will increase. That is the prescription which is given for this Age of Kali to make it easier.

## Govardhana-pūjā

Kṛṣṇa established the Govardhana-pūjā celebration Himself. He said, “This Govardhana Hill, assuming any form He wishes, will kill any residents of the forest who neglects Him. Therefore let us pay our obeisances to Him for the safety of ourselves and our cows.”

In Bhagavad-gītā, the Lord says:

*yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas*  
*tat tad evetaro janaḥ*  
*sa yat pramāṇaṁ kurute*  
*lokas tad anuvartate*

**Whatever action a great man performs, common men follow. And whatever standards he sets by exemplary acts, all the world pursues. (Bg. 3.21)**

Kṛṣṇa also states that even He, Himself, performs prescribed duties, because if He did not and if everyone followed His example, the whole world would be put to ruination. Certainly Kṛṣṇa is the best person to establish the standards we need to follow. On the other hand, there are some things that Kṛṣṇa does that we cannot imitate. Sometimes people distort this, thinking that they can do whatever Kṛṣṇa does, such as enjoying in the forest in the dead of night with married women. However, the Bhāgavatam states that we have to be very careful about imitating. We cannot imitate what great personalities do. Rather, we should follow in their footsteps, and especially follow their instructions.

The example is given that even the demigods who are great controllers can perform great activities, such as Lord Śiva, who, after the poisonous ocean was churned, drank a whole ocean of poison and held it in his throat. However, He performed this activity to protect people in general. Another name for Lord Śiva is Nīlakaṇṭha, because He held this whole ocean in His throat. However, we cannot imitate Lord Śiva and drink a whole ocean of poison. We cannot even imitate him by drinking even a drop of poison. Similarly, we cannot imitate Kṛṣṇa’s activities and think that by so doing, we ourselves are following His instructions. There is a big difference between imitation and following the instructions.

However, it is clear that Kṛṣṇa did establish the worship of Govardhana Hill, and specifically the festival of Govardhana-pūjā, and He intended for it to continue. This is established in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam:

*śrī-śuka uvāca*  
*vaco niśamya nandasya*  
*tathānyeṣāṁ vrajaukasām*  
*indrāya manyuṁ janayan*  
*pitaraṁ prāha keśavaḥ*

**Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: When Lord Keśava \[Kṛṣṇa\] heard the statements of His father, Nanda, and other senior residents of Vraja, He addressed His father as follows, to arouse anger in Lord Indra. (Bhāg. 10.24.12)**

PURPORT

Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī explains that Lord Kṛṣṇa’s intention was not simply to insult a demigod, but rather to knock down the great mountain of false pride that had arisen within the Lord’s tiny servant, who was supposed to represent the Lord as Indra. By lifting Govardhana Hill Lord Kṛṣṇa would thus initiate a blissful annual festival called Govardhana-pūjā, and He would further enjoy the pleasant pastime of dwelling for several days beneath the hill with all His loving devotees.

Thus, Kṛṣṇa’s intention in lifting Govardhana Hill was to initiate this blissful annual festival called Govardhana-pūjā. Of course, lifting Govardhana Hill to protect His devotees is one of the events which led to the observation of this festival. Furthermore, Lord Kṛṣṇa personally established the Annakūṭa, or the offering of a very large variety of foodstuffs for the worship of Govardhana Hill. He requested all the residents of Vṛndāvana-dhāma to bring unlimited quantities of ghee, vegetables, milk preparations, sweets, cakes, and sweet rice. He requested that all the ingredients that were normally used in sacrifice for worship of Lord Indra be instead used to worship Govardhana Hill. Kṛṣṇa arranged for hundreds of brāhmaṇas to provide so many varieties of preparations to offer in sacrifice for the pleasure of Govardhana Hill.

After the Annakūṭa ceremony was performed, Kṛṣṇa assumed a very wonderful, magnificent form, residing on top of Govardhana Hill. In that form, while all the residents of Vṛndāvana were looking at Govardhana Hill when they were making their offering, Kṛṣṇa was drawing their attention, saying, “Just see how this hill has assumed a very wonderful, magnificent form and how He is accepting your offering.” Kṛṣṇa then assumed the form of Govardhana Hill. One could see on Govardhana Hill Kṛṣṇa’s mouth, and His arms reaching out to accept all the offerings that were being given to Him. He was eating everything that was being offered to Him, saying, “Āniyora! Āniyora!—Give Me more! Give Me more!”

The place where the Govardhana-pūjā sacrifice was performed by Kṛṣṇa is called Annakūṭa-kṣetra. Many years later, Mādhavendra Purī also established a very large Annakūṭa at the same place, by offering mountains of prasādam for the pleasure of Govardhana, and for Lord Gopāla whose worship Mādhavendra Purī established on the top of Govardhana Hill. This place is called Gopāla-prakaṭa-sthali, which is where the Gopāla Deity was discovered by Mādhavendra Purī. It is a little bit off the Govardhana parikramā-marga. It is a place that is not very commonly visited within the village of Āniyora—where Kṛṣṇa requested more and more offerings, not being fully satisfied.

Of course Kṛṣṇa is satisfied even with a leaf, flower, fruit, or water when it is offered with love and devotion. It is not necessary to offer unlimited quantities of foodstuffs to satisfy the Lord. One can satisfy the Lord even with a very small, simple offering, and the Lord will be very eager to accept it.

For example, Sanātana Gosvāmī would offer capātīs to his Deity of Kṛṣṇa, even though he could not prepare them properly. Nonetheless, even though he would just offer the dry capātīs, the Lord would accept them. Similarly, when Sudāmā offered the few grains of broken rice, the Lord was so eager to accept them from his hands. Thus, to satisfy the Lord does not necessarily require that we make huge unlimited varieties and mountains of preparations.

However, during this particular event of Govardhana-pūjā, the Lord established that there should be very large quantities of food prepared and distributed to everyone—not only to the brāhmaṇas, the residents of the dhāma, and to all the local people, but even to the animals. Similarly, we can also serve and satisfy the Lord by making hundreds of preparations to be offered for the pleasure of the Lord on this day.

The perfection of any service that is rendered is that the Lord is satisfied. If one does not have the facility or is physically incapable of doing something very great, the Lord will accept even something very small.

For example, Sanātana Gosvāmī used to circumambulate Govardhana Hill as part of his daily worship. He would not take the parikramā-marga that we normally take, which is about twenty-two kilometers. Rather, he would take the long way around, about forty kilometers, every single day as part of his daily worship of Girirāja. He was getting so old and it was very difficult for him to do it, yet he still did it.

One day, a young boy came to Sanātana Gosvāmī and said, “You are getting very old now. Why are you doing this long parikramā every day? It is too difficult for somebody of your age to walk such a long distance every day to worship Govardhana Hill.” Although Sanātana Gosvāmī was still very inclined to continue, this boy was resistant and said, “No, you should not do it.”

The boy therefore went to Govardhana Hill and took a stone from there that had the impression of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, and brought it back to Sanātana Gosvāmī. The boy said, “You should take this stone, and instead of circumambulating Govardhana Hill like you are doing every day, walking forty kilometers, simply circumambulate this stone, and it will be as good as circumambulating Govardhana Hill.”

Sanātana Gosvāmī later realized that that young boy was none other than Kṛṣṇa Himself who had personally come to request him to minimize the strenuous parikramā he was doing every day. Thus, from that day on, Sanātana Gosvāmī would simply circumambulate the stone, and it was as good as doing his forty kilometer parikramā. This is an example of how the Lord is very much inclined to accept the offering of the worshipper according to his capacity and his ability to do so. Kṛṣṇa is known as bhāva-grāhī janārdana—accepting the essence of the devotee’s attitude in his offering. The Lord is not inclined to accept the offering of somebody who does not have the intention to please Him.

The Supreme Personality of Godhead becomes very dear to those devotees who have no material possessions but are fully happy in possessing the devotional service of the Lord. Indeed, the Lord relishes the devotional activities of such devotees. Those who are puffed up with material education, wealth, aristocracy and fruitive activity are very proud of possessing material things, and they often deride the devotees. Even if such people offer the Lord worship, the Lord never accepts them. (Bhāg. 4.31.21)

When Kṛṣṇa says, “If one offers me a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water, I am inclined to accept it,” it is not those actual items that are attractive to Him. Rather, it is the devotion that is attractive to the Lord. It is the quality of the offering which pleases the Lord; not the quantity.

However, the exception is that on Govardhana-pūjā, Kṛṣṇa wants a lot of prasādam prepared and distributed. Thus, if we want to please the Lord during Govardhana-pūjā, who has set the precedent Himself, we should do this. Not only did He arrange for the large quantities of preparations to be made personally, He assumed the form of the hill to accept them, requesting, “Āniyora! Āniyora!” Kṛṣṇa has established that this blissful festival should be performed annually, and that we should all observe it to satisfy Him by bringing quantities of foodstuffs that can be offered for His pleasure, and by following in the footsteps of our previous ācāryas by circumambulating Govardhana Hill which He, Himself, will assume.

## Vyāsa-pūjā

I was reflecting on the debt I have towards all of you who are offering words of appreciation, offering your service, and, of course, your hearts. Moreover that debt is always increasing. Sometimes I find it overwhelming because I cannot properly reciprocate. I feel in debt to all the devotees for everything they are offering to me. However I am also becoming increasingly aware that the offerings are not meant for me. I am not supposed to accept them for myself. Moreover, I should not be like a person who accepts some appreciation or affection and then reciprocates that affection with a mercantile mentality, which means reciprocating affection with the expectation of getting something in return. Kṛṣṇa clearly states that that is not love, and that one who has that mentality is actually selfish, thinking only of his own interests.

Still, sometimes I find it overwhelming. How do I reciprocate that affection and at the same time liquidate the debt I have? Even if I can somehow liquidate the debt, it seems that I am always accumulating more. The only way that I can come close to liquidating the debt is to fully realize that nothing is being offered to me. For your benefit, I have to pass it on. Otherwise, what benefit is there for you to worship me, to serve me, and to offer words of glorification to me? If I do not pass it on, how will you benefit?

I have to accept that position for all of you who offer your affection in this way. I may be able to temporarily liquidate that debt today by passing your offerings to Śrīla Prabhupāda—someone who is obviously very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa. All of you then get the benefit of giving affection, your service, and your hearts in serving Śrīla Prabhupāda and his mission.

The demigods offer an inspiring prayer to Lord Kṛṣṇa:

**“O Lord, who resemble the shining sun, You are always ready to fulfill the desire of Your devotee, and therefore You are known as a desire tree \[vāñchā-kalpataru\]. When ācāryas completely take shelter under Your lotus feet in order to cross the fierce ocean of nescience, they leave behind on earth the method by which they cross, and because You are very merciful to Your other devotees, You accept this method to help them.” (Bhāg. 10.2.31)**

This is a very wonderful verse. It explains that the Lord is very much inclined to satisfy the desires of His devotees, and therefore He is just like a desire tree. Śrīla Prabhupāda, the great ācārya who has fully taken shelter under the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, crossed this fierce ocean of material existence and the Lord satisfied his desire by accepting the method by which he crossed.

Prabhupāda crossed the ocean of material existence and went back to the spiritual world. However, he left behind, for our benefit, the method by which he crossed, and which was accepted by the Lord. In one lecture, Prabhupāda explained how the six Gosvāmīs and the previous ācāryas were always absorbed in chanting the names of Kṛṣṇa. Thus, they were absorbed in chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa just as we are absorbed in chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa. Therefore what we are doing right now is authorized by our previous ācāryas.

Prabhupāda further explains in his purport to Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 10.2.31:

This statement reveals how the merciful ācāryas and the merciful Supreme Personality of Godhead together help the serious devotee who wants to return home, back to Godhead. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, in His teachings to Rūpa Gosvāmī, said:

*brahmāṇḍa bhramite kona bhāgyavān jīva*  
*guru-kṛṣṇa-prasāde pāya bhakti-latā-bīja*

(Cc. Madhya 19.151)

One can achieve the seed of bhakti-latā, devotional service, by the mercy of guru and Kṛṣṇa. The duty of the guru is to find the means, according to the time, the circumstances and the candidate, by which one can be induced to render devotional service, which Kṛṣṇa accepts from a candidate who wants to be successful in going back home, back to Godhead.

Prabhupāda explains here that Kṛṣṇa accepts that method for the benefit of the candidate. The ācārya finds the means according to the time, place and circumstance by which others can be induced to render devotional service to Kṛṣṇa, and Kṛṣṇa accepts that from the candidate for devotional service.

After wandering throughout the universe, a fortunate person within this material world seeks shelter of such a guru, or ācārya, who trains the devotee in the suitable ways to render service according to the circumstances so that the Supreme Personality of Godhead will accept the service. This makes it easier for the candidate to reach the ultimate destination. (Bhāg. 10.2.31, purport)

Kṛṣṇa says:

*daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī*  
*mama māyā duratyayā*  
*mām eva ye prapadyante*  
*māyām etāṁ taranti te*

**“This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross beyond it.” (Bg. 7.14)**

The perfection of all activities is fulfilled when the Lord is ultimately satisfied by them.

*ataḥ pumbhir dvija-śreṣṭhā*  
*varṇāśrama-vibhāgaśaḥ*  
*svanuṣṭhitasya dharmasya*  
*saṁsiddhir hari-toṣaṇam*

**O best among the twice-born, it is therefore concluded that the highest perfection one can achieve by discharging the duties prescribed for one’s own occupation according to caste divisions and orders of life is to please the Personality of Godhead. (Bhāg. 1.2.13)**

Prabhupāda is the perfect ācārya who knew how to apply the siddhānta of the scriptures according to time place and circumstance, and how to apply them in such a way so that his followers could perfect their lives, cross the ocean of material existence and go back to Godhead. We do not have to manufacture anything new. If we strictly follow in the footsteps of the previous ācāryas, and try to serve them and satisfy them, then we can cross over this ocean of material existence.

Therefore, the best way I can liquidate the debt of service, affection and love is to offer it to Śrīla Prabhupāda. If Prabhupāda is pleased by your service, then certainly you will be following that method that he has left behind for you to cross this ocean of material existence. He has come to make the process of surrender easy.

At every moment my debt continues to accumulate. I am a fool to think I can pay it back. I must never forget to whom it is supposed to be offered. If I do, not only will I suffer, but you will not benefit. The whole purpose of the offering is to see that it gets to Śrīla Prabhupāda’s lotus feet. Kṛṣṇa accepted his method because he has already demonstrated that he has crossed this ocean of material existence, and he so mercifully left behind that method for us.

The ācārya’s duty, therefore, is to find the means by which devotees may render service according to references from śāstra. Rūpa Gosvāmī, for example, in order to help subsequent devotees, published such devotional books as Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu. Thus it is the duty of the ācārya to publish books that will help future candidates take up the method of service and become eligible to return home, back to Godhead, by the mercy of the Lord. In our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, this same path is being prescribed and followed. (Bhāg. 10.2.31, purport)

Prabhupāda left behind books, and the chanting of the holy names of the Lord. Śrīla Prabhupāda wrote in his concluding words in Caitanya-caritāmṛta, “I think that His Divine Grace Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura is always seeing my activities and guiding me within my heart by his words.” He then quotes the first verse of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam: tene brahma hṛdā ya ādi-kavaye. Just as Lord Kṛṣṇa impregnated all the Vedic wisdom from within the heart of Lord Brahma, in the same way Śrīla Prabhupāda was describing how he felt his spiritual master was guiding his activities in his translation work of Caitanya-caritāmṛta and Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

Śrīla Prabhupāda left behind his books for the benefit of future generations to learn the process of devotional service, as well as the means for expanding this same method for the benefit of others, by distributing those books. He says:

Thus the devotees have been advised to refrain from four sinful activities—illicit sex, intoxication, meat-eating and gambling—and to chant sixteen rounds a day. These are bona fide instructions. Because in the Western countries constant chanting is not possible, one should not artificially imitate Haridāsa Ṭhākura, but should follow this method. Kṛṣṇa will accept a devotee who strictly follows the regulative principles and the method prescribed in the various books and literatures published by the authorities. The ācārya gives the suitable method for crossing the ocean of nescience by accepting the boat of the Lord’s lotus feet, and if this method is strictly followed, the followers will ultimately reach the destination, by the grace of the Lord. This method is called ācārya-sampradāya. It is therefore said, sampradāya-vihīnā ye mantrās te niṣphalā matāḥ (Padma Purāṇa). The ācārya-sampradāya is strictly bona fide. Therefore one must accept the ācārya-sampradāya; otherwise one’s endeavor will be futile. Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura therefore sings:

*tāṅdera caraṇa sevi bhakta sane vāsa*  
*janame janame haya, ei abhilāṣa*

One must worship the lotus feet of the ācārya and live within the society of devotees. Then one’s endeavor to cross over nescience will surely be successful.

(Bhāg. 10.2.31, purport)

I thought that by sharing this verse and speaking from Śrīla Prabhupāda’s commentary, it would be a relevant way to, at least on this day of Vyāsa-pūjā, liquidate some of the debt that I have accumulated, by offering everything to the lotus feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda and by describing the method that he has left for us to cross this ocean of material existence.

I pray that all of you can increase your endeavors to follow this method that Śrīla Prabhupāda has given to us. This will be very pleasing to Śrīla Prabhupāda and our previous ācāryas, and ultimately it will very much satisfy the Lord, which is the perfection of everything we do. Śrīla Prabhupāda wrote:

Your strong desire to serve me is very beautiful; your serving me means serving Krsna. I am also your servant, so I cannot accept your service from you or from any of my disciples. I accept service from my disciples on behalf of Krsna. Just like a tax collector must collect for the treasury, not for himself. If he himself touches so much as a farthing it would be unlawful. So I have no right to accept service from any disciple, but on behalf of Krsna I can accept. Sincere service to the spiritual master is service to the Supreme Lord. As stated in the prayer, yasya prasadad bhagavat-prasado. Because Krsna accepts service through the via media of spiritual master, pleasing the spiritual master is equal to pleasing the Supreme Lord. (Śrīla Prabhupāda letter, February 13, 1968)

## Initiation

During the initiation ceremony, homa (fire sacrifice) is performed to invoke auspiciousness. The Vedic sacrifices require that we perform fire sacrifice where we may offer various ingredients into the sacrificial fire as an offering to the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu. As prescribed in the Vedic literatures, when all sacrifices are performed, they are ultimately meant for the satisfaction of the Supreme Lord. In previous ages, very elaborate fire sacrifices were performed, and the ingredients offered into the sacrificial fire were the fruits of one’s labor. The sacrificial fire is considered to be like the consuming agent or mouth of the Supreme Lord. It is one of the means by which the Supreme Lord accepts all offerings of sacrifice. Thus, various fruits, vegetables, spices and grains, which are considered to be the fruit of labor or the necessities of life, are offered into the sacrificial fire.

For various Vedic ceremonies, there are various mantras that are chanted, and for each activity, there is a mantra that accompanies it. These mantras invoke auspiciousness. There are also various decorations in the sacrificial arena, which represent certain deities who are requested to come. At the time of placing the decorations, the presence of these deities is invoked by the chanting of various mantras. Thus, both the chanting of Vedic mantras and the performance of offerings to the sacrificial fire is meant to create an auspicious atmosphere for any event. Often, such sacrifices are performed for various events in one’s life, and these are called saṁskāras, or purificatory activities, and are meant for personal purification and simultaneously qualification for associating with the Supreme Lord.

Just as we chant Vedic hymns to invoke auspiciousness, it is also understood that the chanting of the holy names of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra is the recommended sacrifice for satisfying the Lord in this age. If the Lord is pleased by the performance of sacrifice, then He can bestow everything necessary for one to live happily in this world, and ultimately to fulfill the ultimate purpose of human life, which is to realize our eternal relationship with the Supreme Being.

The object of the sacrifice performed during the initiation ceremony—both through chanting and the sacrificial fire—is none other than the Supreme Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is described as the original primeval person and the original cause of all causes.

*īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ*  
*sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ*  
*anādir ādir govindaḥ*  
*sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam*

**Kṛṣṇa who is known as Govinda is the Supreme Godhead. He has an eternal blissful spiritual body. He is the origin of all. He has no other origin and He is the prime cause of all causes. (Brahma Samhita 5.1)**

For anyone who has goals they want to obtain or achieve in life, it requires great endeavor. It is not something that is very easily obtained. If a person wants to become very wealthy, or wants to become very intelligent, it requires great endeavor. Even if it appears that such persons do not perform such great endeavors in this life to achieve some goal, it is understood that in a previous life, those austerities were performed, and therefore, he was able to obtain the goal in this life.

Similarly, in Vedic culture, when a person wishes to ultimately achieve his eternal relationship with the Supreme Lord and to satisfy Him, then he has to make some commitment. Initiation is a form of commitment. To the degree that we make some personal commitment internally, to that degree we can expect that we can make progress towards obtaining our goal. When one makes a commitment to satisfy the Supreme Lord, He helps in His most personal feature.

*yoginām api sarveṣāṁ*  
*mad-gatenāntar-ātmanā*  
*śraddhāvān bhajate yo māṁ*  
*sa me yuktatamo mataḥ*

**“And of all yogīs, the one with great faith who always abides in Me, thinks of Me within himself, and renders transcendental loving service to Me—he is the most intimately united with Me in yoga and is the highest of all. That is My opinion.” (Bg. 6.47)**

Kṛṣṇa is the goal of life for a devotee. The means for achieving that goal in this Age of Kali is through the chanting of the holy names of the Lord. The commitment that the initiate makes at the time of initiation is to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa, and accept the name of the Lord and make it the foundation of his life.

Kṛṣṇa is eternal. He is beginningless and has no end. He is the Supreme Soul. All other living beings who are His parts and parcels are also eternal. Therefore the ultimate objective of life is for the living entity to know his relationship with God, and to please, serve and learn to love the Supreme Lord. One criterion of love is selflessness—wanting to please somebody without expecting anything in return. Furthermore, the basis of that love is with the understanding that we are all parts and parcels of God.

Just as Kṛṣṇa explains—if one sees the sun in the sky, then everything which was previously in darkness becomes revealed. Similarly, when one understands Kṛṣṇa, then everything that was previously unknown becomes known. When we understand our relationship with Kṛṣṇa and learn to love Kṛṣṇa, then we can also love everything that is connected with Him, which means all of His parts and parcels. Therefore, the fullest manifestation of love is realized when we understand our relationship with the Supreme Lord and how to please Him. This is recommended for this Age of Kali—the Age of Quarrel.

No one can dispute that the symptoms of Kali are very prominent, where slight provocation can invoke quarrel and fighting amongst individuals and nations. One of the symptoms of Kali-yuga is that people have many disturbances within the mind. Kaler doṣa-nidhe rājan (Bhāg. 12.3.51)—the Age of Kali is an ocean of all bad qualities. However, it has one good quality—kīrtanād eva kṛṣṇasya, mukta-saṅgaḥ paraṁ vrajet—if one chants these names of Kṛṣṇa, then he can achieve perfection of life, which is to please the Lord. He can become free from his conditioning of the material world and love everyone.

**“One who always sees all living entities as spiritual sparks, in quality one with the Lord, becomes a true knower of things. What, then, can be illusion or anxiety for him?” (Śrī Īśopaniṣad, Verse 7)**

The recommended means for establishing one’s relationship with the Supreme Lord and to serve Him in this age is to chant His names. Whereas sacrifices in previous ages were very difficult, sacrifices in this Age of Kali are not. Our austerity is to simply try to please the Supreme Lord by following the essential instructions, which are given by the spiritual master—the foundation of which is to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa. All other austerities are contained within this chanting. When one dedicates his life to chanting, he begins to realize more and more Kṛṣṇa’s presence within His name. The devotee begins to clear away the unwanted things within the heart, which are obstacles in the path of which he has chosen to obtain, which is His relationship with God. All these impediments are removed by the grace of the Supreme Lord Himself who is present in His name.

In Bhagavad-gītā (9.22), Kṛṣṇa says:

*ananyāś cintayanto māṁ*  
*ye janāḥ paryupāsate*  
*teṣāṁ nityābhiyuktānāṁ*  
*yoga-kṣemaṁ vahāmy aham*

**“But those who always worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on My transcendental form—to them I carry what they lack, and I preserve what they have.”**

Kṛṣṇa recognizes the commitment that is within one’s heart. After many years of studying the Vedic literatures, of chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, of associating with devotees, a person makes the decision within his heart to make a commitment and wants to make progress. He wants to show Kṛṣṇa that he is ready to dedicate more of himself to remembering the Lord, pleasing Him, and worshipping Him by chanting His holy names.

First initiation is actually that type of commitment. It is called harināma initiation, as the candidate is vowing to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa every day, and to follow the basic principles of spiritual life and of human life—to not take any meat, to not take intoxication, to not have illicit sexual connections, and to not gamble.

In spiritual life, one cannot make vows and follow them by his own efforts alone. However, if one satisfies the Lord by chanting His holy names, then He will help him, and the devotee will not be destroyed even if he falls down in the immature stage. There is no danger of his being unsuccessful, because Kṛṣṇa, being bhāva-grāhī, will always accept the attitude. He knows the attitude within the heart of the devotee, and He understands the intention even though the devotee may not be able to perform everything perfectly. In addition to being in everyone’s heart, the Lord is eternally situated in the spiritual world. Therefore, the help that is received for traversing this path to establish love for the Supreme Lord takes place both by the Lord from within the heart as the Supersoul and also through the help of the devotees of the Lord. It is stated (Cc. Antya, 1.2): “My path is very difficult. I am blind, and my feet are slipping again and again. Therefore, may the saints help me by granting me the stick of their mercy as my support.”

Thus, the purpose of initiation is to commit to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa every day of one’s life to please the Lord and to learn to love the Supreme Lord. For one who makes that his goal in life, everything else becomes part and parcel of that one objective. Śrīla Prabhupāda often said that spiritual life does not mean that we have to give everything up. Rather, we simply have to add one thing—Kṛṣṇa. Just as if you have so many zeroes and add them up, the sum equals zero. However, if you put one in front of all of your zeroes, each zero immediately becomes very significant. Thus, we must simply add Kṛṣṇa to everything else that we do in this life. The best means for adding Kṛṣṇa in this Age of Kali is by chanting His names.

*kali-kālera dharma—kṛṣṇa-nāma-saṅkīrtana*  
*kṛṣṇa-śakti vinā nahe tāra pravartana*

**The fundamental religious system in the Age of Kali is the chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. Unless empowered by Kṛṣṇa, one cannot propagate the saṅkīrtana movement. (Cc. Antya, 7.11)**

**Question: Does the spiritual master accept the karma of the disciple at the time of initiation, and then suffer because of the sinful behavior of his disciple?**

Certainly Prabhupāda indicated that that was the cause when he was very sick. In 1974, when Śrīla Prabhupāda was in India, we were having 24-hour kīrtana for Śrīla Prabhupāda who was very ill, and we were very fearful about his health and his possible departure. At that time, Prabhupāda stated that he was in that condition because his disciples were not strictly following. Therefore, Prabhupāda certainly made statements indicating that the sinful behavior of his disciples was one of the causes of his apparent physical suffering.

I do not want let my disciples off the hook by making the following statement, but I do not think that way about my health. By saying this, it does not mean that disciples do not have to worry about strictly following any longer. Having said that, I do not think that my health is as it is because my disciples are engaging in sinful activities, or because I have taken on so much karma. Rather, I consider my health in relationship to the following verse:

*tat te ’nukampāṁ su-samīkṣamāṇo*  
*bhuñjāna evātma-kṛtaṁ vipākam*  
*hṛd-vāg-vapurbhir vidadhan namas te*  
*jīveta yo mukti-pade sa dāya-bhāk*

**“My dear Lord, one who earnestly waits for You to bestow Your causeless mercy upon him, all the while patiently suffering the reactions of his past misdeeds and offering You respectful obeisances with his heart, words and body, is surely eligible for liberation, for it has become his rightful claim.” (Bhāg. 10.14.8)**

In this way, I think about my physical pain, health, and suffering as the result of my own past sinful activities. I have been conditioned to think in that way in terms of personal physical pain, suffering or poor health. However, the nature of another type of suffering is when I see devotees lose faith in chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa. That suffering is far more significant than any other kind of suffering that I may feel from the physical pain of the body. When I see devotees lose faith in chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa or giving up their vows or the association of devotees, then I think about how much I am responsible for helping them to develop their faith, and then I suffer like anything. Sometimes I think that Kṛṣṇa wants me to suffer like that so that I feel the weight of the responsibility I have to help devotees so they do not lose their faith in chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa— especially those devotees for whom I have personally taken responsibility to help develop their faith in chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa.

I think about my physical suffering simply in relationship to my own past activities. However, the mental suffering I experience when I see devotees lose their faith in chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa is my real form of suffering. That mental suffering is far worse for me than any physical suffering I may experience. Therefore, for any of my disciples who are concerned about my suffering, think about that mental suffering instead of the physical suffering.

**Question: What is the importance of maintaining the vow of chanting a minimum of sixteen rounds of Hare Kṛṣṇa every day?**

It is not a vow only for the rest of this life, but chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa is actually the eternal activity of the soul. Sometimes devotees say that they will chant sixteen rounds every day for the rest of their life. However, chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa is something that is always performed—kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ—even in a fully liberated state. If one wants to chant Hare Kṛṣṇa continuously, then he should also be in a proper state of consciousness.

It is stated in Caitanya-bhāgavata: “For one who never blasphemes anyone and who always chants the names of Kṛṣṇa-Kṛṣṇa, he will certainly conquer Lord Caitanya, although otherwise Lord Caitanya is very difficult to conquer.” Indeed all the scriptures declare that one should always offer all respects to anyone and everyone. If one blasphemes anyone—not only devotees—he will never be able to attain the lotus feet of the Lord.

Further, Lord Caitanya instructs in Śrī Śikṣāṣṭaka that we should develop this mentality of humility in order to achieve the state of kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ. If we blaspheme and criticize others, our minds and senses will become disturbed, and when this agitation appears, we lose our taste for chanting the holy name of the Lord.

Faith is required to make the vow for chanting the holy name. At the time of initiation, the disciple is pledging to not give up the chanting of the holy name of the Lord, and to strictly follow the vows that he is making before the spiritual master, the sacrificial fire, the deities, and all the assembled Vaiṣṇavas.

Sometimes out of weakness of heart (hṛdaya-daurbalyaṁ), devotees may slip and deviate in their practices of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. However, they should never blame others for their own deviations and weaknesses. If a person is honest and sincere in his heart, then he understands that it is due to his own weaknesses of heart. We have Kṛṣṇa’s holy name, Śrīla Prabhupāda’s example of his complete faith in the holy name of the Lord, and the association of Vaiṣṇavas who expand the glories of the holy name of the Lord for us to hear and increase our faith in chanting. All these facilities are accessible to everybody in the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. If one fully takes advantage of it, then there is no reason for any deviation in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. This is śraddhā—firm confident faith that chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa is the foundation of everything else that we do.

By taking initiation in this sampradāya, in the International Society for Krishna Consciousness, we are establishing our connection with this mission. Prabhupāda’s mission was for us to taste the holy name of the Lord ourselves and distribute it for the benefit of others. Such is the importance of chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, and that is the commitment the devotee makes when he accepts his vows at the time of initiation.

**Question: It is often very hard to get the personal time of many of the spiritual masters in ISKCON. Although we attend the programs, hear lectures, and see them, we do not get their personal time, nor do we have the specific material or spiritual qualification that will draw their attention. How then should we accept anyone in ISKCON as our spiritual master, if they cannot give us their personal time and attention?**

It is not a cheap thing for Kṛṣṇa to manifest Himself in our heart and to get a confirmation within our heart that the instructions of a particular spiritual master are the foundation for our faith in devotional service. Prabhupāda gave the analogy that we must first prepare the soil before the seed is planted. Thus, we have to do our work to prepare ourselves.

Certainly it is according to scriptural injunction that one has to test the spiritual master before accepting him, and the spiritual master has to test the disciple. There are various ways of associating with the spiritual master through his representatives, which enable us to test the spiritual master. Prabhupāda said that the disciples have to be representatives and they have to be prepared to defeat others’ arguments on behalf of the spiritual master.

There is the example of Jīva Gosvāmī who soundly defeated Rūpacandra, who later took initiation and became known as Rūpa-nārāyaṇa. Because of soundly defeating him, he was able to convince him to accept who Jīva Gosvāmī, himself, had accepted as his gurus— Rūpa and Sanātana Gosvāmīs. In the same way, the representatives of the spiritual master have to be able to defeat the arguments of the candidates for devotional service, and they have to nourish faith. Therefore, if one may not have direct association with the spiritual master, then the spiritual master is thinking of how to give his association in other ways to make himself personally accessible.

The disciples of Śrīla Prabhupāda grew up in a culture where Prabhupāda was present in his books, in his instructions, and in his representatives. Because of that implicit faith in Prabhupāda, we accepted this. If the spiritual master awakens faith in our heart and is somebody from whom we regularly hear, then we should also seek out those who properly represent the spiritual master to see how they can help us overcome our doubts and nourish our strength in devotional service. We should see them as representing the spiritual master and acknowledge that their association is as good as the association of the spiritual master. Once that faith is awakened, it has to be nourished. Without puṣṭiḥ, it is very difficult to advance in spiritual life.
